Omit app only when intentionally querying across all applications. Each execution includes duration, rows, buffer/temp/WAL/JIT/CPU counters, and the error message and SQLSTATE if it failed. Durations are in microseconds. The execution sample is capped at 10 rows, so when aggregate is present rely on its fields for totals.

tools_if_shown.name: get_postgres_metrics
tools_if_shown.description: Returns bucketed time-series metrics for a Postgres service over a time window (CPU, memory, disk, network, connections, cache hit ratio, throughput, transactions, wait events, lock waits, and more). Wait metrics are active_sessions_by_wait (one series per wait event, such as Lock:relation, or None when a session is not waiting), lock_wait_time (p50, p95, and Max series, in seconds), and blocked_sessions. Each metric has a key, name, unit, description, and one series per label dimension, where each series is a list of (timestamp, value) data points. Timestamps are Unix seconds at the bucket start. Provide fromDate and toDate to bound the window; omit bucketSizeSeconds to let the server pick a bucket granularity for the window. Use this to chart or analyze how a service behaved over time.

tools_if_shown.name: list_databases
tools_if_shown.description: Lists the databases in a ClickHouse Cloud service by running SHOW DATABASES as the authenticated identity. Returns only database names as an array of strings, with no tables, sizes, or other metadata; call list_tables with one of these names to see its tables and columns. If the query fails or the user lacks passwordless access to the service, result is an error object instead. Idle services are woken automatically and the call returns an error asking you to retry shortly; stopped services are never started automatically and must be started manually.

tools_if_shown.name: list_tables
tools_if_shown.description: Lists the tables of one database on a ClickHouse service by querying system.tables and system.columns as the authenticated identity, optionally narrowed with the like and notLike name patterns. Each table includes its engine and full engine definition, CREATE TABLE statement, sorting and primary keys, view dependencies, row, byte, part, and mark counts, comment, and its columns with type, default kind and expression, and comment. Returns an empty array when nothing matches. If the query fails or the user lacks passwordless access to the service, result is an error object instead. Idle services are woken automatically and the call returns an error asking you to retry shortly; stopped services are never started automatically and must be started manually.

tools_if_shown.name: get_services_list
tools_if_shown.description: Lists every ClickHouse and Managed Postgres service in an organization. Each entry has serviceType ("clickhouse" or "postgres"), id, name, provider, region, state, and createdAt; ClickHouse services add version, endpoints, replica and memory settings, idle scaling, IP access list, private endpoints, and encryption fields, while Postgres services add version, VM size, storage size, and HA type. Use the id values with the service-scoped tools. If one service kind cannot be listed, result holds the other kind and partialResults and warning explain what is missing; if both fail, result is an error object.

tools_if_shown.name: get_organization_details
tools_if_shown.description: Returns one organization: its id, name, creation time, configured private endpoints, and BYOC (bring your own cloud) configurations. The credentials must belong to the organization; otherwise result is an error object with status "error" and a message.

tools_if_shown.name: get_service_details
tools_if_shown.description: Returns a service that belongs to the organization. Supports both ClickHouse services and Managed Postgres services; the service type is detected automatically from the service id and is reported in the `serviceType` field of the response.

tools_if_shown.name: list_clickpipes
tools_if_shown.description: Lists the ClickPipes of a ClickHouse service. Each entry has id, name, description, state, scaling, source and destination configuration, field mappings, and creation and update times; returns an empty array when the service has none. Pass an id to get_clickpipe for the fully typed definition of one pipe. If the lookup fails, result is an error object.

tools_if_shown.name: list_service_backups
tools_if_shown.description: Lists the backups of a ClickHouse service, most recent first. Each backup has id, status, start and finish times, size in bytes, duration in seconds, type, and, for backups exported to a customer bucket, the backup name and bucket details. On success result has status "success" and a backups array; on failure it is an error object with status "error" and a message.

tools_if_shown.name: get_organization_cost
tools_if_shown.description: Returns usage costs for an organization over an inclusive range of UTC calendar days from from_date to to_date (both required, at most 31 days). result has grandTotalCHC, the total in ClickHouse Credits (CHC), and costs, one record per day per billed entity (data warehouse, service, or ClickPipe) with the entity id and name, a per-metric CHC breakdown, the day total, and whether the record is final. On failure result is an error object with status "error" and a message.

tools_if_shown.name: get_service_backup_details
tools_if_shown.description: Returns one backup of a ClickHouse service: its status, start and finish times, size in bytes, duration in seconds, type, and, when the backup was exported to a customer bucket, its name and bucket details. Use list_service_backups to find backup ids. On failure result is an error object with status "error" and a message.

tools_if_shown.name: get_service_backup_configuration
tools_if_shown.description: Returns the backup schedule of a ClickHouse service: backupPeriodInHours (interval between backups), backupRetentionPeriodInHours (how long backups stay available), and backupStartTime (UTC HH:MM, present only when a custom start time is set). On failure result is an error object with status "error" and a message.

tools_if_shown.name: get_organizations

tools_if_shown.name: list_postgres_slow_query_patterns

tools_if_shown.name: list_pages
tools_if_shown.description: List every published Common Practice page: the Home, About and Contact pages and the sample training pages. Returns each page's ID, title, summary, opening text, Website, Markdown and image addresses, and search metadata. Use it to find a page ID for get_page.

tools_if_shown.name: get_page
tools_if_shown.description: Read one published page by its ID. format data (the default) returns the full page: title, heading, text, sections or training body, addresses and metadata. markdown returns the page as Markdown text, og its social image as base64 PNG, and seo only its search metadata. Training pages are illustrative samples; the Contact form is a preview that cannot send messages.

tools_if_shown.name: list_courses
tools_if_shown.description: List Common Practice's sample training courses. Returns each course's ID, title, summary, audience, outcomes, prerequisites, chapter and page counts, and first page. Use a course ID with get_course. The courses are illustrative and unassessed.

tools_if_shown.name: get_course
tools_if_shown.description: Read one sample course by its ID. Returns the course details and its chapters in order, each with its pages' IDs, titles, summaries and addresses. Use get_page with a page ID for the page body. Browser-saved progress is private to the visitor and never returned.

tools_if_shown.name: get_linkedin_profile
tools_if_shown.description: Fetch one person's LinkedIn profile by its URL: name, headline, location, current company and title, positions, education, skills. It costs what the provider's credits cost us, taken from the Datacircle balance with no markup: up2data $0.002375 per profile found, free when it isn't found, up to $1 a day per account; harvestapi $0.0037 per profile found, every section of the profile; fetchin $0.001485 per lookup, found or not, every section. Every call is live: the provider is asked each time, so the profile is as it is today. The answer is the provider's own JSON plus datacircle_meta {provider, cost_usd, balance_usd}. If up2data answers its daily limit (429), call again with provider fetchin or harvestapi; if the balance is too low (402), add_funds. Details: https://docs.datacircle.dev/pricing

tools_if_shown.name: get_balance
tools_if_shown.description: Read the Datacircle balance, in USD: balance_usd is everything calls can spend now, then what it is made of: signup_credit_usd (left of the sign-up credit), funds_usd (left of the funds added), manual_credit_usd, and temporary_credits, each with its campaign, credit_usd and expires_at. Read it to know whether the balance covers the calls you are about to make. Free.

tools_if_shown.name: list_files
tools_if_shown.description: List the co-op files: one per provider, every profile any customer fetched through it, new every day. Each file has its id, dataset, filename, row_count, size_bytes, created_at and is_unlocked: true once this account has added $50 or more in funds. Get one with get_download_link. This call is free.

tools_if_shown.name: get_download_link
tools_if_shown.description: Get a download link for one file from list_files, by its id: url, a signed link valid one hour, fetched as is without the API key, and next_step: what the file holds, with a ready-to-run call per provider for the live profile behind any row. A locked file answers an error saying how to unlock it. Free.

tools_if_shown.name: add_funds
tools_if_shown.description: Start a Stripe Checkout that adds funds to the Datacircle balance. It answers checkout_url: give it to the user to open and pay; nothing is charged until they do. $50 or more in funds also unlocks the co-op files: the flat file of every API request, new every day.

tools_if_shown.name: get_me
tools_if_shown.description: Read who this connection is signed in as and what it may reach: your actor identity and, for an OAuth connection, the repositories and permissions the user approved and when it expires. Returns null when the credential names no user. Call it first to learn which repositories the other tools can reach; a repository connected later needs a new connection.

tools_if_shown.name: list_repositories
tools_if_shown.description: List the repositories this connection can read, oldest first, one page at a time, narrowed by owner, topic or name prefix (filters combine). Signed in, it lists the approved repositories; without sign-in it lists public repositories only, needs owner or topic, and q is not available. Pass an item's owner and name to the other tools.

tools_if_shown.name: get_repository
tools_if_shown.description: Read one repository: its identity, description, topics, visibility, default branch, fork parent, version and timestamps. Use it to find the default branch before list_refs, list_tree or read_file, and the id before create_pull_request.

tools_if_shown.name: list_refs
tools_if_shown.description: List a repository's branches or its tags, sorted by name, one page at a time, optionally narrowed by a name substring. Each ref carries the commit it points to and, for an annotated tag, its signature check. Pass a ref's name as ref to list_tree, read_file or search_code, or its target commit's oid as oid to pin later reads to one commit.

tools_if_shown.name: list_tree
tools_if_shown.description: List the entries of one directory of a repository, not recursively, at a branch, tag or commit, one page at a time; later pages stay on the same commit. Each entry says whether it is a file, directory, submodule or symbolic link. Omit path for the root; pass a tree's path back to descend and a blob's path to read_file.

tools_if_shown.name: read_file
tools_if_shown.description: Read one file of a repository at a branch, tag or commit, a window of lines at a time. A text file comes with its line window and nextLine to continue; a binary file comes with null content. A window holds at most maxLines lines and 64 KiB; a file over 1 MiB cannot be read. Take path from list_tree or search_code.

tools_if_shown.name: search_code
tools_if_shown.description: Search the text files of a repository at a branch, tag or commit for a literal string, optionally within one file or directory. Matches come one per matching line, in file and line order, with context lines; truncated says when maxMatches or a size limit cut them short, so narrow by path or raise maxMatches. Pass a match's path and lineNumber to read_file.

tools_if_shown.name: list_issues
tools_if_shown.description: List a repository's issues, newest first, one page at a time, optionally narrowed by workflow state or by words in the title or description; total counts every match. Pass an issue's number as issue to issue_read, update_issue and add_comment, and reuse the label, assignee and milestone IDs it shows when creating issues.

tools_if_shown.name: issue_read
tools_if_shown.description: Read one issue, one facet per call. detail (the default): the issue, with its version and what you may do to it. comments: one page of its comments, oldest first, with the IDs and versions update_comment takes. Take the issue number from list_issues or a create_issue receipt.

tools_if_shown.name: list_pull_requests
tools_if_shown.description: List a repository's pull requests, oldest first, one page at a time, optionally narrowed by lifecycle state or by text in the title. Each item carries the number, head commit and version the other pull request tools take. For a pull request's description, merge readiness, reviews, commits, files or comments call pull_request_read.

tools_if_shown.name: pull_request_read
tools_if_shown.description: Read one pull request, one facet per call. detail: the pull request, with its version, headOid, mergeRoute and what you may do to it. status: merge readiness and checks, with the version, headOid and baseOid merge_pull_request needs. reviews, commits, files, comments: one page each; files carries the version and paths get_pull_request_diff takes, comments the IDs and versions add_comment and update_comment take. merge_status: a merge operation's outcome; poll an accepted merge with backoff, as accepted is not completed. Take the number from list_pull_requests or a create_pull_request receipt.

tools_if_shown.name: get_pull_request_diff
tools_if_shown.description: Read the patch of chosen changed files of a pull request, pinned to the version the files were listed at. Each file comes with its hunks and line origins; a binary or too-large file has no hunks, and hunksOmitted marks a file whose hunks did not fit the response, so request fewer paths. Take paths and expectedVersion from pull_request_read facet files; the line numbers are what add_comment target pull_inline anchors to.

tools_if_shown.name: create_issue
tools_if_shown.description: Create an issue in a repository with a title and, optionally, a description, priority, due date, workflow state, labels, assignees and a milestone. Returns the new issue's number and the version its next write takes. Take label, assignee and milestone IDs from the issues list_issues or issue_read return, and your own actorId from get_me. There is no idempotency key: on an unknown outcome, list_issues before trying again rather than retrying automatically.

tools_if_shown.name: update_issue
tools_if_shown.description: Change one issue, one action per call: edit its title, description, priority, due date or open workflow state; close it as completed or canceled; or reopen it. Returns the version the next write takes. Take the number and current version from issue_read, list_issues or the last receipt; the write fails if the issue changed since. An edit overwrites the previous values, which are not kept; title, description and open/closed changes also reach a linked GitHub issue. Labels, assignees and milestones cannot be changed with these tools.

tools_if_shown.name: add_comment
tools_if_shown.description: Post one comment, by target: on an issue; in a pull request's conversation; inline on a file or lines of a pull request's diff, anchored to an exact commit; or as a reply in an existing pull request thread, which inherits the thread's anchor. Returns the comment's id and version for update_comment, and for a pull request comment its threadId. For an inline comment take path and the commit (headOid for the right side and file comments, comparisonBaseOid for the left side) from pull_request_read facet files; for a reply take replyTo from facet comments. There is no idempotency key: on an unknown outcome, read the comments before trying again rather than retrying automatically.

tools_if_shown.name: update_comment
tools_if_shown.description: Change one comment, one action per call: edit the body of an issue or pull request comment, or resolve or unresolve a pull request thread. Returns the version the next write takes. Take the comment ID and current version from issue_read or pull_request_read facet comments or the last receipt; the write fails if the comment changed since. To resolve or unresolve, pass the thread's root comment (its threadId) and that root's version. An edit overwrites the old text, which is not kept; resolution stays in GitCafe and is not written to GitHub. Comments cannot be hidden or deleted with these tools.

tools_if_shown.name: merge_pull_request
tools_if_shown.description: Merge a pull request into its target branch with an explicit strategy, at the exact head, base and version you reviewed. Returns a merge operation: accepted is admitted but not merged yet, completed is merged, failed is not merged. Take headOid, baseOid and expectedVersion from pull_request_read facet status, and which strategies are allowed from its merge verdict; follow an accepted operation with facet merge_status, with backoff. A merge cannot be undone with these tools. On an unknown outcome, retry with the same requestId and input, never with a new key; a different input under the same requestId is rejected.

tools_if_shown.name: ci_read
tools_if_shown.description: Read a repository's CI, one facet per call. runs: one page of Buildkite runs, newest first, narrowed by commit or state. run: one run by runId. checks: one page of the checks on a commit, with a summary over all of them. jobs: one page of a run's jobs. log: the end of a job's log. Runs, run and checks read what GitCafe recorded, including GitHub checks on a linked repository; jobs and log read Buildkite live and need the repository owner to have shared logs. Take the commit from pull_request_read (headOid) or list_refs, runId from a run or check, and jobId from facet jobs. Long text fields are cut to fit, and truncatedFields names them. CI cannot be started, rerun or cancelled with these tools.

tools_if_shown.name: create_pull_request
tools_if_shown.description: Open a pull request that merges a source branch of this repository or a fork into a target branch, with a title and optional description. Returns the new pull request's number and the version its next write takes. Take sourceRepo from get_repository (the fork's id, or this repository's) and the branch names from list_refs; the source branch must already be pushed with git or the Cafe CLI, as these tools cannot push. With a stable submissionKey, retrying after an unknown outcome returns the original pull request instead of a duplicate; without one, list_pull_requests before trying again rather than retrying automatically.

tools_if_shown.name: update_pull_request
tools_if_shown.description: Change one pull request, one action per call: edit its title, description or target branch; close it without merging (which also clears draft); reopen it; mark it as a draft; or mark it ready for review. Returns the version the next write takes. Take the number and current version from pull_request_read, list_pull_requests or the last receipt; the write fails if the pull request changed since. An edit overwrites the previous values, which are not kept; title, description and state changes also reach a linked GitHub pull request. Merging is merge_pull_request; reviewers, labels and assignees cannot be changed with these tools.

tools_if_shown.name: submit_review
tools_if_shown.description: Submit a review of a pull request at an exact commit and version: approve, request changes, or comment without a decision, with an optional overall body. Returns the review with its id, verdict and commit. Take commitOid (headOid) and expectedVersion from pull_request_read facet detail or status; the review fails if the pull request changed since, so read again and resubmit at the new head. To publish a draft review you saved in the GitCafe web UI, with its inline comments, pass its id and version as draft with the same verdict, body and commit it was saved with; these tools cannot create or read drafts. Approving or requesting changes on your own pull request is refused, and a submitted review cannot be withdrawn with these tools. On an unknown outcome, retry with the same requestId and input, which returns the original review; a different input under the same requestId is rejected.

Each entry says whether it is a file, directory, submodule or symbolic link. Omit path for the root; pass a tree's path back to descend and a blob's path to read_file.

tools_if_shown.name: read_file
tools_if_shown.description: Read one file of a repository at a branch, tag or commit, a window of lines at a time. A text file comes with its line window and nextLine to continue; a binary file comes with null content. A window holds at most maxLines lines and 64 KiB; a file over 1 MiB cannot be read. Take path from list_tree or search_code.

tools_if_shown.name: search_code
tools_if_shown.description: Search the text files of a repository at a branch, tag or commit for a literal string, optionally within one file or directory. Matches come one per matching line, in file and line order, with context lines; truncated says when maxMatches or a size limit cut them short, so narrow by path or raise maxMatches. Pass a match's path and lineNumber to read_file.

tools_if_shown.name: list_issues
tools_if_shown.description: List a repository's issues, newest first, one page at a time, optionally narrowed by workflow state or by words in the title or description; total counts every match. Pass an issue's number as issue to issue_read, update_issue and add_comment, and reuse the label, assignee and milestone IDs it shows when creating issues.

tools_if_shown.name: issue_read
tools_if_shown.description: Read one issue, one facet per call. detail (the default): the issue, with its version and what you may do to it. comments: one page of its comments, oldest first, with the IDs and versions update_comment takes. Take the issue number from list_issues or a create_issue receipt.

tools_if_shown.name: list_pull_requests
tools_if_shown.description: List a repository's pull requests, oldest first, one page at a time, optionally narrowed by lifecycle state or by text in the title. Each item carries the number, head commit and version the other pull request tools take. For a pull request's description, merge readiness, reviews, commits, files or comments call pull_request_read.

tools_if_shown.name: pull_request_read
tools_if_shown.description: Read one pull request, one facet per call. detail: the pull request, with its version, headOid, mergeRoute and what you may do to it. status: merge readiness and checks, with the version, headOid and baseOid merge_pull_request needs. reviews, commits, files, comments: one page each; files carries the version and paths get_pull_request_diff takes, comments the IDs and versions add_comment and update_comment take. merge_status: a merge operation's outcome; poll an accepted merge with backoff, as accepted is not completed. Take the number from list_pull_requests or a create_pull_request receipt.

tools_if_shown.name: get_pull_request_diff
tools_if_shown.description: Read the patch of chosen changed files of a pull request, pinned to the version the files were listed at. Each file comes with its hunks and line origins; a binary or too-large file has no hunks, and hunksOmitted marks a file whose hunks did not fit the response, so request fewer paths. Take paths and expectedVersion from pull_request_read facet files; the line numbers are what add_comment target pull_inline anchors to.

tools_if_shown.name: create_issue
tools_if_shown.description: Create an issue in a repository with a title and, optionally, a description, priority, due date, workflow state, labels, assignees and a milestone. Returns the new issue's number and the version its next write takes. Take label, assignee and milestone IDs from the issues list_issues or issue_read return, and your own actorId from get_me. There is no idempotency key: on an unknown outcome, list_issues before trying again rather than retrying automatically.

tools_if_shown.name: update_issue
tools_if_shown.description: Change one issue, one action per call: edit its title, description, priority, due date or open workflow state; close it as completed or canceled; or reopen it. Returns the version the next write takes. Take the number and current version from issue_read, list_issues or the last receipt; the write fails if the issue changed since. An edit overwrites the previous values, which are not kept; title, description and open/closed changes also reach a linked GitHub issue. Labels, assignees and milestones cannot be changed with these tools.

tools_if_shown.name: add_comment
tools_if_shown.description: Post one comment, by target: on an issue; in a pull request's conversation; inline on a file or lines of a pull request's diff, anchored to an exact commit; or as a reply in an existing pull request thread, which inherits the thread's anchor. Returns the comment's id and version for update_comment, and for a pull request comment its threadId. For an inline comment take path and the commit (headOid for the right side and file comments, comparisonBaseOid for the left side) from pull_request_read facet files; for a reply take replyTo from facet comments. There is no idempotency key: on an unknown outcome, read the comments before trying again rather than retrying automatically.

tools_if_shown.name: update_comment
tools_if_shown.description: Change one comment, one action per call: edit the body of an issue or pull request comment, or resolve or unresolve a pull request thread. Returns the version the next write takes. Take the comment ID and current version from issue_read or pull_request_read facet comments or the last receipt; the write fails if the comment changed since. To resolve or unresolve, pass the thread's root comment (its threadId) and that root's version. An edit overwrites the old text, which is not kept; resolution stays in GitCafe and is not written to GitHub. Comments cannot be hidden or deleted with these tools.

tools_if_shown.name: merge_pull_request
tools_if_shown.description: Merge a pull request into its target branch with an explicit strategy, at the exact head, base and version you reviewed. Returns a merge operation: accepted is admitted but not merged yet, completed is merged, failed is not merged. Take headOid, baseOid and expectedVersion from pull_request_read facet status, and which strategies are allowed from its merge verdict; follow an accepted operation with facet merge_status, with backoff. A merge cannot be undone with these tools. On an unknown outcome, retry with the same requestId and input, never with a new key; a different input under the same requestId is rejected.

tools_if_shown.name: ci_read
tools_if_shown.description: Read a repository's CI, one facet per call. runs: one page of Buildkite runs, newest first, narrowed by commit or state. run: one run by runId. checks: one page of the checks on a commit, with a summary over all of them. jobs: one page of a run's jobs. log: the end of a job's log. Runs, run and checks read what GitCafe recorded, including GitHub checks on a linked repository; jobs and log read Buildkite live and need the repository owner to have shared logs. Take the commit from pull_request_read (headOid) or list_refs, runId from a run or check, and jobId from facet jobs. Long text fields are cut to fit, and truncatedFields names them. CI cannot be started, rerun or cancelled with these tools.

tools_if_shown.name: create_pull_request
tools_if_shown.description: Open a pull request that merges a source branch of this repository or a fork into a target branch, with a title and optional description. Returns the new pull request's number and the version its next write takes. Take sourceRepo from get_repository (the fork's id, or this repository's) and the branch names from list_refs; the source branch must already be pushed with git or the Cafe CLI, as these tools cannot push. With a stable submissionKey, retrying after an unknown outcome returns the original pull request instead of a duplicate; without one, list_pull_requests before trying again rather than retrying automatically.

tools_if_shown.name: update_pull_request
tools_if_shown.description: Change one pull request, one action per call: edit its title, description or target branch; close it without merging (which also clears draft); reopen it; mark it as a draft; or mark it ready for review. Returns the version the next write takes. Take the number and current version from pull_request_read, list_pull_requests or the last receipt; the write fails if the pull request changed since. An edit overwrites the previous values, which are not kept; title, description and state changes also reach a linked GitHub pull request. Merging is merge_pull_request; reviewers, labels and assignees cannot be changed with these tools.

tools_if_shown.name: submit_review
tools_if_shown.description: Submit a review of a pull request at an exact commit and version: approve, request changes, or comment without a decision, with an optional overall body. Returns the review with its id, verdict and commit. Take commitOid (headOid) and expectedVersion from pull_request_read facet detail or status; the review fails if the pull request changed since, so read again and resubmit at the new head. To publish a draft review you saved in the GitCafe web UI, with its inline comments, pass its id and version as draft with the same verdict, body and commit it was saved with; these tools cannot create or read drafts. Approving or requesting changes on your own pull request is refused, and a submitted review cannot be withdrawn with these tools. On an unknown outcome, retry with the same requestId and input, which returns the original review; a different input under the same requestId is rejected.

tools_if_shown.name: submit_feedback
tools_if_shown.description: Send a report about GitCafe itself to the GitCafe team: a tool that failed or misbehaved, a confusing result, or a missing capability. Returns a reference to give the user for any follow-up; the report is not readable with these tools. Give a one-line summary, what you tried and what happened in body, and the tool name, request ID or problem code in context. A bug in the user's own repository is an issue for create_issue, not feedback. There is no idempotency key: on an unknown outcome, tell the user rather than retrying automatically, as a retry files a second report.

detail_provenance.offline_parser_correction: Decoded escaped leading dollar literals and omitted Flight undefined properties; original HTML hash/timestamp retained.

tools_if_shown.name: getSelf
tools_if_shown.description: Returns who this connection acts as: `principal_type`, `user_id` or `service_user_id`, granted `scopes`, and the bound workspace's `org_id`, `organization_name` and `organization_slug`. A cheap first call that confirms the connection works and shows which scopes the tools can use.

tools_if_shown.name: getDeployment
tools_if_shown.description: Returns the answering replica's release identity: `reason_version`, `commit_sha`, `artifact_sha`, `environment`, `branch` and `deployment_id` (null when not built in), `checked_at` and supported options such as `session_modes`. It confirms which build serves, not other replicas' health.

tools_if_shown.name: submitFeedback
tools_if_shown.description: Reports a problem with Reason to the Reason team: a wrong or surprising response, an undocumented error, friction or a missing capability. Send one report per problem, with `session_id` when one Session is affected. Returns `ok: true` and `submitted_at` once delivered; any credential may report.

tools_if_shown.name: getOpenApiDocument
tools_if_shown.description: Returns the published OpenAPI 3.1 document of the Reason v3 REST API (`openapi`, `info`, `paths`): every operation's parameters, required scope and error responses. It is large, for settling an exact request or response shape a tool's own schema leaves open. 503 when unavailable.

tools_if_shown.name: listOrganizations
tools_if_shown.description: Lists the workspaces this connection can act on, each with `id`, `slug`, `name` and the caller's `membership_role`, to confirm which workspace calls reach and what the caller may do there. A connection bound to one workspace lists only that one. Reading changes nothing.

tools_if_shown.name: createOrganization
tools_if_shown.description: Creates a workspace owned by the caller from a non-empty `name`; the server generates the slug. Returns it under `organization` with the number of invitations sent as `invited`. An OAuth connection is refused with 403 `oauth_org_bound`.

tools_if_shown.name: getOrganization
tools_if_shown.description: Returns the workspace this connection acts on, under `organization`: its `id`, `slug`, `name` and the caller's `membership_role`, which decides which writes are allowed (renaming or deleting it needs owner). Use it to confirm the target workspace before a write. Reading changes nothing.

tools_if_shown.name: updateOrganization
tools_if_shown.description: Renames the connected workspace and returns it under `organization`. Requires the owner role and a non-empty `name`. The slug is derived again from the new name, so a rename changes the slug as well; no other field changes.

tools_if_shown.name: deleteOrganization
tools_if_shown.description: Permanently deletes the connected workspace; it cannot be undone. Requires the owner role and a `name` equal to the current workspace name, as `getOrganization` returns it. A personal workspace is refused, and 409 means retention, pending charges or settlement blocked the deletion.

tools_if_shown.name: listAgentModels
tools_if_shown.description: Lists the models a session here can run on, Reason's first, then connected provider accounts', each with `id`, `label`, `provider`, `reasoning_efforts` and whether it is `available` now. An `id` goes to `createSession` as `model`, one of its `reasoning_efforts` as `reasoning_effort`.

tools_if_shown.name: getAgentAuthStatus
tools_if_shown.description: Reports whether Reason's managed inference can run sessions now (`reason`, `reason_subscription_available`, `reason_openai_available`); other fields are fixed compatibility values. Runnable models come from `listAgentModels`; a saved account is checked by `checkProviderAccount`.

tools_if_shown.name: listAttachments
tools_if_shown.description: Lists files uploaded to the workspace, newest first, to find an `id` for `downloadAttachment` or `deleteAttachment`. Each item has `id`, `name`, `content_type`, `size_bytes`, `created_at` and a short-lived `url` (null when unsigned). Pass `end_cursor` as `cursor` while `has_next_page` is true.

tools_if_shown.name: createAttachment
tools_if_shown.description: Uploads a file to the workspace, from `filename` and base64 `data_base64` of up to 1 MiB, so it can be referenced or downloaded later. Returns the new `id`, `name` and a short-lived download `url`, which can be null. The stored content type is derived from the bytes, not the filename.

tools_if_shown.name: downloadAttachment
tools_if_shown.description: Gets a short-lived signed `download_url`, with `expires_at` when the link states one, for one workspace or Session attachment. Take the id from `listAttachments`, `createAttachment` or `listSessionAttachments`. Fetch the link with a plain GET and no Authorization header; an unknown id returns 404.

tools_if_shown.name: deleteAttachment
tools_if_shown.description: Deletes a file uploaded to the workspace permanently, with its stored bytes, and returns `ok` and the deleted `id`. Uploaders can delete their own files; owners and admins can delete any. Files kept by a session's agent are a separate store and are unaffected.

tools_if_shown.name: downloadAttachmentWithFilename
tools_if_shown.description: Works like `downloadAttachment` for clients that save the file under a chosen name: returns a short-lived signed `download_url`, with `expires_at` when known. The trailing `filename` only names the download and is not checked against the stored name. Fetch the link with no Authorization header.

tools_if_shown.name: listAuditLogs
tools_if_shown.description: Returns newest-first audit `items`, each with its `action`, actor, target, `metadata` and time, plus `has_next_page` and `end_cursor`. Filter by `action`, `actor`, `since` and `before`; pass `end_cursor` as `before` for the next page. Only owners and admins see other members' secret names.

tools_if_shown.name: listAutomations
tools_if_shown.description: Lists the workspace's automations, newest first, with an `id` that `getAutomation`, `updateAutomation` and `createAutomationTrigger` take. Items have `id`, `name`, `instructions`, `model`, `enabled`, `tools`, `environment` and `triggers`. Set `include` to `system` for system ones; page with `after`.

tools_if_shown.name: createAutomation
tools_if_shown.description: Creates an automation: saved `instructions` an agent runs each time a trigger fires, optionally in a connected `repo`. It starts enabled unless `enabled` is false, and fires nothing until `createAutomationTrigger` adds a schedule. Returns the automation with its `id` and any `warnings`.

tools_if_shown.name: getAutomation
tools_if_shown.description: Returns one automation: instructions, enabled state, tool configuration, environment and triggers. Reading runs nothing. Unknown ids return 404 `automation_not_found`.

tools_if_shown.name: updateAutomation
tools_if_shown.description: Changes an automation's name, instructions, model, tools or `enabled` state for future runs; only the fields sent change, and it is returned updated. Send `enabled` false to pause it. Only its creator edits a user automation (owners and admins may pause it); owners and admins change system ones.

tools_if_shown.name: deleteAutomation
tools_if_shown.description: Permanently deletes a user-authored automation and all its triggers. To stop it but keep it, use `updateAutomation` with `enabled` false. An unknown id, or a system automation's id, also succeeds and deletes nothing. Allowed for the creator and for owners and admins.

tools_if_shown.name: listAutomationTriggers
tools_if_shown.description: Lists one automation's triggers as `items`, each with `id`, `kind`, `enabled`, `schedule` (with `next_run_at`), `github`, `webhook` and `last_fired_at`. Use it to see when a schedule fires next or find a trigger `id` for `deleteAutomationTrigger`. Webhook secrets are never returned.

tools_if_shown.name: createAutomationTrigger
tools_if_shown.description: Adds a schedule trigger from exactly one of `frequency` (cron), `every_seconds` or `scheduled_at` (one-time); more than one returns 400 `schedule_conflict`. Returns the trigger's `id`, `enabled`, `schedule` with `next_run_at`, and any `warnings`. The trigger then starts billed runs.

tools_if_shown.name: deleteAutomationTrigger
tools_if_shown.description: Permanently deletes one trigger of an automation; the automation and its other triggers are unchanged, and it no longer fires on that condition. Runs already started continue. An unknown trigger id also succeeds. The same creator, owner and admin rules as `updateAutomation` apply.

tools_if_shown.name: getCloudAccess
tools_if_shown.description: Returns what a cloud trust policy needs to give runs temporary credentials: `issuer`, `jwks_uri`, `workspace_id`, `subject_format` and `token_url`, plus saved `connections` with `config`, `enabled`, `allowed_triggers` and `last_test_ok`. Read it before `setCloudAccessConnection`; 404 when it is off.

tools_if_shown.name: setCloudAccessConnection
tools_if_shown.description: Saves the workspace's one connection for a cloud `provider`, replacing its `config` of cloud-side identifiers (never secret keys). Owner or admin only. A changed config clears the last test; a new one is enabled for `manual` and `api` triggers. Verify it with `testCloudAccessConnection`.

tools_if_shown.name: deleteCloudAccessConnection
tools_if_shown.description: Removes the workspace's cloud access connection for one provider. Requires owner or admin. Sessions are no longer issued that provider's credentials; a missing connection also succeeds.

tools_if_shown.name: testCloudAccessConnection
tools_if_shown.description: Tests a saved connection with a real token exchange and saves the verdict as its last test. Requires owner or admin. Returns `ok`, the tested `subject`, `tested_at`, and the granted `identity` or an `error` with `code` and `message`; a provider refusal returns `ok` false, not an error.

tools_if_shown.name: getDailyConsumption
tools_if_shown.description: Returns workspace spend, credit and sandbox minutes from `start_date` to `end_date` (the last 30 days by default) as `daily`, one entry per UTC day with activity, plus a window `total`. A date-only `end_date` excludes that day. With `group_by`, `items` holds per-Session or per-user totals.

tools_if_shown.name: listDevices
tools_if_shown.description: Lists the caller's Devices, or every member's with `scope` workspace (owner or admin), including expired and revoked ones but not managed infrastructure. Returns `devices`, each with `id`, `status`, `online`, `compatible` and `roots`, plus `has_next_page` and `end_cursor`; pass it as `after`.

tools_if_shown.name: getDevice
tools_if_shown.description: Returns one Device under `device`, with its approved `roots`, `status`, `online`, `compatible` and `compatibility_reason`, to check before targeting it. It reads the caller's Devices unless `scope` is workspace, which requires owner or admin.

tools_if_shown.name: revokeDevice
tools_if_shown.description: Permanently revokes a Device the caller owns: its queued and claimed work is cancelled and it receives no more Sessions; to return it has to enroll again. Another member's Device cannot be revoked here. Returns `revoked` true, also when it was already revoked.

tools_if_shown.name: addDeviceRoot
tools_if_shown.description: Approves one more folder on the caller's own headless Device, from `listDevices`, without re-enrolling it; it takes the existing roots' execution mode, and a folder already held comes back unchanged. Returns `root` with `id`, `label`, `permissions` and `execution_mode`; 409 when the Device is full.

tools_if_shown.name: removeDeviceRoot
tools_if_shown.description: Revokes an approved folder on the caller's own active personal headless Device and cancels queued and claimed work in it; local files stay. Its last folder cannot be removed (409). Returns `removed` true, also for a folder already removed.

tools_if_shown.name: updateDeviceRootGrant
tools_if_shown.description: Changes a folder's permissions and execution mode on the caller's active headless Device, within its enrollment ceilings, given the current `expected_grant_revision`. Cancels queued and claimed work in that folder. Returns `root` with `permissions`, `execution_mode` and the new `grant_revision`.

tools_if_shown.name: retireEphemeralWorkspace
tools_if_shown.description: Ends a single-use benchmark workspace of this parent after its run: cancels its live work, revokes its Devices and deletes its key, keeping transcripts until purged. Owner or admin only. Returns `organization_id`, `reference`, `retired_at` and the saved `outcome`; retrying returns the same.

tools_if_shown.name: listGitPlugins
tools_if_shown.description: Lists, in one page of `plugins`, the workspace's GitHub App installations and the caller's personal GitHub grant if any, with `id`, `grant` (team or personal), `host`, `account_login` and `account_type`. An `id` goes to `listGitPluginRepositories` to see what that account reaches.

tools_if_shown.name: listGitPluginRepositories
tools_if_shown.description: Lists every repository one account from `listGitPlugins` reaches, in one page of `items` with `full_name`, `web_url`, `private` and `pushed_at`, to check that account's access; `listRepositories` covers all accounts. An id not linked to this workspace returns 404.

tools_if_shown.name: listMachines
tools_if_shown.description: Lists up to 200 Machines (named worker queues a Session can target) in name order under `machines`, each with `id`, `name`, `platform`, `workers` counts (`total`, `online`, `busy`, `idle`) and `sessions` counts (`queued`, `running`). Use it to pick a Machine or find its id; any member may read.

tools_if_shown.name: createMachine
tools_if_shown.description: Creates a Machine: a named queue that Sessions can target to run on workers the workspace enrolls itself. Requires owner or admin; a name already in use, in any letter case, returns 409. Returns `machine` with its `id`, `name`, `platform` and zero `workers`; workers are added over REST.

tools_if_shown.name: getMachine
tools_if_shown.description: Returns one Machine, by id or name from `listMachines`, under `machine`: its `id`, `name`, `platform`, `workers` counts (`online`, `busy`, `idle`) and `sessions` counts (`queued`, `running`). Use it to check for idle workers before targeting it; an unknown Machine returns 404.

tools_if_shown.name: deleteMachine
tools_if_shown.description: Deletes a Machine for good. Requires owner or admin. Every worker and token of it is revoked, workers' queued and claimed work is cancelled, and Sessions waiting in its queue stop. Returns `deleted`, `revoked_workers` and `revoked_tokens`.

tools_if_shown.name: listMachineTokens
tools_if_shown.description: Lists a Machine's tokens under `tokens`, newest first, each with `id`, `name`, `token_prefix`, `last_used_at` and `revoked_at` (null while usable), to find the `id` that `revokeMachineToken` takes. Requires owner or admin; token secrets are never returned.

tools_if_shown.name: revokeMachineToken
tools_if_shown.description: Revokes one Machine token, by the `id` from `listMachineTokens`, so it mints no more enrollment tickets. Requires owner or admin. Workers already enrolled with it keep running; remove them with `revokeDevice` or `deleteMachine`. Returns `revoked` true.

tools_if_shown.name: listMcpServers
tools_if_shown.description: Lists the workspace's MCP servers, whose tools sessions can use, in `items` with `id`, `name`, `transport`, `enabled`, `connection_state` and `tool_names`. No secret values: `secret_names` are credentials stored on each server, not workspace secrets; the secrets API does not list them.

tools_if_shown.name: getMcpServer
tools_if_shown.description: Returns one MCP server by `id` from `listMcpServers`, with `name`, `transport`, `url` or `command`, `auth_type`, `connection_state` and `tool_names`; unknown ids return 404. No secret values: `secret_names` are credentials stored on the server; the secrets API does not list them.

tools_if_shown.name: listMembers
tools_if_shown.description: Lists the workspace's members, each with `user_id`, `email` and `role`, to find the `user_id` that `getMember`, `setMemberRole` and `removeMember` take. Owners and admins also get the pending `invites`; for other members that list is empty. Reading changes nothing.

tools_if_shown.name: inviteMember
tools_if_shown.description: Invites the given `emails` to join the workspace with `role` (admin when omitted). Requires owner or admin. Returns `invited`, the invitations recorded, and `sent`, the emails delivered; a lower `sent` means some people got no email. Invitees appear under `invites` in `listMembers`.

tools_if_shown.name: getMember
tools_if_shown.description: Returns one workspace member by the `user_id` from `listMembers`: `user_id`, `email`, `role`, `avatar_url` and `created_at`. Use it to check someone's role before `setMemberRole` or `removeMember`. A user who is not a member returns 404 `member_not_found`.

tools_if_shown.name: removeMember
tools_if_shown.description: Removes a person, by the `user_id` from `listMembers`, from this workspace; their account and other workspaces are untouched. Requires owner or admin, and only owners can remove owners. Removing the last owner returns 409 `last_owner`.

tools_if_shown.name: setMemberRole
tools_if_shown.description: Changes a member's workspace role, by the `user_id` from `listMembers`, to `owner`, `admin` or `member`; not a product tier or key scope. Requires owner or admin, and only owners grant or change the owner role. Returns `user_id` and the new `role`; demoting the last owner returns 409 `last_owner`.

tools_if_shown.name: getUsageMetrics
tools_if_shown.description: Returns the workspace's model usage for the last 30 days as daily `points`, each with `input_tokens`, `output_tokens` and `sandbox_minutes`, plus the `start_date` and `end_date` of the window. Reading it changes nothing.

tools_if_shown.name: completeOnboardingImport
tools_if_shown.description: Marks an approved local secret import finished, given the `handoff` or a consumed `pairing_id` and `imported_secret_count` (values the CLI imported), and returns `status` completed. It follows an approved `getOnboardingImportDecision`. No values are sent; an unapproved handoff returns 400.

tools_if_shown.name: getOnboardingImportDecision
tools_if_shown.description: Reads, without changing it, the browser's decision on a local secret import by `handoff` or `pairing_id`: `status` (pending, expired, approved or completed), `selected_names` once approved, `imported_secret_count` once completed. The CLI polls it; secret values never pass through it.

tools_if_shown.name: claimExistingCliPairing
tools_if_shown.description: Attaches the current CLI OAuth grant to a browser `pairing_code` and returns the pairing's `pairing_id` (the same one when the same client repeats the claim) and `recovered`. No secrets are imported. Expired or unusable codes return 400 `invalid_cli_pairing`.

tools_if_shown.name: reportCliPairingFailure
tools_if_shown.description: Records `failure_code` on a claimed CLI pairing whose local secret scan could not finish and signals the waiting browser; it imports nothing and returns `status` failed. Only the OAuth grant that claimed `pairing_id` may call; anything else returns 400 `invalid_cli_pairing`.

tools_if_shown.name: createOnboardingImportHandoff
tools_if_shown.description: Creates a short-lived browser handoff listing the secret names and coarse sources a local scan found, for a person to approve. Returns the opaque `handoff` token for `getOnboardingImportDecision` and `completeOnboardingImport`. Secret values and local paths are not accepted.

tools_if_shown.name: listPrReviews
tools_if_shown.description: Lists the latest automated review of each pull request among the workspace's 50 newest review runs, newest first, with `pr_review_id`, `repo`, `pr_number`, `status`, `comment_url`, `head_sha` and `created_at`, to find past reviews; `triggerPrReview` cannot start new ones.

tools_if_shown.name: triggerPrReview
tools_if_shown.description: Would request an automated GitHub pull request review, a feature now off: well-formed requests return 409 `pr_review_disabled` and create nothing. Wrong field types return 400 `invalid_request`; GitLab URLs 410 `gitlab_retired`. A Session from `createSession` can review a pull request.

tools_if_shown.name: listProviderCatalog
tools_if_shown.description: Lists the inference providers the workspace can newly connect: `provider_id`, `label`, `auth_kinds`, API-key `config_fields`, and `oauth_login` (`available`, `methods`, `default_method`, or the `reason` it is not). It picks the provider and method for `startProviderOAuthLogin`. No credentials.

tools_if_shown.name: listPendingProviderOAuthLogins
tools_if_shown.description: Lists the caller's own pending, unexpired provider sign-ins as metadata only: `login_id`, `provider_id`, `method`, `status` and `expires_at`, to recover a lost login id for `getProviderOAuthLogin` to read. Owner or admin through OAuth only; API keys are refused.

tools_if_shown.name: getProviderOAuthLogin
tools_if_shown.description: Returns `login`, a sign-in the caller started, with `status`, `prompt`, `events`, `expires_at` and `next_action` (open a URL, enter a code, answer the prompt, or wait); poll it while pending. A finished one stays readable while retained; 404 means unknown or purged. Owner or admin via OAuth.

tools_if_shown.name: cancelProviderOAuthLogin
tools_if_shown.description: Cancels a pending provider sign-in started by the caller. A sign-in that already succeeded, failed or was cancelled is left as it is and the call still succeeds; 404 means it is unknown or was purged. An account that is already connected stays connected.

tools_if_shown.name: respondToProviderOAuthLogin
tools_if_shown.description: Submits the answer to a pending sign-in's current prompt (`prompt_id`) and returns `ok` true once accepted; the answer is never returned. Read the sign-in with `getProviderOAuthLogin` for its next step. A sign-in that is not pending, or a stale prompt, returns 409.

tools_if_shown.name: checkProviderAccount
tools_if_shown.description: Checks a saved provider account via provider metadata, without inference: `connected` (false if not saved), `authentication` and `capacity` (each `status`, `scope`, `reason`), `inference` (`not_tested`), `observed_at`. It tells whether the credential is accepted, not whether a model runs. Admin.

tools_if_shown.name: getProviderAccountUsage
tools_if_shown.description: Returns provider-reported usage for one saved provider account, without running inference: `status` available with `windows` (`label`, `remaining_percent`, `resets_at`) and `observed_at`, or `status` unavailable with a `reason`. Secret values are not returned.

tools_if_shown.name: startRecoverableProviderOAuthLogin
tools_if_shown.description: Starts a provider sign-in keyed by a caller-chosen `idempotency_key`; a retry with the same key and intent returns the same `login` (`login_id`, `status`, `next_action`) instead of a new one, for clients that may lose the response. Changed intent: 409; purged: 410. Owner or admin via OAuth.

tools_if_shown.name: startProviderOAuthLogin
tools_if_shown.description: Starts a provider's interactive sign-in and returns `login`: its `login_id`, `status`, `expires_at` and `next_action` (open a URL, enter a device code, answer a `prompt`, or wait). It cancels the caller's previous sign-in for the provider. Owner or admin over OAuth only; API keys are refused.

tools_if_shown.name: getQueueStatus
tools_if_shown.description: Returns the workspace's session concurrency: `workspace` and `per_repo` running and queued counts, plus `running_runs` and `queued_runs` (`run_id`, `repo`, `run_kind`; queued ones with `position`). It shows why a new session has not started; `repo` is empty for work with no repository.

tools_if_shown.name: listReasons
tools_if_shown.description: Lists the caller's Reasons (main first, then named) and other members' workspace-visible Reasons as `items`, each with `id`, `name`, `main`, `mine`, `visibility` and, on the caller's own, its conversation `session_id`. Pass an item's `id` to openReasonConversation or updateReason.

tools_if_shown.name: createReason
tools_if_shown.description: Adds a named Reason owned by the caller, a long-running conversation beside the main one, and returns it with its `id`; no machine starts. Message it once openReasonConversation returns its Session. Refused with 409 `reason_limit_reached` at the limit of live named Reasons; archiveReason frees one.

tools_if_shown.name: updateReason
tools_if_shown.description: Changes the name, avatar or both of one of the caller's own Reasons and returns the updated Reason; fields left out keep their value. A rename also retitles its conversation Session. Another member's Reason returns 404, and the main Reason keeps its name (409 `main_reason_name_fixed`).

tools_if_shown.name: archiveReason
tools_if_shown.description: Archives one of the caller's named Reasons that is no longer needed: it leaves listReasons, and its conversation Session is archived with its history, not deleted. Sessions it started stay where they are. No tool restores it. The main Reason is never archived (409 `main_reason_kept`). Returns ok.

tools_if_shown.name: openReasonConversation
tools_if_shown.description: Returns the `session_id` of one of the caller's Reasons' conversation, creating it the first time; repeating the call returns the same Session. Message the Reason with sendSessionMessage on that id and read its replies with listSessionConversation.

tools_if_shown.name: listRepositories
tools_if_shown.description: Lists every repository the workspace's GitHub App or the caller's personal grant reaches, in one page of `items` with `full_name`, `account_login`, `default_branch` and `private`; `id` appears once enabled. A `full_name` is what `createSession` takes as `repo`. `connected` is always true.

tools_if_shown.name: bulkIndexRepositories
tools_if_shown.description: Enables connected repositories for Reason's repository automation, as `indexRepository` does for one; nothing is indexed. Entries are owner/repo strings or { owner, repo } objects. Returns `results` in order with `repo`, `status` (indexed means enabled, or error) and `error`. Repeating is harmless.

tools_if_shown.name: bulkRemoveRepositories
tools_if_shown.description: Deletes each listed repository's enablement for the workspace, given as owner/repo strings or { owner, repo } objects; its agents, triggers and guardrails stay, the GitHub App keeps access, and `indexRepository` re-enables it. Returns `results` with `repo` and `status` (removed or error) per entry.

tools_if_shown.name: deleteRepository
tools_if_shown.description: Deletes one repository's enablement for the workspace and returns ok true, whether or not it was enabled. Its agents, triggers and guardrails stay, and the GitHub App keeps access, so `listRepositories` still lists it and `indexRepository` re-enables it.

tools_if_shown.name: getRepositoryBranchHead
tools_if_shown.description: Returns `full_name`, `branch`, `default_branch`, `is_default_branch` and the tip commit `sha` of a branch of a repository the workspace's GitHub App reaches; omitting `branch` reads the default branch. Answers are reused for up to 5 seconds; GitHub reads are rate-limited (429 with Retry-After).

tools_if_shown.name: getRepositoryGuardrails
tools_if_shown.description: Returns `repo` and its effective `guardrails` (issue fixing, audits, PR Merge Bot enablement, accepted risk, merge requirements), defaults filled in: the current values before `updateRepositoryGuardrails`. A repository the installation cannot reach, even a personal-grant one, returns 400.

tools_if_shown.name: updateRepositoryGuardrails
tools_if_shown.description: Changes only the guardrails sent for a repository and returns `repo` with its full effective `guardrails` after the change; unknown keys are ignored. Owner or admin only. A wrong type, format or range returns 400 naming the guardrail, but a non-numeric value for a numeric one is ignored.

tools_if_shown.name: indexRepository
tools_if_shown.description: Enables a connected repository for Reason's repository automation (nothing is indexed) and returns `repo`, its enablement record: `id`, `repo_full_name`, `installation_id`, `created_at`. With cloud agents on it also provisions the default agent and trigger, best effort. Repeatable; unreachable: 400.

tools_if_shown.name: getOwnRole
tools_if_shown.description: Returns the caller's `user_id` and two unrelated roles: `membership_role` (owner, admin, member or viewer) decides what the caller may do here, such as owner-or-admin writes; `app_role` (pro or regular) is the account's product tier, not a permission. It tells whether an admin-only call is allowed.

tools_if_shown.name: listSessions
tools_if_shown.description: Lists Sessions newest first, each with `session_id`, `title`, `status`, `outcome` and `result_summary`, to find one before getSession reads it in full. Archived ones are left out unless `status` asks; `origin` and `search` (titles only) filter. `end_cursor` passed as `after` reads the next page.

tools_if_shown.name: createSession
tools_if_shown.description: Starts a new Session in which the agent works on `prompt`, optionally in `repo`; it runs asynchronously and incurs usage. Returns `session_id`, `url` and `status` at once. Poll getSession until `status` leaves running, then read the answer in `result`; listSessionEvents streams live output.

tools_if_shown.name: listSessionsWithInsights
tools_if_shown.description: Lists Sessions with their stored insight (summary, category, outcome and metrics), or a not_generated placeholder, to review many Sessions at once. Generates nothing; generateSessionInsight builds one. Takes the listSessions filters; first defaults to 20; pass end_cursor as after for the next page.

tools_if_shown.name: prestartSession
tools_if_shown.description: Starts a new Session's cloud machine ahead of its create, in enabled workspaces. Returns `status` (starting or ready) and `ttl_ms` until an unused machine is removed, or no body when declined. Advisory: a createSession with the same client_session_id within 75 s uses it; create works either way.

tools_if_shown.name: getSession
tools_if_shown.description: Reads one Session: `status`, `outcome`, the opening `prompt`, the latest answer in `result`, `title`, `usage`, `pr_url`, plus a redacted `error_message` when it failed. Poll it after createSession or sendSessionMessage until status leaves running; `fields` narrows each poll.

tools_if_shown.name: deleteSession
tools_if_shown.description: Permanently deletes a Session and its history, which cannot be undone; archive=true archives it instead, as archiveSession does. Returns ok, plus archived=true for archive. 409 `session_delete_blocked` while compute or usage settles (retry later), or for good when history must be retained.

tools_if_shown.name: archiveSession
tools_if_shown.description: Archives a Session, hiding it from the default listSessions results while preserving it and its history. Requires run scope and Workspace membership. Returns ok set to true, also when the Session was already archived; unarchiveSession restores it.

tools_if_shown.name: listSessionAttachments
tools_if_shown.description: Lists the files a session produced, such as diffs, logs, screenshots and build outputs, each with `id`, `name`, `kind`, `content_type`, `size_bytes`, a download `url` and its `url_expires_at`. `view=all` adds the Session's bookkeeping rows, which have no file and a null `url`.

tools_if_shown.name: getSessionAttachment
tools_if_shown.description: Returns a fresh `download_url` for one file a Session produced, with `expires_at` when the link states one. `attachmentId` is the item id listSessionAttachments returns. Fetch the link with a plain GET and no Authorization header; call again for a new link once it expires.

tools_if_shown.name: cancelSession
tools_if_shown.description: Stops a running Session whose work is no longer wanted: graceful (default) tries a final snapshot, hard stops at once from the last checkpoint and upgrades a graceful cancel. Returns `ok`, `requested`, `mode` and `status`; poll getSession until status leaves running, then it reads suspended.

tools_if_shown.name: compactSession
tools_if_shown.description: Folds a Session's earlier turns into a summary that later turns carry instead of the full context, as the app's /compact does, when a long Session nears its limit. It needs credits. Returns `ok` and `outcome` (requested, queued, started, already_compacted or credit_exhausted), with `detail` for why.

tools_if_shown.name: listSessionConversation
tools_if_shown.description: Returns a session's conversation in order: the opening prompt, each user or assistant message, and one `reply` per finished run of the agent, failed or cancelled runs included, with its `status` and `outcome`. `kind` tells items apart; pass `end_cursor` as `after` for the next page.

tools_if_shown.name: listSessionEvents
tools_if_shown.description: Streams a Session's activity to watch it work: each reply as an `assistant` event, reasoning, tool calls and status. `next_seq` passed as `after_seq` returns only newer events; `wait_ms` holds the call until the next event of a running Session. listSessionConversation has just the exchange.

tools_if_shown.name: forkSession
tools_if_shown.description: Starts a new Session from this one's conversation up to its latest reply, as the app's Fork does, to try another direction while the original stays unchanged; files come along when a checkpoint allows. With `message` it runs that first. Returns `ok` and the new `session_id` to poll with getSession.

tools_if_shown.name: getSessionInsight
tools_if_shown.description: Reads a Session's stored insight, to review it without its transcript: `summary`, `category`, `outcome`, `size`, `message_count`, `pr_url`, `cost_usd` and token counts. Generates nothing: when none is stored, `status` is `not_generated` and `summary` is empty; generateSessionInsight builds one.

tools_if_shown.name: generateSessionInsight
tools_if_shown.description: Returns a Session's insight: `status`, `summary`, `category`, `outcome`, `size`, `message_count` and cost and token metrics. When none is stored, builds one from the Session's record, without a model call, and stores it; a stored insight is returned unchanged.

tools_if_shown.name: listSessionMessages
tools_if_shown.description: Lists only the follow-up messages sent to a Session after it was created, each with a note on how it was delivered. `getSession` holds `prompt` and the latest answer in `result`; listSessionConversation has the whole exchange in order. `end_cursor` passed as `after` reads the next page.

tools_if_shown.name: sendSessionMessage
tools_if_shown.description: Continues a Session: a follow-up steers its running turn or starts the next one, and incurs usage. Needs run scope, plus devices:use on a Device; a move needs a finished turn and leaves files behind. Returns `ok`, `delivery` and `continuation_session_id` to poll: acceptance is not completion.

tools_if_shown.name: withdrawQueuedSessionMessage
tools_if_shown.description: Withdraws a follow-up still waiting in the Session's queue, so the agent never gets it, as the app's queue Remove does. Its id comes from sendSessionMessage with delivery queue. A message that already left the queue is refused with 409 and left as is. Returns `ok` and the withdrawn `run_message_id`.

tools_if_shown.name: steerQueuedSessionMessage
tools_if_shown.description: Hands a follow-up waiting in the Session's queue to the running turn now, as the app's Send now does. Its id comes from sendSessionMessage with delivery queue. Returns `ok`, the `run_message_id` sent and the `queue_depth` still waiting. A message that already left the queue is refused with 409.

tools_if_shown.name: renameSession
tools_if_shown.description: Renames a Session, as the app's Rename does. Null or an empty title clears the rename and restores the generated title. Returns `ok` and the stored `title`.

tools_if_shown.name: retrySession
tools_if_shown.description: Runs a finished, failed or stopped Session's last turn again, as the app's Retry does. 409 not_terminal while a turn runs. Returns `ok` and the new `run_id`; poll getSession.

tools_if_shown.name: rewindSession
tools_if_shown.description: Swaps an earlier message for `content` and reruns the Session from it, as the app's Edit does, incurring usage. Later conversation is set aside but kept; files go back to that point if a checkpoint allows. Name it by `message_id` or `client_message_id`. Returns `ok`, `session_id`, `deduplicated`.

tools_if_shown.name: listSessionSharedLinks
tools_if_shown.description: Lists the links shared with a Session's agent, newest first, to check whether each was opened, expired or revoked: `id`, `reference`, `label`, `origin`, `status`, `expires_at`, `opened_at` and `revoked_at`. The stored URLs are never returned. createSessionSharedLink adds one.

tools_if_shown.name: createSessionSharedLink
tools_if_shown.description: Shares a URL with the Session's agent by reference and returns `id`, `reference`, `label`, `origin`, `status` and `expires_at`. The URL is stored encrypted and never returned. The agent can open the reference once in its cloud browser; mention the reference in a message to ask it to.

tools_if_shown.name: revokeSessionSharedLink
tools_if_shown.description: Revokes a shared link so the Session's agent can no longer open it; revoking an already opened link only records the revocation. Returns the link with `status` revoked and `revoked_at` set, never its stored URL.

tools_if_shown.name: listSessionTags
tools_if_shown.description: Returns `tags`, the session's current tag labels, or an empty array when it has none. Reading does not modify the session.

tools_if_shown.name: appendSessionTags
tools_if_shown.description: Adds tags to a Session as a de-duplicated union with its existing tags. Workspace tag policy applies to the added tags. Returns `ok` and `tags`, the Session's full stored list after the union.

tools_if_shown.name: replaceSessionTags
tools_if_shown.description: Replaces a session's entire tag list; `tags: []` clears it. Workspace tag policy applies to every tag sent. Returns `ok` and `tags`, the normalized list now stored on the Session.

tools_if_shown.name: updateSessionTags
tools_if_shown.description: Replaces a session's entire tag list, identically to `replaceSessionTags`; it is not a partial edit. `tags: []` clears the list. Returns `ok` and `tags`, the normalized list now stored.

tools_if_shown.name: getSessionTrajectory
tools_if_shown.description: Exports a Session's full trajectory as one ATIF v1.7 document for evaluation or audit: `agent`, `steps` (user messages, agent reasoning, tool calls with their results) and `final_metrics` (token and cost totals). Secret values are masked as captured. For progress, listSessionEvents is lighter.

tools_if_shown.name: unarchiveSession
tools_if_shown.description: Restores an archived Session to the default listSessions results with its history intact, undoing archiveSession or deleteSession with archive=true. Repeating the call is safe. Returns ok.

tools_if_shown.name: listSettings
tools_if_shown.description: Returns `settings`, a map from each settings namespace the workspace has stored (such as model_tiers or default_provider) to its value object; unset namespaces are absent and sensitive ones are left out. Namespace names for `getSetting` and `updateSetting` come from here.

tools_if_shown.name: getSetting
tools_if_shown.description: Returns one settings namespace as `namespace` and its `value` object, null when unset; names come from `listSettings`. It shows the current value before `updateSetting`, which replaces the whole value. A sensitive namespace returns 404.

tools_if_shown.name: updateSetting
tools_if_shown.description: Replaces a settings namespace's whole value with the body (no merge) and returns the stored `namespace` and `value`. Writable: model_tiers, model_source_order, default_provider, agent_profile and desktop_browser_logins; `getSetting` reads the current one. Owner or admin; a bad value: 400.

tools_if_shown.name: listSkills
tools_if_shown.description: Lists the skills the caller can see, authored or installed, with the `skill_id` that `getSkill`, `updateSkill` and `deleteSkill` take. Each has `name`, `description`, `instructions`, `is_enabled`, `installation_scope` and `provenance` (what can be edited). Others' personal skills are left out.

tools_if_shown.name: createSkill
tools_if_shown.description: Creates an authored skill from a `name` and `instructions`, enabled unless `is_enabled` is false and shared with the workspace unless `installation_scope` is personal. `description` says when it applies. Returns the skill with its `skill_id`; a name in use returns 409.

tools_if_shown.name: getSkill
tools_if_shown.description: Returns one skill by its id from `listSkills` or `createSkill`: `name`, `description`, full `instructions`, `is_enabled`, `installation_scope` and `provenance`. Read it before `updateSkill`: `provenance` decides which fields can change. An unknown id returns 404.

tools_if_shown.name: updateSkill
tools_if_shown.description: Edits a skill by its id from `listSkills`; only the fields sent change, and it is returned updated. Authored skills take any field. One installed from the public registry accepts only `is_enabled` and `activation_keywords` (409 otherwise); other origins return 404; a taken `name` returns 409.

tools_if_shown.name: deleteSkill
tools_if_shown.description: Permanently deletes an authored skill, or one installed from the public skills registry, by its id from `listSkills`. To keep it but stop agents using it, call `updateSkill` with `is_enabled` false. Integration and built-in skills, and unknown ids, return 404.

tools_if_shown.name: listSshConnections
tools_if_shown.description: Lists the caller's own saved SSH connections under `connections`, each with `id`, `name`, `host`, `port`, `username`, `status`, `error_code` and the enrolled `device_id`; pass an `id` to `getSshConnection` for one. Other members' connections and credential values are never returned.

tools_if_shown.name: getSshConnection
tools_if_shown.description: Returns the caller's saved SSH `connection` and `latest_operation_id`. Compare that ID with the caller's accepted operation before attributing completion. `connected` means setup completed, not current Device liveness; its `device_id` is the Device a Session can target.

tools_if_shown.name: getUsageQuota
tools_if_shown.description: Returns which usage quota the workspace is measured against as `label`, how much of it is used as `used_percent`, when it renews as `resets_at`, and whether it is `exhausted`. The last three are null when unknown. Requires owner or admin.

detail_provenance.offline_parser_correction: Decoded escaped leading dollar literals and omitted Flight undefined properties; original HTML hash/timestamp retained.

tools_if_shown.name: whoami
tools_if_shown.description: Returns the signed-in email and the Tolt organization this MCP session works in (the organization selected in the Tolt dashboard). Result fields: email, organization_id.

tools_if_shown.name: program_overview
tools_if_shown.description: Org-wide totals for a date range. Returns revenue and commissions as per-currency lists (strings, minor units), plus commission_count, customer_count (leads included) and partner_count. Use this (never a list tool) to answer 'how is my program doing'. Filters: program_id, start_date, end_date. Result fields: revenue (each with currency, amount), commissions (each with currency, amount), commission_count, customer_count, partner_count.

tools_if_shown.name: all_time_totals
tools_if_shown.description: All-time (lifetime) totals for the account or one program: partners, clicks, leads, customers, paying customers, transactions, revenue, refunds and commissions. commissions is approved + paid (also split into commissions_approved and commissions_paid); pending commissions are not included, use commission_status_breakdown for those. Use this whenever the user asks for all-time, lifetime, total-ever or since-launch numbers, instead of widening a date window on the other report tools. Built from Tolt's pre-aggregated partner metrics, refreshed every few minutes (clicks_updated_at shows the last click refresh). Money is integer minor units in `currency`; when the account has several program currencies, currency is null and amounts are summed across them, so pass program_id for exact money. Result fields: partners, clicks, leads, customers, paying_customers, transactions, revenue, refunded, commissions, commissions_paid, commissions_approved, clicks_updated_at, currency, currencies.

tools_if_shown.name: top_partners_all_time
tools_if_shown.description: Partners ranked by a lifetime total such as revenue or clicks, with name, email and program; commission totals count approved and paid commissions. Use for 'best partners ever', 'most clicks all time', lifetime leaderboards. Same pre-aggregated source as all_time_totals. Money is per program currency: integer minor units in each row's currency. When the account has programs in more than one currency, ranking by revenue or commissions requires program_id. Result fields: data (each with partner_id, first_name, last_name, email, program_id, currency, clicks, customers, revenue, commissions).

tools_if_shown.name: top_partners
tools_if_shown.description: Partners ranked by revenue, commissions, clicks, customers, or conversion_rate, as per-partner aggregates (not raw rows) incl. name and email. Use for 'who are my best/top partners'. Set min_clicks to drop low-sample partners when ranking by conversion_rate. Covers a date window (defaults to the last 90 days, max 92) so it stays fast on large programs; pass start_date/end_date within that span for a different period. Paged with offset and limit. Filters: program_id, start_date, end_date, sort, order, min_clicks, currency. For a program with more than one currency, pass currency when ranking by revenue or commissions so amounts are not summed across currencies. Result fields: data (each with partner_id, first_name, last_name, email, clicks, customers, revenue, commissions, conversion_rate), has_more.

tools_if_shown.name: top_links
tools_if_shown.description: Referral links ranked by revenue, commissions, clicks, customers, or conversion_rate, aggregated per link. Same shape, paging, and 90-day default window (max 92) as top_partners, including min_clicks. Result fields: data (each with link_id, param, value, clicks, customers, revenue, commissions, conversion_rate), has_more.

tools_if_shown.name: performance_timeseries
tools_if_shown.description: Revenue, commissions, customers, and clicks bucketed by period (granularity) over a date window (defaults to the last 90 days, max 186). Returns data: one point per bucket that has any activity, oldest first, each with period (its first day), revenue and commissions (strings, minor units, 0 when there were none), customers that became active, and clicks. Use for trends and charts. Filters: granularity, program_id, start_date, end_date, currency. For a program or org with more than one currency, pass currency so the revenue and commission trend is not summed across currencies. Result fields: data (each with period, revenue, commissions, customers, clicks).

tools_if_shown.name: customer_stats
tools_if_shown.description: Customer counts by status (trialing, active, canceled, suspended). Returns one object with a count per status; leads are not counted. Filters: program_id, start_date, end_date. Result fields: trialing, active, canceled, suspended.

tools_if_shown.name: commission_status_breakdown
