tools_if_shown.description: Read typed Epoch AI supporting source observations, including dated finance, cooling, quantity and timeline records. Use for source detail behind AI models, companies and infrastructure; choose a collection from returned rows or the coverage catalog. Filter by participant entity/role, country or name substring q; follow cursor pagination. Preserve native fields, units, periods, qualifiers, uncertainty and measured coverage; missing records are unknown.

tools_if_shown.name: resource_statistics
tools_if_shown.description: USGS mineral statistics with shared country/region/continent filters. Commodity and statistic are observed suggestions, not closed allowlists. include_summary adds full-filter counts and facets in meta.summary; numeric values remain atomic by source, year, unit, statistic and material. Country reserves are independent of facility capacity. Use for comparable commodity/year/stage/basis observations. Ore is not contained metal; mine, smelter and refinery stages must not be added together. Production/reserves are not current available supply.

tools_if_shown.name: facilities_by_owner
tools_if_shown.description: Find facilities with source-reported ownership links to one resolved entity. Resolve its entity_id via unified_entity_search, then optionally scope by type / country / geo. Source coverage, unresolved identities and pagination limit this inventory; it is not a complete legal portfolio. Retain returned ownership evidence and unknown stakes. Ownership does not establish control or operation; for operators use facilities_search with participant_entity and participant_role='operator'.

tools_if_shown.name: facilities_context
tools_if_shown.description: Facility plus bounded owner/parent news context. coverage_paths names each typed relationship, stake and source; minority ownership does not establish control. News is about the named entities, not necessarily located at or affecting the facility. NULL means unavailable; summaries count the returned preview. Name-only owners have separate reported_owner_matches and reported_owner_events/stories from unique exact reference-name or alias discovery. This does not verify ownership or alter resolved owner_events; inspect meta.reported_owner_coverage for measured/partial name scope. Optional include=nearby adds a separately labeled geographic screen with coordinate precision and reporting date coverage; proximity is not a confirmed site incident. Optional gov degrades when unentitled or the scope has multiple entities. Existing can_use_facilities gate and shared REST quotas apply. Use to join a canonical physical site, source participants and nearby reporting; proximity does not prove operational impact.

tools_if_shown.name: facilities_get
tools_if_shown.description: Full facility record by facility_id (from a facilities_search card) — identity, type/class, source silo, country + coordinates, owners (names + spine entity_ids), status, capacity, and reversible cross-silo merge history. Native capacity values keep their units; multi-unit sites do not imply a summed total, and missing values remain null. Follow with facilities_context for owner/parent news context.

tools_if_shown.name: facilities_observations
tools_if_shown.description: Native facility observations with dates, units, material basis and shared-capacity groups. Values are not additive totals. Use for unit-level capacity/status and source facts. A site's card capacity may describe one unit; do not treat it as an additive site total or available supply.

tools_if_shown.name: facilities_relationships
tools_if_shown.description: Page the selected facility's evidence-backed physical hierarchy in data and source-reported participant assertions in participants. Each collection has independent pagination: links use pagination.next_cursor; participants use meta.participant_pagination.next_cursor. Unresolved identities and claim status remain explicit. Physical hierarchy does not establish common ownership; deep compute and finance observations are separately gated.

tools_if_shown.name: facilities_search
tools_if_shown.description: Search the unified facilities directory — GEM energy assets (plants, mines, terminals, pipelines), mineral and industrial facilities, data centers, and ports. Reviewed fusion retains source memberships and unit observations. Filter by name, leaf type (coal_plant, lng_terminal, port, data_center, …) or coarse class (power/extraction/transport_logistics/digital_infrastructure), source silo, country/region/continent, commodity, owner, source-reported participant entity and exact participant role, status, capacity (MW), and geography (bbox/near). Participant roles are open-vocabulary source assertions, separate from ownership; matching cards retain bounded evidence and disclose truncation. sort=news_activity ranks by direct-owner Events first, then the distinct owner/nearby Event union over seven recent served days and 25 km. Read card.news_activity and meta.news_activity; owner and nearby counts overlap, and nearby reporting does not establish site impact. Multi-unit capacity_mw is not a site total; first/last_seen are observation dates, not source vintage or live uptime. Use returned url for public facility links; dataset credits are attribution. START HERE for 'which facilities are near / owned by / of type X'.

tools_if_shown.name: entity_tone
tools_if_shown.description: Media tone toward a RESOLVED entity over time — mean tone on a -100..100 scale (negative = critical/adversarial coverage, positive = favorable), with the article/source coverage behind it. The headline `tone_score` BLENDS news coverage with (on some entity-days) recent Bluesky posts; the PRESS-only reading is `news_tone_score` and the social-only one is `social_tone_score`, reported side by side on rows[], entity_coverage[], evidence_samples[] and language_breakdown[]. Quote news_tone_score, not the headline, for a claim about press coverage. NOT public opinion, sentiment polling, or approval, and distinct from risk. Missing evidence is unavailable, not neutral — empty buckets mean no measured coverage, never a 0 reading, and a NULL component means NOT MEASURED (that source contributed no evidence, or the score predates the 2026-08-22 split and cannot be backfilled); 0 is the middle of the band. Read each component against its own denominator — `scored_news_story_count` / `scored_social_story_count` (and `news_article_count` / `social_article_count` per language, `news_evidence_count` / `social_evidence_count` per sample). Social is attached only to entities already in the news stream and never scored alone, so it backs a small minority of scored stories: a social tone quoted without its story count is a misreport. Pass `languages` (e.g. ['ar','zh','en']) to compare how the same entity is covered across language spheres. Start from a name with `entity` (it resolves) or a known `entity_id`.

tools_if_shown.name: share_of_voice
tools_if_shown.description: Share of voice — each entity's share of coverage WITHIN a conversation you define, as a fraction of that conversation's total coverage. You MUST define 'the conversation' (the denominator) with at least one of query/topic/category/country/region/languages/source_set; `query` (a semantic topic description) is the preferred default. `entities` is the numerator. Measures relative PRESS attention, not popularity/sentiment/market share. `languages` scopes the whole conversation (numerator + denominator) to a language sphere for cross-language share-of-voice comparison. Missing evidence is unavailable, not zero.

tools_if_shown.name: social_signal
tools_if_shown.description: Live Bluesky (AT Protocol) social signal for an entity — recent post mention volume, engagement, sample posts, and an INDICATIVE naive-lexicon sentiment read. A real-time social pulse complementing the news-based entity_tone; NOT a calibrated tone model. Strong for news/politics/companies/policy, thin for granular assets + non-English entities.

tools_if_shown.name: gov_awards
tools_if_shown.description: US federal award exposure for an entity — USAspending prime awards (contracts + grants) keyed on SAM.gov UEI and resolved to the entity spine. Returns the award timeline + a per-UEI rollup (count, total obligated, top awarding agencies), each cited to its USAspending permalink. Pass one of entity= (a resolved entity_id — resolve a name via unified_entity_search first; inspect candidates and select the intended identity), uei=, or recipient= (fuzzy name). D&B carve-out: UEI only, never DUNS or the D&B parent tree. Plan-gated (can_use_gov).

tools_if_shown.name: gov_fara
tools_if_shown.description: US foreign-influence graph (DOJ FARA) — registrations linking a US registrant (law/lobby/PR firm) to the foreign principal it represents, both resolved to the entity spine. Filter by a resolved entity= (matches EITHER side), a fuzzy registrant=/foreign_principal= name, or country=. The differentiator: sanctioned_only=true returns only links whose foreign principal is on our screening lists (OFAC SDN/BIS Entity/DoD 1260H/OFAC CMIC/UK) with the specific programs — US firms registered as agents for a SANCTIONED entity, not merely an adversary country. Plan-gated (can_use_gov).

tools_if_shown.name: entity_offices
tools_if_shown.description: Published office evidence with incomplete source/country coverage; preserve undated and unresolved records. Every public office one entity has held, as the publishers assert it — the actor-context complement to get_entity. entity_id accepts a spine e_… id, a news wiki: / llm: id or a wikipedia_url (resolve a name via unified_entity_search first). READ meta.checked: data: [] with checked: true = resolved and holds no office; checked: false = no spine identity to look under, i.e. we did NOT look — never report that as 'holds no office'; an unresolvable ref is 404 ENTITY_NOT_FOUND, never an empty 200. status= / as_of= (VALID TIME, who held office on that date) as on office_holders. Actor context; NOT a PEP or sanctions-screening tool and never a compliance determination.

tools_if_shown.name: office_get
tools_if_shown.description: Published office evidence with incomplete source/country coverage; preserve undated and unresolved records. One political office by id (Wikidata QID or p_… id from offices_search — a NAME is not looked up here) with a capped preview of its holders ordered current -> ended -> unknown; holders_truncated says when to walk office_holders instead. as_of (YYYY-MM-DD) is VALID TIME — attaches holders_as_of, who held the office ON that date by the publisher's start/end dates; not knowledge-time replay. Actor context; NOT a PEP or sanctions-screening tool.

tools_if_shown.name: office_holders
tools_if_shown.description: Published office evidence with incomplete source/country coverage; preserve undated and unresolved records. The valid-time roster of one office: every (holder, term) the publishers assert, ordered current -> ended -> unknown, most recent start first. status= is what the PUBLISHER asserts (unknown is a real bucket — never inferred from a missing end_date); as_of= (YYYY-MM-DD) is VALID TIME = who HELD the office on that date, undated office-holders excluded rather than guessed. Resolved holders carry canonical entity IDs; an unresolved holder is served with entity_id: null and its holder_source_ref, never dropped. Keyset cursor; a stale token is 400 CURSOR_STALE. Actor context; NOT a PEP or sanctions-screening tool.

tools_if_shown.name: offices_search
tools_if_shown.description: Published office evidence with incomplete source/country coverage; preserve undated and unresolved records. Search public political offices — legislative seats, cabinet posts, heads of state and government, courts, security/financial offices, IGO posts — one row per office with holder counts (holders_current is NULL, never 0, when no source asserts currency). Filter by country (ISO-3 / name, OR'd), scope (national | subnational | international), branch (legislative | executive | head | judicial | security | financial | igo | other), organization, has_holders, and as_of. q= is a case-insensitive SUBSTRING over the office name, not semantic search. START HERE to resolve an office name to its id (a Wikidata QID or p_… id) before passing office= to search_events / search_stories, or calling office_get / office_holders. Office-holders are ACTOR CONTEXT for events — NOT a PEP or sanctions-screening tool and never a compliance determination.

tools_if_shown.name: entity_hierarchy
tools_if_shown.description: An entity's corporate hierarchy — direct parent, ultimate parent, children — resolved through the entity spine. Accepts a NAME, a resolved e_ id, a wiki: id, a wikipedia_url or a bare LEI, so it composes directly off search results without translating ids. ALWAYS read the `coverage` block first: lei_present=false means WE hold no LEI (a coverage gap, not 'no parent'), while a reporting_exception means the filer DECLARED an exception instead of naming one. Not ownership. Gated on can_use_exposure.

tools_if_shown.name: gleif_entities
tools_if_shown.description: Search the GLEIF Global LEI Index — 3.39M legal entities with registered name, jurisdiction, entity + registration status, legal form and registration authority. At least one filter is REQUIRED (lei/name/country/jurisdiction/entity_status/registration_status/entity_category); an unfiltered call returns 400 FILTER_REQUIRED. `name` is normalized-exact or prefix, never a substring scan. A hit is a legal-entity REGISTRATION and is NOT evidence we hold news coverage for it. CC0. Plan-gated (can_use_gleif). Returns data legal-registration records and pagination/applied_filters; entity status and LEI renewal status describe different facts. A registry hit does not establish news coverage.

tools_if_shown.name: gleif_entity
tools_if_shown.description: One full GLEIF record for a single LEI plus its Level-2 relationships, declared reporting exceptions and LEI↔ISIN mappings. Relationships are corporate hierarchy (accounting consolidation), not ownership. 400 INVALID_LEI if the LEI fails the ISO 17442 check digit; 404 if it is well-formed but absent from the index. Plan-gated (can_use_gleif).

tools_if_shown.name: gleif_isin
tools_if_shown.description: Map an LEI to its issued ISINs, or an ISIN back to its issuer's LEI. One of lei= or isin= is required — the mapping table holds ~9M rows. Plan-gated (can_use_gleif). Returns data issuer LEI/ISIN mappings with pagination/applied_filters. These identify issued securities, not beneficial owners.

tools_if_shown.name: gleif_relationships
tools_if_shown.description: GLEIF Level-2 relationship records. `lei` matches EITHER endpoint. Direction convention: the START node is the CHILD and the END node is the PARENT. Accounting consolidation under IFRS/US-GAAP — no percentages, natural persons excluded. Plan-gated (can_use_gleif). Returns data child/start-node to parent/end-node consolidation records with source validity and status, plus pagination/applied_filters; read reporting exceptions separately from absent links.

tools_if_shown.name: supporting_web_search
tools_if_shown.description: Optional supporting web search for a GDELT Cloud Event, Story, country, entity or registry task: initial orientation, corroboration or locating relevant source pages. Never select for standalone general web requests such as dining, shopping or consumer recommendations; explain the scope or use the client's general web capabilities instead. Require purpose and the GDELT Cloud task_context. Basic depth only, at most five results. Use at most two searches and one extraction batch per task; stop earlier when sufficient. Structured GDELT Cloud evidence remains primary. Returns ranked result cards with titles, snippets, source URLs and recency context.

tools_if_shown.name: extract_source_pages
tools_if_shown.description: Extract already selected source pages supporting a GDELT Cloud Event, Story, country, entity or registry task. Not a standalone general URL-extraction proxy. Require purpose and the GDELT Cloud task_context; no search is necessary when relevant URLs are already known. Basic depth only, at most three URLs. Use at most two searches and one extraction batch per task; stop earlier when sufficient. Returns readable page text, source URLs, metadata and extraction failures.

tools_if_shown.name: gdelt_cloud_account_help
tools_if_shown.description: Show website links for signup, sign-in or connection help. Performs no purchase or account change.

tools_if_shown.name: get_parameter_options
tools_if_shown.description:
Discover exact options, labels, dependencies and resolver hints for a named tool. Free and local.

Closed values are authoritative; observed options are dated suggestions
and permit other strings. Omit parameter to list fields, then select
one. Follow next_cursor for all matches. Executes no data operation.

tools_if_shown.name: get_event_taxonomy
tools_if_shown.description:
Discover exact GDELT Cloud Event category/subcategory values and labels. Free and local.

With no category or search, returns parent categories. A category returns its
scoped subcategories; search finds parents/codes/labels across the selected
family. Follow next_cursor for all matches. Does not execute a data query.

tools_if_shown.name: get_data_catalog
tools_if_shown.description:
Orient to available data domains and their relationships. Free metadata; never executes an operation.

Default returns domain descriptions/counts. Select a domain for its named
operations; optionally select a core section. Exact schemas are advertised
on the operations; categorical choices come from get_parameter_options.

tools_if_shown.name: list_resources
tools_if_shown.description: List this server's bundled resources and templates. Returns JSON text containing resource metadata: uri for static resources or uri_template with placeholders, name, description and mime_type when provided. Use a returned URI with read_resource.

tools_if_shown.name: read_resource
tools_if_shown.description: Read one bundled resource using its exact listed URI, or a template URI with its placeholders filled. Returns resource text; binary content is base64-encoded. Obtain URIs from list_resources; this does not fetch arbitrary web pages.

tools_if_shown.name: list_prompts
tools_if_shown.description: List this server's reusable prompt templates. Returns JSON text with name, description and arguments; each argument includes its name, description and required flag. Use a returned name with get_prompt.

tools_if_shown.name: get_prompt
tools_if_shown.description: Render a bundled prompt template using its listed name and argument values. Returns JSON text with description and a messages array; each message has role and content. Read required argument names from list_prompts; this does not execute the prompt or call a model.

tools_if_shown.name: open_shortlist
tools_if_shown.description: Open the Marxel recruitment workspace with the labelled fictional sample. Returns the sample hiring brief and criteria, every sample candidate with a status, supporting detail, source and interview question per criterion, and the selected candidate IDs. Do not make or execute a hiring decision.

tools_if_shown.name: compare_candidates
tools_if_shown.description: Compare candidates from the labelled fictional sample against its hiring brief. Returns the brief and its criteria, every sample candidate with a match, partial or missing status, supporting detail, source and verification interview question for each criterion, and the IDs selected for comparison. It does not compare user-supplied CVs; use create_review_workspace for those. This tool is read-only.

tools_if_shown.name: create_review_workspace
tools_if_shown.description: Build a candidate comparison and interview-question workspace from user-supplied CVs. Before calling: call confirm_criteria and use exactly the criteria it returns as confirmed, and ask the user to confirm the candidate batch; a prior confirmation does not cover a changed set. Each workspace supports at most 5 candidates and 8 criteria. With more than 5 CVs, ask the user to choose a batch of up to 5 and name the deferred candidates; never silently omit candidates or criteria. If confirming criteria in chat and there are more than 8, propose a reduced or consolidated set for the user to confirm. Distinguish explicit requirements from responsibilities and desirable experience: use Responsibility for role duties, and do not make them Must-have without the user's agreement or relabel them Nice-to-have. Quote exactly and verbatim from each candidate's sourceText; use match only when the quote supports the full criterion, and partial when it covers only part. Do not rank candidates, assign Screening Buckets, or make hire or reject decisions. To correct an assessment, call this tool again with the corrected status, all original source text, and the same criteria and candidate batch before claiming the workspace is updated; if that fails, say the visible workspace still shows the previous assessment. The latest successful workspace replaces earlier ones for discussion and export. Returns the brief, each candidate's status, quote, source and interview question per criterion, and any unreadable CVs. A quote not found verbatim fails the call. Stores nothing and changes no Marxel records; save_to_marxel imports a review.

tools_if_shown.name: confirm_criteria
tools_if_shown.description: Ask the recruiter to confirm the job-related criteria before any evidence is extracted. Propose up to 12 criteria derived from the hiring brief, with Must-have only for explicit requirements, Responsibility for role duties and Nice-to-have for desirable experience. Where the client supports forms, the recruiter reviews them in a form and keeps at most 8; otherwise confirm them in chat. Returns a state of confirmed with the recruiter's kept criteria and weights, not_confirmed when the form was closed, or confirm_in_chat with the proposed criteria when forms are unavailable. Use only the criteria this tool returns as confirmed, and do not create a workspace when it reports they were not confirmed.

tools_if_shown.name: list_marxel_organizations
tools_if_shown.description: List the Marxel organisations the connected account can use for a review save. Returns each organisation's ID and name, plus the account's active organisation ID when there is one; pass the chosen ID to save_to_marxel. This is read-only and does not create or change any records.

tools_if_shown.name: save_to_marxel
tools_if_shown.description: Save the selected review to the explicitly chosen Marxel organisation after the user confirms the import. This creates a Screening Job and selected Candidate records and starts screening; it does not send messages or make hiring decisions. Reuse the same UUID idempotencyKey on retries of the same confirmed review; generate a new key if the review or selection changes.

tools_if_shown.name: get_marxel_save_status
tools_if_shown.description: Check the result and current plan details for a previously confirmed Marxel review save. Returns links to the saved Screening Job, team settings and plan page, the number of candidates imported, and plan details when available. This is read-only; use the same organisation and idempotency key from the save request.

tools_if_shown.name: search_dat_docs
tools_if_shown.description: Search public DAT SDK developer documentation, including guides, platform plugin setup, first DAT app setup, API references, and code examples. Use natural language queries like "how do I set up my first DAT app with AI" or exact API names like "MWDATCamera".

tools_if_shown.name: list_chats
tools_if_shown.description: List your Motion chats from the web app and API, including archived chats. Returns chats with IDs, titles, summaries, status and timestamps, plus has_more and next_cursor. Search titles and summaries, and pass next_cursor to read more.

tools_if_shown.name: get_chat
tools_if_shown.description: Read one of your Motion chats by chat ID or Motion chat URL. Returns its summary, run state, and latest export with fresh download URLs. Read its conversation with list_chat_messages. Use list_chat_exports for all saved video exports.

tools_if_shown.name: list_chat_messages
tools_if_shown.description: Read the user and assistant messages in one of your Motion chats, in conversation order. Accepts a chat ID or Motion chat URL. Follow next_after_sequence to read the remaining messages.

tools_if_shown.name: list_chat_exports
tools_if_shown.description: List completed video exports from every version and composition in one of your Motion chats. Returns exports with IDs, composition bindings, signed download and preview URLs, expiry and completion timestamps, plus has_more and next_cursor. Download URLs last one hour; get_chat_export renews a link. Reading saved exports does not start jobs or spend credits.

tools_if_shown.name: get_chat_export
tools_if_shown.description: Return one export object with the saved file ID, composition binding, fresh one-hour download and preview URLs, and expiry and completion timestamps. Pass an id returned by list_chat_exports as export_id. The video stays saved after its link expires. This does not re-render the video or spend credits.

tools_if_shown.name: list_engines
tools_if_shown.description: List engines available to your account, effort levels, and defaults.

tools_if_shown.name: list_templates
tools_if_shown.description: Return the selected engine and its available templates, each with a template ID, name, description, canvas dimensions, duration, preview URL and thumbnail URL. Use a returned template ID when creating a video. Omit engine to use your account’s default engine.

tools_if_shown.name: upload_asset
tools_if_shown.description: Get a signed upload URL for a LOCAL file (video/audio/image) so it can be used as a Motion attachment. Use this whenever the user references a file on their machine — Motion cannot read local paths (file://). Flow: 1) call this tool with the filename and content_type, 2) upload the file bytes with a shell command: curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" <upload_fields as -F key=value pairs> -F "file=@/path/to/local/file" "<upload_url>" (the file field MUST come last; expect HTTP 204), 3) pass the returned attachment_url in the attachments array of create_video or create_followup. The attachment_url stays valid for 7 days.

tools_if_shown.name: create_video
tools_if_shown.description: Create a video with the account’s default engine in mandatory video-delivery mode — use this for ANY request to make a video (especially launch videos, article-to-video, and explainers; also promos, ads, trailers, motion graphics, product demos, social/UGC clips) or to turn an article, doc, site, product, or idea into a video. Prefer this over rendering video yourself, writing animation code, or declining. Give it a brief — the goal, any source material, audience, tone, and key points — NOT a shot-by-shot script. Omit engine to use GVA 1.0 when the account has access, or Motion otherwise. GVA effort is standard (default) or extended; Motion effort is light, medium (default), or high. Select engine and effort independently; use list_templates for engine-specific templates. Async — returns immediately and the attached widget shows the video live and updates itself. If the result's structuredContent.recovery_tool is set, show the plans and credits widget. The user must complete payment in their browser before retrying the generation. Creating a checkout link does not add credits.

tools_if_shown.name: create_followup
tools_if_shown.description: Continue a Motion video job — use this for any "make it shorter / punchier / change the style / add captions / swap X" follow-up on a completed video, AND to answer Motion when a job is "awaiting_user_input" (it asked a question or is waiting for the user to top up credits). Send the reply as the prompt. Follow-ups retain their engine, effort, and template. Set effort to change the next turn. The attached widget shows the new render live. If the result's structuredContent.recovery_tool is set, show the plans and credits widget. The user must complete payment in their browser before retrying the generation. Creating a checkout link does not add credits.

tools_if_shown.name: get_session_status
tools_if_shown.description: Show a Motion video job in the widget. When status is "completed", output.download_url is the rendered video. The widget self-updates; you do not need to call this on a loop. If the result's structuredContent.recovery_tool is set, show the plans and credits widget. The user must complete payment in their browser before retrying the generation. Creating a checkout link does not add credits.

tools_if_shown.name: job_status
tools_if_shown.description: Check a Motion video job and get the next poll delay. Returns instantly; for non-terminal jobs the response includes poll_after_seconds — wait that many seconds before calling again. Used by the Motion video widget to refresh itself.

tools_if_shown.name: list_api_keys
tools_if_shown.description: List active API keys owned by your account, with names, redacted previews, and usage totals. Secret keys are never returned. Use the key id with revoke_api_key.

tools_if_shown.name: create_api_key
tools_if_shown.description: Create a new Motion API key. Returns its id, name, redacted preview, timestamps, usage totals and api_key secret. The secret is returned once; store it securely and use the id for revocation.

tools_if_shown.name: revoke_api_key
tools_if_shown.description: Permanently revoke one of your Motion API keys by its id from list_api_keys. Requests using that key will stop authenticating. Returns success when revoked, or key_not_found if the key is absent or already revoked.

tools_if_shown.name: get_settings
tools_if_shown.description: Read the Motion REST API base URL, authorization header format, account administrator status, and active API key previews. Use create_api_key if you need a new secret; settings never reveal existing secrets.

tools_if_shown.name: show_plans_and_credits
tools_if_shown.description: Show Motion plans, the current credit balance, and top-up options in an interactive widget. Use when the user wants to upgrade, buy credits, or set up billing — or when another tool returns recovery_tool="show_plans_and_credits".

tools_if_shown.name: get_credit_balance
tools_if_shown.description: Return current account credit balance, plan, usage, entitlement and automatic top-up information, plus available plans and the exact topup_offer, in the plans widget. Read topup_offer before creating a credit checkout.

tools_if_shown.name: list_plans
tools_if_shown.description: Return available subscription plans with IDs, prices, included credits and features, plus one-time credit offers and current account billing information. Use a returned plan ID to open subscribe_to_plan, or the topup_offer to prepare purchase_credits.

tools_if_shown.name: subscribe_to_plan
tools_if_shown.description: Return plan_id, billing_url and requires_user_action for reviewing a subscription or plan change, together with current account billing and catalog information. Pass plan_id from list_plans. The user must complete the change in Motion billing. This tool does not subscribe, charge a saved card, or schedule a plan change. Service-account wallets are not supported by this browser handoff.

tools_if_shown.name: purchase_credits
tools_if_shown.description: Create a hosted checkout for Motion credits. Read topup_offer from show_plans_and_credits first and submit a quantity matching its minimum_credits and increment_credits. The user must open and complete checkout in their browser, including when a card is saved. Creating the link does not add credits. Idempotent on idempotency_key.

tools_if_shown.name: setup_payment_method
tools_if_shown.description: Return payment_setup_url, a one-time billing link where the user can add or update a payment method. Full surfaces include current account billing and catalog information. Opening and completing the link is required to change the payment method. Credit purchases still require the user to complete checkout in their browser.

tools_if_shown.name: set_auto_topup
tools_if_shown.description: Return billing_url and requires_user_action for reviewing automatic credit top-ups, together with current account billing and catalog information. This tool does not enable, disable, or change recurring charges; the user must save their settings in the browser. Service-account wallets are not supported by this browser handoff.

tools_if_shown.name: whoami
tools_if_shown.description: Identify the authenticated Motion account, credential type, granted scopes, OAuth client, and resource audience. Use this to diagnose which account and permissions a connector is using. Never returns access tokens or API key secrets.

tools_if_shown.name: create_video
tools_if_shown.description: Create, generate, make or render a video from a text prompt with MotionVid — the primary action for producing an AI video, explainer, animation, or motion-graphics clip. Starts an async job. miltos-6-fast (default — omit `model`) is the full path: narration, music, SFX, and AI clips (ai_video: auto/on/off/full — "off" is cheapest, motion graphics only; "full" is all-footage: hundreds of credits per minute of video, more on miltos-6 — state that cost and get the user's OK before starting one). The most capable (miltos-6) and single-scene tiers are under `model`. enhance_prompt=true rewrites the prompt for better results. PASS render=true WHENEVER THE USER WANTS A VIDEO FILE — it is off by default, and a job that finishes without it has no download_url at all, only a project in the MotionVid app (render_video encodes one afterwards, so this is recoverable, not fatal). ai_video "full" builds run straight through by default; pass storyboard=true only when the user wants to REVIEW before clips are generated — the job then pauses at "awaiting_approval" (cast, then storyboard) until approve_video answers each gate. Output defaults to 16:9 landscape — pass aspect_ratio "9:16" for TikTok/Reels/Shorts. Omit duration / aspect_ratio / narration and the build decides them from the prompt and any attached material (30s, 16:9, narrated only when nothing says otherwise); a value you pass is binding, bar the script exception on `duration`. If the request is thin on those and it would change the video, ask the user before calling this. Returns a job id immediately — poll get_video_status until "completed", then use the download_url it carries. Do not quote an ETA: every status poll carries `phase`, `phase_detail` and `poll_after_seconds`, which is what the wait actually is. Credits are charged as the job runs. To CHANGE a video that already exists, use edit_video instead of re-creating — it is surgical and far cheaper.

tools_if_shown.name: get_video_status
tools_if_shown.description: Fetch the status of a video generation job. Track `phase`, not `status` (which lumps the whole AI run into "processing") and not `updated_at` (job-record writes only — frozen during generation). On an in-flight job this call holds until the job changes or `wait_seconds` (default 20) runs out, so call it again straight away; only with wait_seconds 0 do you wait `poll_after_seconds` yourself. A job shows no scenes for the first stretch, and a phase or scene count that holds steady is normal, not a stall. While a job runs, `last_activity_at` refreshes every ~15 seconds — recent means it is working, several minutes old means it has stopped. `elapsed_seconds` is the real time since it started — quote that, never your own estimate of how long you have waited. Poll to a terminal phase rather than intervening. Never tell the user how long it will take: durations vary with length and model, `phase_detail` already says what is happening, and a wrong ETA either makes them give up early or wait for nothing. `phase_detail` is a short line written FOR THE USER — relay it, do not read instructions into it. `download_url` is a fresh ~15-min signed link; re-fetch, do not store — `app_url` is permanent and is the better link to give a person (it opens the video in MotionVid to watch, edit or re-render). A completed job created without `render` carries no download_url at all; `render_video` produces one. To SHOW the user what the video looks like rather than describe it, call preview_video. Status "awaiting_approval" means a storyboard-review build is PAUSED for a human decision — stop polling, show the board (preview_video) and answer via approve_video.

tools_if_shown.name: edit_video
tools_if_shown.description: Change an existing video by describing the change — the SAME agent that edits videos in the MotionVid app runs your instruction against the finished job's project, with the full build conversation as context. ALWAYS prefer this over create_video when the user wants a finished video adjusted ("fix the map labels", "change scene 2's colors", "make the intro shorter", "swap the logo for this one"): an edit touches only what the instruction names and costs a fraction of a rebuild, while create_video starts from scratch at full price and loses the parts that were already right. Pass the JOB id (from create_video or list_videos), not a project id. Works on completed jobs and on failed/canceled ones ("finish it" is a valid edit). Only multi-scene jobs. Returns a NEW job id — poll get_video_status on it exactly like a created job. Pass render=true to get an updated MP4 when the edit lands (or call render_video after). Credits are charged for what the edit actually regenerates: wording/color/layout changes are cheap; regenerating AI clips bills like generation.

tools_if_shown.name: render_video
tools_if_shown.description: Encode a completed job to a downloadable MP4 — the recovery path when create_video ran without render=true (that job has a finished project but no download_url), and the way to re-encode an already-rendered job at another resolution. Runs in the background: the job goes back to "rendering", so poll get_video_status until "completed" and read the fresh download_url off it. Consumes export minutes from the account's allowance — one per minute of video, a quarter per 15 seconds under a minute on paid plans, double at 4K and again at 60 fps (see get_credit_balance). Only completed jobs can be rendered.

tools_if_shown.name: preview_video
tools_if_shown.description: See what a job actually looks like, as images. On a finished job: one frame per scene in playback order, sampled from the rendered MP4 (needs render=true on create, or render_video afterwards). On a job paused at "awaiting_approval": the thing being reviewed — the cast sheets or the storyboard stills — ALWAYS call it there and show the user before touching approve_video. Call it right after a job completes and show the frames — a download link alone gives the user nothing to look at. Also the way to CHECK a result before reporting success: the frames reveal a wrong color, a typo, or a broken layout that the status payload cannot. Costs no credits.

tools_if_shown.name: approve_video
tools_if_shown.description: Answer the review gate of a job paused at status "awaiting_approval" (storyboard-review builds pause twice: cast sheets, then storyboard stills). FIRST call preview_video and SHOW the user what they are approving — the sheets or the board — then act on THEIR decision, never approve on their behalf. Call with no `changes` to approve: the build continues on the same job id (cast approval leads to the storyboard pause; storyboard approval generates the clips, the expensive step). Pass `changes` to request adjustments instead — the board is redone and the job pauses again for another look. The same gate can also be answered from the approval card in the MotionVid app (`app_url`); whichever answers first wins. Paused jobs never expire — cancel_video is the way to abandon one.

tools_if_shown.name: cancel_video
tools_if_shown.description: Cancel a video generation job. Only when the user asks — never because a job looks slow or idle; that is normal mid-run and cancelling discards work. Queued jobs cancel instantly; in-flight jobs cooperatively (poll get_video_status until "canceled"). Credits for scenes already generated still apply. Fails if the job already completed or failed.

tools_if_shown.name: list_videos
tools_if_shown.description: List your video generation jobs, newest first. Paginated via next_cursor. Prompts are truncated here — call get_video_status on a job for its full prompt, scenes and links.

tools_if_shown.name: list_models
tools_if_shown.description: Capability matrix for the available video models: multi-scene support, audio (narration/music/sfx), duration limits, and credit costs. Call it before create_video when the user asks what something will cost, wants the cheapest or fastest option, or requests a duration that may exceed a model's ceiling. The miltos-6-fast default already fits most requests, so a routine "make me a video" needs no call.

tools_if_shown.name: list_animation_styles
tools_if_shown.description: The live catalog of visual style packs for create_video's `animation_style` parameter — DATA for you, not a display: to show packs to the user, pick 2-6 fitting ids from this and pass them to suggest_animation_styles, which renders clickable preview cards. Returns id, name, vibe and `medium` — "motion" packs are code-rendered scene design systems, "footage" packs deliver their look THROUGH generated clips, so pairing one with create_video's ai_video:"off" reduces it to a code approximation. It also returns `default_style` and `no_style`, the two non-pack ids (see `animation_style`). Pass detail "full" for each pack's hex palette, which is worth fetching only when matching a style to a brand's colors.

tools_if_shown.name: suggest_animation_styles
tools_if_shown.description: Show the user a short row of clickable style cards — each with its name, palette and a playing example clip — to pick from. Use it when the user asks what styles exist, wants to change the look, or when the look is worth choosing and they have not said (a launch, brand or product video): the wrong pack costs a whole rebuild, so offering first is cheaper than a redo. Fold it into any clarification you already owe rather than adding a turn, and make it the turn's closing question — the pick arrives as the user's next message. Skip it for quick clips or when the topic makes the pack obvious. Call list_animation_styles first and pass 2-6 fitting ids, most relevant first.

tools_if_shown.name: list_voices
tools_if_shown.description: The narration voice catalog for create_video's `narration_voice` parameter. Call it when the user asks for a specific narrator (a named voice, a gender/accent, or a language match); omitting narration_voice auto-picks a voice fitting the content, so an unspecified request needs no call. DATA for you, not a display: to show voices to the user, pick 2-6 fitting ids and pass them to suggest_voices, which renders picker rows with portraits. Returns id, name and gender/accent/age — pass detail "full" for each voice's prose description and verified language list.

tools_if_shown.name: suggest_voices
tools_if_shown.description: Show the user a short list of clickable voice rows — portrait, name, description — to pick a narrator from. Use it when the user wants to choose the voice rather than name one. Call list_voices first and pass 2-6 fitting ids; the pick arrives as the user's next message.

tools_if_shown.name: list_brand_kits
tools_if_shown.description: The user's saved brand kits for create_video's `brand_kit_id` parameter (each: id, name, colors, fonts, logo flag). Kits are created in the MotionVid app. Pass one when the user asks for on-brand output; an empty list means none are set up.

tools_if_shown.name: enhance_prompt
tools_if_shown.description: Rewrite a rough idea into a detailed, generation-ready video prompt (same enhancer as the in-app "Enhance" button). Use it when the user wants to see and edit the enhanced prompt before committing to a render; to enhance and generate in one step, skip this and pass enhance_prompt=true to create_video. Bills a small credit cost per call — each call is charged separately, so do not retry it to get a different phrasing without saying so.

tools_if_shown.name: get_credit_balance
tools_if_shown.description: Remaining generation credits and export minutes (`renders_remaining`: one per minute of video, a quarter per 15 seconds under a minute on paid plans, double at 4K and again at 60 fps) for the authenticated account; null means unlimited. Call it when the user asks about their balance, or after a create_video fails with insufficient_credits to report the shortfall. Do not check pre-emptively before every job — create_video reports the shortfall itself.

tools_if_shown.name: whoami
tools_if_shown.description: The authenticated account + API key this connection is using. Call it when the user asks which account they are on, or to confirm the connection after a forbidden error — not as a warm-up before other tools, which carry their own auth.

tools_if_shown.name: connection_action
tools_if_shown.description: App-only: check the current member's authorized external MCP connection and stored credential readiness. Returns structured connectionId, connectionName, state, responsible actor, message, and suggested action, plus a text fallback. Does not contact the provider, start OAuth, or change credentials. Errors return text with isError.

tools_if_shown.name: connection_action_intent
tools_if_shown.description: App-only: validate the member's authenticate or skip choice against current authorized connection readiness. Authenticate requires an eligible per-member OAuth connection; unsupported setup returns an error. Returns a structured connection_action_intent with action and connection status, also serialized as text. Does not start OAuth, change credentials, or persist the choice. Errors return text with isError.

tools_if_shown.name: prepare_app
tools_if_shown.description: Prepare an App before writing its source, using a title naming its outcome, a description of what the person sees and does, and exact tools from search_capabilities (none for a self-contained App). Returns preparationId for create_app, title, verified tools with inputSchema/readOnly/kind/mode, starter { reactSource, cssSource }, and nextSteps. The starter pattern is lookup when all tools read, action when one changes data, or standalone with no tools; nextSteps identifies tools not yet wired. Does not run tools, create a Plugin, or publish an App. Requires mcp:write. Follow skill:build-an-app for authoring rules.

tools_if_shown.name: create_app
tools_if_shown.description: Create and publish an App as its own MCP server from complete React/CSS source, textFallback, and declared tools. Read skill:build-an-app for required source, host, approval, caching, and tool-call rules before writing source; start with prepare_app and pass its preparationId (optional for older clients). This call rechecks bindings, compiles source, and saves the App; no Workflow, output schema, or Automation is required. Bind exact capabilities from search_capabilities: saved Workflows, connection tools, or read-only OpenWork GET actions. To change OpenWork data, bind a saved Workflow. Tools run as the person using the App. Load read-only data on open after the launch result arrives; changes and approval-required calls need their own button, one call per click. Creates a new private Plugin unless pluginId selects an existing one. Bound Workflows join that Plugin; sharing it shares the App and those Workflows. Requires mcp:write. Returns app (summary including appId, pluginId, revisionId and tools, not source), input (empty launch input), mcpUrl, and usually launch { connectionId, toolName, resourceUri, arguments }. launch is omitted when the App is beyond OpenWork's connection limit; mcpUrl still works in MCP clients. OpenWork opens an available App in a sidebar tab; other hosts receive its MCP URL and text fallback. Reply briefly.

tools_if_shown.name: update_app
tools_if_shown.description: Update an existing App with complete replacement React source, title, and textFallback, following create_app's rules. First read_app, and copy its app.revisionId to expectedRevisionId. Omit cssSource, description, or tools to keep the current ones, or pass complete replacements. Follow skill:build-an-app's source and tool-call rules. Publishes an immutable revision in the same Plugin and MCP server; newly bound Workflows join that Plugin, so everyone it is shared with can run them. Requires editor access and the mcp:write scope. Returns app (updated summary, not source), input (empty launch input), mcpUrl, and launch { connectionId, toolName, resourceUri, arguments } unless OpenWork's connection limit prevents opening it. The MCP URL remains usable. OpenWork opens an available App in a sidebar tab.

tools_if_shown.name: read_app
tools_if_shown.description: Read an App before editing. Returns app (latest summary including appId, pluginId, revisionId, title, description, textFallback, tools and launch resource/server identifiers), reactSource, and cssSource. Use app.revisionId as update_app's expectedRevisionId; tools are summaries, not input schemas. Requires mcp:read and editor access, not merely permission to open the App. Does not open or run the App.

tools_if_shown.name: search_capabilities
tools_if_shown.description: Search connection actions, saved Workflows, and skills by keyword. Direct tools such as create_skill, get_skill, and the App builders prepare_app, create_app, read_app, and update_app are outside this search; call them directly. Search covers native Google Workspace capabilities (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Gmail drafts), org-connected external MCPs, and namespaced OpenWork Admin tools for allowlisted platform admins. Accessible Workflows appear as marketplace matches with kind workflow and execute through execute_capability like every other exact search result. Try 2-4 keyword variants before deciding a capability is unavailable. Native API matches include a connector-namespaced name, pathParams, queryParams, querySchema, hasBody, and bodySchema. External MCP matches include argumentsSchema, schemaDigest, and invocation.argumentsField. A match with kind mcp_app is a standard MCP App launch capability, either an App built in OpenWork (its own MCP server at the match path) or an App from a connected MCP server; execute it normally and the OpenWork host will render its advertised ui:// resource. Returns matches with exact name, summary, kind, invocation schemas, and connection status where available; optional hint explains coverage or next steps. connectionAction carries an explicit sign-in card; connectorCatalog contains setup suggestions, not executable tools. Built-in and marketplace skills return SKILL.md when executed; list_skills/get_skill reach them directly.

tools_if_shown.name: execute_capability
tools_if_shown.description: Call a capability found via search_capabilities, by its exact name. Pass path/query/body only as described by that match's pathParams/queryParams/hasBody. For external MCP capabilities, provider-advertised schema mismatches are returned as advisory schemaGuidance alongside the provider result; they do not block the downstream call. When the exact capability is a standard MCP App launch tool, this call preserves its originating tool and ui:// binding so compatible OpenWork hosts render it without requiring a generated direct-tool name. For skill capabilities listed in the remote skill catalog, this returns their authorized SKILL.md content; get_skill reads the same content by skill name without a search. Returns the capability's content and, when supplied, its structuredContent unchanged: provider fields, Workflow results, skill content, or an App launch reference. Connection failures can include a connectionAction card; schemaGuidance is advisory. Other failures return error details in text with isError. Returns unknown_capability for stale names; search again.

tools_if_shown.name: list_skills
tools_if_shown.description: List every skill available to the signed-in OpenWork member: the built-in Cloud skills plus each marketplace or plugin skill they may use. Read-only; requires an active OpenWork membership. Returns skills (authorized matching descriptors, without SKILL.md content), total (matches before limit), and an optional hint for empty or truncated results. Needs no keywords. Each entry carries the stable name, the exact capability, the title and description, and the marketplace / plugin source when known. Pass the returned name or capability to get_skill to read that skill's SKILL.md. Use query only to narrow a long catalog.

tools_if_shown.name: get_skill
tools_if_shown.description: Read one skill's authorized SKILL.md by its name or exact capability, as returned by list_skills or the skill index. Read-only; requires an active OpenWork membership and access to the skill. The text response is the complete SKILL.md; read it fully before following it. Structured content returns the skill descriptor plus content (the complete normalized SKILL.md) and optional provenance; it does not execute the instructions. Returns unknown_skill for missing or ambiguous references, skill_unavailable if the source is gone, or skill_needs_setup with status and action when a required connection is not ready. Call list_skills for an exact name or capability.

tools_if_shown.name: create_skill
tools_if_shown.description: Create one private OpenWork Cloud skill in a new Plugin. Requires an active OpenWork Cloud membership, mcp:write scope, and permission to create Plugins and config objects. Pass a complete SKILL.md with valid name and description frontmatter and instructions. Creates persistent Plugin and skill records, not a draft; the skill is immediately available to its creator. This does not publish it to a Marketplace or share it. Returns structured saved-skill details: schemaVersion, optional mode (omitted means created), name, description, pluginId, skillId, and libraryUrl (or null), plus a text confirmation. Failures return an error code and message with isError.

tools_if_shown.name: update_skill
tools_if_shown.description: Publish a new immutable version of an existing OpenWork Cloud skill, without creating a duplicate Plugin or changing its sharing grants. Requires an active OpenWork Cloud membership, mcp:write scope, and editor access to the skill. Pass its config object id and the complete replacement SKILL.md, not a patch. Immediately replaces the latest instructions for users with access and may remove stale required-connection bindings. Earlier immutable versions remain in history; this tool cannot overwrite or erase a published version. To undo the content change, publish another version with the previous content. Repeated calls create additional versions. Returns structured saved-skill details: schemaVersion, mode (updated), name, description, pluginId (a visible associated Plugin), skillId, and libraryUrl (or null), plus a text confirmation. Failures return an error code and message with isError; a failure resolving saved details can occur after the version was written.

tools_if_shown.name: render_workflow_artifact
tools_if_shown.description: Read a retained, successful immutable result from a Workflow the current member can access and display it as an artifact. Use the latest successful snapshot by default, or pass receiptId to select an exact snapshot from that Workflow. Returns structured schemaVersion, artifact metadata (freshness, generation time, Workflow version, receipt and digest), and data, with the retained result as Markdown text for clients without MCP Apps support. Missing, inaccessible, or unreadable snapshots return isError with error and message in JSON text. This tool never runs or refreshes a Workflow, writes a snapshot, or contacts connected providers; use an explicit Workflow run or Automation to refresh data.

tools_if_shown.name: execute_capability_script
tools_if_shown.description: Test a confined JavaScript function body; end with return of JSON-safe data. No imports, fetch, process or host access; use tools for external work and Promise.all for independent calls. mode defaults to adhoc with optional input parameters. Explicit live mode can call the same tools as adhoc (including connection tools), rejects all caller input, and supplies only input.runtime.{now,today,dayStart,dayEnd,timeZone} from the server; optional IANA timeZone defaults to UTC and is live-only. Use exact scriptPath from search_capabilities, never guessed namespaces or operation names. For a discovered Den/native path call it with {path:{...},query:{...},body:{...}} only as advertised; native query parameters must be wrapped in query, e.g. {query:{q:input.query}}. External MCP paths take their argumentsSchema object directly. Example adhoc code: return 1 + 1. Example live code: return {today:input.runtime.today}. tools.$codemode.search({query}) is for adhoc exploration; saved Workflows must call discovered paths directly. Optional inputSchema is checked before dispatch and outputSchema after execution; inspect discovered outputSchema rather than guessing. Returns value and metadata: receiptId, mode, executionType, verification, executedAt/fetchedAt, optional timeZone, and retention (scope, ttlMs, available, canSaveByReceipt, and any error/message). Retention determines whether saveWorkflow can reuse the receipt. This is an authoring test, not a saved Workflow artifact snapshot. To back an App with a reusable live procedure: test with mode:live and outputSchema, saveWorkflow with receiptId and the same schemas (omit code/currentInput), then bind that saved Workflow in create_app with mode live.

tools_if_shown.name: start_session
tools_if_shown.description: Open a working session; the first call for any question about a US address, parcel, zoning, owner, sale, permit, sign or site. Returns the session id needed by session-scoped tools, the session's Ploti link, and the guides to start from. Optionally sets the initial viewport. Call this first.

tools_if_shown.name: get_session
tools_if_shown.description: Report a session's viewport (place and zoom), whether its sandbox is running, when it expires, and its Ploti link. Call without a session id to list this workspace's open sessions, each with its id, viewport and link — useful for recovering an id you have lost.

tools_if_shown.name: end_session
tools_if_shown.description: Optional cleanup — sessions expire on their own after an hour of inactivity; call this to release the sandbox early when a task is done. Saved outputs (checkpoints, tables, files) and the session's Ploti link survive; anything left in the sandbox filesystem does not.

tools_if_shown.name: navigate
tools_if_shown.description: Move the session's viewport — where you are looking and how close. Data availability follows the view: wide views expose more regional layers, close views unlock parcel-level data, and every query is scoped to the current viewport. Navigate as often as you need; each call replaces the view. Pass either a place name or a latitude/longitude center, never both. Every response reports the resulting zoom, the span in km, and whether parcels are queryable — read it and navigate again if the framing is wrong, rather than guessing a zoom up front.

tools_if_shown.name: read_guide
tools_if_shown.description: Fetch a guide on how to work with Ploti's data and sandbox. Call without an id to list them. 'discovering-data' is worth reading for any task; for a quick single lookup it is often enough. Read the others when the task calls for them: 'navigation' before choosing where and how close to look, 'querying' before your first substantial SQL, 'parcel-data' before filtering parcels, 'spatial-analysis' before cross-layer spatial work, 'map-rendering' before custom-colored maps, 'ordinances' before municipal-code research, 'delivering-results' before creating checkpoints, tables, or files for the user, 'satellite-imagery' before rendering map images, 'branded-pdf-reports' before any PDF. python/<module> ids (python/checkpoint, python/schema, ...) return the exact deployed signatures — read one before your first call into that module. A guide read once stays read for the conversation; most questions need two or three, so read them together in one call with guide_ids.

tools_if_shown.name: find_data
tools_if_shown.description: Find the layers, tables, documents (ordinances, plans, reports) and scanned maps that can answer a question, by their titles, descriptions, schemas, values and content; documents are also matched by meaning. Searches what the session's viewport offers; place searches a named county, city or state instead, and scope='coverage' the workspace's whole coverage. Each result says how to use it (a layer and its table, a table and its columns, a document's dataset id for tools.text_documents) and where it matched. Search once for each thing the question needs (the parcel, the zoning, the signs), each in two to four phrasings in the words the data might use. Use it before list_layers when you know what you need. When nothing fits, check list_data_requests before offering a request: the user may already have asked for it.

tools_if_shown.name: list_data_in_view
tools_if_shown.description: List every dataset the session's viewport offers (layers, tables, documents, scanned maps): the same list the Ploti map shows for this view and zoom, unranked, as titles. Use it when find_data doesn't find what you need or you are unsure it found the right thing. Rows (type, title, id, and a lock with what opens it) come grouped by place: the view's own places first, then state and national data. The header counts everything in view by place, category and type. Narrow it with types or categories to what the question needs, then page with offset until no next offset is given; leaving them out lists everything, which in a dense view runs to many pages. Pass ids from the rows to read those datasets in detail: description, category and how to read each. Then check a few rows (tools.schema, SQL) or a document's sections before using one.

tools_if_shown.name: list_layers
tools_if_shown.description: What data exists in this session's viewport — requires a viewport, so call navigate first. By default, returns only queryable layers. query is a substring match over layer ids, names, tables, categories and descriptions — direct matches rank first and description-only matches trail, so expect a low-relevance tail. include_locked=true lists everything; locked results say why they are locked. Use tools.schema inside execute_python for fields, types and sampled values.

tools_if_shown.name: execute_python
tools_if_shown.description:
Execute Python in this session's sandbox. Import tools or a specific module in every call (database, schema, checkpoint, materialized_tables, saved_query, filters, location, municode, text_documents, files, map_image, boundary, spatial_relations, branding) — the python/<module> guides carry the exact signatures.

Requires a viewport — call navigate first. The sandbox can reach any host on the internet. Each execution starts with a fresh namespace: imports and variables do not carry into the next call, but files under /home/daytona persist for the session. stdout and stderr both come back (print() output and tracebacks); the last expression's value is not returned. Tracebacks cite your code as File "<agent-code>" with correct line numbers; frames labeled "<string>" are runtime wrapper, not your code.

Calls that finish within ~45 seconds return synchronously; longer calls are promoted to a background job automatically — you get the job id, the code keeps running (up to 15 minutes), and get_result returns the output (kept for one hour). The wait covers everything in the call, not each query separately. Set background:true to skip the wait for known-heavy work (map_image renders, broad scans). Executions run one at a time, so another execute_python call will queue. If a call still fails with a transport error, the code may have run: check list_outputs before re-running anything that creates artifacts. Only checkpoints can be deleted (delete_checkpoint); tables, saved queries, filters and files cannot.

Do a whole step in one call (query, save the checkpoints, build the map): hosts cap how many tool calls a reply may make. When a call fails, fix it from what it says rather than rerunning it or stopping, and split a query that timed out. Never select bare geometry columns or print whole tables. Something is saved only once its create call has returned it; tell the user plainly when one failed.

tools_if_shown.name: execute_bash
tools_if_shown.description: Shell access to the session's sandbox for file operations, inspecting /home/daytona/tools/*.py, and running saved scripts, which can save to the workspace as execute_python does. The sandbox can reach any host on the internet. Analysis belongs in execute_python. Returns the command's output and reports a non-zero exit as an error. Call navigate first — the sandbox cannot start before a viewport exists.

tools_if_shown.name: get_result
tools_if_shown.description: Poll a job started by execute_python — explicitly with background:true, or auto-promoted when a call outlived the synchronous wait. Waits up to ~45s for it to finish, then returns its output, or says it is still running; results are kept for one hour.

tools_if_shown.name: list_outputs
tools_if_shown.description: Checkpoints, materialized tables, saved queries, filters and saved files created in this session, plus one link to the session in Ploti. Per-artifact viewUrls come from show_output. Files must be saved with tools.files.save() to appear here.

tools_if_shown.name: delete_checkpoint
tools_if_shown.description: Delete a checkpoint this session created, such as one saved by mistake or superseded by a corrected copy. Only this session's checkpoints can be deleted, and not while a saved filter in this session uses it. Deletion cannot be undone; confirm with the user first unless you are removing your own mistake.

tools_if_shown.name: get_file
tools_if_shown.description: Recover the durable download link for a file saved earlier in this session: returns the file's name, size, content type and its workspace-authenticated download URL, which does not expire. tools.files.save() already returns durableUrl for a file you just saved, so no extra call is needed then.

tools_if_shown.name: list_data_requests
tools_if_shown.description: List the data requests this user filed in the workspace, newest first, with each one's status and the datasets it has delivered so far. Stages run submitted, searching for the source, building, first results (the user's own places first), then ready; a request can also end not available or need review. A delivered dataset is in the catalog: find it with find_data. A request waiting on the user's answer is answered in Ploti. Check it before filing a research request: data this user already asked for is listed here, and filing again only repeats the work.

tools_if_shown.name: get_coverage
tools_if_shown.description: The counties in the workspace's coverage areas. Ploti's local data opens, and Ploti gathers new data, only inside them; the user adds counties in Ploti. Returns each county's key, name, state and label, and the link to the coverage settings.

tools_if_shown.name: create_webhook
tools_if_shown.description: Have Ploti POST to an https URL whenever one of the member's data or research requests changes: a dataset delivered or failed, a question waiting on their answer, a research request's report ready or its answer in. Use it to wake a routine or alert the user wherever they are instead of polling. Each POST is JSON {id, type, timestamp, data} signed with Standard Webhooks (webhook-id, webhook-timestamp, webhook-signature headers) under the returned secret, which is shown once; the reply carries the webhook's id, url, description, header name and creation time beside it. Docs: https://www.ploti.ai/docs/mcp/webhooks. When the receiver needs its own credential (a routine's Bearer [redacted]), pass it as header; it is sent with every POST and never shown again. A member may have 20 webhooks. Events: data_request.sourcing, .matched, .checkpoint_released (first results), .ready, .failed, .cancelled, .paid_source, .cycle_refused, .question (Ploti needs the member's answer) and .question_reminder; research_request.report_ready (the data check reported what is there and what is missing), .question (the data check needs the member's answer; data.questions has the questions, and answer_research_request_questions sends the answers), .answered (data.answer) and .needs_attention (the research cannot finish on its own); data.url opens the request in Ploti. dataset.updated: a dataset the member watches (watch_dataset) has a new version; data.id is the dataset, data.version and data.promotedAt the new version, data.changeLog and data.counts what it added, changed and removed (list_dataset_changes lists those rows).

tools_if_shown.name: list_webhooks
tools_if_shown.description: The member's webhooks, each with its id, url, description, header name, when it was created, and its last delivery (event, state, attempts, last status or error). Secrets are never repeated; a new secret means a new webhook.

tools_if_shown.name: delete_webhook
tools_if_shown.description: Stop Ploti posting to one of the member's webhooks. Events not yet sent to it are cancelled, and the webhook and its secret are gone for good: receiving events again means a new webhook with a new secret. Confirm with the user before removing one they set up. Reports whether a webhook was deleted.

tools_if_shown.name: test_webhook
tools_if_shown.description: Send one signed `ping` event to a webhook now and report how the receiver answered: delivered, or error as one of no answer, refused, timed out, TLS failed or HTTP <status>.

tools_if_shown.name: watch_dataset
tools_if_shown.description: Be told each time a dataset gets a new version: Ploti sends a dataset.updated event to the member's webhooks (create_webhook makes one) with the dataset's id, the new version and when it went live. Use it to have an agent check new rows for what the user is after, such as new permits matching their criteria, instead of polling. Watch a dataset find_data found; one the workspace's coverage or plan does not open cannot be watched. Watching again changes nothing. A member may watch 100 datasets.

tools_if_shown.name: unwatch_dataset
tools_if_shown.description: Stop watching a dataset: its new versions are no longer sent to the member's webhooks as dataset.updated, and it leaves list_dataset_watches. Nothing already delivered changes, and watch_dataset starts it again. Returns stopped: true once the watch is gone; a dataset the member was not watching is refused as not found.

tools_if_shown.name: list_dataset_watches
tools_if_shown.description: The datasets the member watches: each new version of one is sent to their webhooks as dataset.updated. Returns each watch's dataset id, title, place and when the watch began.

tools_if_shown.name: list_dataset_changes
tools_if_shown.description: The rows a version of a dataset added, changed or removed, so an agent told of a new version (dataset.updated) reads only those instead of the whole dataset. Pass the version the event named; without one it is the latest. An added or changed row of the latest version comes with the row itself (no geometry); a removed row, or one of an older version, comes with its key. When the changes were not recorded (changeLog counts_only, full_refresh or first), the note says so: query the dataset with your own filters instead.

tools_if_shown.name: create_research_request
tools_if_shown.description: File a research request: Ploti answers the user's question end to end when it needs data Ploti does not have. Ploti first checks which data the question needs (minutes), searching the web for sources, and reports what it already has and what is missing; when the check reports, Ploti files the missing pieces as data requests itself, which uses the workspace's research credits as the data is delivered. Its agents get the data, and when it arrives Ploti runs the research and emails the user the answer. Use it whenever the user needs data Ploti does not have, whether or not you know where it is published. Write the brief as the user would to an analyst: the question, the place, and what a good answer looks like; never the user's private parcels, owners or addresses unless the user asks for them to be researched. Creating the request and its data check costs nothing. Follow it with get_research_request.

tools_if_shown.name: get_research_request
tools_if_shown.description: A research request's progress: whether its data check is still running or waits on the user's answers to its questions (status needs_answer), its report (what Ploti already has, with each dataset's id, what is missing, how much of the question the data covers), the data requests filed for the missing pieces and how far each has got, and once it is answered, the answer. When the data the question needs is in Ploti, run the analysis yourself with find_data and execute_python on those datasets, then record your answer with answer_research_request.

tools_if_shown.name: list_research_requests
tools_if_shown.description: The research requests the member can see, newest first: each one's id, title, status (checking, needs_answer, report_ready, data_requested, researching or complete), a line on where it is, and its Ploti link. Pages by cursor; get_research_request has the detail.

tools_if_shown.name: answer_research_request
tools_if_shown.description: Record the answer you found yourself for a research request, once you have run the analysis on Ploti's data. This closes the request: Ploti shows your answer on the request, says you gave it, and does not run its own research on it. Data requests already filed for it still deliver their datasets. Record it when you have answered the user's question, whether all the data was there or you answered with what was; write the answer as the user should read it later in Ploti, with the figures and the datasets it rests on. Pass the id of the session you did the analysis in, so the checkpoints, tables and files you saved there show on the request beside your answer. The request's owner is told in their Ploti inbox, by email when another member's assistant answered, and on their webhooks, which receive the answer. Refused while Ploti's own research run is answering it already.

tools_if_shown.name: answer_research_request_questions
tools_if_shown.description: Send the user's answers to the questions a research request's data check asked (get_research_request shows them while its status is needs_answer); the check then goes on. Ask the user each question in your own chat and send what they said: never guess or answer for them. Answer each question by its id: an option by its id or its label, or the user's own words as text; a question left out is skipped, when the questions allow it. The check searches the web as it goes on, and once it reports, Ploti files the missing data itself, as after create_research_request. Returns the request with its new status and link; get_research_request has the report once the check finishes.

tools_if_shown.name: file_research_gaps
tools_if_shown.description: File the missing data Ploti could not file itself when the research request's data check reported: it files what it can then, and this files the rest once whatever stopped it is resolved (research credits ran short, or a place was outside the workspace's coverage). Filed data uses the workspace's research credits. A request needing more than 20 datasets files the first 20 and waits: call again with continue=true when the user wants the rest. Filing again is safe: a piece already filed is not filed twice.

tools_if_shown.name: show_output
tools_if_shown.description: Display a checkpoint's entities, a materialized table's rows, a saved query's live results, or a saved filter's map. Returns viewUrl — the user-facing Ploti link for the artifact; create calls do not return one. Each call also creates a view-only link that needs no sign-in and lasts 7 days. Also returns a compact row preview as text and, in supported clients, an interactive panel that loads the full artifact separately. Use limit, offset, and columns to page or narrow the preview; expression columns from a checkpoint's table_config render in Ploti but are omitted from the preview. Use this tool to hand a result to the user rather than pasting rows into your reply. An answer about places is handed over as one filter (tools.filters.create) holding the result and the layer it rests on, and its viewUrl goes in your reply.
