tools_if_shown.name: whoami
tools_if_shown.description: Who this token is: its label, scopes, the revnu account it belongs to, and the rate limits it is held to. Needs no scope. Its scopes say which tools this token can use.

tools_if_shown.name: review_list
tools_if_shown.description: List what is waiting for the customer's approval: drafts, questions, budgets and other cards their revnu growth agent has queued. Each card carries `actions`, the exact verbs the API accepts for it, and `primaryLabel`, what the dashboard's main button would say. One call returns up to 50 open cards (pass `limit` for up to 100; any beyond that are not returned): pending ones and ones the agent is revising together, with `status` on each card saying which. There is no status filter. In hosts that support MCP Apps, the user also sees the cards, with their buttons, in the Revnu app. Read-only.

tools_if_shown.name: review_get
tools_if_shown.description: One review card by id, including its full payload (draft text, options, research). Read-only.

tools_if_shown.name: agent_status
tools_if_shown.description: Check whether Revnu is working when the customer asks about progress or agent liveness. Returns `status` with the sandbox lifecycle state, last activity and finished-turn timestamps, whether a turn is running, and the number and next time of scheduled wakes. Read-only; does not start or interrupt work.

tools_if_shown.name: results_get
tools_if_shown.description: The customer's growth scoreboard for a window ending now: per-channel sections that are either `{available: true, data}` or `{available: false, reason}`. Zero and unknown are different. `since` is epoch milliseconds, clamped to the last 31 days; default 24 hours. In hosts that support MCP Apps, the user also sees this result in the Revnu app.

tools_if_shown.name: workflows_list
tools_if_shown.description: The customer's recurring workflows with their schedule, next run and steps. Read-only. In hosts that support MCP Apps, the user also sees this result in the Revnu app.

tools_if_shown.name: workflow_runs
tools_if_shown.description: Run history for one workflow, newest first, with per-step outcomes. Read-only.

tools_if_shown.name: leads_list
tools_if_shown.description: The customer's leads, newest first, with status and outreach counts but never draft bodies. `workflowRunId` (a run id from workflow_runs) lists only the leads that run found, each with `runContactIds`. Pass back `nextCursor` for the next page. Read-only. In hosts that support MCP Apps, the user also sees this result in the Revnu app.

tools_if_shown.name: lead_get
tools_if_shown.description: One lead with its contacts (capped at 50; `contactsTruncated` says when). Read-only. In hosts that support MCP Apps, the user also sees this result in the Revnu app.

tools_if_shown.name: linkedin_person
tools_if_shown.description: One person's LinkedIn relationship with each of the customer's connected LinkedIn accounts (or the one named in `account`): whether they're connected, any pending invite and when it was sent, Revnu's own invite record with when it saw acceptance, and the newest 50 messages with who sent each. `profile` is a linkedin.com/in/ URL or id. Read live from LinkedIn: each account is one paced profile lookup, so look people up as you need them rather than in bulk. Read-only.

tools_if_shown.name: blocklist_list
tools_if_shown.description: The customer's block list, newest first: the domains and addresses their agent will never research or contact. Pass back `nextCursor` for the next page. Read-only.

tools_if_shown.name: list_projects
tools_if_shown.description: List the workspace's projects, newest first. Each project holds one app's screens, theme, and design chat. Check here before create_project to avoid duplicates.

tools_if_shown.name: create_project
tools_if_shown.description: Create an empty project. Returns it in data, plus projectUrl. Pass data.id as projectId to design, then call screenshot. Creating a project is instant and uses no credits. Only design runs do. Share projectUrl so your user can watch and edit the designs.

tools_if_shown.name: get_project
tools_if_shown.description: Fetch a project and its projectUrl. Use it to confirm the project exists and share the URL with your user. Use list_components to see its screens.

tools_if_shown.name: delete_project
tools_if_shown.description: Permanently delete a project and all its screens. Designs cannot be recovered. Call only after your user confirms the exact project by name. Never delete projects to tidy up on your own initiative.

tools_if_shown.name: list_components
tools_if_shown.description: List a project's screen names and active version numbers without generated HTML. Pass each item's screenId to design. Pass its id as componentId to get_component or in componentIds to screenshot. Use get_component only when you need a screen's code.

tools_if_shown.name: get_component
tools_if_shown.description: Fetch a screen's generated HTML. Returns the screen in data, with the HTML at data.versions[].code. versions holds only the version the screen currently shows. Use allVersions for the full history, which can be large. The returned screenId is the value design takes. Use this for a build handoff, not to check whether a design run worked.

tools_if_shown.name: list_references
tools_if_shown.description: List curated app styles and their preview images. When your user asks for a look such as Airbnb, brutalist, or dark fintech, pass the closest reference's id as referenceId to design. Without a reference, the agent picks a style.

tools_if_shown.name: design
tools_if_shown.description: Run Sleek's design agent to create or edit screens from a plain-language brief. Send the whole request as ONE message, such as 'a food delivery app with onboarding, restaurants, dish detail, cart, tracking, and profile'. The agent plans the screens together, so separate calls produce mismatched screens. A run uses workspace credits only when it completes or saves changes. By default this waits for the run to finish. If it returns 'queued' or 'running', poll get_design_run. Only one run can be active per project. On CONFLICT, poll get_design_run until the run settles, then retry. cancel_design_run stops it sooner. If a failed run has data.error.url, send your user there. They have to act before you retry. On completion, share projectUrl with your user and call screenshot.

tools_if_shown.name: get_design_run
tools_if_shown.description: Poll a run that design returned as 'queued' or 'running'. Wait a few seconds between polls. On 'completed', data.result.operations lists the saved screens and theme changes. Share projectUrl and call screenshot. On 'failed', read data.error.message and send your user to data.error.url if present. A failed run, including a cancelled one, keeps what it saved in that same list and uses credits only when the list is not empty. Check it before resending the brief.

tools_if_shown.name: cancel_design_run
tools_if_shown.description: Ask a design run to stop, for example when the brief was wrong. Returns the run as it stands right after the request. A queued run comes back 'failed' with error code 'cancelled' and never starts. A running run comes back still 'running' and stops at its next step. A run cut short settles as 'failed' with error code 'cancelled', or 'execution_failed' if saving its changes failed. It keeps any screens and theme changes it saved, listed in data.result.operations, and uses credits only when that list is not empty. A run that finishes before it stops settles as 'completed'. A run that had already settled comes back unchanged. The project stays locked until the run settles, so poll get_design_run before starting another run. A run that stopped responding settles as 'failed' with error code 'execution_timeout' 15 minutes after creation.

tools_if_shown.name: screenshot
tools_if_shown.description: Render up to four project screens side by side as one inline image, after a design run completes. Returns the image, PNG unless format asks for WebP, and a one-line text note. Rendering uses no credits. Send projectUrl with the image so your user can open and edit the designs.

published_tools.source: published FAQ (same names as visible imported tool chips)

tools_if_shown.name: list_streams
tools_if_shown.description: Find streams and their ids — the starting point for every other stream tool. Each row carries the name, current state, scheduled start and whether that schedule repeats, which is enough to tell a one-off from a daily loop without a second call. Filter by name, run state and creation window. Returns a page of rows plus nextCursor and total. Use get_stream for one stream's full configuration.

tools_if_shown.name: get_stream
tools_if_shown.description: One stream's full configuration: current state, output quality and framerate, the destinations it publishes to (each enabled or not, with its delivery state), and its scheduled window including recurrence and repeat weekdays. Use it before changing a stream. For whether it could start right now, call check_stream_readiness instead (this tool reports what is configured, not what is missing); for live viewer numbers, get_stream_live_stats.

tools_if_shown.name: start_stream
tools_if_shown.description: Start streaming now, looping the stream's playlist (or playing its scene) until it is stopped. THIS PUTS VIDEO IN FRONT OF THE PUBLIC, so confirm with the user first unless they just asked for it. Requires a destination plus either a playable video playlist (at least one item) or an attached published scene (set_stream_scene) — check_stream_readiness reports what is missing without changing anything, and is worth calling first. A failed pre-flight is NOT an error: the call succeeds and the answer's `state` is `invalid` — read `state` first: invalid means refused, with `issues` saying why (fix them and start again); `preparing` means accepted. Media facts (duration, sound) arrive about 15-25 s after an upload completes, so a playlist of just-finished uploads can be refused until then. Other refusals (a state that cannot start, a guard failing at the moment of starting) are errors. Credits are NOT part of the pre-flight: the balance is verified when the stream actually activates, so an otherwise-ready stream can still fail to start on an empty wallet — get_billing_overview is what tells you that. A playlist loop takes the playlist as it currently is, with nothing to publish first; a scene plays its published version (publish_scene). Asynchronous: the stream reports a starting state immediately and is live within about a minute. To start at a future time (or every day) use schedule_stream instead. Returns state, started (false when refused), issues (when refused) and startStream (the stream: id, name, state).

tools_if_shown.name: stop_stream
tools_if_shown.description: Stop a stream that is live or starting. It stops publishing and becomes inactive; nothing is deleted and it can be started again with the same configuration. Does NOT cancel a recurring schedule — a daily or weekly stream stopped here starts again at its next window, so call cancel_stream_schedule as well to keep it off.

tools_if_shown.name: delete_stream
tools_if_shown.description: Permanently delete a stream, its playlists and its schedule. Irreversible, and it cannot be undone by re-creating the stream: uploads survive but the arrangement does not. Stop the stream first if it is live. To keep a stream but take it off the air, use stop_stream (plus cancel_stream_schedule). Requires confirm=true and the streamloop:destructive scope.

tools_if_shown.name: create_stream
tools_if_shown.description: Use this to set up a new loop or a stream for a scene. The stream is created empty and CANNOT start until it has (1) a destination — add_stream_destination with one from list_destinations, or get_connection_hints for how to make one — plus (2) either a playable video playlist (at least one item) or an attached published scene (set_stream_scene). Creating a stream also creates its two empty playlists (one video, one audio): for a loop, find them with list_playlists(streamId) and fill them with apply_playlist_operations — a playlist loop needs nothing published before the first start. Media facts (duration, sound) of an upload arrive about 15-25 s after it completes: a start right after uploading can be refused (state invalid) until then. When it runs is schedule_stream's job. Returns the new stream under createStream: id (stream_...), name, state, quality, framerate, createdAt.

tools_if_shown.name: update_stream
tools_if_shown.description: Change a stream's settings (name, quality, framerate, duration, storage, backup ingest) and/or its YouTube broadcast settings via the `youtube` object. Where it publishes is add_stream_destination / set_stream_destination_enabled / remove_stream_destination; when it runs is schedule_stream. The `youtube` settings only apply when one of the stream's destinations is a YouTube channel connected through Streamloop — not a custom RTMP destination, and not YouTube reached through a raw RTMP URL and key — and are otherwise skipped with a notice. Set retryMirror=true to re-attempt mirroring the schedule onto YouTube after a reconnect or a quota recovery. PARTIAL SUCCESS: settings are applied first, so if the YouTube settings then fail, `stream` still reflects the applied settings and `youtubeSettingsError` explains the YouTube failure — the settings change is NOT rolled back.

tools_if_shown.name: schedule_stream
tools_if_shown.description: Set the window a stream runs in, once or on a repeat, and arm it. The stream must already be startable — a destination plus either a playable video playlist or an attached published scene (check_stream_readiness) — otherwise the window arrives and the start fails. repeat=daily re-arms the window exactly 24h later; repeat=weekly re-arms +7 days, or on the weekdays given in `days`. Both repeats REQUIRE scheduleEndAt and a window shorter than 24h; a one-off (repeat=none, the default) may be open-ended. `days` are UTC weekdays of the start instant, so a 9pm Monday Eastern window repeats on TUESDAY — the result echoes the committed window in UTC with its UTC weekday so this is visible. Replaces any existing window; cancel_stream_schedule disarms it. Returns the stream (id, name, state, scheduleStartAt, scheduleEndAt, scheduleRepeat, scheduleRepeatDays) and committedWindow: the window in UTC, its UTC start weekday, and the times exactly as you sent them.

tools_if_shown.name: cancel_stream_schedule
tools_if_shown.description: Disarm a scheduled stream and return it to an unscheduled, inactive state, clearing any daily or weekly repeat. Use this to stop a recurring stream coming back; it has no effect on a stream that is currently live (stop_stream does that).

tools_if_shown.name: check_stream_readiness
tools_if_shown.description: Answer 'would start_stream work right now?' without changing anything. Runs the same pre-flight configuration checks a start does and returns ready plus every blocking issue — typically a missing or archived destination, an empty video playlist, media too big for the stream's storage, or, for a stream playing a scene, a scene that is missing, not published or invalid. It does NOT check whether uploads have finished processing: a playlist takes only completed uploads, but their media facts (duration, sound) arrive about 15-25 s after an upload completes, so wait that long after uploading before starting. Credits and YouTube live eligibility are deliberately NOT part of it (both are re-checked at the moment the stream activates), so ready=true means correctly configured, not guaranteed to go live — pair it with get_billing_overview when a ready stream still will not start. Call it before start_stream and before relying on a schedule_stream window. Returns streamReadiness: ready, and issues[] each with code, error, suggestion, path and stage.

tools_if_shown.name: get_stream_live_stats
tools_if_shown.description: How a live stream is doing ON YOUTUBE: watch URL, broadcast status, concurrent viewers, views and likes. Only meaningful while the stream is live to a YouTube channel connected through Streamloop — a custom RTMP destination reports nothing here, since those numbers live with that platform. Returns the stream as node: id, name and youtubeLiveStats (watchUrl, lifecycle, concurrentViewers, totalViews, likeCount, fetchedAt, and mirrorStatus / mirrorLastError for the YouTube broadcast sync); youtubeLiveStats is null when there is no connected YouTube broadcast. For whether Streamloop itself considers the stream healthy, read state from get_stream.

tools_if_shown.name: list_stream_destinations
tools_if_shown.description: Where a stream publishes, in the order they were added: each destination, whether it is enabled, and while the stream runs its delivery state (connecting, live, reconnecting, failed with a reason). Returns the stream id and destinations[]: destinationID, enabled, disabledReason, state, stateReason, stateSince, and the destination's id, name, kind and status.

tools_if_shown.name: add_stream_destination
tools_if_shown.description: Make a stream also publish to one of the workspace's destinations (list_destinations), enabled. Up to 5 per stream and one YouTube channel at most (DESTINATION_LIMIT, YOUTUBE_DESTINATION_LIMIT, DESTINATION_DUPLICATE). A second destination needs multistream on the workspace (MULTISTREAM_NOT_ENABLED). Refused while the stream is live (STREAM_LIVE), and for a destination the stream's quality or codec cannot reach (DESTINATION_INCOMPATIBLE). Returns the stream's whole destination list after the change, as list_stream_destinations does.

tools_if_shown.name: set_stream_destination_enabled
tools_if_shown.description: Stop or resume sending to one of a stream's destinations without removing it. Disabling works while the stream is live — that output goes off the air at once — except for its last enabled destination (LAST_DESTINATION: stop_stream instead). Enabling is refused while live (STREAM_LIVE). Returns the stream's whole destination list after the change, as list_stream_destinations does.

tools_if_shown.name: remove_stream_destination
tools_if_shown.description: Take a destination off a stream (the destination itself stays in the workspace). Refused while the stream is live (STREAM_LIVE): disable it with set_stream_destination_enabled instead. Returns the stream's whole destination list after the change, as list_stream_destinations does.

tools_if_shown.name: get_connection_hints
tools_if_shown.description: Use this FIRST when the user names a platform they want to stream to ("put this on YouTube", "also send it to Twitch") and there is no destination for it yet. Returns, for that platform: the connection methods, the exact `ingestUrl` to pass to create_rtmp_destination (or null when the platform issues one per session), what each method can and cannot do afterwards, the Streamloop tools to call in order, where in the platform's own UI the user finds the stream key, and the behaviour that otherwise ends a 24/7 loop early. NEVER guess an ingest url — a wrong host is a stream that silently never connects. Static guidance: it reads nothing, changes nothing and costs nothing. YouTube in particular has TWO answers and they are not equivalent: a managed connection (Google consent, and only then can titles, privacy, thumbnails and viewer counts be managed from here) or a plain stream key (video only).

tools_if_shown.name: list_destinations
tools_if_shown.description: Find the places this workspace can publish to — connected YouTube channels and custom RTMP endpoints — and their ids, which is what add_stream_destination needs. Check `status`: only an `active` destination can carry a stream; `needs_reauth` and `revoked` mean the YouTube connection must be re-consented (start_youtube_connection) before a stream using it will start. Returns a page of rows (id, name, kind, status, rtmpURL, ytChannelTitleCached, archivedAt, lastUsedAt, createdAt) plus nextCursor and total.

tools_if_shown.name: create_rtmp_destination
tools_if_shown.description: Create a destination for any platform that gives out an RTMP ingest URL and stream key (Twitch, Facebook, Kick, X, TikTok, Telegram, a self-hosted server, or YouTube when its channel is not connected here). Take rtmpUrl from get_connection_hints(platform).ingestUrl rather than guessing it — a wrong host is a stream that silently never connects. The key is stored encrypted and never read back. Use create_youtube_destination instead when the channel is connected through Streamloop: only then can titles, privacy and thumbnails be managed from here. Attach the new destination to a stream with add_stream_destination.

tools_if_shown.name: update_destination
tools_if_shown.description: Maintain an existing destination: rename it, replace the stream key after the platform rotated it (custom RTMP only — a connected YouTube channel has no key to set), and archive or restore it. Archiving hides a destination from the picker without deleting it; it is reversible with archived=false. A live stream keeps publishing with the key it started with, so restart the stream after rotating a key. Pass only the fields to change. NOT transactional: each change commits on its own, and on a failure the response lists which ones already applied.

tools_if_shown.name: start_youtube_connection
tools_if_shown.description: Begin connecting a Google account so its YouTube channels can be streamed to with managed broadcasts (titles, privacy, thumbnails, live stats). Returns a Google consent URL — give it to the user to open in a browser; consent cannot be completed by an agent. Afterwards, list_youtube_channels shows the authorized channels and create_youtube_destination turns one into a destination. Also the fix for a destination whose status is needs_reauth or revoked. Not needed for plain RTMP publishing to YouTube — that is create_rtmp_destination, but it cannot manage the broadcast.

tools_if_shown.name: list_youtube_channels
tools_if_shown.description: The YouTube channels this workspace has Google consent for, with live channel data (title, handle, country, subscriber count, connection status). These are NOT destinations yet: pass a channel's `id` to create_youtube_destination to get something a stream can publish to. Use list_destinations to see which channels already have one. An empty result means no Google account is connected — start_youtube_connection.

tools_if_shown.name: create_youtube_destination
tools_if_shown.description: Turn an already-consented YouTube channel into a destination a stream can publish to, with managed broadcasts (update_stream's `youtube` settings, get_stream_live_stats). Takes the channel `id` from list_youtube_channels — NOT the YouTube channel URL or handle. If that list is empty, the account has not consented yet: start_youtube_connection first.

tools_if_shown.name: list_playlists
tools_if_shown.description: Use this to get from a stream to something you can edit: pass streamId and you get the two playlists that stream owns — one video, one audio, created empty with it. Pass sceneId for the playlists a scene's sources play. Also the way to find a playlist id before any other playlist tool. Returns a page of rows (id, name, streamID, sceneId, kind, mode, version, createdAt) plus nextCursor and total; get_playlist has the items.

tools_if_shown.name: create_playlist
tools_if_shown.description: An empty playlist owned by a scene, for one of its playlist sources to play (a stream's own two playlists come with the stream). Fill it with apply_playlist_operations. Each call creates another. Returns the new playlist: id (pl_...), name, sceneId, kind, mode, version, createdAt.

tools_if_shown.name: get_playlist
tools_if_shown.description: Use this before editing a playlist (item ids for remove and reorder come from here, and so does the `version` the edit tools take) and after swapping one onto a live stream (to see the swap finished). Returns the draft items in play order, what a running stream is playing right now, whether the draft differs from that, how it differs, and any custom playback order attached: id, name, kind, mode, version, liveVersion, hasUnpublishedChanges, publishStatus, items, liveItems, diff, orderSequencer and its version and status.

tools_if_shown.name: apply_playlist_operations
tools_if_shown.description: Use this for every playlist change: add media, remove items, reorder, or switch between sequential and shuffle, as one ordered batch. All-or-nothing — if any operation is invalid, nothing is written. A stream that is NOT currently live picks the change up on its next start, with nothing else to call. A stream that IS live keeps playing the arrangement it started with until swap_live_playlist replaces it. Media ids (obj_...) come from list_uploads; item ids (plitm_...) come from get_playlist. Operations apply in sequence, each seeing the result of the previous, so an index in a later operation must account for the earlier ones. Pass basedOnVersion (the `version` from get_playlist) to be told about a concurrent edit instead of overwriting it.

tools_if_shown.name: copy_playlist
tools_if_shown.description: Use this to reuse an arrangement on a second stream instead of rebuilding it: copies one playlist's contents into another playlist of the same kind. The target must be EMPTY — this never merges or overwrites. The target stream picks the contents up on its next start; if it is already live, swap_live_playlist puts them on the air.

tools_if_shown.name: swap_live_playlist
tools_if_shown.description: Use this ONLY to put an edited playlist on the air while its stream is LIVE — the hot swap the product calls publishing. The stream changes over to the new arrangement without going off the air. NOT needed to set a stream up and NOT needed before a first start: starting a stream takes the playlist as it is then, so on a stream that is not live this tool just fails with NOT_LIVE. Asynchronous — newly added media may have to be encoded first, so poll get_playlist until the swap is no longer in progress. expectedDraftVersion is required (the `version` from get_playlist) so a concurrent edit is reported instead of going live by accident. Other failures name their cause: STALE_DRAFT (refetch and retry), EMPTY_PLAYLIST, BROKEN_ITEM (an item's media was deleted or never finished uploading), RECIPE_MISMATCH, NOT_FOUND.

tools_if_shown.name: list_playlist_orders
tools_if_shown.description: Find saved custom playback orders (order sequencers) and their ids. Use it before creating one — an order the user already has can be assigned to another playlist instead of rewritten. Pass streamId to see only orders that can run over that stream's playlist. `latestReadyVersionID` null means nothing usable has been produced yet. Which order a given playlist is using is on get_playlist, not here. Returns a page of rows (id, name, description, latestReadyVersionID, retiredAt, createdAt, assignedPlaylistsCount) plus nextCursor and total.

tools_if_shown.name: get_playlist_order
tools_if_shown.description: One saved order: its description, how many playlists use it, and its newest usable version with any validation problems. Pass playlistId as well to get the answer that actually matters before assigning — whether this order can run over THAT playlist (`assignable`), which items it expects but cannot find, and a dry-run of the first items it would pick, in order. Do that instead of assigning to find out. Returns orderSequencer (id, name, description, assignedPlaylistsCount, latestReadyVersion with validationStatus and diagnostics) and, with playlistId, againstPlaylist (assignable, missingRefs, dependencyWarnings, blockingDiagnostics, version.dryRun.picks).

tools_if_shown.name: create_playlist_order
tools_if_shown.description: Describe a playback order in plain language and have one written and validated. Pass the playlist it is for as playlistId: the order is written against that playlist's REAL items, so leaving it out produces a rule aimed at nothing. Creating does NOT apply it — assign_playlist_order does. Read `status` on the result: READY = usable; INVALID = written but it failed validation, and `diagnostics` say why (refine it, this is not a transport error); MESSAGE = a clarifying question or refusal, nothing was produced; PENDING = still running, poll get_playlist_order. The answer, under createOrderSequencer, also has sequencer (the order: id oseq_..., name, latestReadyVersionID) and version (the version written, or null).

tools_if_shown.name: refine_playlist_order
tools_if_shown.description: Continue the conversation about an existing order — 'never end on an instrumental', 'put the announcement second instead' — producing a new version. Use this rather than creating a second order for the same purpose. Pass the playlist currently being composed against so the rewrite sees its real items. Interpret `status` exactly as for create_playlist_order. A new version does NOT reach playlists already using this order: they stay on the version they were assigned, until assign_playlist_order is called again. Returns, under refineOrderSequencer, the same status, diagnostics, sequencer and version as create_playlist_order.

tools_if_shown.name: assign_playlist_order
tools_if_shown.description: Make a playlist play in a saved order. This is the step that changes playback, and unlike a playlist edit it needs no swap_live_playlist — a running stream picks the new order up for its next items. The version in use is pinned at assign time and never advances on its own, so call this again after refine_playlist_order to adopt an improvement. Check get_playlist_order(id, playlistId) first: assignment succeeds even when items the order names are missing, returning dependencyWarnings, and those items simply never get picked. Only a rule that cannot run over the playlist at all is refused. Returns dependencyWarnings, the playlist (id, version, compatibility status), the order and the version now pinned.

tools_if_shown.name: unassign_playlist_order
tools_if_shown.description: Stop a playlist using a custom order; it returns to playing in its own item order (or shuffled, per the playlist's mode). The order itself is kept and can be assigned again. Like assigning, it takes effect on a running stream immediately, with no swap_live_playlist needed.

tools_if_shown.name: list_uploads
tools_if_shown.description: Find media and their ids (obj_...) — what apply_playlist_operations adds to a playlist. Removed media is not listed. `uploaded` false means the media is still arriving or processing and cannot be streamed yet. Returns a page of rows (id, name, type, mimeType, fileSize, uploaded, createdAt) plus nextCursor and total; get_upload has one item's duration, resolution and import progress.

tools_if_shown.name: get_upload
tools_if_shown.description: One media file in detail: duration, resolution, framerate, whether it has video and audio (probed from the file itself, not from its name), a temporary download URL, a thumbnail, and — for a URL import — how far the download has got and why it failed. Use it to confirm media is ready to stream, and to read the duration a schedule window has to fit. Returns id, name, type, mimeType, fileSize, uploaded, duration, width, height, fps, hasVideo, hasAudio, downloadUrl, thumbnailUrl, meta and externalSource.

tools_if_shown.name: create_upload
tools_if_shown.description:
Step 1 of uploading a LOCAL file: reserves the media record and returns `uploadUrl`, a presigned PUT you can use immediately. This server does not relay bytes, but YOU probably can — if the client can run a command or make an HTTP request, do the PUT itself:
  curl -X PUT -H 'Content-Type: <the mimeType you passed>' --data-binary @<file> '<uploadUrl>'
The Content-Type header MUST equal the mimeType given here, or the signature is rejected. The url is valid for about 11 hours and takes the whole file in one request (up to 5 GB; a bigger file, up to 15 GB, must come in through import_upload_from_url). If the client cannot make requests, hand `uploadUrl` to the user. Then call complete_upload — media that is never PUT and completed stays unusable. If the file is already reachable over https (including a file the user attached in this conversation), skip all of this and use discover_external_media + import_upload_from_url instead. Returns object (the media record: id obj_..., name, type, mimeType, fileSize, uploaded false, createdAt), uploadUrl and next (the next step).

tools_if_shown.name: complete_upload
tools_if_shown.description: Step 2 of uploading a local file: call it once the bytes have been PUT to the url create_upload returned — by you, or by the user — which starts processing. Until this is called the media is unusable, and calling it before the PUT finishes leaves a broken record. Nothing to call for a url import: import_upload_from_url completes on its own.

tools_if_shown.name: discover_external_media
tools_if_shown.description: Look at any media url and report what could be imported from it: each asset with its quality options, sizes and duration. REQUIRED BEFORE import_upload_from_url, which takes the opaque asset and quality ids only this tool hands out — they cannot be constructed. Works for a media page AND for a direct file link, which is what makes it the right tool for a FILE THE USER ATTACHED in this conversation: pass the attachment's https url and import from it, with no local file and no PUT. Reads the url only; nothing is imported and no credits are spent. Import only the user's own or otherwise licensed content. Returns externalLinkContents: provider, and items[] each with id (assetId), name, mime, size, durationSeconds and qualities[] (id = qualityId, label, width, height, fps, estimatedSize).

tools_if_shown.name: import_upload_from_url
tools_if_shown.description: Import chosen assets from a media url — a page, a direct file link, or a file the user attached in this conversation — straight into the workspace, with no local file and no PUT. Each selection must echo an assetId and qualityId from discover_external_media for the SAME url; invented ids are rejected. One selection produces one media item, so the same asset can be imported twice with different ranges to get two clips. Downloading is asynchronous: poll get_upload until it reports the import finished. Attachment urls usually expire, so import promptly rather than storing the link for later. Returns one media record per selection (id obj_..., name, type, uploaded, externalSource with its download state).

tools_if_shown.name: delete_upload
tools_if_shown.description: Permanently remove a media file from the library: its stored bytes and every file derived from it are deleted. Irreversible. An upload that never finished (no complete_upload after the PUT, an import that failed) is dropped too: nothing was stored. Refused, with nothing changed, while a playlist or a recent stream still uses it (IN_USE) — remove it from those playlists first with apply_playlist_operations — and for an image (UNSUPPORTED_TYPE). Requires confirm=true and the streamloop:destructive scope.

tools_if_shown.name: get_billing_overview
tools_if_shown.description: Use this to answer 'can this keep streaming, and for how long' — and whenever a stream fails to start or stops with no configuration problem, since check_stream_readiness deliberately does not look at credits. One call returns the credit balance, credits left, whether the account is in good standing, how fast credits are being spent right now, which streams are live and what they are costing, and the per-minute rate of each output quality (so a remaining-time estimate needs no second call). Read-only: buying credits is not possible from here, so if the balance is short, point the user at the Streamloop dashboard. Returns me.billing (balance, creditsLeft, goodStanding, eligibleForFreeCredits), spendSummary, activeUsage and pricingTiers.

tools_if_shown.name: get_streaming_usage
tools_if_shown.description: Use this for questions about the past — 'how many hours did I stream last month', 'is my spend going up' — not about the present. Returns minutes streamed, credits spent and session counts bucketed over a period and split by output quality. get_billing_overview has the current balance and burn rate instead. Returns usageAnalytics: totalMinutes, totalCredits, sessionCount, byQuality[] (quality, minutes, credits) and buckets[] (date, minutes, credits, sessions).

tools_if_shown.name: get_account
tools_if_shown.description: Who this token belongs to: the signed-in account's id, email, name, language and the default run-length new streams inherit. Use it to confirm which account an agent is acting for. It says nothing about which workspace is in use (get_selected_workspace) or about credits (get_billing_overview). Returns me: id, email, firstName, lastName, avatarURL, role, locale, defaultStreamDuration, createdAt.

tools_if_shown.name: list_workspaces
tools_if_shown.description: Every workspace this account belongs to, with the account's role in each and which one is currently in use. Streams, media, playlists, destinations and credits all belong to ONE workspace and are never shared between them, so when a user says something exists and it is not in a list, check here before concluding it is missing — the answer is usually that another workspace is selected. Pass an `id` from here to select_workspace, or give the user the id to pin in their client configuration. `role` matters for workspace administration, which happens in the dashboard. Returns workspaces[] (id, identityId, name, slug, personal, role, active), selectedWorkspaceId and selectionSource (explicit, header, env or token-hint).

tools_if_shown.name: select_workspace
tools_if_shown.description: Switch which workspace this connection works in, for every later tool call on this connection (other connections, even ones sharing the same login, are unaffected). Takes an `id` from list_workspaces; membership is checked here and again by the API on every request, so this grants no access by itself. Use it when a stream, upload or destination the user describes is not in this workspace. Overrides a workspace the client pinned in its own configuration (the X-Workspace-Id header, or MCP_WORKSPACE_ID on stdio) for the rest of this connection. Call it again at any time to switch back.

tools_if_shown.name: get_selected_workspace
tools_if_shown.description: Which workspace this connection is working in right now, and where that came from: `explicit` (a select_workspace call), `header` or `env` (the client pinned it in its own configuration), or `token-hint` (the default the login carries). Call it when a result is unexpectedly empty, to confirm you are looking in the right workspace before telling the user something does not exist.

tools_if_shown.name: scene_get
tools_if_shown.description: Read the scene's draft (or a published version, with version): a resource (with its revision and children, the sub-paths to read next), a type such as element/Text or source/data (its props), a mask ending in /* (a list), or "" (the types). as: "image" on a frame or layer → a picture of it. (In a scene's draft; scene: its id.) Answers summary and value (the resource, with its revision and children), or image for as "image"; plus draftRevision (version, for a published version).

tools_if_shown.name: scene_probe
tools_if_shown.description: Fetch a URL once, changing nothing in the show: HTTP status, content type, an outline of the JSON (keys, their values, array lengths) or the page's title and text, and the rows a table would get from it with connector, pick and headers — or, with connector mcp, an MCP server's tools, or one tool's rows with tool and args. Use it before creating a URL or MCP table, and to find the pick path or selector. (In a scene's draft; scene: its id.)

tools_if_shown.name: scene_remove
tools_if_shown.description: Delete whole resources (frames, layers, sources, components). All or nothing: anything in use by something not removed in the same call is refused, with what uses it. (In a scene's draft; scene: its id.) Removing a resource needs its revision in `revisions` (path → the revision you read; "*": whatever is there, on purpose); without it the answer is REVISION_REQUIRED. It changes the draft only: viewers see nothing until publish_scene, and discard_scene_draft brings back what was published. Answers summary, removed (the paths) and draftRevision.

tools_if_shown.name: scene_set
tools_if_shown.description: Create, replace or change one resource; get <type> shows what each takes, with an example. value is the whole resource, as get answers it: a frame { code: "<JSX>" } or, as JSON, { name, root }; a component { description, props, tsx }; a source or table its fields. edits change part of it: [{ old, new }] replaces text in its code (copy old from what get answers: code is stored formatted), or an object is merged into its fields. One layer changes alone at its own path: frame/<id>/<layer> with edits { props: { … } }. Every set is checked as the studio checks it; a refused set changes nothing: read the error, fix, send again. The answer has the path it is stored at, its new revision, what changed, and draftRevision (the draft as it is now: what publish takes). (In a scene's draft; scene: its id.) Changing a resource that exists needs its `revision`, from the answer that read it ("*" overwrites whatever is there, on purpose); without it the answer is REVISION_REQUIRED. A new path needs none.

tools_if_shown.name: list_scenes
tools_if_shown.description: Lists the workspace's scenes, newest first: id, name, the version last published (0: never) and when. Read one's draft with scene_get (path "" lists what it holds). Answers items (id, name, version, publishedAt, createdAt, updatedAt), nextCursor and hasMore.

tools_if_shown.name: create_scene
tools_if_shown.description: Creates a scene with an empty draft, nothing published. Build it with scene_set (frame/<id> for each frame, source/… for what it reads), then publish_scene. Each call creates another scene. Answers the scene: id (scn_…), name, version 0, and its timestamps.

tools_if_shown.name: publish_scene
tools_if_shown.description: Publishes the draft exactly as it was at draftRevision (required) as the scene's next version: what streams playing it play from then on. All of it is checked first; a refusal (SCENE_INVALID) lists each problem — fix them with scene_set and publish again. Edits made after draftRevision are not published (the answer says so, stale: true). If someone published after the version your draft is based on, it is refused (STALE_PUBLISH: publishedVersion and what would be reverted) — read the draft again; only with the user's say-so send overwritePublished: <that version>. When that version is a revert (publishedVersionIsRevert), reading again changes nothing: overwritePublished, or discard_scene_draft to keep it.A scene on air is refused with CONFIRM_REQUIRED naming the streams — tell the user, then send confirm: true. An unchanged draft publishes nothing; dryRun checks it and lists what would change. Answers summary (what happened and what to do next), version, publishedAt, changes (what changed, as resource paths), notes, and the streams playing it.

tools_if_shown.name: discard_scene_draft
tools_if_shown.description: Puts the draft back to the published version: every change made since it was published is lost (nothing on air changes). draftRevision (required) is the draft you reviewed: if it changed after that, nothing is discarded (CONFLICT). dryRun: true lists what would be lost and discards nothing — show the user that first. Refused (NOT_PUBLISHED) when nothing is published.

tools_if_shown.name: list_scene_versions
tools_if_shown.description: Lists a scene's published versions, newest first. Answers items (version, publishedAt, publishedBy), nextCursor and hasMore. Read one with scene_get and version.

tools_if_shown.name: revert_scene
tools_if_shown.description: Publishes an earlier version's document as the next version (the versions in between stay; the draft is untouched — publishing the draft later is refused with STALE_PUBLISH until you send overwritePublished, and discard_scene_draft makes the draft this version too). expectedVersion (required) is the latest published version you saw (list_scene_versions, list_scenes): if someone published since, nothing changes (STALE_PUBLISH: publishedVersion and what the revert would also take off air). On air it is refused with CONFIRM_REQUIRED like a publish: tell the user, then send confirm: true.

tools_if_shown.name: delete_scene
tools_if_shown.description: Deletes the scene, its draft and every published version, for good. Refused (SCENE_IN_USE) while a stream plays it. Its ingest keys are revoked and its cameras removed.

tools_if_shown.name: set_stream_scene
tools_if_shown.description: Makes a stream play a scene (its published version) instead of a video playlist, or with scene null stops doing so. Refused (STREAM_LIVE) while the stream runs: stop it, set the scene, start it again. The scene must be published first (publish_scene).

tools_if_shown.name: get_scene_state
tools_if_shown.description: What a scene has on air. Answers streams: each stream that plays it, with its id (stream), name and state and, under onAir while it runs, the frame/<id> on air (frame) and the one cued next, the controls' values, each source's status and what its playlists play. With no stream playing it, streams is empty and summary says how to put it on air.

tools_if_shown.name: control_scene
tools_if_shown.description: Acts on the scene on air, as its operator would: goFrame (take frame/<target> to air, with a transition), next (cue frame/<target> so the take is instant; no target clears the cue), setControl (set one of its controls; scene_get control/* lists them), setData (replace a table's rows), skip (a playlist source to its next item). Viewers see it at once. The arguments are checked first, then against what is published (a frame, control, table or playlist source it doesn't have, a toggle given "yes": INVALID_INPUT); only then is it refused while nothing plays it (SCENE_OFFLINE). A SCENE_TIMEOUT may or may not have applied: send an actionId (a new uuid per action, kept by you) and retry with the SAME actionId and arguments — it is applied at most once. Without an actionId, never retry an action that isn't idempotent (skip, a button) blind: read get_scene_state first. Needs a stream playing the published scene (set_stream_scene, start_stream); it changes what is on air, never the draft. Answers streamId, online, frame (on air after the action) and next.

tools_if_shown.name: create_scene_ingest_key
tools_if_shown.description: Makes the key an encoder (OBS, vMix, a phone app) sends a live feed with, for one of the scene's rtmp or srt sources: RTMP, RTMPS and SRT URLs with the key, shown in this answer only — give them to the user. Make the source first (scene_set source/rtmp/<id>). The source's status is waiting until an encoder connects with this key, and live while it publishes. The key's own id (ingkey_…) is what revoke_scene_ingest_key takes. Answers id, sourceId, key, keyPrefix, status, live, rtmpUrl and rtmpsUrl.

tools_if_shown.name: rename_scene
tools_if_shown.description: Changes the scene's display name, the one list_scenes and the dashboard show. Its draft, published versions and the streams playing it are untouched. Answers the scene: id, name, version.

tools_if_shown.name: list_scene_inputs
tools_if_shown.description: Lists a scene's ingest keys (id ingkey_…, which source, live or not, never the key itself), its secrets (names only) and its IP cameras: what create_scene_ingest_key and set_scene_secret made. Answers ingestKeys (id, sourceId, keyPrefix, status, live, rtmpUrl, rtmpsUrl), secrets (name, updatedAt) and cameras (id, sourceId, url without credentials, transport, the last connection test).

tools_if_shown.name: revoke_scene_ingest_key
tools_if_shown.description: Revokes an ingest key for good: the encoder using it is cut off at once. It cannot be restored; a new key for the same source: create_scene_ingest_key. Answers revoked (the key's id).

tools_if_shown.name: delete_scene_secret
tools_if_shown.description: Deletes a saved secret for good: its value cannot be read back, and a table that names it ("$secret:<name>") stops getting it. Only set_scene_secret with the key again restores it. Answers deleted (the name).

tools_if_shown.name: set_scene_secret
tools_if_shown.description: Saves an API key or token a scene's tables send (sealed; never shown again). A table names it as "$secret:<name>" in a header value or a URL's query. A name that exists already has its value replaced, and tables using it send the new one. Only a key the user gave you. Answers name and updatedAt.

tools_if_shown.name: person_enrich
tools_if_shown.description:
Enrich a person by email, phone, name, social URL, or other identifiers.

Requires at least one primary identifier (email, phone, social_url, linkedin_id,
legion_id, email_hash) OR name + context (location, company, school, job_title, birth_date).

Returns detailed person profile including contact info, work experience,
education, skills, and more. Each successful match consumes one credit.
Field access is determined by the team's contract.

Returns JSON `{"matches": [{"person": {...}, "match_metadata": {...}}], "total": n}`:
the best match, its `match_metadata` (`matched_on`: the input fields that matched,
`match_type`, `match_confidence`: high, moderate or low), and `total`, the number of
matches found. No match is an error (HTTP 404) and costs nothing.

Key person fields: `legion_id`, `full_name`, `job_title`, `seniority_level`,
`job_function`, `company_name`, `company_domain`, `work_email`, `mobile_phone`,
`emails`, `phones`, `linkedin_url`, `city`, `state`, `country`, `experience`,
`education`, `skills`, `last_seen`. `emails` and `phones` are lists with
`address`/`number` and `type`.

tools_if_shown.name: person_search
tools_if_shown.description:
Search for people using SQL WHERE syntax.

Write a SELECT query against the 'people' table. The query must start with
SELECT. Do NOT include a LIMIT or OFFSET clause (the API rejects both); page
with the `limit` and `offset` parameters instead. Example:
  query: "SELECT * FROM people WHERE company_name ILIKE '%google%' AND state = 'california'"
  limit: 2
  offset: 0   # page 1; pass offset: 2 for page 2 with limit: 2

Available columns include: first_name, last_name, full_name, email, phone,
job_title, company_name, company_industry, city, state, state_code, country,
linkedin_url, and more. Text values are lowercase: `state` is the full name
('texas'), `state_code` the ISO code ('US-TX'), `country` the full name
('united states'). A title filter alone (`job_title ILIKE '%sales%'`) scans
everyone and can time out; pair it with a state, city or company filter.
Cross-table columns (title, organization_name, skills, headline, summary)
are automatically rewritten to subqueries.

Returns JSON `{"matches": [{"person": {...}}], "total": n}`: one page of person
records (the same fields as person_enrich) and `total`, the number of people the
WHERE clause matches across the database (an estimate for very broad queries).
Each person returned consumes one credit.

`include_fields` / `exclude_fields` take the same names as person_enrich. Full
profiles are large (up to ~10k tokens each), which is why `limit` defaults to 2,
like person_enrich; to list more people, name the fields you need in
include_fields and raise `limit`.

tools_if_shown.name: company_enrich
tools_if_shown.description:
Enrich a company by domain, name, LinkedIn, or ticker symbol.

Requires at least one identifier. The 'industry' field narrows name-based matching
but is not a standalone lookup. It must be a lowercase LinkedIn Industry V2
taxonomy value (e.g. 'software development') — a free-text value matches nothing
and silently zeroes the results. Returns company profile including employee counts,
workforce analytics, hiring/attrition trends, and distribution breakdowns.

Returns JSON `{"matches": [{"company": {...}, "match_metadata": {...}}], "total": n}`:
the best match, its `match_metadata` (`matched_on`, `match_type`,
`match_confidence`: high, moderate or low), and `total`, the number of matches
found. Each match consumes one credit; no match is an error (HTTP 404) and costs
nothing.

Key company fields: `legion_id`, `name` (object: `display`, `cleaned`, `raw`), `domain`,
`industry`, `size` (band), `founded`, `type`, `description`, `linkedin_url`,
`linkedin_employee_count` (the company's LinkedIn figure),
`legion_employee_count` (people Data Legion tracks at the company; a floor, not a
full headcount), `legion_new_hire_count`, `legion_attrition_count`,
`legion_employee_growth_rate`, `legion_employee_count_by_month`,
`legion_seniority_distribution`, `legion_job_function_distribution`, `tickers`,
`socials`, `domains`.

The hiring, attrition, growth and turnover windows (1m/3m/6m/12m) end at the
last month of `legion_employee_count_by_month`, not today. Job changes reach
profiles months after they happen, so the most recent months fill in over later
releases: read a low recent month as incomplete data, not a hiring freeze.

tools_if_shown.name: company_search
tools_if_shown.description:
Search for companies using SQL WHERE syntax.

Write a SELECT query against the 'companies' table. Do NOT include a LIMIT or
OFFSET clause — use the limit and offset parameters instead. Example:
  query: "SELECT * FROM companies WHERE industry ILIKE '%software%' AND legion_employee_count > 100"
  limit: 3
  offset: 0   # page 1; pass offset: 3 for page 2 with limit: 3

Returns JSON `{"matches": [{"company": {...}}], "total": n}`: one page of company
profiles (the same fields as company_enrich: name, domain, industry, size,
headcount, hiring and attrition trends, socials and more) and `total`, the number
of companies the WHERE clause matches across the database (an estimate for very
broad queries). Each company returned consumes one credit.

`include_fields` / `exclude_fields` take the same names as company_enrich. Full
companies are large (up to ~6k tokens each), which is why `limit` defaults to 3;
to list more companies, name the fields you need in include_fields and raise
`limit`.

tools_if_shown.name: utility_clean
tools_if_shown.description:
Clean and normalize one or more data fields.

Pass a dict of field names to values. Supported person fields: email, phone,
full_name, first_name, last_name, state, country, social_url, school. Supported
company fields: company, domain, linkedin_company_url, ticker_symbol.

Returns JSON `{"results": {<field>: {"original", "cleaned", "normalized"}}}`: for
each field, the value sent, the cleaned value, and whether cleaning changed it.
`cleaned` is a string, except state and country (always `{full_name, code}`; an
unrecognized value comes back lowercased as `full_name`), social_url (`{url,
network}`), and company and school (`{name, type}`, `{domain, type}` or `{url,
network, type}`). Any other value it can't clean comes back as the trimmed input.
An unsupported field name or an empty value is an error. Free; no credits.

tools_if_shown.name: utility_hash_email
tools_if_shown.description:
Hash an email address for privacy-preserving lookups.

Returns JSON `{"email", "normalized_email", "hashes": {"sha256", "sha1", "md5"}}`:
the email sent, the normalized form that was hashed, and its hex digests. Any of
the hashes can be used with person_enrich's email_hash parameter. Free; no credits.

tools_if_shown.name: utility_validate
tools_if_shown.description:
Validate person or company data and get cleaning suggestions.

Pass any combination of fields to validate. Use this before enrichment to ensure
data quality and improve match rates.

Returns JSON `{"valid", "errors", "warnings", "suggestions"}`: `valid` is false
when any field has an error; each error and warning names the `field`, the
`value`, the problem (`error` / `warning`) and an optional `suggestion`; each
suggestion gives a `field` and its `cleaned` value. Free; no credits.

tools_if_shown.name: report_person
tools_if_shown.description:
Report a data-quality issue with a person record (by legion_id).

Use this to flag bad/incorrect/outdated person data you got from
person_enrich or person_search so it can be reviewed and corrected. No credit
cost; available to any signed-in user or valid API key.

`field`: omit for 'record'; required for 'group' (a field-group slug) and
'field' (a response field name). At least one of `correct_value` or `comment`
is required.

Returns JSON confirming the recorded report: `report_id`, `status`, `subject_type`,
`legion_id`, `issue_type`, `issue_level`, `field` and `created_at`. Each call
records a new report.

tools_if_shown.name: report_company
tools_if_shown.description:
Report a data-quality issue with a company record (by legion_id).

Use this to flag bad/incorrect/outdated company data you got from
company_enrich or company_search so it can be reviewed and corrected. No credit
cost; available to any signed-in user or valid API key.

`field`: omit for 'record'; required for 'group' and 'field'. At least one of
`correct_value` or `comment` is required.

Returns JSON confirming the recorded report: `report_id`, `status`, `subject_type`,
`legion_id`, `issue_type`, `issue_level`, `field` and `created_at`. Each call
records a new report.

tools_if_shown.name: show_journey
tools_if_shown.description: Use this when the user wants to see a planned journey's route, mode and arrival countdown displayed as a card. Renders a journey card showing origin, destination, transport mode and a countdown to arrival based on the given duration.

tools_if_shown.name: search_lyon_content
tools_if_shown.description: Use this when the user asks about Lyon or the subjects it covers. Covers: restaurant recommendations, brunch spots, pizzerias in Lyon, where locals eat, morning walks, weekend outings, neighborhood food guides, Lyon dining tips. Returns verbatim passages from the space's own content, kept current by its owners, each under the title of the entry it comes from. An empty result can mean the query was too narrow; a rephrased query may find the answer. Time-limited content (e.g. a daily special or a weekly schedule) is filtered out once expired, so when nothing current answers a question about today or this week, it has not been published yet. A passage carrying a "validUntil" date is a time-limited exception (e.g. an exceptional closure or opening) that overrides a permanent passage on the same topic until that date; the passage says when the period ends, or when it starts if it hasn't started yet.

tools_if_shown.name: display_lyon_map
tools_if_shown.description: Use this when the user wants to see Lyon places plotted on an interactive map. Renders a map with the given places plotted by their titles and coordinates. Get the places and their coordinates from search_lyon_places first.

tools_if_shown.name: get_lyon_weather
tools_if_shown.description: Use this when the user asks for the current weather in Lyon or any other city. Returns the current temperature in °C, conditions in words such as 'light rain', and wind speed and direction. Not for rendering a weather card; use show_lyon_weather.

tools_if_shown.name: show_metro_line
tools_if_shown.description: Use this when the user wants to see a metro line's stations, current position and next arrivals displayed as a diagram. Renders a metro line diagram with the ordered stations, the current station, transfer points and the next arrivals in minutes. Get the stations and next departures from get_metro_line first.

tools_if_shown.name: get_parking_lot
tools_if_shown.description: Use this when the user asks about a specific named parking lot's availability or price in Lyon. Returns the full real-time record for the matched parking lot, including availability and pricing. Not for searching for parking lots near a destination; use search_parkings.

tools_if_shown.name: search_parkings
tools_if_shown.description: Use this when the user wants parking options near an address, point of interest or neighbourhood in Lyon. Returns open parking lots within a radius of the given destination, sorted by distance, with real-time availability. Not for looking up one specific named parking lot; use get_parking_lot.

tools_if_shown.name: send_lyon_email
tools_if_shown.description: Use this when the user wants to contact the person behind this Lyon space, for example to make a request or ask a question. Sends an email with the collected date and time, phone number and reason for the request to the space's fixed recipient. The email is sent for real to the fixed recipient and cannot be recalled; confirm the date, time, phone number and reason with the user before sending.

tools_if_shown.name: search_lyon_places
tools_if_shown.description: Use this when the user asks where something is in Lyon, what is nearby, or which places Lyon covers. Covers: restaurant locations, places to eat, walking routes, neighborhoods in Lyon, points of interest, addresses in Lyon, maps of Lyon spots. Returns matching places with their coordinates, from content kept current by the space's owners. Map and display tools render only the values they are given, so this is where their coordinates come from. An empty result can mean the query was too narrow; a rephrased query may find the place.

tools_if_shown.name: show_lyon_weather
tools_if_shown.description: Use this when the user wants a weather forecast for a city shown as a visual card. Renders a weather card with temperature, condition, sunrise and sunset for one city and day. Get the current temperature and conditions from get_lyon_weather first.

tools_if_shown.name: search_lyon_news
tools_if_shown.description: Use this when the user asks for recent news articles about Lyon or any other topic, country or time period. Returns matching news articles, ten per page, optionally filtered by country, language and recency period.
