tools_if_shown.name: save_event_link
tools_if_shown.description: Add or edit a web link on a gig. Without link_id this adds url: the label and kind default from the link (a discord.gg link is a community link labelled Discord), and a gig keeps each address once, so adding the same address again returns 409. With link_id (from list_event_links) it edits that link: pass only the fields to change; an edited link counts as added by a person, so a later import of the event page leaves it alone. Requires gig-operations access.

tools_if_shown.name: remove_event_link
tools_if_shown.description: Remove a link from a gig. Confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set. Requires gig-operations access.

tools_if_shown.name: get_event_labor_call
tools_if_shown.description: Get a gig's local labor call: the stagehand order placed with the venue or union (e.g. IATSE), one row per department with a call time and a headcount of hands for load-in, show and load-out. Hands are counts, not named crew — for named crew use the staffing tools. Call times are HH:MM wall clocks in the gig's timezone. Returns the whole labor call: union_local, steward, steward_call, head_electrician, head_electrician_call, notes, departments (id, department, load_in_call, load_in_hands, show_call, show_hands, load_out_call, load_out_hands, load_out_next_day, notes, sort_order) and totals (load_in_hands, show_hands, load_out_hands). Each department phase with hands or a call is a house labor shift on the gig's Staffing board: load-in on the first day, show every day, load-out on the last day. A load-out call earlier than the show call (or the load-in call, or 06:00 when neither is set) falls on the next morning and load_out_next_day is true. Anyone on the gig can read it.

tools_if_shown.name: update_event_labor_call
tools_if_shown.description: Set the labor call header: union_local (e.g. "IATSE Local 51"), steward (name or contact), steward_call (HH:MM in the gig timezone), head_electrician (the house electrician tying in company power), head_electrician_call (HH:MM) and notes (union rules and penalties: meal breaks, dark stage, overtime). Pass only the fields to change; null or "" clears. Departments are edited with add/update/remove_event_labor_call_department. Returns the whole labor call: union_local, steward, steward_call, head_electrician, head_electrician_call, notes, departments (id, department, load_in_call, load_in_hands, show_call, show_hands, load_out_call, load_out_hands, load_out_next_day, notes, sort_order) and totals (load_in_hands, show_hands, load_out_hands). Each department phase with hands or a call is a house labor shift on the gig's Staffing board: load-in on the first day, show every day, load-out on the last day. A load-out call earlier than the show call (or the load-in call, or 06:00 when neither is set) falls on the next morning and load_out_next_day is true. Requires gig-operations access.

tools_if_shown.name: save_event_labor_call_department
tools_if_shown.description: Add or edit a department row on a gig's labor call. Without department_id this adds a row, e.g. department "Rigging — Ground" with load_in_call 09:00 and load_in_hands 11. With department_id (from get_event_labor_call) it edits that row: pass only the fields to change; null or "" clears a call time, null sets hands to 0. Returns the whole labor call: union_local, steward, steward_call, head_electrician, head_electrician_call, notes, departments (id, department, load_in_call, load_in_hands, show_call, show_hands, load_out_call, load_out_hands, load_out_next_day, notes, sort_order) and totals (load_in_hands, show_hands, load_out_hands). Each department phase with hands or a call is a house labor shift on the gig's Staffing board: load-in on the first day, show every day, load-out on the last day. A load-out call earlier than the show call (or the load-in call, or 06:00 when neither is set) falls on the next morning and load_out_next_day is true. Requires gig-operations access.

tools_if_shown.name: remove_event_labor_call_department
tools_if_shown.description: Remove a department row from a gig's labor call. Returns the whole labor call: union_local, steward, steward_call, head_electrician, head_electrician_call, notes, departments (id, department, load_in_call, load_in_hands, show_call, show_hands, load_out_call, load_out_hands, load_out_next_day, notes, sort_order) and totals (load_in_hands, show_hands, load_out_hands). Each department phase with hands or a call is a house labor shift on the gig's Staffing board: load-in on the first day, show every day, load-out on the last day. A load-out call earlier than the show call (or the load-in call, or 06:00 when neither is set) falls on the next morning and load_out_next_day is true. Confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set. Requires gig-operations access.

tools_if_shown.name: get_crew_requirements
tools_if_shown.description: Read what the crew must wear and remember for a gig: the dress preset (label plus men, women and any text), the gig's dress notes, its own reminders and the org standing reminders every gig inherits.

tools_if_shown.name: set_crew_requirements
tools_if_shown.description: Set a gig's dress code and crew reminders. Only the fields you pass change; pass null to clear one. dress_preset_key must be one of the org dress presets. Reminders are one per line. Requires gig-manager access. Does not notify crew.

tools_if_shown.name: list_outside_gear
tools_if_shown.description: List the gear outside parties bring to a gig (the band, a vendor or the venue): name, count, who provides it and notes. Owned inventory is listed by the inventory tools.

tools_if_shown.name: add_outside_gear
tools_if_shown.description: Add a line of gear an outside party brings to a gig, such as a vendor sound package, band fronts or venue instruments. It does not touch inventory. Requires gig-manager access.

tools_if_shown.name: list_event_agreements
tools_if_shown.description: List native gig agreements (contracts) for one event, with canCreate and eligible recipients when the caller can edit finances. Recipients see only their own rows.

tools_if_shown.name: create_event_agreement
tools_if_shown.description: Create a native gig agreement for signature on the Venue tab. Supply title, recipient_id, recipient_kind (musician or client), and either content text and/or pdf_base64 + pdf_filename (inline base64 — not request_attachment_upload, which is ingestion-only). recipient_id and recipient_kind must match a row from list_event_agreements (published roster crew or a client contact linked to the gig). EventMembers added as INVITED on draft or template gigs are rejected until the gig is published (ACTIVE). notify_recipient defaults false; when true, queues the assignment email if an address exists. Requires financial editing access. Confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set.

tools_if_shown.name: void_agreement
tools_if_shown.description: Void an unsigned native gig agreement. Signed agreements keep their record; this marks the agreement void for the gig. Requires financial editing access. Confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set.

tools_if_shown.name: list_event_plans
tools_if_shown.description: List the organization's event plans (brief-to-plan drafts) newest first, with status, step hint, title, date, and readiness. Statuses: DRAFTING (still being filled in), REVIEWED (summary accepted, ready for create_draft_event_from_plan), CREATED (a draft gig exists), ABANDONED. Read-only.

tools_if_shown.name: get_event_plan
tools_if_shown.description: Read one event plan in full: details (title, date, timezone, clocks, location, guest count) with per-field provenance and competing candidates, schedule entries, staffing roles, checklist phases, matched venue/customer records, the plan's own open questions, conflicts, and readiness (can_review / can_create_draft plus what is blocking). The plan is the source of truth — ask the user the plan's `questions` verbatim rather than inventing answers. Every edit needs the `version` this returns. Read-only.

tools_if_shown.name: suggest_plan_templates
tools_if_shown.description: Rank the organization's gig templates against a plan and explain each match: template_event_id, title, template_version, score, human-readable reasons, and what the template would contribute (schedule entries, roles, seats, tasks). Show the user the ranked options and let them choose — do not silently pick the top one. Apply the choice with update_event_plan {op:"set_template"} or rebase_event_plan_template. Read-only.

tools_if_shown.name: preview_save_event_as_template
tools_if_shown.description: Preview what saving a gig as a reusable template would keep and drop: retained sections with counts, excluded sections with reasons, what is always left out (people, money, client data), the existing templates a new version could replace, and a preview_token. Pass target_template_id when the user is replacing an existing template — that mode forces extra exclusions (attachments, inventory), and previewing without it mints a token bound to the wrong mode, which save_event_as_template will reject. Writes nothing — pass the preview_token to save_event_as_template to save exactly what was previewed.

tools_if_shown.name: create_event_plan
tools_if_shown.description: Turn a client brief into a reviewable event plan. Pass the brief verbatim as brief_text, attach it as brief_file (base64, max 8 MiB), and/or start from a gig template with template_event_id — at least one is required. The plan is the source of truth — after this call, ask the user the plan's own `questions` verbatim (the ones with `blocking:"draft"` first, `batch:true`). Never infer or default a year, date, timezone, budget, headcount, venue, or client the brief does not state. Nothing here sends an invitation, offer, message, or notification. Nothing is created on the calendar either: a plan becomes a gig only through create_draft_event_from_plan.

tools_if_shown.name: update_event_plan
tools_if_shown.description: Apply edits to a plan: answer or dismiss its questions, set a field, choose between competing candidates, resolve the venue/customer match, edit schedule entries and anchors, adjust staffing roles, edit checklist tasks, acknowledge a conflict, or switch template. Send the user's own answers — never infer or default a year, date, timezone, budget, headcount, venue, or client the brief does not state. When a field has more than one candidate, show every candidate to the user and let them choose. dry_run=true previews the effect (including how anchored schedule entries move) and writes nothing. On a version conflict, call get_event_plan again and retry with the fresh version. Nothing here sends an invitation, offer, message, or notification.

tools_if_shown.name: revise_event_plan_brief
tools_if_shown.description: Replace the plan's brief with a corrected or more complete one and re-extract. This REPLACES, it does not merge: send the full brief text again (the original content plus whatever changed), not just a follow-up snippet — any unlocked value or schedule/staffing item the new text doesn't repeat is dropped from the plan (named in the diff as removed). Returns the plan plus a per-field diff of what changed; user answers already recorded are kept. Never infer or default a year, date, timezone, budget, headcount, venue, or client the brief does not state. dry_run=true previews the diff and writes nothing. On a version conflict, call get_event_plan again and retry with the fresh version. Nothing here sends an invitation, offer, message, or notification.

tools_if_shown.name: rebase_event_plan_template
tools_if_shown.description: Re-apply the plan's template at its newest version when get_event_plan reports `template.update`. Template-sourced schedule entries, roles, and tasks are refreshed; anything the user pinned or edited is kept and the returned diff names every change. dry_run=true previews the diff and writes nothing. On a version conflict, call get_event_plan again and retry with the fresh version. Nothing here sends an invitation, offer, message, or notification.

tools_if_shown.name: review_event_plan
tools_if_shown.description: Mark a plan REVIEWED and get the proposed-changes summary: the exact gig that would be created (title, date, timezone, clocks, DRAFT status), the venue and customer that would be linked, how many schedule entries, roles, seats, and checklist tasks come across, and which decisions carry onto the gig for later. Show this summary to the user verbatim before create_draft_event_from_plan — it is the thing they are approving. Reversible: another edit sends the plan back to DRAFTING. On a version conflict, call get_event_plan again and retry with the fresh version. Nothing here sends an invitation, offer, message, or notification.

tools_if_shown.name: create_draft_event_from_plan
tools_if_shown.description: Create ONE DRAFT gig from a reviewed plan: details, schedule, staffing roles, and checklist come across, and the venue/customer links are made. Nothing is sent — no invitations, offers, or messages — and the gig stays a DRAFT until someone promotes it. Publishing (which sends any held invitations) happens in the Soundcheck app (web or mobile), not over MCP: offer get_soundcheck_link to the gig. Unanswered execution-blocking decisions carry onto the gig as open items. Call review_event_plan first and show the user its summary. Confirmation-gated: the first call returns confirmation_required with a summary, and only the second call with that confirmation_token creates the gig. Re-running after a successful create returns the same gig instead of a second one.

tools_if_shown.name: abandon_event_plan
tools_if_shown.description: Discard a plan the user no longer wants. The plan moves to ABANDONED and stops appearing in the working list; nothing that was already created is touched. On a version conflict, call get_event_plan again and retry with the fresh version. Nothing here sends an invitation, offer, message, or notification.

tools_if_shown.name: save_event_as_template
tools_if_shown.description: Save a gig as a reusable gig template (a TEMPLATE-status event) that brief-to-plan can plan from. Structure is kept — schedule shape, roles, checklist — while people, money, and client data are always left out. Run preview_save_event_as_template first, show the user what is kept and dropped, and pass its preview_token back so the save matches the preview. target_template_id saves a NEW VERSION of an existing template instead of creating another one. Nobody is notified.

tools_if_shown.name: set_template_planning_rules
tools_if_shown.description: Set the planning rules on a gig template: anchors (named schedule landmarks such as doors or downbeat), constraints between entries, the entry keys that stay fixed when a plan moves, and match hints (event types and keywords) that steer suggest_plan_templates. Rules make every future plan built from this template land better. The event must be a TEMPLATE and the caller an org admin or gig manager. Nobody is notified.

tools_if_shown.name: get_org_agent_profile
tools_if_shown.description: Load the organization's knowledge-base profile — how this event business works, curated from its website, reviews, closeout notes, lost leads and saved playbook. Call once at the start of a session before planning, quoting or staffing work. Returns {status, playbook, static, dynamic, sections}: static = durable facts, dynamic = recent context, sections = [{key, title, facts}] in knowledge-base order (overview, services, service_area, clients, venues, staffing, operations, money_rules, incidents, voice, playbook, glossary). status is ready, not_enabled (the org has not turned the knowledge base on; playbook is still returned) or not_configured. For the team-reviewed written pages, use get_org_knowledge_page. This is guidance, never the source of truth for dates, crew, or money — verify those with the event, staffing and ledger tools. Read-only; managers and admins only.

tools_if_shown.name: search_org_knowledge
tools_if_shown.description: Search the organization's knowledge base for what it has learned: venue quirks, past incidents and how they were fixed, staffing lessons, and why leads were lost. Ask in plain language (e.g. "load-in problems at The Fillmore", "why do we lose corporate leads"). Each result has text, similarity, kind (profile | incident | learning), occurred_on, and source {type, id} citing the record it came from — use that id with the matching tool (get_event, get_venue) to confirm details before acting. Returns status not_enabled with no results when the org has not turned the knowledge base on. Read-only; managers and admins only.

tools_if_shown.name: get_org_knowledge_page
tools_if_shown.description: Read the written knowledge-base page for one section (or all sections) — the same pages the team sees under Settings → Knowledge base. Pages are written from the org's curated knowledge and may have been edited by the team (origin HUMAN), which makes them the most trusted guidance. Returns {status, updated_at, sections: [{key, title, version, origin, markdown, updated_at}]}. Omit section for every written page. Guidance only — verify dates, crew, and money with the SoR tools. Read-only; managers and admins only.

tools_if_shown.name: get_event_cancellation_impact
tools_if_shown.description: Preview what cancelling a gig would touch before calling cancel_event: crew who will be released and notified, open offers, and ledger lines affected. Read-only; gig managers (owner/admin/coordinator).

tools_if_shown.name: cancel_event
tools_if_shown.description: Cancel a DRAFT or ACTIVE gig: sets it CANCELLED, releases booked crew and notifies them. The gig and its history stay (unlike delete_event). Call get_event_cancellation_impact first and show the user who is affected. Calling again on an already-cancelled gig retries the crew release. Gig managers only. Confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set.

tools_if_shown.name: delete_event
tools_if_shown.description: Delete a gig: it is hidden right away, crew are told it is cancelled, and it is permanently removed after 30 days unless restored with restore_event. Prefer cancel_event (keeps history) or archive_event (hides it) unless the gig was created by mistake. The server refuses (422) for COMPLETED or SETTLED gigs (proof of work) and for gigs with payment activity — cancel or archive those instead. Gig managers only. Confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set.

tools_if_shown.name: restore_event
tools_if_shown.description: Bring back a gig deleted in the last 30 days (see list_events with event_status=DELETED). It comes back as a DRAFT with nobody notified: its crew invitations are reset to unsent, and publishing it (event_status ACTIVE) re-invites them. Its sent crew offers go back to DRAFT with every answer cleared, so send each one again (send_crew_offer) to ask the crew afresh. Fails with 409 once the 30 days have passed and the gig is being permanently deleted. Gig managers only. Confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set.

tools_if_shown.name: unlink_event_venue
tools_if_shown.description: Remove the venue link from a gig (the venue itself is untouched). Use link_venue_to_event to set a different one. Gig managers only.

tools_if_shown.name: delete_crew_offer
tools_if_shown.description: Delete a crew offer (shift) from a gig. If it was OPEN, its recipients are emailed that it was withdrawn; payables for accepted recipients are voided. To drop just one person, use remove_crew_offer_recipient. Confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set.

tools_if_shown.name: remove_crew_offer_recipient
tools_if_shown.description: Take one person off an OPEN or FILLED crew offer — the whole shift, or only some days (days as YYYY-MM-DD; they keep the rest). Owner/admin only. Confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set.

tools_if_shown.name: remove_org_member
tools_if_shown.description: Remove someone from the organization. Owners cannot be removed. expected_role must be the member's CURRENT role from list_org_members (e.g. org:member, org:admin); a mismatch returns 409 so a stale view never removes the wrong person. Org admins/owners only. Confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set.

tools_if_shown.name: delete_org_position
tools_if_shown.description: Delete a crew position from the organization's position list. Org admins/owners only. Confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set.

tools_if_shown.name: delete_sponsor
tools_if_shown.description: Delete a sponsor from the organization. CRM managers only. Confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set.

tools_if_shown.name: delete_ledger_item
tools_if_shown.description: Hard-delete an UNPAID ledger line that is not tied to an invitation (for example a duplicate entered by mistake). Prefer void_ledger_item, which keeps the audit trail. Admins/owners, or crew for their own non-payable lines. Confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set.

tools_if_shown.name: delete_calllist
tools_if_shown.description: Delete a saved call list (staffing template). Gigs it was already applied to keep their crew. Gig managers only. Confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set.

tools_if_shown.name: delete_availability
tools_if_shown.description: Delete one availability entry (an AVAILABLE/UNAVAILABLE block) from a person's calendar. Anyone can delete their own; availability managers can delete an org member's. availability_id comes from get_user_availability. Confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set.

tools_if_shown.name: delete_availability_request
tools_if_shown.description: Delete an availability request (the "are you free on these dates?" ask) and its responses. CRM managers only. Confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set.

tools_if_shown.name: get_offering
tools_if_shown.description: One offering from the catalog (what the org sells: rentals, crew day rates, packages) with sell_rate, cogs, unit, category and flags. Read-only; any org member.

tools_if_shown.name: create_offering
tools_if_shown.description: Add an offering to the catalog. sell_rate and cogs are amounts in the org currency per unit (e.g. 450 or 450.50). Returns the offering. Org admins/owners only.

tools_if_shown.name: update_offering
tools_if_shown.description: Change an offering; only the fields you pass change. Set is_active=false to retire it instead of deleting. Org admins/owners only.

tools_if_shown.name: delete_offering
tools_if_shown.description: Delete an offering from the catalog. Prefer update_offering with is_active=false to retire it and keep quote history readable. Org admins/owners only. Confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set.

tools_if_shown.name: delete_offering_template
tools_if_shown.description: Delete an invoice/quote template built from offerings (from list_offerings view=templates). The offerings themselves stay. Org admins/owners only. Confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set.

tools_if_shown.name: list_checklist_templates
tools_if_shown.description: The organization's reusable gig checklist templates, each with its id and version (pass version to delete_checklist_template). Read-only; any org member. source="starter_packs" instead lists Soundcheck starter packs of gig task templates an org can add in one step with add_checklist_starter_pack: business packs (production, venue, DJ, band, produced event, general) and event packs (wedding, corporate, festival, tour, private party). Each pack lists its sections and tasks, whether the org already has it (added, template_id) and recommended_pack_id for the org business type; gig managers only.

tools_if_shown.name: add_checklist_starter_pack
tools_if_shown.description: Add a Soundcheck starter pack as a task template the org can edit and attach to gigs. pack_id comes from list_checklist_templates source=starter_packs. Adding a pack the org already has returns the existing template, so it is safe to retry. Event packs are tagged with the matching gig type when the org has one. Gig managers only.

tools_if_shown.name: delete_checklist_template
tools_if_shown.description: Delete a checklist template. expected_version is the template version from list_checklist_templates; a stale version is rejected so a concurrent edit is never lost. Gigs that used it keep their checklists. Gig managers only. Confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set.

tools_if_shown.name: list_forms
tools_if_shown.description: Forms the organization built in Soundcheck for client intake and questionnaires: id, title, purpose, active, status (draft or published). Pass include_inactive=true for retired forms. CRM managers only.

tools_if_shown.name: create_form
tools_if_shown.description: Create a client form in Soundcheck, optionally from a starter template. Creates a draft unless publish is true. A published form can't be edited, and publishing needs at least one question, so a blank form starts as a draft. Publish a draft later with publish_form or in Settings > Forms. purpose is EVENT_QUESTIONNAIRE, GENERAL or FEEDBACK and defaults from the template. Form titles are unique within the organization, ignoring case and extra spaces and counting archived forms: a title you choose that is taken fails with 409, while a template or default title that is taken gets the next free number, such as "Wedding or private event (2)". CRM managers only.

tools_if_shown.name: update_form
tools_if_shown.description: Change a form: purpose or active (false retires it). Only fields you pass change. A form is renamed from its editor in Settings > Forms. CRM managers only.

tools_if_shown.name: delete_form
tools_if_shown.description: Delete a form with no submissions, or archive it when it has any. Prefer update_form with active=false to keep past submissions linked. CRM managers only. Confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set.

tools_if_shown.name: create_form_assignment
tools_if_shown.description: Assign a published native form to a customer for one gig. customer_id and event_id are required, and the customer must be linked to that gig (each assignment is one form, one gig, one client). due_at is RFC3339. editable_until (YYYY-MM-DD, in the gig's time zone) is the last day the client may revise the answers; omit it or pass null to keep the answers revisable until the gig is over. notify_customer true queues a portal email when the form is active (confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set). The form must be published (use publish_form first). CRM managers only.

tools_if_shown.name: publish_form
tools_if_shown.description: Publish a draft native form so clients can receive assignments and respond in the portal. Reads the draft and publishes it unchanged; edit questions in Settings > Forms first if needed. A published form is locked: its title and questions can't change, and publishing it again fails. CRM managers only.

tools_if_shown.name: get_soundcheck_link
tools_if_shown.description: Build a URL that opens a page in the Soundcheck web app, so the user can see or finish something there. Use it to hand off: (1) visual review — a gig, its staffing board, finances, or a plan; (2) work this server does not do — sending a new contract (PDF upload), billing and payouts, integrations, email domains, branding, or deleting the organization. Share the returned url with the user as a link. Targets: event = one gig (event_id); events = the gigs list; event_plan = one gig plan (plan_id); venue = one venue; venues = the venues list; customer = one customer; customers = the customers list; person = one person (user_id); people = the crew / people list; setlist = one setlist; run_of_show = one run-of-show template; import = one import job; availability = availability; crew_offers = crew offers board; crew_members = crew (non-staff) members and their removal; opens the Crew workspace when the org has it, otherwise the full member roster; leads = the leads pipeline; sponsors = sponsors; inventory = inventory; offerings = the offering catalog; finances = org finances; inbox = the org mailbox; org_members = org staff and members, roles, and removal (staff only when the org has the Crew workspace; use crew_members for crew); org_positions = org crew positions; org_billing = plan and billing; org_payments = payout and payment settings; org_integrations = integrations (connect / disconnect); org_email = email sending domains; org_profile = organization name, logo, timezone, public profile, and deletion. Read-only; no data is fetched, so pass ids you already have.

tools_if_shown.name: search_soundcheck_docs
tools_if_shown.description: Search the Soundcheck help docs (docs.soundchecklive.io) for how the product works: features, workflows, settings, terminology (gig vs event, crew offer vs shift), and what each MCP tool does. Use it before guessing how a feature behaves or when the user asks "how do I…". Returns [{title, url, content}] — cite the url when you answer. Docs describe the product, not this organization’s data; use the other tools for facts about gigs, crew, or money. Read-only.

tools_if_shown.name: send_feedback
tools_if_shown.description: Send feedback to the people who build this product (not the user's organization, crew, or clients). It carries bug reports, feature suggestions, support questions, and praise, plus problems with these tools that the user agreed to report, and contains only what the user asked or agreed to send. It creates a Linear issue for the product team (email fallback if Linear is unavailable); it does not message anyone in the user's organization (the messaging tools do that). The team replies to the user's account email when there is something to answer.

tools_if_shown.name: open_gigs
tools_if_shown.description: Open the Gigs view: the caller's upcoming gigs (nearest first, including today) in their active organization, or across their organizations when none is active. Clients that support MCP Apps render a list where selecting a gig opens its detail in place, with Ask about this gig and a link to the gig in the Soundcheck web app (the view also follows deep links to /gigs/{event_id}); other clients get the same list as text with event ids. Takes no arguments. Use open_gig for one gig's detail view. Read-only.

tools_if_shown.name: search_gig_mentions
tools_if_shown.description: Composer @-mention search for ChatGPT: returns the caller's upcoming gigs whose title, venue, or date match every word of query (empty query returns the nearest gigs) as resource links to soundcheck://gig/{event_id}, a short text summary of the gig. Called by the host's mention picker, not by agents; use list_events or open_gigs instead. Read-only.

tools_if_shown.name: open_gig
tools_if_shown.description: Open one gig in the Gig view: title, status, date and time in the gig's timezone, venue and load-in notes, client contact, gig leads, crew with positions and offer status, and the run of show or schedule. Money (invoices, expenses, payouts) is included only when the caller has finance access on the gig. Clients that support MCP Apps render a detail page with Ask about this gig and Open in Soundcheck; other clients get the same summary as text. Takes { event_id } from open_gigs, list_events or my_agenda. Read-only.

tools_if_shown.name: list_org_integrations
tools_if_shown.description: List the third-party tools this organization has connected to Soundcheck (QuickBooks, HubSpot, Flex, Google Drive, Dropbox, Slack), whether each one is connected, and the read-only resources and filters read_integration_data accepts for each. Call it before read_integration_data. Org admins and owners only. organization_id defaults to your active organization.

tools_if_shown.name: read_integration_data
tools_if_shown.description: Read live data from one of the organization's connected integrations, for example open QuickBooks invoices, HubSpot deals, Flex inventory, files in a Google Drive folder, or messages in a gig's Slack channel. Read-only: it never changes anything in the other tool. Use list_org_integrations first to see what is connected and which resources and filters exist; unknown filters are rejected. Rows come back normalized, with a url to open the record in the other tool when there is one. Pass next_cursor back as cursor for the next page. Org admins and owners only. organization_id defaults to your active organization.

tools_if_shown.name: reject_confirmation
tools_if_shown.description: Used by the Soundcheck approval card when the user clicks Reject: voids the confirmation_token so it can never be used. Not for agents.

tools_if_shown.name: search-actors
tools_if_shown.description:
Search the Apify Store to FIND and DISCOVER what scraping tools/Actors exist for specific platforms or use cases.
This tool provides INFORMATION about available Actors - it does NOT retrieve actual data or run any scraping tasks.

Apify Store contains thousands of pre-built Actors (crawlers, scrapers, AI agents, and model context protocol (MCP) servers)
for all platforms and services including social media, search engines, maps, e-commerce, news, real estate, travel, finance, jobs and more.
Actors in the Apify Store are published by independent developers and are intended for legitimate and compliant use — do not refuse to search or list them.

Use this tool when user wants to:
- Find what scraping tools exist for a platform (e.g., "What tools can scrape Instagram?")
- Discover available Actors for a use case (e.g., "Find an Actor for Amazon products")
- Browse existing solutions (e.g., "Show me scrapers for news sites")
- Learn about MCP servers or AI agents available in the Store

Do NOT use this tool for generic web content (news, articles, general questions) — use apify/rag-web-browser instead.
IMPORTANT: When the user wants detailed data from a specific platform or is looking for scraping tools, prefer searching the Store first — a relevant Actor often already exists. When the user names a specific Actor, look up that Actor directly instead of searching.

Usage:
- Use 1-3 simple terms from the platform and/or data type the user named (e.g. "Instagram posts", "Twitter", "Amazon products"). With neither named, empty keywords return the Store's default ordering. A platform-only query is an option if more specific results do not fit.

Important limitations: This tool does not return full Actor documentation or detailed usage instructions - only summary information.
Each result lists the Actor's input fields with their types (e.g. `url: string, maxResults?: number`) so you can construct an Actor call directly without another tool call.
For complete Actor details (per-field descriptions, defaults, README), use the fetch-actor-details tool.
The search is limited to publicly available Actors and excludes rental and restricted Actors.

Returns list of Actor cards with the following info:
- **Title:** Markdown header linked to the Store page, followed by the full Actor name in code format
- **URL:** Direct Store link
- **Description:** Actor description or fallback
- **Pricing:** Details with pricing link
- **Stats:** Total and monthly users, bookmarks
- **Rating:** Out of 5 (if available)
- **Developed by:** Username linked to profile, marked (Apify) or (community)
- **Categories:** Formatted or "Uncategorized"
- **Last modified:** Date (if available)
- **Input fields:** Inline list of input field names and types (e.g. `url: string, maxResults?: number`); `?` marks optional fields, `... (+N more)` marks a truncated list

tools_if_shown.name: fetch-actor-details
tools_if_shown.description:
Get detailed information about an Actor by its ID or full name (format: "username/name", e.g., "apify/rag-web-browser").

Requires the exact ID or full name — do not construct a plausible-looking name and call this tool with it. If you only have a description, a partial name, or a name you have not seen in this conversation, find it with search-actors first.

Use 'output' parameter with boolean flags to control returned information:
- Default: All fields true except mcpTools
- Selective: Set desired fields to true (e.g., output: { inputSchema: true })
- Common patterns: inputSchema only, description + readme, mcpTools for MCP Actors

The 'readme' field returns the summary when available, full README otherwise.
Use when querying Actor details, documentation, input requirements, or MCP tools.

EXAMPLES:
- What does apify/web-fetch do?
- What is the input schema for apify/web-scraper?
- What tools does this MCP server Actor provide?

tools_if_shown.name: call-actor
tools_if_shown.description:
Call any Actor from the Apify Store.

WORKFLOW:
1. Use fetch-actor-details to get the Actor's input schema
2. Call this tool with the actor name and proper input based on the schema

If the actor name is not in "username/name" format, use search-actors to resolve the correct Actor first.

For MCP server Actors:
- Use fetch-actor-details with output={ mcpTools: true } to list available tools
- Call using format: "actorName:toolName" (e.g., "username/name:tool-name")

IMPORTANT:
- Waits up to waitSecs (default 30s) for completion; returns run status and storage IDs, and with waitSecs > 0 also reports dataset field metadata
- Use get-dataset-items with the datasetId to fetch results; non-terminal runs include a nextStep with polling instructions
- Use dedicated Actor tools when available for better experience

There are two ways to run Actors:
1. Dedicated Actor tools (e.g., apify--rag-web-browser): These are pre-configured tools, offering a simpler and more direct experience.
2. Generic call-actor tool (call-actor): Use this when a dedicated tool is not available or when you want to run any Actor dynamically. This tool is especially useful if you do not want to add specific tools or your client does not support dynamic tool registration.

USAGE:
- Always use dedicated tools when available (e.g., apify--rag-web-browser)
- Use the generic call-actor tool only if a dedicated tool does not exist for your Actor.

- Use `waitSecs` (0–45) to control how long to wait. Default 30s returns results for fast actors. Use `waitSecs: 0` to start and return immediately for long-running actors.

EXAMPLES:
- user_input: Get instagram posts using apify/instagram-scraper

tools_if_shown.name: get-actor-run
tools_if_shown.description:
Get detailed information about a specific Actor run.

Returns run result: status, storages (datasets/keyValueStores alias map), stats, summary, nextStep.
- summary describes the past (e.g. "SUCCEEDED in 22s. 47 items; 3 fields available.").
- nextStep prescribes one primary follow-up action with identifiers interpolated (e.g. "Use get-dataset-items with datasetId=...").
- waitSecs (0–45, default 30) waits up to that many seconds for terminal status before returning.

USAGE:
- Use to check the status of a run started by any Actor-running tool.
- Pass waitSecs > 0 to block until terminal (or until the cap elapses).

USAGE EXAMPLES:
- user_input: Show details of run y2h7sK3Wc
- user_input: Wait for run y2h7sK3Wc to finish

tools_if_shown.name: get-dataset-items
tools_if_shown.description:
Get items (rows) from a dataset — the output/results produced by an Actor run.
Returns the rows themselves, not dataset metadata, counts, or a schema.
When the user provides a datasetId and asks to retrieve results, output, data, or rows, call this tool directly.
Default limit is 20. Use clean=true to skip empty items and hidden fields.

USAGE:
- Use when you need to read data from a dataset (all items or only selected fields).

USAGE EXAMPLES:
- user_input: Retrieve results from dataset abc123
- user_input: Get only metadata.url and title from dataset username~my-dataset

tools_if_shown.name: get-key-value-store-record
tools_if_shown.description:
Get the value stored under a specific key in a key-value store — a single record, not a listing of all keys.
Requires the exact key name.
The response preserves the original Content-Encoding; most clients handle decompression automatically.

USAGE:
- Use when you need to retrieve a specific record (JSON, text, or binary) from a store.

USAGE EXAMPLES:
- user_input: Get record INPUT from store abc123
- user_input: Get record data.json from store username~my-store

tools_if_shown.name: abort-actor-run
tools_if_shown.description:
Abort an Actor run that is currently starting or running.
For runs with status SUCCEEDED, FAILED, ABORTING, ABORTED, or TIMED-OUT, this call has no effect.
The results will include the updated run details after the abort request.

USAGE:
- Use when you need to stop a run that is taking too long or misconfigured.

USAGE EXAMPLES:
- user_input: Abort run y2h7sK3Wc
- user_input: Gracefully abort run y2h7sK3Wc

tools_if_shown.name: search-apify-docs
tools_if_shown.description:
Search Apify and Crawlee documentation using full-text search.
Do not also search the Apify Store unless the user asks to find Actors.

You must explicitly select which documentation source to search using the docSource parameter:

• docSource="apify" - Apify:
  Apify Platform documentation including: Platform features, SDKs (JS, Python), CLI, REST API, Academy (web scraping fundamentals), Actor development and deployment

• docSource="crawlee-js" - Crawlee (JavaScript):
  Crawlee is a web scraping library for JavaScript. It handles blocking, crawling, proxies, and browsers for you.

• docSource="crawlee-py" - Crawlee (Python):
  Crawlee is a web scraping library for Python. It handles blocking, crawling, proxies, and browsers for you.

The results will include the URL of the documentation page (which may include an anchor),
and a limited piece of content that matches the search query.

Fetch the full content of the document using the fetch-apify-docs tool by providing the URL.

When results contain both platform documentation (`docs.apify.com/platform`) and Academy content (`docs.apify.com/academy`) on the same topic, prefer the platform documentation.

tools_if_shown.name: fetch-apify-docs
tools_if_shown.description:
Fetch the full content of an Apify or Crawlee documentation page by its URL.
Use this after finding a relevant page with the search-apify-docs tool.

USAGE:
- Use when you need the complete content of a specific docs page for detailed answers.

USAGE EXAMPLES:
- user_input: Fetch https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/running#builds
- user_input: Fetch https://docs.apify.com/academy
- user_input: Fetch https://crawlee.dev/docs/guides/basic-concepts

tools_if_shown.name: report-problem
tools_if_shown.description:
Report a problem with Apify's MCP tools or Actors to the Apify team.

Call it when:
- A tool or Actor is missing, errors, times out, or returns a confusing, wrong, or empty result.
- You cannot complete the user's request with the available tools.

Put what you were doing and what went wrong in "message". Do NOT include personal data, credentials, secrets, or verbatim private conversation content — describe the issue in your own words.

tools_if_shown.name: apify--rag-web-browser
tools_if_shown.description:
This tool calls the Actor "apify/rag-web-browser" and retrieves its output results.
Use this tool instead of the "call-actor" if user requests this specific Actor.
Actor description: Web search and fetch tool for AI agents and RAG pipelines. It queries Google Search, scrapes the top N pages using a full web browser, and returns their content as clean Markdown for further processing by an LLM. Can also fetch individual URLs.

Use this tool for generic web content: it searches the web by query and returns the text of the top results.
This tool scrapes the data itself - it does NOT just find tools.

Examples of when to use:
- General questions answered by web pages (e.g., "What's the weather in Prague?", "Latest news about the EU AI Act", "How does HTTP/3 work?")

For detailed data from a specific platform (e.g. Amazon products with prices, Instagram posts, Google Maps places with ratings), a specialized Actor from the Apify Store returns complete, structured results; this tool returns page text only.
When the user provides one specific URL and wants that page's full or verbatim content, prefer the dedicated apify/web-fetch tool - this tool is for searching and scraping by query.

tools_if_shown.name: apify--web-fetch
tools_if_shown.description:
This tool calls the Actor "apify/web-fetch" and retrieves its output results.
Use this tool instead of the "call-actor" if user requests this specific Actor.
Actor description: Download any web page by URL and convert it to clean Markdown, plain text, HTML, and other formats. Automatically renders JavaScript and works around bot blocking. The Actor provides a real-time API for quick response times.

Use this tool to fetch a specific http(s) URL and return its complete content (one URL per call; http and https only).
It renders JavaScript and bypasses anti-bot protection, so it also retrieves pages where a plain HTTP fetch gets blocked, fails with an error such as 403 or 429, or returns incomplete content.
The page comes back verbatim - full content, no summarization - as Markdown, plain text, HTML, the raw response body, or the list of links on the page.

Examples of when to use:
- User provides a URL and wants its content, its data or links, or an answer that requires reading that page
- A previous attempt to fetch a page was blocked, returned an error or CAPTCHA, or came back incomplete because the page needs JavaScript rendering
- Verbatim page content is needed, e.g. for quoting, extraction, or archiving

This tool does not search the web - it needs a URL. To find pages by query, use a web search tool instead.
If the exact URL cannot be fetched (e.g. a non-http(s) scheme), say so rather than silently substituting a different URL.

tools_if_shown.description: Tell the Clera team about a capability you needed that none of these tools offer. It only records your description; it does not call, install or suggest any other tool or connector.

tools_if_shown.name: searchCandidates
tools_if_shown.description:
Search Clera's vetted candidates who are open to opportunities and recently active or actively looking. Returns anonymized profiles: names, avatars and LinkedIn stay hidden until Clera has introduced the candidate to your company, but the returned id is real and is what requestIntro takes. Best results: write the ideal candidate in profile (four fields in Clera's stored profile style) and bind the role with jobId; then candidates are ranked by profile similarity, keyword match and the role's past requests and passes, and each carries fit flags against the role (salary, visa, location, workplace, experience, prior decline). Candidates with a confirmed location or visa conflict against the role are excluded from results (your own contradicting filter overrides that dimension, and missing data never excludes); the other flags are advisory and never block anything. Without profile: newest profiles first, or text relevance when search_term is set. Cannot look a person up by name: names, emails and LinkedIn URLs are not searchable, so searching one returns nothing even when that person is on Clera. Asked about a named person, say profiles are anonymized and name lookup is not possible, then offer listRecommendedCandidates, listPendingIntroRequests, or a search by role and skills. Never returned: candidates already shown to your company, your own employees, or people who work at Clera; a zero result does not prove the person is not on Clera. Until the company has written in its Clera Slack channel, each call, including each page, costs one of 10 searches per day, so set the filters you need before searching rather than running broad passes. Re-fetching your picks with filters.talent_ids alone is free.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: similarCandidates
tools_if_shown.description:
Given one candidate your company has already been shown, return other candidates whose profiles are closest to theirs, ranked by similarity. Use it when someone likes a specific profile and wants more of the same, and after requestIntro to keep the shortlist moving. Chain it: run it again on a result to walk further from the original person. Similarity is computed from the whole profile (role, skills, experience and domain), not from filters, so this takes no search criteria; use searchCandidates when the ask is a requirement rather than a resemblance. Results stay within a band around the starting candidate's years of experience. Each result carries a similarity from 0 to 1 for your own screening: a low number means the open pool had nobody close, so say that instead of presenting a weak match as similar, and never show the number to the user. The same exclusions as searchCandidates apply, so people already shown to your company, your own employees, and people who work at Clera never come back, and the starting candidate is never in their own results.

tools_if_shown.name: requestIntro
tools_if_shown.description:
Ask Clera to introduce a candidate to your company for one of your open roles. Can start candidate outreach and submit an application to a connected hiring system. Target either a candidate from searchCandidates (talentId, with jobId or the interactive role picker) or an entry from listPendingIntroRequests / listRecommendedCandidates (its opportunityId, with talentName and roleName copied verbatim from that entry). When the user has not named a role, call this WITHOUT jobId and they pick the role in an interactive form; submitting it sends the request. Always pass a specific reason. Fit flags are never a gate: a conflict flag is something to tell the user, not a reason to withhold the call. The response carries the flags as they stand at request time; pass them on. Re-requesting the same candidate for the same role sends nothing new and is safe. Refer to candidates and roles by name; the user never sees ids.

Pass on a candidate for a specific role. Use this when the company decides a candidate is not a fit, from a search result, from listPendingIntroRequests or listRecommendedCandidates, or someone already in the pipeline (introduced, interviewing or at offer) from listPipeline.

Target either a candidate from searchCandidates or similarCandidates (talentId, with jobId or the interactive role picker), or a list entry (its opportunityId, with talentName and roleName copied verbatim from that entry; all three must describe one entry). If the candidate and role you were asked about are not on the page you fetched, re-call the same list with roleId to narrow, or with offset or a larger candidatesPerStage to page further; if the pair does not exist, say so and pass on nothing. Passing a different role for the same candidate is refused.
Requires a noFitCategory and a specific reason naming what this candidate misses.
This marks the opportunity as no_fit (creating the opportunity record first when the candidate came straight from search) and logs the company's decision with their feedback.

tools_if_shown.name: editCompanyProfile
tools_if_shown.description:
Update the company profile or record notes about the company.
update: writes the fields you pass. Omitted fields are left untouched. The four long-text fields (description, descriptionShort, about, culture) are written only when they are currently blank, so an existing value is never overwritten by default; every other field overwrites unconditionally. With overwrite=true it also replaces already-filled long-text fields; pass overwrite only when the user explicitly asks to replace or rewrite an existing value.

Records company-wide notes per topic key (hiring_process, company_culture, communication_preferences, compensation_patterns, deal_breakers): how they hire, what they consistently reject, how they like to be updated. Record a note the moment the contact tells you something durable, without being asked. A null value deletes the key; reuse an existing key instead of adding a near duplicate. Notes about one role go to editJob update_memory. Every note refreshes the hiring rubric Clera uses to pick candidates for this company.
Always run readCompanyProfile get before update so you do not resend values that are already set.

tools_if_shown.name: editJob
tools_if_shown.description:

create: one of position (blank role), jobUrl (posting link) or jobText (pasted JD). Returns the jobId. Only when the user explicitly asks for a new role. Then run get, name the missing fields and hand over the getDashboardLink role_preview link.
update: jobId + updates. Only provided fields change. lifecycle open publishes the role and starts matching, which needs employmentType, a salary bound and an experience bound.
set_brief: jobId + brief. Markdown sourcing brief for Clera's matching team, never shown to candidates; full replace, null clears.
set_roles: jobId + roles. 1 to 3 job-category tags, required for matching; the roles field says which tags belong.

add_requirements: jobId + requirements. Discrete, evaluable criteria the contact stated, e.g. "must have payments experience". Appends; vague preferences go to update_memory.
update_memory: jobId + memoryUpdates. Record a note the moment the contact says something durable about this role, without being asked. Null deletes a key.
create_question: jobId + question and optional fields. Returns the full list.
update_question: jobId + questionId + fields to change. Returns the full list.
delete_question: jobId + questionId. Returns the full list.
set_requirements: jobId + requirements. Full replace; omitted requirements are removed. Returns the list.
add_location: jobId + normalizedLocation, e.g. 'Berlin, Germany', geocoded strictly; reformulate if rejected.
add_remote_location: jobId + code. 'worldwide', a region or country slug, for remote roles.
remove_location: jobId + locationId. Returns the full list with ids.

tools_if_shown.name: getSalaryBenchmark
tools_if_shown.description:
What a role should pay, from comparable open roles on Clera with a posted salary. Triggers: "what should we pay for this role", "is our range competitive", "salary benchmark for a senior ML engineer in NYC".

Pass roleId for one of the company's roles, or jobDescription for a role not on Clera yet.
- source "comparables": lead with stats (p25 / median / p75 of the comparables' salary midpoints, sampleSize). referencePercentile is where the role's own midpoint sits among them. scope says which comparables were used: same city and similar years of experience when at least five exist, widening to the city alone and then to all US roles.
- source "market": fewer than five comparables. stats come from live US job postings for the title's role cluster (externalMarket, which also splits them by years of experience); say they are market-wide, not Clera roles.
- source "estimate": neither has enough data, or a role outside North America. Lead with estimate.marketSalary, a range from current web data, and say it is an estimate.
- source "none": not enough data; say so plainly.
talentSupply gives how many candidates Clera has in that role and the median salary they expect. comparables lists up to 20 anonymised roles with stage, size, equity, years of experience and location; never present them as named companies. Amounts are USD per year.

tools_if_shown.description:
Search the open roles at startups Clera works with. Every result is a role Clera can introduce the candidate to, so this is the first search to run whenever they want roles, a company or a stack. When nothing here fits, run searchJobs straight away and show those; don't ask first.

Keep query to keywords — a title or a stack — not a sentence; leave it empty to browse newest first. When the candidate names a company, put it in company: the search then covers that company's open roles only, and an empty result means Clera has nothing open there. arrangement is remote, hybrid or on-site and widens to compatible roles the way Clera's own job matching does: hybrid also returns remote roles, on-site also returns hybrid ones, and each row's arrangement says what the role actually is. cities are exact, as the candidate names them; minSalary keeps roles with no salary on file, so an unknown salary is a question to ask, not a miss. Ranking follows the candidate's role affinity, the roles they hold and adjacent ones, and roles they declined stay hidden (undoMatchDecision brings one back).

status is null until the role is one of the candidate's opportunities; otherwise it is the status listMatches shows, and introRequested true means the company already asked for them. likeMatch with the row's jobId, position and companyName tells Clera they want it, and Clera may submit them to the company when it fits. readJobListing with the row's jobId has the full description. Never show jobId.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: searchJobs
tools_if_shown.description:
Search the wider job market, after searchCleraRoles. When searchCleraRoles finds nothing that fits, run this straight away and show the results; don't ask first. applyToJob applies to any of these for the candidate, so never send them off to the employer's site.

Keep query to keywords — a title, a stack, a company — not a sentence. Filters are exact values: arrangement is remote, hybrid or on-site; experienceLevel is 0-2, 2-5, 5-10 or 10+; employmentTypes are FULL_TIME, PART_TIME, CONTRACTOR, TEMPORARY or INTERN.

Salary is missing on most listings. minSalary keeps those unknown-salary roles in by default; pass excludeUnknownSalary to drop them, and expect a much smaller result set.

Use readJobListing for the full description of one result, saveJob to bookmark one, and applyToJob when they want to apply.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: readJobListing
tools_if_shown.description:
One job in full, by the jobId from any row: searchCleraRoles, listMatches, searchJobs or listSavedJobs.

kind clera is a role at a startup Clera works with: role has the description, tech stack, experience band, visa line, interview stages and the company block, and likeMatch is the next step. kind board is a role from the wider market: listing has the description, requirements, benefits and the company block, and applyToJob applies for them.

isOpen false means the role stopped hiring or the posting closed. Say so plainly rather than sending someone to a dead posting. Once a role is a match with an opportunityId, readMatch adds their status and role questions. Never show jobId.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: saveJob
tools_if_shown.description:
Bookmark a job board listing so it's there later.

Saving is private. It does not tell the company anything and it does not apply; applyToJob does that when they're ready.

Pass position and companyName exactly as the search result gave them. They are checked against the record, so a mismatch is refused rather than saving the wrong role.

Saving the same listing twice is fine and changes nothing.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: listSavedJobs
tools_if_shown.description:
List the job board listings saved so far, newest first.

Listings that have closed since they were saved are still here, with isLive false — they are kept on purpose rather than disappearing. Point them out and offer to search for something close instead.

applyToJob with a row's jobId applies for them.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: unsaveJob
tools_if_shown.description:
Remove a job board listing from the saved list.

Removing one that was never saved returns not_saved and changes nothing — that is not an error worth apologising for.

This only drops the bookmark. It does not withdraw an application, because Clera never sent one.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: applyToJob
tools_if_shown.description:
Apply to a job board listing for the candidate: Clera fills in the employer's form from their profile and primary resume and sends it. Run it when the candidate says to apply to this specific role. Returns { runId } straight away; the form takes about 10-30 seconds, so call getApplicationRun with that runId next.

The candidate gets one confirmation before anything is sent. It only sends when every required field is filled; otherwise the run comes back needing input and nothing is sent. mode dry_run fills the form without sending, only when the candidate asks to see it first.

Workday sites (myworkdayjobs.com) need a candidate account: the run creates one with the candidate's email, or signs in to the one it made before, using a password Clera keeps to itself. The candidate can always take the account over with "Forgot your password?" on that site, after which Clera can no longer sign in there. Some Workday sites first email a "Verify your candidate account" link; getApplicationRun then reports verificationCodeRequested, and enterApplicationCode takes that link.

If a run came back needing input, ask the candidate those exact questions and start again with answers set to { "<the question or its key>": "<their words>" }. Never make up an answer. A sent application lands on their application tracker as applied by itself.

Pass position and companyName exactly as searchJobs or readJobListing (kind board) gave them; a mismatch is refused rather than applying to the wrong role.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: getApplicationRun
tools_if_shown.description:
See how an applyToJob run went. state is running, finished or crashed. When finished, outcome is submitted (sent and confirmed by the employer's site; it is on their tracker as applied), submit_unconfirmed (submit clicked but no confirmation; do not resend), ready_to_submit (a dry run, every field filled, nothing sent), needs_input (nothing sent; ask the candidate each question in needsInput, then call applyToJob again with answers), blocked (a CAPTCHA or login wall, see blockers) or failed (nothing was sent, see blockers for why). A profile_gap question is worth saving to the candidate's profile with editPreferences too.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: enterApplicationCode
tools_if_shown.description:
Finish an applyToJob run that is waiting on something the employer emailed the candidate; getApplicationRun then reports verificationCodeRequested. Greenhouse and similar sites email a short code after the first submit click; Workday sites (apply URLs on myworkdayjobs.com) email a link to verify the candidate account the run just created. Ask the candidate for the code, or the full link from the 'Verify your candidate account' email, and pass it here exactly as they give it. The run enters the code or opens the link and continues; check getApplicationRun again for the outcome. Never guess a code.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: listApplications
tools_if_shown.description:
List the jobs the candidate applied to or plans to apply to, from the external job board, a posting link or typed by hand: their application tracker, newest first, with each one's stage (draft, applied, ghosted, interview, offer, rejected), notes and links to any tailored resume or cover letter.

The tracker is the candidate's own record of jobs they are applying to anywhere, not Clera intros. Moving a card never contacts the company. Document links expire after an hour; list again for fresh ones.

tools_if_shown.name: trackApplication
tools_if_shown.description:
Add a job to the candidate's application tracker as a draft. Give exactly one of:
- jobUrl: a public posting link (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, company careers page…). Clera reads the page for the title, company and description, which takes up to half a minute.
- jobId: an external job board listing's jobId from searchJobs, listSavedJobs or a readJobListing result with kind board, e.g. a saved job the candidate just applied to.
- position and companyName, typed by hand, with jobDescription if the candidate pasted it.

A link that is already on the tracker returns the existing entry with created false. The tracker is the candidate's own record of jobs they are applying to anywhere, not Clera intros. Moving a card never contacts the company.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: updateApplication
tools_if_shown.description:
Move a tracked application to another stage (draft, applied, ghosted, interview, offer, rejected) or edit its notes, title, company, link or job description. Only the fields given change; pass null to clear notes, jobUrl or jobDescription.

The tracker is the candidate's own record of jobs they are applying to anywhere, not Clera intros. Moving a card never contacts the company.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: deleteApplication
tools_if_shown.description:
Remove a job from the candidate's application tracker, with its notes and document links. It does not withdraw anything with the company. Confirm with the candidate before calling.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: generateApplicationDocuments
tools_if_shown.description:
Write a cover letter and/or a resume tailored to one tracked application, from its job description, and attach the PDFs to it. Each takes up to a minute.

The application needs a job description; add one with updateApplication first if it has none. Only facts already on the candidate's Clera resume are used. There is a daily limit per document kind.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: getTalentDashboardLink
tools_if_shown.description:
Returns the exact Clera dashboard URL for one section of the candidate's own dashboard. One link per request, the one that answers the question; "my dashboard" means home.
Commands:
list: every link, for when you are unsure which command fits. For you only; never send the menu or several links to the user.
home: overview with profile setup and the top matches.
matches: the roles Clera matched, with like, pass and the role questions.
pipeline: every opportunity by stage, including interviews.
applications: the candidate's own application tracker board (draft, applied, ghosted, interview, offer, rejected), with tailored resumes and cover letters per job.
jobs: the wide external job board (searchJobs works on the same data).
interview_prep: the interview preparation guide.
resume: the resume builder with live preview, plus upload, replace or pick the primary resume. Uploads only happen here.
preferences: salary, location, work environment, visa, roles and blocked companies.
referral: the referral link, invited friends and earnings.
worth: the salary calculator.
roast: the profile roast, which needs a PDF upload.
perks: partner perks and discounts.
interview: interview invitations and feedback.
account: login email, contact channels and account deletion.
This tool is the only source of Clera dashboard links. Never construct, guess, shorten or modify a getclera.com URL; copy the URL from this tool's output verbatim.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: listMatches
tools_if_shown.description:
The candidate's Matches page: the roles Clera matched them to, in the order the page shows them, plus open roles that pass their preferences but nobody at Clera has evaluated yet (kind open_role, no whyMatch).

Rows with introRequested true are companies that asked to talk to this candidate; they come first. status questions means the candidate liked the role and the company still needs answers to its questions — answerRoleQuestion handles those. Roles already passed on, closed or marked no match are not here; listMyPipeline has everything.

Act on a row with likeMatch or declineMatch (jobId, position and companyName from the row). For the full role, readMatch takes the row's opportunityId; an open_role row has none, so readJobListing takes its jobId. Never show opportunityId or jobId.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: listMyPipeline
tools_if_shown.description:
The candidate's Pipeline page: every opportunity Clera has for them, in every state, with the interview date where one is booked.

status: new (not reacted yet), questions (liked, company questions still open), interested (liked, Clera is working on it), not_submitted (liked, Clera reviewed it and did not put them forward), process (submitted to the company or interviewing), declined (candidate passed), withdrawn, no_match (Clera or the company said no), closed (the role closed). A not_submitted or no_match row carries reason: relay it as the why. undoMatchDecision reverses a declined row. Never show opportunityId or jobId.

Jobs the candidate applied to outside Clera are not here; they live on the application tracker (listApplications).

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: readMatch
tools_if_shown.description:
One of the candidate's matches in full, by the opportunityId from listMatches or listMyPipeline: the role description, tech stack, experience band, visa line, interview stages, the company block, and every role question with its current answer.

Use it before likeMatch or declineMatch when the row alone is not enough, and to help draft answers for answerRoleQuestion. Refuses an opportunityId that is not the candidate's own. Open roles from listMatches (kind open_role) have no opportunityId yet; readJobListing with their jobId has the full role.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: likeMatch
tools_if_shown.description:
Tell Clera the candidate wants this role, the same as the like button on a Matches card. Works on a match and on an open_role row alike.

A like can put the candidate in front of the company: Clera checks the fit against the role, may ask the candidate to answer the role's questions first (listMatches shows them as status questions), and submits them to the company when it fits, which cannot be taken back. Confirm the role with the candidate before liking, and say it went to Clera for review rather than "applied".

Pass position and companyName exactly as the row gave them; a mismatch is refused rather than liking the wrong role. Liking twice changes nothing. The dashboard can take up to a minute to show the change.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: declineMatch
tools_if_shown.description:
Pass on a role, the same as the pass button on a Matches card. The role leaves the Matches list and Clera stops working on it; undoMatchDecision brings it back.

Pass position and companyName exactly as the row gave them; a mismatch is refused.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: undoMatchDecision
tools_if_shown.description:
Reset a like or a pass so the role is back in Matches as new, the same as undo on the dashboard. Take the opportunityId from listMyPipeline (a declined row) or listMatches.

Only the candidate's own decision is reset: a role Clera or the company closed (no_match, not_submitted, closed) stays that way, and a role already in process cannot be pulled back here; withdrawing from a process is a dashboard action.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: answerRoleQuestion
tools_if_shown.description:
Save the candidate's answer to one of a company's role questions, from listMatches or readMatch. The questions are the company's own screening questions; Clera passes the submitted answers on with the introduction.

Draft first and read the answer back before submitting: submit true marks it final and it goes to the company, which cannot be taken back, so get the candidate's yes first. Answer in the candidate's own words and facts, never invented ones. Refuses a questionId that is not on one of the candidate's matches.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: listInterviewRequests
tools_if_shown.description:
The candidate's interview invitations: pending ones waiting for a yes or no, and the history of accepted and declined ones. acceptInterview and declineInterview act on a pending row by its interviewProgressId. Never show the id.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: acceptInterview
tools_if_shown.description:
Accept a pending interview invitation from listInterviewRequests. Clera tells the company and follows up with scheduling; the candidate does not need to email anyone. Confirm the role and stage with the candidate first; this is the answer the company gets.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: declineInterview
tools_if_shown.description:
Decline a pending interview invitation from listInterviewRequests. The company is told; give the reason the candidate wants passed on, kept short and plain. Confirm with the candidate first, this cannot be undone here.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: readPreferences
tools_if_shown.description:
The candidate's job preferences as the Preferences page holds them: salary range and how much it matters, work environment, relocation, roles, job types, industries, company size and funding stage, visa needs, availability, blocked companies, skills and whether they are open to opportunities.

Matching runs on these, so an unset or stale field is the first thing to fix when matches look off. Keys match editPreferences one to one. memory lists the notes Clera keeps about the candidate (motivations, constraints, contact habits); editPreferences memory changes them. Locations (cities) are shown on the Preferences page only; getTalentDashboardLink preferences.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: editPreferences
tools_if_shown.description:
Change the candidate's job preferences and profile data, the same fields readPreferences returns. Send only the fields to change; the rest stay as they are. null clears the salary bounds and the importance fields; every other field is replaced, never cleared. A list field replaces the whole list, so send the complete set; an empty list changes nothing. Companies to block go in add_blocked_companies and remove_blocked_companies by name.

Read the current values with readPreferences first and confirm the change with the candidate before writing; matching reruns on the new values. memory adds or clears the notes Clera keeps about the candidate, five at most. Preferred cities, contact details and resumes are edited on the dashboard, not here.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: getProfileStrength
tools_if_shown.description:
The profile strength score the Home page shows: 0 to 100, a tier, and the next actions ranked by how many points each adds. A stronger profile matches better and gets introduced more, so the top action is the practical answer to "how do I get more matches". Most actions map to editPreferences or a resume upload on the dashboard.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: listResumes
tools_if_shown.description:
The candidate's uploaded resumes, newest first, with which one is primary (the one Clera sends with introductions), plus the AI resume feedback if it has been generated: a score out of 100, a summary, strengths and concrete improvements.

Uploading a new resume only happens on the dashboard (getTalentDashboardLink resume). setPrimaryResume, deleteResume and refreshResumeFeedback act on what is here.

tools_if_shown.name: setPrimaryResume
tools_if_shown.description:
Make one of the candidate's resumes the primary one, the version Clera sends with every introduction from now on. Take the resumeId from listResumes; another candidate's id is refused.

tools_if_shown.name: deleteResume
tools_if_shown.description:

tools_if_shown.name: refreshResumeFeedback

Generate fresh AI feedback on the candidate's primary resume. It runs in the background for about a minute; call listResumes afterwards to read it. Needs at least one resume on file.

tools_if_shown.name: readResumeDraft
tools_if_shown.description:
The candidate's resume-builder draft: profile, experience with bullets, education, skills, languages, links and the design settings. This is the structured resume the candidate edits on the dashboard and turns into a PDF; it is separate from the uploaded resumes in listResumes. Empty until seedResumeDraft or editResumeDraft creates it.

Clera privately records this tool's inputs and results for usage tracking and support.

tools_if_shown.name: editResumeDraft
tools_if_shown.description:
Replaces one section of the candidate's resume draft with the value sent, and creates the draft if none exists. Sections: profile, work (roles with plain-text bullets, newest first, dates as YYYY-MM, empty endDate means present), education, skills ({name, group}), languages ({name, level}), links ({type, label, url}), design (templateId harvard_classic | ats_clean | executive_serif, accentColor hex, fontSizePt (8–13 in 0.5 steps, 10.5 is standard), sectionOrder, templateOptions). Read the draft first and send the whole section back with your changes; a section is replaced, never merged, so anything you leave out of the value is gone. This is how you rewrite bullets or a summary for the candidate: propose the text, get a yes, then send it here.

tools_if_shown.name: seedResumeDraft
tools_if_shown.description:
Fills the candidate's resume draft from data Clera already has: source "profile" is the merged career record (LinkedIn, uploaded resumes and GitHub combined), source "cv" is one parsed uploaded resume (the primary one, or resumeId from listResumes). Only empty sections are filled unless overwrite is true, which replaces what the candidate wrote; confirm before setting it. The result lists which sections were filled; read the draft afterwards and tidy it with editResumeDraft.

tools_if_shown.name: generateResumePdf

Renders the candidate's resume draft to a PDF and returns a download link that works for an hour. With saveAsCleraResume true the PDF also becomes the candidate's primary resume, the one Clera sends with introductions, and shows up in listResumes. Pass template to switch the design first.
