tools_if_shown.name: get_overview_funnel
tools_if_shown.description: Two numbers for the last 30 days: crawls30d (visits from AI crawlers) and aiVisits30d (people who arrived from an AI engine). Zeros until crawler or visit data comes in.

tools_if_shown.name: get_visibility_trend
tools_if_shown.description: Your AI visibility score by day across the 6 AI engines, oldest first: date, score (percent of checks that cited you), totalChecks and cited. days picks 30, 60 or 90 (default 30). Days without checks are left out, so expect gaps between weekly checks.

tools_if_shown.name: list_citations
tools_if_shown.description: Recent AI citation checks: which tracked queries were checked on which AI model and whether the brand was cited.

tools_if_shown.name: get_web_footprint
tools_if_shown.description: How much of the web links to your domain and to each competitor you track, scored 0 to 10: your domain and score, peers (name, domain, score; highest first) and the peers' median. Null until a score exists. A new domain scoring near zero is why AI citations are still absent.

tools_if_shown.name: get_web_total_history
tools_if_shown.description: Web total history for the workspace and every competitor it tracks: each domain's monthly web total over the last 3 months, oldest month first. The web total counts citations in ChatGPT and Google answers, including queries you do not track.

tools_if_shown.name: get_visibility_score
tools_if_shown.description: Composite AI visibility score for the workspace, blending AI citation rate across the tracked models with Google and Bing rank share. Returns the composite and the score of each part: AI citations, Google and Bing (the AI part includes a per-model breakdown).

tools_if_shown.name: get_setup_progress
tools_if_shown.description: The workspace's expeditions on the Overview: the current expedition, each step's name and whether it is done, and the next step. Use it to help the user finish setting up.

tools_if_shown.name: get_citability_report
tools_if_shown.description: Published pages ranked by citability score (how extractable each page is for AI answers), worst first, each with its top open fixes. Use to decide which articles to improve.

tools_if_shown.name: get_citation_sentiment
tools_if_shown.description: How AI answers frame the brand when it's cited: positive / neutral / negative counts, daily trend, and recent answer snippets as receipts.

tools_if_shown.name: get_citation_sources
tools_if_shown.description: Which domains AI engines cite when answering the brand's tracked queries, typed brand / competitive / UGC / editorial with counts and share. Shows where citation presence must be earned.

tools_if_shown.name: get_share_of_voice
tools_if_shown.description: Share of voice vs competitors: the brand's citation rate, top competitor mention rates, and the brand's share of all brand appearances in AI answers over the window.

tools_if_shown.name: list_tracked_queries
tools_if_shown.description: The workspace's tracked queries — the questions RankControl checks weekly across the 6 AI engines for brand citations — with their status and, for each tracked query, how many of the 6 engines cited it in their latest check.

tools_if_shown.name: get_query_slots
tools_if_shown.description: How many queries you track against your plan's limit, as Query Control shows it (18/50 tracked): used and limit. At the limit, add_tracked_query needs a free slot first.

tools_if_shown.name: get_crawler_access
tools_if_shown.description: Daily AI-crawler reachability probe result — a DIAGNOSTIC, not a traffic metric: whether the site's edge (e.g. Cloudflare Bot Fight Mode) or robots.txt blocks GPTBot/ClaudeBot. 'shielded' means browsers and bots are both challenged (site-wide shield, ambiguous for real, signed crawlers).

tools_if_shown.name: get_analytics_sources
tools_if_shown.description: Per-workspace analytics source setup: the selected writer for human traffic and AI-crawler data, which sources the setup qualifies for, and install state (Cloudflare zone/sync, WordPress plugin version, embed liveness). Both Analytics and Reports screens ship disabled until activated.

tools_if_shown.name: set_analytics_source
tools_if_shown.description: Select the active writer for a data type. Validated server-side against what the customer's setup supports. Switching aiCrawlers to cloudflare starts a backfill sync.

tools_if_shown.name: activate_analytics_screen
tools_if_shown.description: Turn on the Analytics or Reports screen for this workspace (they ship disabled; activation is one-time per screen).

tools_if_shown.name: get_cloudflare_connect_url
tools_if_shown.description: OAuth URL to connect read-only Cloudflare analytics (AI-crawler data source). Open it in a browser; the grant is scoped to Analytics:Read.

tools_if_shown.name: list_cloudflare_zones
tools_if_shown.description: Cloudflare zones visible to the connected grant, for picking which zone to poll.

tools_if_shown.name: select_cloudflare_zone
tools_if_shown.description: Pick the Cloudflare zone to poll. A crawler source already set stays; Cloudflare becomes the source only when none is set, and its first sync backfills up to 7 days.

tools_if_shown.name: install_framer_embed
tools_if_shown.description: Install site-wide visit tracking on the connected Framer project via its custom-code API. Dry run unless confirm is true. Confirming ALSO PUBLISHES the customer's Framer site. When the person asked for this, call it with confirm=true.

tools_if_shown.name: install_webflow_custom_code
tools_if_shown.description: Register and apply the tracking loader via Webflow's Custom Code API. Dry run unless confirm is true. When the person asked for this, call it with confirm=true. Needs a site token with CMS + Custom code scopes (pass apiToken to upgrade the stored one). Goes live on the customer's next Webflow site publish.

tools_if_shown.name: add_tracked_query
tools_if_shown.description: Add a query. Weekly AI citation checks start immediately when a tracking slot is free; otherwise it is saved untracked. Pass coveredByContentId when the query is one of that article's question headings, so Content Ideas does not offer it again.

tools_if_shown.name: remove_tracked_query
tools_if_shown.description: Delete a query. Frees its tracking slot if it was tracked.

tools_if_shown.name: set_query_tracking
tools_if_shown.description: Pause or resume weekly AI citation checks on a saved query. Tracking uses one of the plan's tracking slots; pausing frees it. The query is kept either way.

tools_if_shown.name: update_tracked_query
tools_if_shown.description: Rewrite a tracked query's text. Future weekly checks use the new text.

tools_if_shown.name: get_competitors
tools_if_shown.description: Tracked competitors used in share-of-voice and visibility comparisons, with each one's AI visibility score, citations of checks over the last 30 days, domain metrics and positioning analysis.

tools_if_shown.name: add_competitor
tools_if_shown.description: Start tracking a competitor (10 at most). It joins the weekly share-of-voice comparison with your own citation rate and the weekly competitor checks. Leave out websiteUrl to have the site found from the name. remove_competitor stops it.

tools_if_shown.name: remove_competitor
tools_if_shown.description: Stop tracking a competitor: it leaves share of voice and the weekly competitor checks. It waits for the workspace owner to approve it in RankControl; the answer is an approval link.

tools_if_shown.name: get_topics
tools_if_shown.description: The workspace's topics, each with id and name. Tracked queries, content ideas and planned articles all group under them, and plan_content takes their names. Empty until topics are set with set_topics.

tools_if_shown.name: set_topics
tools_if_shown.description: Replace the FULL topic list. Send every topic that should exist; missing ones are removed, new ones created, duplicates merged. Read get_topics first and modify that list. Up to 20 topics.

tools_if_shown.name: delete_planned_title
tools_if_shown.description: Remove a planned title from the content calendar. The title's keyword returns to Content Ideas as a saved query, so the topic is not lost. Only planned rows qualify; use archive for generated articles.

tools_if_shown.name: get_traffic_overview
tools_if_shown.description: Traffic overview from RankControl's own page analytics: total page views, unique visitors, sessions, bounce rate, and average time on page. With scope "site" and Google Analytics connected, the whole site from Google Analytics instead: visits with the same days before, visits from search and from AI by engine, a visits trend, and top pages.

tools_if_shown.name: get_rankings
tools_if_shown.description: Verified Google and Bing positions per keyword (top 30), with Search Console clicks, impressions and average position when connected (gscPosition is an average over the searches you appeared in, never a rank), which page earned each query and whether it is one of your articles (isOurs), and how often Google's AI Overview shows above each keyword and cites one of your pages (a rate over the last 8 weekly checks). Defaults to queries your published articles appear for.

tools_if_shown.name: get_planning_capacity
tools_if_shown.description: How many article titles can still be planned onto the content calendar within the scheduling horizon. Check before plan_content.

tools_if_shown.name: get_team
tools_if_shown.description: Workspace members and pending invites, with each member's per-screen permission matrix and the seat cap.

tools_if_shown.name: invite_team_member
tools_if_shown.description: Invite a member to the workspace with per-screen none/read/write access (unspecified screens default to none — grant at least one). Dry-run unless confirm is true; confirming sends the invite email. When the person asked for this, call it with confirm=true.

tools_if_shown.name: revoke_team_invite
tools_if_shown.description: Cancel a pending team invite so it can no longer be accepted. It waits for the workspace owner to approve it in RankControl; the answer is an approval link. Invitation ids come from get_team.

tools_if_shown.name: remove_team_member
tools_if_shown.description: Remove a member from the workspace (access revoked immediately). Dry-run unless confirm is true. When the person asked for this, call it with confirm=true.

tools_if_shown.name: list_outreach_prospects
tools_if_shown.description: Your link outreach prospects, newest first, one row per site: domain, url, status (identified, contacted, replied, link_placed or rejected), the article it's for, Domain Rating (dr, with drSource ahrefs; dataforseo marks an estimate for a domain Ahrefs has no number for), contact email and name once found, send and reply dates, the latest reply and how it was classed, follow-ups, and whether a placed link was seen on the page.

tools_if_shown.name: get_outreach_stats
tools_if_shown.description: Outreach funnel for the last 90 days by how each prospect was found (intersection = competitor linkers, footprint = resource pages, mention = topical mentions, fresh = fresh competitor links, brand_mention = brand mentions, legacy = earlier rows): prospects, sent, replied and placed with reply and placement rates per send, plus the total. The harvest reads the same numbers to weight its methods; nothing to configure.

tools_if_shown.name: find_outreach_contact
tools_if_shown.description: Find an outreach email for one prospect site. Returns the stored contact or found:false. Capped at 5/min.

tools_if_shown.name: draft_outreach_reply
tools_if_shown.description: AI-draft the next reply to a prospect who answered (status replied or rejected; auto-replies don't count). Returns subject and body only. Nothing sends: pass that subject and body to queue_outreach_email to send it.

tools_if_shown.name: queue_outreach_email
tools_if_shown.description: Queue an outreach email to a prospect. It sends from the workspace's own connected mailbox, paced automatically with a daily cap. Uses the stored draft unless subject/body are given (a reply to a prospect who answered must pass both); a "[Your name]" sign-off in the draft is replaced with the owner's profile name at send time. Dry-run unless confirm is true — a confirmed queue leads to a REAL email being sent. When the person asked for this, call it with confirm=true.

tools_if_shown.name: cancel_outreach_email
tools_if_shown.description: Cancel a queued outreach email (a first email, a reply or a follow-up) before it sends. Refused once it has gone out.

tools_if_shown.name: list_jobs
tools_if_shown.description: Recent agent runs (job status feed). Async actions like content planning show up here with their outputs.

tools_if_shown.name: list_content
tools_if_shown.description: Every article in the workspace, archived ones included: id, title, status (planned, draft, published or archived), contentType, slug, wordCount, scheduledAt, publishedAt, the live url, health and citability scores, and Google clicks, impressions and position for published articles with Search Console data.

tools_if_shown.name: plan_content
tools_if_shown.description: Generate candidate article titles (capacity-gated). This DOES NOT put anything on the calendar: review the returned titles, then call commit_planned_titles with the keepers. To plan titles about something specific, pass it as subject with the workspace topics it fits as topics. If it fits none of them, offer to add a topic first (set_topics). Costly; capped at 5/min.

tools_if_shown.name: commit_planned_titles
tools_if_shown.description: Approve reviewed titles onto the content calendar (the approval half of the plan→commit gate). Pass rejected candidates in `discarded` so their keywords recycle into Content Ideas.

tools_if_shown.name: publish_content
tools_if_shown.description: Publish an article to the customer's connected CMS. Defaults to a DRY RUN describing what would happen. When the person asked for this, call it with confirm=true. Delivery runs after this call returns. If the article does not go live, list_content shows its lastPublishError. Webhook receivers: https://rctrl.com/docs/webhook

tools_if_shown.name: update_article_meta
tools_if_shown.description: Change a written article's title, meta title (60 characters at most) or meta description (155 at most). The article's URL does not change. Defaults to a DRY RUN describing what would happen. When the person asked for this, call it with confirm=true. On a published article the change also goes to the customer's site.

tools_if_shown.name: generate_article
tools_if_shown.description: Write a PLANNED article's body immediately instead of waiting for the scheduled pipeline (generate-only: its publish slot is unchanged). Allowed for past-due slots and up to 3 days ahead, and at most 5 articles in any 24 hours (the dry run reports withinDailyLimit and nextWriteAt). Defaults to a DRY RUN. When the person asked for this, call it with confirm=true. To write several articles, use write_articles.

tools_if_shown.name: write_articles
tools_if_shown.description: Write several PLANNED articles one after another, and publish each one when publish is true: the next ones in calendar order (next), or the ones you name (contentIds). Each article follows Write now's rules: Auto-write off, next in line, up to 3 days before its day, at most 5 in any 24 hours. News and trending articles are written but never published by a run. Defaults to a DRY RUN that lists what would be written and what would stop it. When the person asked for this, call it with confirm=true. Follow progress with get_write_runs.

tools_if_shown.name: get_write_runs
tools_if_shown.description: Recent write runs: each article's state (waiting, writing, written, publishing, live, review: written and waiting for a person to publish, failed, skipped) and why a run stopped.

tools_if_shown.name: stop_write_run
tools_if_shown.description: Stop a write run: nothing new starts, and an article being written finishes as a draft.

tools_if_shown.name: get_approval
tools_if_shown.description: Where a change that waits for the workspace owner stands: pending, running, done, failed, declined or expired, and what happened. The approvalId comes from an approval_required answer; only the owner approves, in RankControl.

tools_if_shown.name: get_article_settings
tools_if_shown.description: The workspace's article settings: articleSettings (auto-write, auto-publish, images, title in hero image, section infographics, Related Reading, YouTube, emojis, link counts, global instructions and the formats turned on), flexibleScheduling and styleSet (the hero image style). Change them with update_article_settings. News and trending articles always publish manually, whatever auto-publish says.

tools_if_shown.name: update_article_settings
tools_if_shown.description: Change the workspace's article settings. Only the fields you pass change; the rest keep their values. flexibleScheduling true allows 1 to 5 articles a day and lets you move planned articles by hand. styleSet picks the image style for hero images. get_article_settings shows the current values.

tools_if_shown.name: reschedule_article
tools_if_shown.description: Move a PLANNED article to another day (requires the flexible schedule; max 5/day; the exact hour is placed automatically). Pass the target day as YYYY-MM-DD in the workspace's timezone.

tools_if_shown.name: update_planned_article
tools_if_shown.description: Change a planned article's own settings before it is written: length, tone, image style and custom instructions. Locked once writing starts.

tools_if_shown.name: get_internal_links
tools_if_shown.description: How the workspace's articles interlink: how many published articles link TO this page (with the source list) and how many internal links it sends out. Recorded from the real injected links at publish render time.

tools_if_shown.name: list_site_pages
tools_if_shown.description: Your site's pages that articles can link to, in the text and in the Related Reading block. Each row: id, url, title, description, isLinkable (whether new articles may link to it), isAlive (whether the page still loads) and priority. Empty until pages are added or detected.

tools_if_shown.name: detect_site_links
tools_if_shown.description: Scan the customer's sitemap (nested indexes handled) or crawl a blog root page and return same-site page URLs, minus the articles RankControl published (those are linked already). The source is remembered and re-read daily. Costly (3/min); review the URLs, then call add_site_pages with the keepers.

tools_if_shown.name: add_site_pages
tools_if_shown.description: Add site page URLs for internal linking. Duplicates and articles RankControl published are skipped; page titles fill in automatically in the background.

tools_if_shown.name: set_site_page_linking
tools_if_shown.description: Turn linking to a site page on or off. Off keeps the page in your list, but articles published after this don't link to it.

tools_if_shown.name: remove_site_page
tools_if_shown.description: Remove a page from your site pages. Articles published after this don't link to it, and scans don't add it back; add_site_pages adds it again.

tools_if_shown.name: list_repurpose_queue
tools_if_shown.description: Published articles with their social repurpose drafts per platform (platform + status chips). Shows which articles still need drafts and which scheduler is connected (Buffer or Postiz).

tools_if_shown.name: get_repurpose_drafts
tools_if_shown.description: Full social drafts (title, body, images, status) for one published article across the 8 platforms (LinkedIn, X/Twitter, Pinterest, Instagram, Facebook, Threads, YouTube, TikTok).

tools_if_shown.name: generate_repurpose_drafts
tools_if_shown.description: Draft platform-native social posts for all eight platforms from a published article. Only for an article with no drafts yet; edit existing drafts in the dashboard. Defaults to a DRY RUN. When the person asked for this, call it with confirm=true.

tools_if_shown.name: update_repurpose_draft
tools_if_shown.description: Change a social post draft's text or title before you push or post it. Only the fields you pass change. Draft ids come from get_repurpose_drafts.

tools_if_shown.name: mark_repurpose_posted
tools_if_shown.description: Mark a repurpose draft as posted — use after publishing its text manually (outside Buffer or Postiz).

tools_if_shown.name: list_postiz_channels
tools_if_shown.description: Connected social channels across Postiz and Buffer (scheduler, id, name, platform). Channel ids are required by push_repurpose_draft.

tools_if_shown.name: push_repurpose_draft
tools_if_shown.description: Send a repurpose draft to a connected scheduler's channels: Postiz or Buffer (schedule, save as a draft, or add to Buffer's queue). YouTube and TikTok drafts are recording scripts and never push. PUBLICLY VISIBLE side effect: defaults to a DRY RUN. When the person asked for this, call it with confirm=true.

tools_if_shown.name: get_content_ideas
tools_if_shown.description: Scored content-idea backlog: uncovered tracked queries ranked by citation gaps, competitor citations, trending topics, and quick-win rankings. Each idea carries a suggested title, winnability metrics and, where the site already ranks for it or ChatGPT read one of its pages, that page: rankingPage or readPage, with articleId when it is one of the workspace's articles and insightItemId when the page has an open Insights item.

tools_if_shown.name: hide_content_idea
tools_if_shown.description: Hide an idea from Content Ideas. A tracked query keeps its weekly checks and its slot; use remove_tracked_query to delete a query outright.

tools_if_shown.name: get_insights
tools_if_shown.description: List Insights: what to work on next on the workspace's own site: its product and service pages, searches Google shows it for that no page is about, and problems across the whole site from the weekly crawl. Each item has the problem, its evidence lines, a suggested fix when there is one, and its one action. todo comes in the page's order; done holds finished and hidden items.

tools_if_shown.name: hide_insight
tools_if_shown.description: Hide an Insights item the person doesn't want. It moves under Done as Hidden and does not come back. Item ids come from get_insights.

tools_if_shown.name: move_insight_to_ideas
tools_if_shown.description: Move a Search Console item (a search Google shows the site for, but no page is about) to Content Ideas: the Insights item's "Move to Content Ideas". The search becomes an untracked idea tagged Search Console, planned like any other idea, and the item moves under Done. Item ids come from get_insights.

tools_if_shown.name: plan_insight_articles
tools_if_shown.description: Plan articles that link to one of the person's product or service pages: the Insights item's "Plan 3 articles that link here". Up to 3 articles about the page's main search, in the formats the workspace has on, each asked to link to the page once; they go on the calendar as planned articles. Defaults to a DRY RUN. When the person asked for this, call it with confirm=true. Item ids come from get_insights.

tools_if_shown.name: plan_content_idea
tools_if_shown.description: Put one of your Content Ideas on the calendar as a planned article. Pass its queryText from get_content_ideas. The idea's own title and numbers are used; a title is generated only when it has none. Returns created: 1 when it went on the calendar, or 0 when nothing was added, for example when the calendar is full.

tools_if_shown.name: archive_content
tools_if_shown.description: Archive an article: it moves to the Archived tab and RankControl stops refreshing it. The published post stays live on your site; remove it there separately to take it down. It can't be restored. Refused while the article is still being written.

tools_if_shown.name: get_page_engagement
tools_if_shown.description: Per-page engagement for the last 30 days: views, AI citations, and a view sparkline per published page.

tools_if_shown.name: get_exec_summary
tools_if_shown.description: Executive report: last 30 days vs the 30 before — cite rate, citations, page views, AI-referred views, crawler hits, and articles published.

tools_if_shown.name: get_top_wins
tools_if_shown.description: Up to four wins from the last 30 days, each with kind (page, query, keyword or backlink), title, detail and stat: the most-cited page, the biggest citation-rate jump for a query, the biggest Google ranking climb and the best new backlink. A win with nothing to show is left out. Null, with a hint, until the Reports screen is turned on (activate_analytics_screen).

tools_if_shown.name: get_agent_activity
tools_if_shown.description: Recent runs per agent (radar, forge, recon, outreach, sentinel, amplify, social), each with startedAt, completedAt, status and triggeredBy. perAgent sets runs per agent (default 15, max 50) and sinceDays the window (default 30). Agents with no runs in the window are left out.

tools_if_shown.name: list_backlinks
tools_if_shown.description: Every backlink row for the workspace, newest first: the linking page (linkingUrl, linkingDomain), targetUrl, anchorText, dofollow, domainAuthority, status and dates, plus its source (index, outreach, managed or network). Filter with status; get_backlink_stats gives the totals.

tools_if_shown.name: get_backlink_stats
tools_if_shown.description: Backlink and outreach numbers in one call: total rows, discovered and lost links, average domain authority (avgDA), uniqueDomains, your site's indexed backlink and referring-domain totals once measured, outreach counts by stage (identified, contacted, replied, linkPlaced, rejected) and links built by source (outreach, social, network, managed). list_backlinks returns the rows.

tools_if_shown.name: update_outreach_status
tools_if_shown.description: Move an outreach prospect through the pipeline. A move to link_placed is confirmed by reading their page now and again tomorrow; the row keeps Placed and shows what was seen.

tools_if_shown.name: get_link_network
tools_if_shown.description: Your Editorial Circle standing: stats (credit balance, earned30d, spent30d, creditValue, optedIn) and placements in two lists, hosted (links on your articles) and received (links to your site). Each placement has partner, page titles, targetUrl, anchorText, credits, status and createdAt, newest first.

tools_if_shown.name: set_link_network_opt_in
tools_if_shown.description: Join or leave the Editorial Circle. SIDE EFFECT on partner sites (leaving retires live links): defaults to a DRY RUN. When the person asked for this, call it with confirm=true.

tools_if_shown.name: remove_network_placement
tools_if_shown.description: Remove one Editorial Circle link from an article on your site. RankControl republishes that article without the link, and the partner loses it. A link you received stays until the site that hosts it removes it. Dry run unless confirm is true; a confirmed call waits for the workspace owner to approve it in RankControl. Placement ids come from get_link_network.

tools_if_shown.name: list_social_threads
tools_if_shown.description: Social thread prospects (Reddit/X) where the brand's articles could earn a mention, with subreddit rules context, sorted by intent.

tools_if_shown.name: get_social_stats
tools_if_shown.description: Counts of the Social tab's Reddit and X threads: total, by stage (identified, replyDrafted, engaged for posted, skipped), by platform (reddit, twitter) and by age (ranked, new), plus replies drafted in the last 30 days with and without a product mention (mention30d, helpful30d). All zeros until threads are found; list_social_threads returns the threads.

tools_if_shown.name: update_social_thread_status
tools_if_shown.description: Skip a social thread so it leaves the queue (the only manual status; Posted is set automatically once your reply is found in the thread).

tools_if_shown.name: open_social_thread
tools_if_shown.description: Open a drafted social thread to post the reply yourself: returns the thread URL (for X, a link that opens X's composer with the reply filled in) and starts four checks over 72 hours that mark the thread Posted once your reply is found there. Pass text to use an edited reply; X replies must be 280 characters or fewer.

tools_if_shown.name: set_social_x_handle
tools_if_shown.description: Save the X handle used to recognise your posted replies (optional; text matching covers the rest). Pass an empty handle to clear it.

tools_if_shown.name: set_reddit_profile
tools_if_shown.description: Save the Reddit account the Social tab drafts for: username (optional), comment karma, account age (under1mo, 1to6mo, 6moto2yr or over2yr), goal, founderStory and tone. Karma and age decide whether drafts may mention your product; the reply returns the readiness tier (warmup or ready). Replaces the stored profile — send every field.

tools_if_shown.name: draft_social_reply
tools_if_shown.description: AI-draft a reply for a social thread. Nothing posts — the draft lands on the thread for human review. Subject to the same warm-up/pacing guards as the dashboard.

tools_if_shown.name: contact_support
tools_if_shown.description: Send a message or bug report to the RankControl team (emails support with the workspace identified; the org owner is set as reply-to). Use when an API call errors unexpectedly or data looks wrong — include the failing request, ids, and what you expected. Capped at 3/min.

tools_if_shown.name: get_help_page
tools_if_shown.description: RankControl's help pages: setup guides for each publishing destination, the crawler and its IP address, AI crawler access, the API, CLI and MCP, getting started, and the plan and pricing. Without a page, lists the pages.

tools_if_shown.name: get_billing
tools_if_shown.description: This workspace's billing as Settings, Billing shows it: status (trial, active or cancelling), billing cycle, next charge, add-ons, usage against the plan's limits and recent payments. Read-only; changes are made in Settings, Billing.

tools_if_shown.name: get_brand
tools_if_shown.description: The workspace's brand data in one read: brand profile (voice, colors, meta), links/CTAs, products, buyer profiles (ICPs) and brand guidelines. This is the context RankControl's writers use.

tools_if_shown.name: confirm_brand_reviewed
tools_if_shown.description: Mark your brand as reviewed, as the Overview's Mark reviewed button does. It completes the Confirm your brand step of Expedition I and can't be undone; marking it again changes nothing.

tools_if_shown.name: add_brand_guideline
tools_if_shown.description: Add a brand guideline, as Brand Control, Writing, Brand Guidelines does: a rule the writer follows in every article from now on, with its type, what to avoid and what to write instead (300 characters each). It starts switched on; set_brand_guideline_active turns it off. Returns the new guidelineId.

tools_if_shown.name: set_brand_guideline_active
tools_if_shown.description: Turn a brand guideline on or off. Guideline ids come from get_brand.

tools_if_shown.name: remove_brand_guideline
tools_if_shown.description: Delete a brand guideline. This can't be undone; turning it off keeps it.

tools_if_shown.name: update_brand_profile
tools_if_shown.description: Patch brand voice/style fields: tone, colors, defaultLocale, flexibleScheduling. They steer all future article generation. Also Brand Profile's Local business switch: localBusiness, and serviceArea (the area the business serves, like "Austin, Texas"; 100 characters at most, empty clears it). Only provided fields change.

tools_if_shown.name: update_brand_identity
tools_if_shown.description: Update workspace identity: name, industry and subIndustry (values from the dashboard's industry list; a new industry without a subIndustry clears the old one), productDescription, authors (EEAT bylines used in article JSON-LD), styleReferenceUrls (articles whose writing style the writer imitates), brandAliases (other spellings and short forms of the brand; pages using them count as brand mentions) and brandExclusions (same-name companies or products whose pages are skipped). Every array REPLACES the stored list — call get_brand first and send the full updated list. Saving a name change runs the brand-mention search once a day at most. websiteUrl is immutable and cannot be changed.

tools_if_shown.name: write_brand_product
tools_if_shown.description: Create, update, or delete a product in brand memory (feeds article context + entity triples). Create: name+description+category. Update: productId + changed fields. Delete: productId + del=true.

tools_if_shown.name: write_brand_icp
tools_if_shown.description: Create, update, or delete a buyer profile / ICP (feeds article targeting + entity triples). Create: title+industry+demographics. Update: profileId + changed fields. Delete: profileId + del=true.

tools_if_shown.name: suggest_brand_icps
tools_if_shown.description: Suggest up to 8 audiences for this site from its brand, products, competitors and topics. Saves nothing. Pick one and pass it to draft_brand_icp, or write your own with write_brand_icp.

tools_if_shown.name: draft_brand_icp
tools_if_shown.description: Draft one buyer profile from a one-sentence description or a suggestion from suggest_brand_icps. Returns the fields to review; nothing is saved until write_brand_icp. Fields passed in given are kept as written.

tools_if_shown.name: write
tools_if_shown.description: Drafts an email, message, post, reply, doc, or report in the user's style. Use for new writing for or on behalf of the user, using their current Writing Profile when available. It writes from their request, facts, notes, or an outline, without inventing missing facts. The tool produces the draft. There is no need to draft it first. Works without a Writing Profile. Put the user's directions in `instructions`. It returns finished writing for direct presentation. When presenting the writing, preserve its wording.

tools_if_shown.name: rewrite
tools_if_shown.description: Rewrites text: 'make this sound like me', 'less AI', shorter, or clearer. Use for writing for or on behalf of the user, including drafts the host wrote for them. It rewrites in the user's style using their current Writing Profile when available. It covers an email, message, post, reply, or doc, from a grammar fix to a complete rewrite. Covers asks such as 'make this less AI-written' or 'make it less formal'. Changes include grammar, spelling, clarity, length, structure, tone, style, audience, or format. It can summarize, expand, simplify, paraphrase, or repurpose. Works without a Writing Profile. Unless the user asks to change them, it keeps supplied facts and protected wording. Put the user's change request in `instructions`. It returns finished writing for direct presentation. When presenting the writing, preserve its wording.

tools_if_shown.name: refine_writing
tools_if_shown.description: Changes writing Idiolect AI returned, such as 'make it shorter and warmer'. The user does not need to name Idiolect AI again. It covers follow-ups on writing from `write`, `rewrite`, or `refine_writing`. The `refine_writing` tool revises returned writing, applies a ready-made template, or records its use. Send the latest `writingJobVersionId`, or `outputReference` when no version was returned, but not both. Send one of `change`, `templateId`, or `outcome`. If the change sets a new form, language or fact of the situation, send it in `format`, `language` or `situation`. The `finalText` field may come alone or with `outcome`. When the user reports use or the host observes completed use, send `outcome` with its `decisionSource`. When the final wording is known, send it in `finalText`. Set `editAuthor` to whoever edited it.

tools_if_shown.name: view_writing_profile
tools_if_shown.description: Shows the user's current Writing Profile and rules, and lists their Writing Profiles. To view another Writing Profile, set `profile` to its id or name. To list its writing samples, set `samples` true. Writing Profiles update continuously as the user writes, so read the current one here each time instead of keeping a saved copy.

tools_if_shown.name: manage_profile
tools_if_shown.description: Change the user's Writing Profiles and default writing template. Choose an `action`: `create_profile`, `add_samples`, `remove_sample`, `add_rule`, `remove_rule`, `rename_profile`, `set_current_profile`, or `set_default_template`. When the user shares writing they authored in this conversation, save it with `add_samples`. Without a Writing Profile, use `create_profile`. When the user states a lasting writing preference, save it with `add_rule`. Keep stated rules in the user's words and preserve their scope. Do not save inferred patterns as stated rules. Reuse that permission for the rest of this conversation without asking again. The user can delete a whole Writing Profile on the Idiolect AI website.

tools_if_shown.name: search_docs
tools_if_shown.description: Full-text search across API modules, endpoints (name, path, description) and the integration guides (Shop Micro Frontend, Guidelines, Webhooks). The reference is English; German search terms are understood as well (a generated language layer maps them onto the English vocabulary, e.g. 'aussteller' → exhibitor, 'gutschein' → voucher). Returns ranked hits with ids usable in get_endpoint / get_guide.

tools_if_shown.name: list_modules
tools_if_shown.description: All top-level ADITUS API modules with direction (inbound = your systems call ADITUS, outbound = ADITUS data into your systems), endpoint counts and documentation URLs. Also lists the integration guides.

tools_if_shown.name: list_endpoints
tools_if_shown.description: Every endpoint of one module (id, method, path, sub-group, one-line summary). Use the module id from list_modules.

tools_if_shown.name: get_endpoint
tools_if_shown.description: Full contract of one endpoint: method, URL, auth, query and header parameters, request body example, example responses (large bodies truncated, full text on the docs page). Accepts the endpoint id from search/list, or 'METHOD /path'. Path parameters may use any name or spelling (':cart', '{cartId}', a concrete value); a leading '/api' or '/v1' is ignored. Some routes are recorded several times with different query parameters: a reference without query string resolves to the recording without query parameters, a reference with a query string (e.g. '?$expand=All') to the recording with exactly (or at least) those keys. If that still leaves several recordings, the result is { ambiguous: true, candidates: [{ id, name, method, path }] } instead of the contract — call again with one of the candidate ids. When nothing matches, the error lists the nearest endpoints of that method.

tools_if_shown.name: get_guide
tools_if_shown.description: Markdown of an integration guide. 'micro-frontend' is the Shop Micro Frontend contract (mounting, sessions, styling, Web Component, lifecycle, security); module guides such as 'guidelines' or 'webhooks' come from the API reference. Pass a section heading to fetch only that section.

tools_if_shown.name: find_trails_near_location
tools_if_shown.description:
Find hiking, running, biking, backpacking or other trails for outdoor activities near a set of coordinates within an optional specified maximum radius (meters).

Use this tool when the user:
* Requests trails near a specific point of interest or landmark.
* Requests trails near a named location within a specified radius or accessible within a specified time constraint.
* Provides specific latitude and longitude coordinates.

For most named places, use the "search within bounding box" tool if possible. Use this tool as a fallback when the bounding box of the named place is unknown.

Users can specify filters related to appropriate activities, attractions, suitability, and more. Numeric range filters related to distance, elevation, and length are also available. These filter values MUST be specified in meters.

In the response, length and distance values are returned both in meters and imperial units. These MUST be displayed to the user in the units most appropriate for the user's locale, e.g. feet or miles for US English users.

tools_if_shown.name: find_trails_within_bounds
tools_if_shown.description:
Find hiking, running, biking, backpacking or other trails for outdoor activities within a specified bounding box defined by southwest and northeast coordinates.

Use this tool when the user:
* Requests trails within specific geographic boundaries or coordinates.
* Requests trails near a named geographic or political place, such as a continent, country, state, province, region, city, town, or neighborhood and you know the bounding box for that place.
* Requests trails within a national, state or local park or other protected area and you know the bounding box for that park.

If the bounding box for the named place is not known, use the "find trails near a location" tool instead to find trails around a center point.

Users can specify filters related to appropriate activities, attractions, suitability, and more. Numeric range filters related to distance, elevation, and length are also available. These filter values MUST be specified in meters.

In the response, length and distance values are returned both in meters and imperial units. These MUST be displayed to the user in the units most appropriate for the user's locale, e.g. feet or miles for US English users.

tools_if_shown.name: search_trails_by_name
tools_if_shown.description:
Search for hiking, running, biking, backpacking or other trails by full or partial name match.

Use this tool when the user:
* Requests a specific trail by name (e.g., "Avalanche Lake Trail", "Half Dome")
* Searches for trails with specific keywords in the name

The search can biased towards results near the provided coordinates if they are provided explicitly or available from the request metadata.

If there is a clear match to the user's query, the model should automatically make a subsequent call to the `get_trail_details` tool to present the user with complete details for the matching trail.

In the response, length and distance values are returned both in meters and imperial units. These MUST be displayed to the user in the units most appropriate for the user's locale, e.g. feet or miles for US English users.

tools_if_shown.name: get_trail_details
tools_if_shown.description:
Find detailed information about a trail from AllTrails.

Get descriptive overviews and specific accessibility information. Includes structured data about suitable activities, and feature highlights along the trail.

Get stats about the trail geography and length, and stats about associated user-generated content.

In the response, length and distance values are returned both in meters and imperial units. These MUST be displayed to the user in the units most appropriate for the user's locale, e.g. feet or miles for US English users.

tools_if_shown.name: query_metrics
tools_if_shown.description:
Query analytics metrics for this company over a date range. Returns aggregate totals and, if groupByTime or groupByDimensions is set, all grouped rows (the server paginates metricsTable in pages of 1000 edges until complete; paginationPagesFetched reports how many GraphQL calls were used). tools_if_shown.name: list_brand_assets

tools_if_shown.name: get_email_branding_styles
tools_if_shown.description: Get the company's email brand kit styles (buttons, headings, paragraphs, dividers, images, rows, spacers, titles, and template-wide defaults). Use `initialized=false` to detect a company that has never customized brand styles.

tools_if_shown.name: list_email_brand_kit_compatible_fonts

tools_if_shown.name: get_brand_voice_settings

tools_if_shown.name: get_campaign
tools_if_shown.description: Get detailed campaign info by ID, including message groups and messages.

tools_if_shown.name: get_campaign_metrics
tools_if_shown.description: Get SMS campaign performance metrics for a company over a date range (defaults to the last 30 days). Returns query-wide aggregate values and one page of grouped campaign rows for delivered, clicks, click rate, conversions, conversion rate, revenue, AOV, revenue per send, unsubscribes, unsubscribe rate, and fatigues. tools_if_shown.name: list_campaigns

tools_if_shown.name: get_campaign_message_group

tools_if_shown.name: get_creative

tools_if_shown.name: list_creatives
tools_if_shown.description: List creatives for a company with optional search, status filter, type filter, and pagination.

tools_if_shown.name: get_email_template

tools_if_shown.name: list_email_templates

tools_if_shown.name: get_journey
tools_if_shown.description: Get detailed information for a single journey by ID, including name, state, trigger, tags, schedules, and category.

tools_if_shown.name: get_journey_branch
tools_if_shown.description: Read how a branching node is currently configured: the dimension it tests, each branch's conditions with a readable label and node id, the steps under each branch, and the selection schemas for that dimension. tools_if_shown.name: get_journey_configuration
tools_if_shown.description: Read the configuration options available for a journey: which node types can be added/copied/moved (allowedSteps), and the valid branching dimensions for its trigger (each with its dimensionValue, branch count limits, and required selection schemaTypes). Call this before adding nodes or configuring branches to discover valid values for this specific journey/trigger instead of guessing.

tools_if_shown.name: get_journey_graph
tools_if_shown.description: Get a summarized view of a journey's graph structure, including all steps (triggers, delays, messages, branches, experiments) with message text content. Filters out internal structural nodes for a clean readable flow. Returns the draft revision by default, whose node ids are the ones the journey write tools accept; revisionKind reports which revision was read.

tools_if_shown.name: get_journey_message
tools_if_shown.description: Get the content of a journey message by its GraphQL message ID. Returns the message body text (SMS/RCS) or subject/preheader (email).

tools_if_shown.name: get_revision_settings
tools_if_shown.description: Read a journey revision's settings, including entry frequency (eligibilityDurationSeconds and eligibilityDurationUnits). Defaults to the draft revision if no revisionId is specified.

tools_if_shown.name: list_journeys
tools_if_shown.description: List journeys for the company. Returns a paginated, summarized list of journeys (journeyId, name, description, state, triggerId, category, lastUpdated, tag display names). tools_if_shown.name: list_journey_templates
tools_if_shown.description: List available journey templates that can be used when creating a new journey. Templates provide pre-built journey flows for common use cases. Filter by language or channel (SMS, EMAIL, MULTI, PUSH).

tools_if_shown.name: list_journey_triggers

tools_if_shown.name: list_product_attribute_values

tools_if_shown.name: create_or_update_workflow

tools_if_shown.name: list_projects

tools_if_shown.name: list_workflows

tools_if_shown.name: get_workflow_and_preview_url

Step ids are for reading only; when asking create_or_update_workflow for changes, describe steps by what they do. Do not use to create, update, publish, or unpublish workflows.

tools_if_shown.name: get_analytics
tools_if_shown.description: Read-only. Use to query Dreamlit analytics for overview metrics, notification rows, recipient engagement, or workflow run rows with filters, sorting, and cursor pagination. Do not use for CSV exports, bulk dumps, workflow edits, publishing, or low-level database access.

tools_if_shown.name: send_workflow_test

Returns the published workflow status and app URLs. Do not call speculatively or without carrying forward the prepare_publish safety fields.

tools_if_shown.name: unpublish_workflow
tools_if_shown.description: Use after explicit user intent to unpublish a Dreamlit workflow. Side effect: disables live triggers or schedules for that workflow and stops future automated sends. Returns updated workflow status and app URLs. Do not use for deleting drafts, canceling one broadcast run, or editing workflow content.

tools_if_shown.name: quote_task
tools_if_shown.description:
Check whether Eyes can answer a question at a place before you spend anything. Free and read-only.
Returns workers_nearby, est_minutes_to_answer, suggested_bounty_usd, allowed, reason_if_not and resolved_location (where Eyes thinks you mean).
suggested_bounty_usd already fits this API key's max_bounty_usd, the daily cap left and your balance, so ask_eyes accepts it. allowed is false only when you cannot post this task right now: the safety rules refuse this task_type at this place, the task_type is not allowed for this key, or even the 1 USD minimum bounty plus the 0.50 USD fee does not fit your limits or balance; reason_if_not says what to do. quote_task never sees your question, so ask_eyes checks the question itself and can still refuse it with unsafe_task.
location is {lat, lng} or a string such as "Blue Bottle Coffee, Mint Plaza, San Francisco". task_type is one of: is_open, line_length, in_stock, photo_of_place, price_check, crowd_level, other_public.
Example: quote_task({ "location": "Ferry Building, San Francisco", "task_type": "line_length" })
Next: if allowed is true and workers_nearby > 0, call ask_eyes with the same location and task_type, using suggested_bounty_usd as bounty_usd. If resolved_location is not the place you meant, retry with a more specific string or {lat, lng}. If workers_nearby is 0, try a nearby busier place or later.

tools_if_shown.name: ask_eyes
tools_if_shown.description:
Pay a nearby human to look at a public place right now and answer your question, usually with a live photo. Eyes texts nearby workers; the first to accept walks over and captures the answer on site, and Eyes verifies it (GPS within about 150 m, photo taken live before the deadline, vision check) before you receive it.
Money: bounty_usd (default 3) plus a 0.50 USD fee is escrowed from your balance now. The worker is paid only after a verified answer. If nobody answers before deadline_minutes (default 30), or you cancel_task before a worker claims it, everything is refunded.
Only public, commercial or civic places: stores, cafes, parks, transit stops, venues. Never specific private people, homes, vehicles or private property; those are refused with an unsafe_task error.
idempotency_key is required: any unique string for each task you intend to create, for example a UUID. Reuse the same key when you retry that task: the same key and parameters return the original task instead of charging again, so retries after a timeout or network error are safe. Use a new key for a new question.
Example: ask_eyes({ "question": "How many people are waiting in line right now?", "location": "Blue Bottle Coffee, Mint Plaza, San Francisco", "task_type": "line_length", "bounty_usd": 3, "idempotency_key": "6f1c2a9e-line-check" })
Next: immediately call await_answer with the returned task_id and keep calling it until answered is true.

tools_if_shown.name: await_answer
tools_if_shown.description:
Wait for the answer to a task you created with ask_eyes. Call it immediately after ask_eyes, then keep calling it with the same task_id until answered is true or the status is expired, refunded or disputed. You cannot watch for events in the background, so this loop is the only way to receive the answer.
Each call waits up to timeout_seconds (default 50, max 55) and returns as soon as the answer arrives. A task usually takes 5 to 20 minutes. deadline_at (from ask_eyes) is the latest time a worker can still answer; a human review outcome can come later.
How to read the result:
- answered true: stop calling. answer holds answer_text, answer_bool, photo_url, captured_at, worker_distance_m, verification, confidence and cost_usd. Show your user the answer and photo_url. If confidence is below 0.7, hedge when you relay it.
- Then check answer.verification. If gps_ok, fresh_ok and vision_ok are all true, the answer is verified (status verified or paid). If any is false, status is needs_review: a worker answered but a check failed (vision_reason says why). Your escrow stays held until a human review settles it, either paid to the worker or refunded to you. Tell your user, check get_task later, and if the answer is wrong call dispute_answer to add your reason to that review.
- answered false with status dispatched, claimed or submitted: call await_answer again right away, and give your user a one-line progress update about every other call.
- status expired: nobody answered before the deadline; your escrow was refunded. Stop calling; ask again later, at a busier place or with a higher bounty_usd.
- status refunded: you cancelled the task and the escrow was refunded. Stop calling.
- status disputed: you disputed this answer and it is under human review. Stop calling and check get_task later.
Example: await_answer({ "task_id": "3f0e8c1a-5b7d-4e2f-9a6b-1c2d3e4f5a6b" })
Next: follow next_step in the response.

tools_if_shown.name: get_task
tools_if_shown.description:
Look up a task's current status and details, including the answer once there is one. Read-only and instant; it does not wait.
Statuses: dispatched (workers notified), claimed (a worker is on the way), submitted (answer received, verifying), verified or paid (answer ready), needs_review (a worker answered but a check failed; escrow held until a human review pays the worker or refunds you), disputed (under human review), expired (nobody answered before the deadline; your escrow was refunded), refunded (you cancelled; escrow refunded).
Example: get_task({ "task_id": "3f0e8c1a-5b7d-4e2f-9a6b-1c2d3e4f5a6b" })
Next: to wait for an answer call await_answer instead of polling get_task.

tools_if_shown.name: list_tasks
tools_if_shown.description:
List the tasks this API key created, newest first, with task_id, status, question, place_label, bounty_usd, created_at, deadline_at and answered. Read-only and instant. You only ever see your own tasks.
Call it when you lost a task_id (context reset, crash, restart) and before you ask a question again, so you resume an open task instead of paying twice. Find yours by question and place_label.
status keeps only tasks in that status, for example "dispatched" for tasks no worker has claimed yet. limit is 1 to 50 (default 20); raise it if the task you want is older.
Example: list_tasks({ "status": "dispatched", "limit": 5 })
Next: for a task with status dispatched, claimed or submitted, call await_answer with its task_id. For a task where answered is true, call get_task to read the answer. Call ask_eyes only if no listed task covers your question.

tools_if_shown.name: cancel_task
tools_if_shown.description:
Cancel a task that no worker has claimed yet; the full escrow (bounty plus fee) goes back to your balance. Only works while status is dispatched; once a worker has claimed it you get task_not_cancellable.
Example: cancel_task({ "task_id": "3f0e8c1a-5b7d-4e2f-9a6b-1c2d3e4f5a6b" })
Next: call get_balance to see the refund, or keep calling await_answer if the task was already claimed.

tools_if_shown.name: dispute_answer
tools_if_shown.description:
Flag a delivered answer as wrong or unhelpful. If the worker has not been paid yet, the payout is held; either way the task goes to human review. Works on tasks whose status is verified, paid or needs_review. Give a specific reason of at least 5 characters.
Example: dispute_answer({ "task_id": "3f0e8c1a-5b7d-4e2f-9a6b-1c2d3e4f5a6b", "reason": "The photo shows a different cafe, not Blue Bottle." })
Next: call get_task later to see the outcome. To get a fresh answer now, call ask_eyes again with a new idempotency_key.

tools_if_shown.name: get_balance
tools_if_shown.description:
Show your prepaid balance and how much is escrowed in open tasks, in USD, plus top_up_url, a link your human can open to add funds. Read-only.
Example: get_balance({})
Next: if balance_usd is less than bounty_usd + 0.50, give your user top_up_url and wait for them to fund it, or lower bounty_usd.

tools_if_shown.name: get_spend_policy
tools_if_shown.description:
Show the limits your user set on this API key: max_bounty_usd per task, daily_cap_usd, spent_today_usd and remaining_today_usd (UTC day), and the allowed_task_types you may post. Read-only.
Example: get_spend_policy({})
Next: keep bounty_usd at or below max_bounty_usd and within remaining_today_usd when you call ask_eyes, and use only allowed_task_types. Only your user can change these limits.

Call it immediately after ask_eyes, then keep calling it with the same task_id until answered is true or the status is expired, refunded or disputed. You cannot watch for events in the background, so this loop is the only way to receive the answer.
Each call waits up to timeout_seconds (default 50, max 55) and returns as soon as the answer arrives. A task usually takes 5 to 20 minutes. deadline_at (from ask_eyes) is the latest time a worker can still answer; a human review outcome can come later.
How to read the result:
- answered true: stop calling. answer holds answer_text, answer_bool, photo_url, captured_at, worker_distance_m, verification, confidence and cost_usd. Show your user the answer and photo_url. If confidence is below 0.7, hedge when you relay it.
- Then check answer.verification. If gps_ok, fresh_ok and vision_ok are all true, the answer is verified (status verified or paid). If any is false, status is needs_review: a worker answered but a check failed (vision_reason says why). Your escrow stays held until a human review settles it, either paid to the worker or refunded to you. Tell your user, check get_task later, and if the answer is wrong call dispute_answer to add your reason to that review.
- answered false with status dispatched, claimed or submitted: call await_answer again right away, and give your user a one-line progress update about every other call.
- status expired: nobody answered before the deadline; your escrow was refunded. Stop calling; ask again later, at a busier place or with a higher bounty_usd.
- status refunded: you cancelled the task and the escrow was refunded. Stop calling.
- status disputed: you disputed this answer and it is under human review. Stop calling and check get_task later.
Example: await_answer({ "task_id": "3f0e8c1a-5b7d-4e2f-9a6b-1c2d3e4f5a6b" })
Next: follow next_step in the response.

tools_if_shown.name: get_task
tools_if_shown.description:
Look up a task's current status and details, including the answer once there is one. Read-only and instant; it does not wait.
Statuses: dispatched (workers notified), claimed (a worker is on the way), submitted (answer received, verifying), verified or paid (answer ready), needs_review (a worker answered but a check failed; escrow held until a human review pays the worker or refunds you), disputed (under human review), expired (nobody answered before the deadline; your escrow was refunded), refunded (you cancelled; escrow refunded).
Example: get_task({ "task_id": "3f0e8c1a-5b7d-4e2f-9a6b-1c2d3e4f5a6b" })
Next: to wait for an answer call await_answer instead of polling get_task.

tools_if_shown.name: show_task
tools_if_shown.description:
Show your user a task as a card: status, place, question, the answer with its photo, the verification checks and what it cost. Read-only and instant; the JSON result is the same as get_task's. Chat apps that render MCP Apps, such as ChatGPT and Claude, draw the card; other clients get only the JSON.
Example: show_task({ "task_id": "3f0e8c1a-5b7d-4e2f-9a6b-1c2d3e4f5a6b" })
Next: call it once await_answer returns answered true, so your user sees the answer and the photo. To wait for an answer call await_answer instead.

tools_if_shown.name: list_tasks
tools_if_shown.description:
List the tasks this API key created, newest first, with task_id, status, question, place_label, bounty_usd, created_at, deadline_at and answered. Read-only and instant. You only ever see your own tasks.
Call it when you lost a task_id (context reset, crash, restart) and before you ask a question again, so you resume an open task instead of paying twice. Find yours by question and place_label.
status keeps only tasks in that status, for example "dispatched" for tasks no worker has claimed yet. limit is 1 to 50 (default 20); raise it if the task you want is older.
Example: list_tasks({ "status": "dispatched", "limit": 5 })
Next: for a task with status dispatched, claimed or submitted, call await_answer with its task_id. For a task where answered is true, call get_task to read the answer. Call ask_eyes only if no listed task covers your question.

tools_if_shown.name: cancel_task
tools_if_shown.description:
Cancel a task that no worker has claimed yet; the full escrow (bounty plus fee) goes back to your balance. Only works while status is dispatched; once a worker has claimed it you get task_not_cancellable.
Example: cancel_task({ "task_id": "3f0e8c1a-5b7d-4e2f-9a6b-1c2d3e4f5a6b" })
Next: call get_balance to see the refund, or keep calling await_answer if the task was already claimed.

tools_if_shown.name: dispute_answer
tools_if_shown.description:
Flag a delivered answer as wrong or unhelpful. If the worker has not been paid yet, the payout is held; either way the task goes to human review. Works on tasks whose status is verified, paid or needs_review. Give a specific reason of at least 5 characters.
Example: dispute_answer({ "task_id": "3f0e8c1a-5b7d-4e2f-9a6b-1c2d3e4f5a6b", "reason": "The photo shows a different cafe, not Blue Bottle." })
Next: call get_task later to see the outcome. To get a fresh answer now, call ask_eyes again with a new idempotency_key.

tools_if_shown.name: get_balance
tools_if_shown.description:
Show your prepaid balance and how much is escrowed in open tasks, in USD, plus top_up_url, a link your human can open to add funds. Read-only.
Example: get_balance({})
Next: if balance_usd is less than bounty_usd + 0.50, give your user top_up_url and wait for them to fund it, or lower bounty_usd.

tools_if_shown.name: get_spend_policy
tools_if_shown.description:
Show the limits your user set on this API key: max_bounty_usd per task, daily_cap_usd, spent_today_usd and remaining_today_usd (UTC day), and the allowed_task_types you may post. Read-only.
Example: get_spend_policy({})
Next: keep bounty_usd at or below max_bounty_usd and within remaining_today_usd when you call ask_eyes, and use only allowed_task_types. Only your user can change these limits.

tools_if_shown.name: query_granola_meetings
tools_if_shown.description:
Query Granola about the user's meetings using natural language. Returns a tailored response with inline citation links in mark  (e.g. [[0]](url)) that reference source meeting notes.

IMPORTANT: The response includes numbered citation links to specific Granola meeting notes. These citations MUST be preserved in your response to the user — they provide transparency and allow the user to verify information by clicking through to the original notes.

This tool is slow: an AI agent behind it searches and reads the user's notes before answering. Prefer a faster tool when it can answer the question:
- list_meetings: find meetings by date range
- get_meetings: read notes for meetings whose IDs you already have

When to use:
- User asks about what was discussed, decided, or action-items from meetings
- User asks about follow-ups, todos, or commitments from recent meetings
- User references 'Granola notes' or 'meeting notes'

When NOT to use:
- User is asking about calendar scheduling or upcoming events
- User explicitly asks for a specific meeting by ID (use get_meetings instead)

Prioritize using query_granola_meetings over list_meetings/get_meetings for open-ended or natural language queries about meeting content.

If this tool does not find a requested detail, meeting summaries may have omitted it. Use list_meetings/get_meetings to identify the most relevant meetings, then get_meeting_transcript only where that meeting's workspace permits transcript access. If access is denied, report that limitation; do not retry through another tool or conclude the information was never discussed.

tools_if_shown.name: list_meetings
tools_if_shown.description:
List the user's Granola meeting notes within a time range. Returns meeting titles, metadata, and note URLs.

IMPORTANT: For short-term questions about recent meeting details, prefer using query_granola_meetings instead.

When to use:
- User asks to list their meetings
- User asks about action items, decisions, or summaries from meetings over a longer or specific date range
- User asks about content from their meeting transcripts
- User references 'Granola notes' or 'meeting notes' or 'transcripts'

When NOT to use:
- User is asking about upcoming calendar events or scheduling
- User wants to create/modify calendar invites

Filtering:
- Omit workspace_only and involvement to return every meeting the user is allowed to access
- For 'my meetings' or meetings the user was involved in, set both involvement conditions to true; true conditions combine using OR
- Set captured_by_me to true for meetings whose Granola notes the user captured, or false to exclude them
- Set listed_as_participant to true for meetings where the user is a known participant, or false to exclude them
- False involvement conditions are exclusions and combine with the positive conditions using AND; omit a condition to ignore it
- For Team Space or public workspace meetings, set workspace_only to true
- workspace_only and involvement combine using AND

Use get_meetings to retrieve detailed meeting content after identifying relevant meetings.
Use list_meeting_folders to discover folder IDs, then pass a folder_id to list meetings within a specific folder.

tools_if_shown.name: list_meeting_folders
tools_if_shown.description:
List the user's Granola meeting folders. Returns folder ID, title, description, and note count including nested folders.

When to use:
- User asks about their folders or wants to browse meetings by folder
- User wants to narrow down meeting searches to a specific folder

Use the returned folder IDs with list_meetings (folder_id parameter) to list meetings within a specific folder.

tools_if_shown.name: get_meetings
tools_if_shown.description:
Get detailed meeting information for one or more Granola meetings by ID. Returns private notes, AI-generated summary, attendees, metadata, and note URLs.
Does not return transcripts. Notes and summaries can omit details that were discussed.
If a detail is missing, use get_meeting_transcript on the most relevant meetings only where that meeting's workspace permits transcript access. If access is denied, report that limitation; do not retry through another tool or conclude it was never discussed.
Use this when you already have specific meeting IDs (e.g. from list_meetings results). For open-ended questions about meeting content, use query_granola_meetings instead.

tools_if_shown.name: get_meeting_transcript
tools_if_shown.description:
Get the full transcript for a specific Granola meeting by ID. Returns only the verbatim transcript content, not summaries or notes.
Transcript blocks separate audio source (Microphone/System audio) from speaker identity. Participant attribution and user-confirmed names are preserved. Desktop diarization is omitted; mobile/imported transcripts can retain Speaker A/B/... labels for unnamed voices. Recording context identifies the document owner as the recorder for native recordings, not as the speaker. Missing recorder data stays unknown; the current viewer is not substituted. Channels and room labels may include multiple people. Older preformatted transcripts keep their original labels.
Requires access to the meeting and transcript access permitted by that meeting's workspace. Use this for exact quotes or when query_granola_meetings/get_meetings does not surface a requested detail, such as a person, example, or explanation. Start with the most relevant meetings; a detail missing from summaries may still be in the transcript. If access is denied, report that limitation and do not retry through another tool. For general summaries or action items, start with query_granola_meetings or get_meetings.

tools_if_shown.name: get_account_info
tools_if_shown.description:
Get the email, active workspace, joined workspaces (names and IDs), and effective note-access scopes for the Granola account currently connected to this MCP session.

Workspace membership does not imply MCP access to its meetings.

When to use:
- User asks 'who am I signed in as?', 'which Granola account is this?', or 'what's my email?'
- User suspects they connected the wrong Granola account
- User asks which workspaces they belong to or mentions another workspace
- Meeting results may be missing because the wrong workspace is active
- Meeting results may be incomplete or empty because of the user's Granola plan or workspace MCP access controls
- Before performing actions, to confirm identity if the user references a specific account

mcp_note_access.scopes contains the note categories this connection can search:
- personal: notes the connected user owns, notes shared directly with them, and notes accessible through private folders
- public: notes accessible through workspace-visible Team Space folders
- Both scopes means both categories can be searched. These scopes describe access, not who captured or participated in a meeting.

tools_if_shown.name: list-orders
tools_if_shown.description: List or search the Zinc orders on the configured account, newest first. Renders an interactive order list. Use `search` for a partial order ID or tracking number, `status` to filter by order status, and `has_tracking` to show only shipped orders.

tools_if_shown.name: get-order
tools_if_shown.description: Fetch one Zinc order by its UUID and render a detail card: line items, retailer price breakdown, shipping destination, and shipment timeline.

tools_if_shown.name: get-order-tracking
tools_if_shown.description: Return the carrier tracking timeline (scan checkpoints) for one Zinc order. Use this when the question is only about where a package is, not about pricing or line items.

tools_if_shown.name: list-addresses
tools_if_shown.description:
Destinations from the signed-in user's recent orders, each with an id you can pass to prepare-order as address_id. Only useful once the user has signed in (list-orders has worked, or they asked for their history); for anyone else it has nothing, and the shopper enters the address on the payment page instead. It never prompts for sign-in.

Labels are deliberately partial — a name, a city, a truncated postal code. You are not shown the street, and you do not need it: the full address is resolved server-side and shown to the user in the review card before anything is placed. Never reconstruct or guess an address from a label; if none of these is the right destination, ask the user.

tools_if_shown.name: prepare-order
tools_if_shown.description: Show the user an order to review: items, what it will cost and the hold on the card. This does NOT place the order or spend anything — the user places it by clicking Pay & place in the card that appears, and enters their shipping address on the payment page that opens. Use this whenever the user wants to buy something; never ask them for an address first. Pass each product's title, image and price_cents from search so the card shows the item and quotes the total; leave max_price out unless the user named a budget. address_id, from list-addresses, is only for a signed-in user shipping somewhere they have shipped before. Not sold through this connector: weapons, tobacco and nicotine, regulated drugs and paraphernalia, prescription medication, adult products, gambling, covert surveillance and counterfeit goods. An order for one of those is refused.

tools_if_shown.name: place-order
tools_if_shown.description: Internal: places an order the user already confirmed in the review card, paying by card. Requires a confirmation issued by prepare-order, which is not available to you — call prepare-order and let the user confirm instead.

tools_if_shown.name: get-payment-status
tools_if_shown.description: Where a card payment stands after place-order sent the buyer to a payment page: requires_action until they pay, then placed with the order_id. The review card polls this itself; call it only if the user asks whether their payment went through.

tools_if_shown.name: search-products
tools_if_shown.description:
Find products across Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy and more. Each result carries an orderable URL that can be passed straight to prepare-order, along with its title, image and price_cents — pass those too, so the review card can show the item and quote the total. Use this when the user wants to buy something but has not given a product URL. Then stop and let the user choose from the card — do not go on to prepare-order in the same turn unless they already named the exact item or asked you to pick.

Search once with the user's best query rather than issuing speculative variations, and do not retry a failed search without saying why.

When the user names the store they want to buy from, pass it in retailers rather than in the query; otherwise leave retailers out and search everywhere.

Not sold through this connector: weapons, tobacco and nicotine, regulated drugs and paraphernalia, prescription medication, adult products, gambling, covert surveillance and counterfeit goods. A search for one of those is refused and matching results are dropped; tell the user plainly rather than rephrasing the query to get around it.

tools_if_shown.description: Records feedback about this MCP server, including unexpected tool failures, unhelpful responses, or missing capabilities observed by the agent or reported by the user.
