tools_if_shown.name: get_company
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Get the details of the company this connection is signed in to: its display name, legal name, entity type, incorporation and legal address.
Not for: Financial figures, accounts, the team or connected integrations. The full EIN is never returned, only its last four digits.
Returns: id, name (the display name), legal_name, entity_type (c_corp, pbc, llc, s_corp or other), federal_ein_last4, delaware_file_number, incorporation (date and state), legal_address and created.
When to use: "What's our legal name?", "When were we incorporated?", "What's our registered address?", or to confirm which company you're working in before making changes.
Workflow: Use name when talking to the user and legal_name only where the legal name is asked for.

tools_if_shown.name: list_categories
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: List the company's chart of accounts in Finta, from top-level account types down to detail categories, with their stable cat_ IDs.
Not for: Amounts, balances or transactions; categories carry no totals. Departments are a separate list.
Returns: Every category in one response, ordered by tier, position and name. Each has id, name, account_type (asset, liability, equity, income or expense), tier (1 is top level), parent_id, and point_in_time (true for balance sheet categories).
When to use: "What categories do we use?", "Where do software subscriptions go?", or to find the cat_ ID of a category the user names.
Workflow: Use parent_id to place a category under its parent. Names can repeat under different parents, so check the parent before picking one, and refer to categories by id.

tools_if_shown.name: list_departments
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: List the company's departments in Finta, such as Engineering or Sales, with their stable dept_ IDs.
Not for: Categories or the chart of accounts, which are a separate list. Departments carry no amounts.
Returns: Every department in one response, in display order. Each has id, name, tier (1 is top level), parent_id, and assignable.
When to use: "Which departments do we track?", or to find the dept_ ID of a department the user names.
Workflow: Only departments with assignable: true can be assigned to a transaction; the others are groups. Use parent_id to place a department under its group, and refer to departments by id.

tools_if_shown.name: create_team_invitation
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Invite someone to the company's Finta team with the access they should have. Finta emails them a link to join.
Not for: Changing a pending invitation's access (update_team_invitation) or sending its email again (resend_team_invitation). People who already joined; they're managed in the Finta web app.
Returns: invitation, the same object get_team lists, with its invite_ ID; created, true for a new invitation and false when the same invitation was already pending; and changed, true when a repeat renewed an expired invitation or retried its email.
When to use: "Invite sam@example.com as an admin", "Give our accountant read-only access to Finta".
Workflow: Confirm the person's name, email and access with the user before inviting. Inviting with the same details again is safe and returns the pending invitation; a different pending invitation or an existing teammate with that email is refused (invitation_invalid). You can't grant more access than the signed-in user has (insufficient_permission). read_only and custom need the Growth plan (plan_upgrade_required) and custom roles to be on for the company (feature_disabled); otherwise only admin is available, so tell the user rather than reporting it.

tools_if_shown.name: get_team
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: List the company's team: active and inactive members, and pending invitations, with each person's access.
Not for: Changing anyone's access. Members are managed in the Finta web app; pending invitations with create_team_invitation, update_team_invitation, resend_team_invitation and revoke_team_invitation.
Returns: members (id, email, name, state active or inactive, access_template, permissions, created) and invitations (id, email, name, access_template, permissions, invited_by, created, expires), in the order the Settings team page shows them. access_template is admin, read_only or custom; permissions gives every area's level (none, view or manage), so read it for custom access. Timestamps are Unix seconds; an invitation whose expires has passed is expired but still pending. An id can be null when it isn't available.
When to use: "Who's on our Finta team?", "Who has admin access?", "Did Sam accept the invite?", or to find the invite_ ID of an invitation to change, resend or revoke.

tools_if_shown.name: resend_team_invitation
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Email a pending invitation again with a fresh link, extending its expiry. Works for expired invitations too.
Not for: Changing who it's for or their access (update_team_invitation). People who already joined.
Returns: invitation, the same object get_team lists, with its new expires, and changed, normally true. Neither means the email has arrived.
When to use: "Sam never got the invite", "Sam's invitation expired, send it again".
Workflow: Find the invitation's invite_ ID with get_team. Each call sends another email and replaces the earlier link, so call it once per request, and don't retry an uncertain result unless the user is fine with another email. An accepted invitation is refused (resource_missing).

tools_if_shown.name: revoke_team_invitation
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Cancel a pending invitation, so its link no longer lets the person join.
Not for: Removing someone who already joined; the API refuses an accepted invitation (resource_missing), and members are managed in the Finta web app.
Returns: revoked: true and the invitation's id. An invitation that was already revoked, or that doesn't exist, returns the same.
When to use: "Cancel the invite to sam@example.com", "We sent that invite to the wrong address".
Workflow: Find the invitation with get_team, show the user who it's for, and get their confirmation before revoking.

tools_if_shown.name: update_team_invitation
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Change the access a pending invitation will give the person once they join.
Not for: Changing the invitee's name or email; revoke the invitation and create a new one. Sending the email again (resend_team_invitation). People who already joined; they're managed in the Finta web app.
Returns: invitation, the same object get_team lists, and changed, false when the access was already what you sent.
When to use: "Make Sam's invite read-only instead", "Give the pending invite for our accountant Reports: View only".
Workflow: Find the invitation's invite_ ID and current access with get_team, and confirm the change with the user. The access you send replaces the old access entirely. Needs the Growth plan (plan_upgrade_required), and you can't grant more access than the signed-in user has (insufficient_permission). An accepted invitation is refused (resource_missing).

tools_if_shown.name: create_account
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Create a manual bank or credit card account in Finta that transactions can be uploaded to.
Not for: Accounts that sync from an integration such as Mercury, Brex or Plaid; those already exist, and creating one here makes a separate manual account. Adds no transactions or categories.
Returns: The account (id, account_name, vendor, type) and created: true, or created: false when a matching manual account already existed.
When to use: The user wants to add transactions for an account Finta doesn't have yet, such as "set up our Chase checking account".
Workflow: Call list_accounts first and use the existing account if one matches. Confirm the bank, name and type with the user when they're unclear. Calling again with the same vendor, account_name and type returns the same account, so retrying is safe.

tools_if_shown.name: list_accounts
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: List the company's bank, credit card and other transaction-source accounts in Finta, with their stable acct_ IDs.
Not for: Chart-of-accounts categories, balances or transactions. An account being listed does not mean its bank connection is currently working.
Returns: One page of accounts, each with id, account_name, vendor and type (such as bank or credit), plus has_more and next_cursor.
When to use: "Which accounts do we have in Finta?", or to find the acct_ ID of an account the user names.
Workflow: If has_more is true, call again with starting_after set to next_cursor, unchanged. Names can repeat or change, so refer to accounts by id.

tools_if_shown.name: list_cards
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: List the company's individual corporate cards from Brex, Ramp, Mercury, Slash and Rho, with their stable card_ IDs.
Not for: Bank accounts or card accounts, which list_accounts returns. Plaid credit cards appear there as accounts, not here. A card being listed does not mean its integration is currently working.
Returns: One page of cards, each with id, account_id, name, last_four, type (physical or virtual) and status (active or inactive), plus has_more and next_cursor. Inactive and deleted cards are included. Every field but id can be null when it isn't known; Rho cards always have a null account_id, last_four, type and status. Rho cards are known only from their past transactions, so a Rho card that has never been used is missing: when the company uses Rho, don't present the list as every card it has.
When to use: "Which cards do we have?", "Which card ends in 4821?", or to find the card_ ID of a card the user names.
Workflow: Pass account_id from list_accounts to list only the cards linked to that account. Ramp and Rho cards are never linked to an account, so they appear only without account_id, and an empty filtered list doesn't mean the account has no cards. If has_more is true, call again with starting_after set to next_cursor, unchanged, and the same account_id. Names can repeat or be missing, so match on last_four when the user gives it, and refer to cards by id.

tools_if_shown.name: bulk_update_transactions
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Make the same change to many transactions at once, up to 5,000, chosen by txn_ IDs or by filters: such as recategorizing every AWS charge, or moving a quarter's accounting dates by a month.
Not for: Different changes for different transactions; call update_transaction for each. Changing future transactions; a rule does that.
Returns: The job: id, status (queued, processing, success or failed), matched_count (null until the transactions are selected), updated_count, and errors (a page of failures, each with transaction_id, code, param and message). The job is all or nothing: a failed job changes no transactions, and errors say why.
When to use: "Recategorize all our Gusto transactions as Payroll", "Set the department to Engineering on every GitHub charge this year".
Workflow: Preview the selection with search_transactions using the same filters, then confirm the change and how many transactions it touches with the user before calling. To change the transactions from one account or card, find them with search_transactions and pass their transaction_ids. Pass exactly one of transaction_ids or filters, plus updates. This tool waits about 20 seconds for the job; if status is still queued or processing, call again with only job_id to check on it. A failed job with more than one page of errors has errors.has_more; pass job_id with starting_after set to errors.next_cursor for the next page. Calling again with the same transaction_ids or filters and updates within an hour of the first call returns the job that call started instead of starting another, so a retry is safe; after that, the same request runs again and picks up transactions that match now. With accounting_shift, the same request returns the first job for 30 days after it finishes, so dates never move twice; if that job comes back when the user meant to shift again, tell them.
Rules: Filters all must match, and select transactions by their values before the update. Split transactions are never selected by filters, and naming one in transaction_ids fails the job. In updates, null clears department_id or spread, or restores the original accounting date; merchant and category_id can't be null; accounting_date and accounting_shift can't be used together.

tools_if_shown.name: get_transaction
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Get one transaction by its txn_ ID.
Not for: Finding transactions by merchant, date or amount; search_transactions does that. The journal entries a transaction created.
Returns: id, date, accounting_date (the date reports use), amount_cents, currency, merchant, description, category_id and category_name, categorized, department_id and department_name, transaction_type (standard, transfer or split), source (vendor, type and account_name), status (approved or pending), spread, transfer_id, created and updated. amount_cents is signed integer cents: positive for money in, negative for money out, so divide by 100 for dollars.
When to use: To check a transaction's current state, such as after updating it, or when the user gives a txn_ ID.

tools_if_shown.name: list_merchants
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: List the company's merchants and counterparties: the distinct names recorded in one category and every category under it, across all time.
Not for: Amounts or rankings; get_category_total gives a merchant's total, or with group_by merchant ranks merchants by amount a page at a time, so a top 10 of vendors or customers is one call and the full ranking continues while has_more is true. Never call get_category_total once per merchant. Names have no IDs.
Returns: One page of names, sorted alphabetically ignoring case, each exactly as recorded, plus has_more and next_cursor. Newly imported names can take a little while to appear.
When to use: "List my merchants", "Who are our vendors?", "Which vendors do we pay for software?", "Who pays us?", or to find the exact spelling of a merchant name before filtering by it.
Workflow: Get category_id from list_categories. For the vendors the company has expensed, use the top-level Expenses category (parent_id null); for everyone the company has income from, the top-level Income category; for a narrower list, a category under them, such as Software. A vendor paid only for purchases recorded as assets, such as capitalized equipment, appears under that asset category instead. Use names exactly as returned, case included, as the merchant in get_category_total or search_journal_entries. If has_more is true, call again with the same category_id and starting_after set to next_cursor, unchanged.

tools_if_shown.name: list_spreads
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: List the company's spreads, the amounts recognized evenly over several months instead of all at once, as the Spreads page in Finta shows them. This includes spreads on one line of a split transaction, which search_transactions can't show.
Not for: The monthly amounts a spread books, which are journal entries (search_journal_entries with source_type spread). Spreads still awaiting approval, which aren't listed. Totals of any kind, which get_category_total returns.
Returns: One page of spreads, newest date first, plus has_more and next_cursor. Each has transaction_id, split, months, date, accounting_date, amount_cents, currency, merchant, category_id and category_name, department_id and department_name. When split is true, the spread is on one line of the split transaction named by transaction_id, and the amount, category and dates are that line's. Spreads have no ID of their own. amount_cents is signed integer cents: negative for money out, so divide by 100 for dollars.
When to use: "Which transactions are spread?", "List our spreads", "Is this charge spread, and over how many months?".
Workflow: Pass a txn_ ID as transaction_id for the spreads on that transaction or on its split lines. All filters must match. If has_more is true, call again with the same filters and starting_after set to next_cursor, unchanged.

tools_if_shown.name: list_transaction_splits
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: List the lines of the company's split transactions: the parts one bank or card transaction was divided into, each with its own amount, category, department and spread.
Not for: The split transactions themselves, which search_transactions returns with transaction_type split at their full amount. Department splits and payroll bulk splits, which aren't listed. Totals of any kind, which get_category_total returns.
Returns: One page of lines, newest date first, plus has_more and next_cursor. Each has transaction_id (the split transaction it belongs to), date, accounting_date, amount_cents, currency, merchant, category_id and category_name, department_id and department_name, and spread (months, or null). Lines have no ID of their own. amount_cents is signed integer cents: negative for money out, so divide by 100 for dollars. A split's lines add up to its amount.
When to use: "What was this charge split into?", "Show me all our split transactions with their breakdown", "Which split lines are spread?".
Workflow: To break down one split, pass its txn_ ID as transaction_id. To see every split's lines, omit it and page through: that's one list, not one call per split. All filters must match. If has_more is true, call again with the same filters and starting_after set to next_cursor, unchanged.

tools_if_shown.name: search_transactions
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Find the company's bank, card and reimbursement transactions in Finta by date, merchant, amount, category, source or status, with their stable txn_ IDs.
Not for: Accounting-level debits and credits, which are journal entries. Totals of any kind, including what was spent with or received from one merchant ("What did we pay Justwork last year?"): get_category_total returns the exact figure in one call, while a page of transactions isn't a total and adding up pages is slow and easy to get wrong.
Returns: One page of transactions, newest date first, plus has_more and next_cursor. Each has id, date, accounting_date (the date reports use), amount_cents, currency, merchant, description, category_id and category_name, categorized, department_id and department_name, transaction_type (standard, transfer or split), source (vendor, type and account_name), status (approved or pending), spread and transfer_id. amount_cents is signed integer cents: positive for money in, negative for money out, so divide by 100 for dollars.
When to use: "Show me our AWS charges from last month", "Show me our uncategorized transactions", "Find the $35.27 charge", or to find the txn_ ID of a transaction the user describes.
Workflow: All filters must match. If the user doesn't say whether an amount is money in or out, search both signs. Uncategorized transactions still have a category_id (Uncategorized Income or Uncategorized Expenses), so use categorized: false to find them. If has_more is true, call again with the same filters and starting_after set to next_cursor, unchanged.

tools_if_shown.name: update_transaction
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Change one transaction's merchant, category, department, accounting date or spread.
Not for: Making the same change to many transactions; bulk_update_transactions does that in one call. Changing future transactions; a rule does that.
Returns: The updated transaction, with the same fields as get_transaction.
When to use: "Categorize this charge as Software", "Move this invoice to March", "Spread this annual subscription over 12 months".
Workflow: Find the transaction with search_transactions. Get category_id from list_categories and department_id from list_departments, where assignable is true. Send only the fields to change. All of them apply together, or none do if one fails. If the user will want the same change on future transactions, offer to create a rule.

tools_if_shown.name: upload_transactions
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Add bank or credit card transactions from a file or pasted data to one Finta account.
Not for: Changing transactions already in Finta, or accounts that sync automatically unless the user confirms the sync is broken.
Returns: Validation for every row sent so far (errors, warnings, open_questions, ready_to_commit, next_step, summary in dollars), or the import result after a commit, including a url where the user can review or undo the upload.
When to use: "Add these transactions", "import this statement", "upload our Chase CSV".
Workflow: list_accounts, then create_account if no account matches, then call this tool with rows in chunks of up to 500, resolve what each result reports, and finish with commit: true once ready_to_commit is true. Nothing is visible in Finta until the commit. If the commit returns status importing, call again with only upload_id to check on it; that changes nothing.
Rules: Parse the whole file yourself and send every row, including rows you leave out, which you mark in exclude with a reason. Compute file_totals from the file itself. Pass dates exactly as the file writes them. Send amounts as plain signed decimals such as -45.00: convert accounting notation like (45.00) to -45.00 and drop currency symbols, but don't otherwise flip signs; if the file shows charges as positive, keep them and set sign_convention. Buying or selling investments doesn't change cash, so exclude those rows, but keep interest and dividends. Exclude a charge and its reversal together. Acknowledge a blocking warning only after checking the rows it lists, and mention acknowledged possible duplicates to the user. Answer open questions from the file and context, and ask the user only when you can't tell; otherwise use the suggested default. After committing, tell the user what was uploaded, what was left out and why, and give them the url.

tools_if_shown.name: get_balance_sheet
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Get the company's balance sheet as of one date: cash, assets, liabilities and equity.
Not for: Activity over a period, such as revenue or spending (get_income_statement) or cash movement (get_cash_flow). One section on its own; the full statement always comes back.
Returns: date is the exact inclusive cutoff used, with currency, refreshed_at, cash_cents, assets and liabilities (each with total_cents and categories), equity (total_cents, categories and retained_earnings), and liabilities_and_equity_cents, which equals assets.total_cents. Each category has category_id, name, balance_cents, position and parent_category_id. Amounts are integer cents, so divide by 100 for dollars.
When to use: "How much cash do we have?", "What were our total liabilities at the end of June?", "Show me the balance sheet".
Dates and source: Calendar dates use America/Los_Angeles (Pacific Time); balances include all activity through the exact date. Whole months use whole-month rollups. A cutoff of today uses fresh current-month month-to-date (MTD) rollups for month-start through today. Other non-month-end cutoffs use slower raw-entry reads for just the cutoff month. Stale or unfilled MTD safely falls back to raw entries; reported balances are unchanged.
Freshness: refreshed_at covers the entire report through its exact cutoff. For rollup-only reads it is the maximum contributing rollup timestamp, including MTD. Any live raw portion is current as of the call, even when no raw entries match. It is null only when no contributing timestamp or live raw read is available.
Workflow: Omit date for today in Pacific Time. A parent category's amount already includes its children, so to total a section, add only the categories whose parent_category_id is null, or use the section's total_cents.

tools_if_shown.name: get_cash_flow
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Get the company's cash flow statement for one date range: cash from operating, investing and financing activities, and cash at the start and end.
Not for: Profit and loss (get_income_statement) or balances on a date (get_balance_sheet). One section on its own; the full statement always comes back.
Returns: start_date and end_date are the exact inclusive dates used, with currency, refreshed_at, operating_activities, investing_activities and financing_activities (each with total_cents and categories), beginning_cash_cents, ending_cash_cents and change_in_cash_cents. Each category has category_id, name, amount_cents, position and parent_category_id. Amounts are signed integer cents, so divide by 100 for dollars.
When to use: "How much cash did we burn last quarter?", "Where did our cash go this year?", "What was our operating cash flow in August?"
Dates and source: Calendar dates use America/Los_Angeles (Pacific Time), and both boundaries are honored exactly, inclusive. Whole months use whole-month rollups. Current-month start through today uses fresh month-to-date (MTD) rollups, keeping month-aligned month-to-date and year-to-date requests fast. Other partial months, including a midmonth start, use slower raw-entry reads for just those months. Stale or unfilled MTD safely falls back to raw entries; the report's numerical semantics are unchanged.
Freshness: refreshed_at covers the entire report, including partial months and opening and closing balances. For rollup-only reads it is the maximum contributing rollup timestamp, including MTD. Any live raw portion is current as of the call, even when no raw entries match. It is null only when no contributing timestamp or live raw read is available.
Workflow: Omit both dates for the current quarter to date in Pacific Time. One call covers one period; for a month-by-month view, call once per month. Operating activities include the groups "Changes in Working Capital" and "Non-Cash Expenses", whose IDs start with grp_ rather than cat_. A parent's amount already includes its children, so to total a section, add only the entries whose parent_category_id is null, or use the section's total_cents.

tools_if_shown.name: get_category_total
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Get an exact total in one call: for a category and everything under it, or for one merchant, over an inclusive date range or as of an exact date. Or split that total in one call by merchant, ranked, or by month.
Not for: The whole income statement or balance sheet; the report tools return those. Listing individual transactions or entries; never add those up yourself for a total or a ranking.
Returns: Without group_by: total_cents, debit_cents, credit_cents, currency, point_in_time, the exact dates used and refreshed_at. With group_by: data, a list of rows, each with merchant (null for activity recorded without one) or month, and total_cents, debit_cents and credit_cents, plus the dates used, refreshed_at, has_more and next_cursor. Amounts are signed integer cents, so divide by 100 for dollars: assets are debits minus credits, and every other category is credits minus debits, so expenses come out negative. For a balance sheet category, each month row is cumulative through that month's closing date, with the last calendar month's cutoff at end_date, so never add month rows up for it.
When to use: "How much did we spend on software this year?", "What's our total for OpenAI, all time?", "Which vendors do we spend the most on?", "Who are our top 10 customers?", "What did we pay AWS each month?", "Which month did we spend the most?", "What was our accounts receivable balance at the end of June?"
Dates: All dates are calendar dates in America/Los_Angeles (Pacific Time). Periodic totals include exactly start_date through end_date, inclusive; point-in-time totals include all activity through the exact date. This replaces the old behavior that ignored the day. For group_by month, periodic first and last rows are clipped to the exact range; point-in-time start_date selects the first displayed month without excluding earlier cumulative activity, and the last calendar month's cutoff is end_date. Whole months use whole-month rollups. Current-month start through today uses fresh month-to-date (MTD) rollups, so month-aligned month-to-date and year-to-date requests stay fast. Other partial months, including a midmonth start, use slower raw-entry reads for just those months. Stale or unfilled MTD safely falls back to raw entries.
Freshness: refreshed_at covers the whole total or returned page, including partial months, not only full months. For rollup-only reads it is the maximum contributing rollup timestamp, including MTD. Any live raw portion is current as of the call, even when no raw entries match. It is null only when no contributing timestamp or live raw read is available.
Workflow: Get category_id and point_in_time from list_categories. When point_in_time is false (income statement categories), pass start_date and end_date; when it's true (balance sheet categories), pass date only, except with group_by month, which always takes start_date and end_date. For vendors use the top-level Expenses category (parent_id null), and for customers the top-level Income category. group_by merchant ranks merchants: order desc, the default, puts the biggest first in the category's own direction (most spent under Expenses, most received under Income), and asc the smallest first; limit takes that many rows from the top, so limit 10 is a top 10. group_by month gives one row per month, up to 120 months, oldest first unless you set order. If has_more is true and you need more rows, call again with the same arguments and starting_after set to next_cursor, unchanged. Merchant names are exact as recorded, so one vendor can appear under several spellings: combine obvious variants and say you did. For one merchant's total, pass merchant, matching the name exactly, including case, from list_merchants or a group_by merchant row. If you don't know the exact spelling, find it with one search_transactions call using merchant and a small limit, then pass the name exactly as it appears there; the total still comes from this tool. Expenses and Income cover every category under them, but not purchases recorded as assets, such as capitalized equipment or the part of a prepaid plan not yet expensed, so a vendor's total can be less than what was paid; say so when it matters. For all time, start at the company's incorporation date from get_company and end today in Pacific Time. Use as few calls as the question needs: a total is one call without group_by, so add group_by only when the question asks for a ranking or a month-by-month breakdown.

tools_if_shown.name: get_income_statement
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Get the company's income statement (profit and loss) for one date range: revenue, expenses, operating income, non-operating income, taxes and net income. Use group_by=department for the GAAP P&L; group_by=category is the default.
Not for: Balances on a date (get_balance_sheet) or cash movement (get_cash_flow). One category on its own; the full statement always comes back.
Returns: start_date and end_date are the exact inclusive dates used, with currency, refreshed_at, operating_income_cents and net_income_cents, plus one top-level field per section: revenue, expenses and non_operating_income always, and uncategorized_income and taxes only when the company has those rows. With category grouping, uncategorized_expenses is also present when the company has that row. The response echoes group_by. With category grouping, each section has total_cents and categories. Each category has category_id, name, amount_cents, position and parent_category_id. Amounts are signed integer cents: income is positive and expenses are negative, so divide by 100 for dollars.
Department grouping: Expenses have total_cents and rows instead of categories. Each row has row_id, parent_row_id, kind (department, category, or group), nullable department_id and category_id, name, amount_cents and position. Parent amounts include their children. No Department is an assignment group, not uncategorized expenses. Revenue, non-operating income, optional uncategorized income and taxes keep their category format. Department grouping has no top-level uncategorized_expenses field, requires the departments feature and returns refreshed_at=null.
When to use: "What was our net income last quarter?", "How much revenue did we make in September?", "What are our biggest expenses this year?"
Dates and source: Calendar dates use America/Los_Angeles (Pacific Time), and both boundaries are honored exactly, inclusive. With category grouping, whole months use whole-month rollups. Current-month start through today uses fresh month-to-date (MTD) rollups, keeping month-aligned month-to-date and year-to-date requests fast. Other partial months, including a midmonth start, use slower raw-entry reads for just those months. Stale or unfilled MTD safely falls back to raw entries; the report's numerical semantics are unchanged.
Category freshness: refreshed_at covers the entire report, including partial months. For rollup-only reads it is the maximum contributing rollup timestamp, including MTD. Any live raw portion is current as of the call, even when no raw entries match. It is null only when no contributing timestamp or live raw read is available.
Workflow: Omit both dates for the current quarter to date in Pacific Time. One call covers one period; for a month-by-month view, call once per month. A parent category's amount already includes its children, so to total a section, add only the categories whose parent_category_id is null, or use the section's total_cents.

tools_if_shown.name: search_journal_entries
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Find the company's journal entries, the debits and credits behind its reports, by date, category, merchant, department, transaction or source, with their stable je_ IDs.
Not for: Bank and card activity as it came in, which search_transactions returns. Totals of any kind, including one merchant's total: get_category_total returns the exact figure in one call, while adding up entries page by page is slow and easy to get wrong.
Returns: One page of entries, newest date first, plus has_more and next_cursor. Each has id, date, merchant, amount_cents, type (debit or credit), currency, category_id and category_name, department_id, transaction_id and source_type. amount_cents is always positive integer cents, so use type for the direction and divide by 100 for dollars.
When to use: "Which entries make up our Software expense in September?", "What did this transaction post to the ledger?", "Show me the spread entries for our annual insurance".
Workflow: Filters all must match. Get category_id from list_categories and department_id from list_departments. transaction_id returns every entry the transaction created, including its split lines' and its spread and capitalization entries. source_type split covers only department splits and payroll bulk splits: a transaction split into lines with their own categories posts transaction entries. merchant must match the name exactly, including case. If has_more is true, call again with the same filters and starting_after set to next_cursor, unchanged.

tools_if_shown.name: create_rule
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Create an automation rule, so transactions that match its conditions get a merchant, category, department, spread or accounting-date offset automatically.
Not for: A one-off change to transactions; update those directly. Creating categories or departments.
Returns: The saved rule: id, conditions and actions.
When to use: "Always categorize AWS as Hosting", "From now on, put Gusto under Payroll" (future only, so apply_to_existing_transactions: false).
Workflow: Get IDs from list_categories, list_departments, list_accounts and list_cards, and check list_rules for a rule that already does this. Confirm the conditions and actions with the user, and ask whether the rule should also change transactions already in Finta; apply_to_existing_transactions is required, so pass their answer, or false when they asked only about the future. With true, the rule also runs in the background on matching transactions already in Finta: approved ones that are uncategorized, never pending ones; and only if the rule sets a department, also any matching transaction without a department, pending ones included. It never replaces a department already set, or the category or merchant of an approved transaction that's already categorized. A pending transaction it selects does take the rule's category and merchant, replacing any it has, so when the rule sets a department along with either, say so before the user decides. It needs Transactions: Manage. A saved rule doesn't mean that run has finished. If the API answers rule_already_exists, its message names the existing rule; use that rule rather than creating another.
Rules: merchant matches the merchant name Finta assigned, and description matches the bank's description, both ignoring case. transaction_type can only be "transfer".

tools_if_shown.name: delete_rule
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Delete an automation rule so it stops applying to new transactions.
Not for: Undoing everything the rule did. Transactions the rule categorized can have their categories reset to the default, while matched transfers keep theirs; other changes the rule made stay.
Returns: deleted: true and the rule's id. A rule that was already deleted, or that doesn't exist, returns the same.
When to use: "Delete the AWS rule", "That rule keeps miscategorizing things, remove it".
Workflow: Find the rule with list_rules, show the user its conditions and actions, and get their confirmation before deleting. Deleting needs both Accounting setup: Manage and Transactions: Manage. If the API answers rule_busy, the rule is running on existing transactions; wait a little and try again.

tools_if_shown.name: list_rules
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: List the company's automation rules, which match incoming transactions by their conditions and set a merchant, category, department, spread or accounting date, with their stable rule_ IDs.
Not for: Running rules or changing transactions; reading rules changes nothing. Rules Finta manages itself, and rules that belong to a category or department, aren't listed.
Returns: One page of rules, newest first, each with id, conditions and actions, plus has_more and next_cursor. A transaction must match every condition. Only the actions a rule sets are present. amount_cents conditions are signed integer cents, negative for money out, so -5000 is a $50.00 charge.
When to use: "What rules do we have?", "Is there a rule for AWS?", or to find a rule's rule_ ID before update_rule or delete_rule.
Workflow: There is no search, so page through and read the conditions. If has_more is true, call again with starting_after set to next_cursor, unchanged. Conditions on account or card_name text are older rules; new rules can't use them. category_id and department_id are the IDs list_categories and list_departments return.

tools_if_shown.name: update_rule
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Change an automation rule's conditions or actions.
Not for: Fixing transactions the rule already touched. An update affects only transactions matched from now on; it never re-runs the rule on existing transactions.
Returns: The complete saved rule: id, conditions and actions.
When to use: "Make the AWS rule only match charges over $100", "Change the Gusto rule to put it under Benefits".
Workflow: Find the rule and its current definition with list_rules, and confirm the change with the user. conditions replaces the whole list, so send every condition the rule should keep; omit conditions to leave them as they are. actions changes only the keys you send: set a key to null to remove that action, and omit keys to keep them. The rule must still have at least one condition and one action. If the API answers rule_busy, the rule is running on existing transactions; wait a little and try again.

tools_if_shown.name: connect_integration
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Start connecting a bank or card provider to Finta, or reconnecting one whose status is requires_reconnect, by getting the link the user opens to approve access.
Not for: Integrations whose api_connectable is false in list_integrations; the user connects those in the Finta web app under Settings -> Integrations. Checking whether a connection finished; use get_integration_connection.
Returns: A connect_request with status pending and url, the provider's single-use authorization page, valid until expires_at (Unix seconds). intent is reconnect when it re-authenticates an existing connection.
When to use: "Connect our Mercury account", "Hook up Brex", "Our Ramp connection needs reconnecting".
Workflow: Check list_integrations first for the key and api_connectable. If you can open links in the user's own browser and they allow it, open url; otherwise show it to them. It only works in a browser where they are signed in to Finta as themselves. Never fill in or click through the provider's page: the approval has to come from the user. Ask them to tell you once they've approved, then call get_integration_connection. Calling this again returns the same open link; after a request fails or expires, it starts a new one.

tools_if_shown.name: get_integration_connection
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Check how a connection started with connect_integration is going.
Not for: Starting a connection; use connect_integration. The status of integrations in general; list_integrations returns that.
Returns: The latest connect_request you started for this integration. status is pending until the user approves at the provider, authorizing while Finta finishes the connection, then complete or failed, or expired when nobody finished the link before expires_at. failure_code says why a failed request failed: access_denied (the user declined), provider_admin_required (the approving account isn't a provider admin), provider_error or connection_failed.
When to use: After the user says they've approved access at the provider. "Did the Mercury connection go through?"
Workflow: Call it once the user says they've approved, not in a loop while they're still at the provider. If it's pending, the user hasn't finished approving; ask them to finish before checking again. If it's authorizing, Finta needs a few more seconds; check once more. If it failed, tell the user why; if they want to retry, call connect_integration for a new link. A request that failed or expired stays here until a new one starts.

tools_if_shown.name: list_integrations
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: List the integrations Finta offers this company, such as banks, cards, payroll, revenue and cap table providers, and whether each one is connected.
Not for: The accounts or cards an integration brings in; list_accounts and list_cards return those. Connecting or reconnecting an integration; connect_integration does that.
Returns: Every integration in one response. Each has key (such as mercury, ramp or carta), name, type (banking, cap_table, payroll, revenue, notifications or legal) and status: connected, not_connected, connecting, or requires_reconnect when a connection that used to work needs the user to sign in to the provider again. api_connectable says whether connect_integration can start a connection; when it's false, the user connects it in the Finta web app.
When to use: "Is our Brex connected?", "Which banks feed Finta?", "Why did our Mercury transactions stop coming in?"
Workflow: Most integrations are not_connected, so filter by status when the user asks what's connected. When an integration is requires_reconnect, its data stops updating until it's reconnected: offer to reconnect it with connect_integration when api_connectable is true, otherwise tell the user to reconnect it in Finta.

tools_if_shown.name: create_invoice
tools_if_shown.description:
Not available to this company yet (early access: invoices). Contact Finta to request access.
Purpose: Record an invoice the company already sent a customer, which books its revenue: Accounts Receivable for the total, and revenue for each line item.
Not for: Sending an invoice; Finta doesn't send anything to customers. Recording a payment; once the money arrives, use match_invoice_payment.
Returns: The recorded invoice, status open, with its inv_ ID. Amounts in it are integer cents, so divide by 100 for dollars.
When to use: "Record this invoice" (from a PDF or another billing system), "We invoiced Globex $12,000 for an annual contract today".
Workflow: Get revenue category IDs from list_categories, or omit category_id for the company's default revenue category. Use the invoice's own date, customer name and amounts. spread_months recognizes a line's revenue monthly instead of on the invoice date, such as 12 for an annual contract billed up front; ask the user when the invoice doesn't say. If the API answers invoice_already_exists, the invoice is already recorded under the ID in the message: tell the user rather than creating it again. A date in a tax year the company finished with Finta is refused (closed_books).
Rules: Amounts are in dollars, such as "12000.00". A line item's amount is negative for a refund, which can't be spread. Discounts and customer balance credits reduce the total and tax adds to it; give each as a positive amount, at most one of each kind. The total must be more than 0.

tools_if_shown.name: get_invoice
tools_if_shown.description:
Not available to this company yet (early access: invoices). Contact Finta to request access.
Purpose: Get one invoice by its inv_ ID, with the bank deposit that paid it.
Not for: Finding invoices by customer, status or amount; list_invoices does that.
Returns: invoice, the same object list_invoices returns, and paid_transaction: for a paid invoice, the matched deposit as get_transaction returns it (null while the invoice is open or voided, or when the deposit can't be read, such as one deleted after it was matched). Amounts are integer cents, so divide by 100 for dollars.
When to use: "Did Acme pay invoice inv_…?", "When was this invoice paid?", or to check an invoice after create_invoice, void_invoice or match_invoice_payment.

tools_if_shown.name: list_invoices
tools_if_shown.description:
Not available to this company yet (early access: invoices). Contact Finta to request access.
Purpose: Find the company's invoices: ones it sent its customers and recorded in Finta so their revenue is booked, with their inv_ IDs.
Not for: Sending invoices or reminders; Finta doesn't send anything to customers.
Returns: One page of invoices, newest invoice date first, plus has_more and next_cursor. Each has id, status (open, paid or voided), customer_name, invoice_date, amount_cents (the total due), currency, line_items, adjustments, paid_transaction_id and paid_date (set once a bank deposit is matched as its payment), source (manual or stripe) and stripe_url. Amounts are integer cents, so divide by 100 for dollars.
When to use: "What invoices are still open?", "What does Acme owe us?", "Which invoice did this deposit pay?" (pass paid_transaction_id), "Which open invoice is this $4,500 deposit for?" (status open and amount "4500.00"), or to check an invoice isn't already recorded before create_invoice.
Workflow: Filters combine; all must match. If has_more is true, call again with the same filters and starting_after set to next_cursor, unchanged.

tools_if_shown.name: match_invoice_payment
tools_if_shown.description:
Not available to this company yet (early access: invoices). Contact Finta to request access.
Purpose: Record a bank deposit as the payment for an open invoice, which marks the invoice paid. With unmatch: true, undo that.
Not for: Recording a payment that isn't in Finta's bank transactions; wait until the deposit syncs. Partial payments: the deposit must be for the invoice's exact total.
Returns: The invoice, status paid with paid_transaction_id and paid_date; or, after unmatching, status open.
When to use: "Acme paid their invoice", "This $4,500 deposit is the Globex invoice", "That payment was matched to the wrong invoice" (unmatch, then match the right one).
Workflow: To find the deposit for an invoice, call search_transactions with the invoice's total as a positive amount in dollars, source_type bank and transaction_type standard; add a start_date around the invoice date if there are several. To find the invoice for a deposit, call list_invoices with status open and the deposit's amount. Matching changes the deposit: it takes the invoice's revenue category, its accounting date becomes the invoice date, and unmatching later returns it to Uncategorized Income rather than its previous category. So if the deposit is already categorized, tell the user what will change and get their confirmation first. Split deposits are refused; the user can match those in the Finta app. Matching and unmatching need Transactions: Manage as well as Invoices: Manage.

tools_if_shown.name: void_invoice
tools_if_shown.description:
Not available to this company yet (early access: invoices). Contact Finta to request access.
Purpose: Void an open invoice, removing the revenue and Accounts Receivable it booked. It can't be undone.
Not for: A paid invoice; the API refuses it (invoice_not_open), so unmatch its payment with match_invoice_payment first. Correcting an invoice; void it and record the correct one with create_invoice.
Returns: The invoice, status voided.
When to use: "That invoice was canceled", "Void the duplicate Acme invoice".
Workflow: Find the invoice with list_invoices, show the user which one it is, and get their confirmation before voiding.

tools_if_shown.name: create_file_upload
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Get a one-time URL to upload a PDF of a tax return or Delaware franchise tax report the company already filed, and the file_id it becomes.
Not for: Anything but PDFs, or sending the PDF itself; this tool only prepares the upload.
Returns: file_id, url, method (PUT), headers to send with the PUT, and expires_at; the url works for 10 minutes.
When to use: Before upload_income_tax_return or upload_delaware_franchise_tax_report, when the user has the filed PDF on this computer.
Workflow: Get an upload URL with this tool, PUT the PDF, then call the upload tool with the file ID. Compute size with `wc -c < FILE` and checksum with `openssl md5 -binary FILE | base64`. PUT from a terminal with every returned header, such as curl --fail -X PUT --upload-file FILE -H "Content-Type: application/pdf" -H "Content-MD5: <checksum>" -H "Content-Disposition: <Content-Disposition from headers>" "<url>". For a company with no records for that year, upload the return first, then the Delaware report.
Rules: One URL per PDF. The file must be attached within 24 hours and attaches once; a PUT can't change it, since storage only accepts bytes matching size and checksum.

tools_if_shown.name: search_1099s
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Search the company's tracked vendor 1099 filing records, or retrieve one by its f1099_ ID, including available W-9 and 1099 documents.
Not for: Generating or filing forms, sending W-9 requests, changing records, determining legal obligations, or income/franchise returns (use search_taxes).
Returns: data, has_more, next_cursor and summaries. Filter searches include annual filing status and counts for complete reports selected by year, independent of other filters or pagination. ID lookups return one record and summaries: []; search by year for annual summaries.
When to use: "Are our 2025 1099s filed?", "Which vendors need a W-9?", or to refresh a known record's document links.
Workflow: Pass id alone, or omit id and use filters/pagination. Omit year for all years. Filters combine with AND; comma-separated statuses combine with OR. Continue with unchanged filters and next_cursor as starting_after; never sum repeated summaries across pages. Names can repeat, so counts describe records, not unique recipients. Missing reports are unknown; not_required reflects tracked records, not legal obligations. Read filing_status for progress even without PDFs. Links expire after five minutes; search again by id to refresh them. forms_not_ready means retry later.

tools_if_shown.name: search_tax_credits
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Search the company's tracked federal R&D credits by tax year and claim status, or retrieve one by its tcred_ ID.
Not for: Determining eligibility, calculating or claiming credits, submitting payroll credits, filing progress (use search_taxes), or 1099s.
Returns: data, has_more and next_cursor, with credit amounts, amount_basis, income-tax and payroll allocations, and payroll_submission (provider and status). Amounts are integer cents; divide by 100 for dollars. Null means unknown, never zero.
When to use: "How much R&D credit do we have for 2025?", "Was it claimed?", or "Does payroll submission need action?"
Workflow: Pass id alone for one record, or omit id and use filters/pagination. Omit year for all years. Filters combine with AND. Continue with the same filters and next_cursor as starting_after. State amount_basis when reporting amounts. claimed concerns the tax return; payroll_submission.status separately describes submission recorded in Finta, not provider acceptance or a refund received.

tools_if_shown.name: search_taxes
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Search the company's income and Delaware franchise tax filings by filters, or retrieve one by its public ID.
Not for: 1099s (use search_1099s), R&D credits (use search_tax_credits), calculating tax owed, or filing or changing returns.
Returns: data, has_more and next_cursor, with filing progress, covered and unmapped jurisdictions, filing/extension timestamps, and available PDF links. Income jurisdictions share one filing record; status does not establish authority acceptance or tax payment.
When to use: "Have we filed our 2025 taxes?", "Which returns need review?", or to refresh a known filing's document links.
Workflow: Pass id alone for one record, or omit id and use filters/pagination. Omit year for all years. Filters combine with AND. Continue with the same filters and next_cursor as starting_after. Links expire after five minutes; search again by id to refresh them. Read filing_status, not PDF availability, for progress. Preserve unmapped_jurisdictions; taxes_not_ready means retry later.

tools_if_shown.name: upload_delaware_franchise_tax_report
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Record a Delaware franchise tax and annual report the company already filed outside Finta, with its PDF, exactly as uploading it on the Taxes page does.
Not for: Income tax returns (use upload_income_tax_return), or reports Finta is filing.
Returns: The year's Delaware franchise tax record, marked filed, with the PDF in documents.
When to use: "Upload our Delaware report", or moving a customer's filed reports from another provider into Finta.
Workflow: Get an upload URL with create_file_upload, PUT the PDF, then call this tool with the file ID. For a company with no records for that year, upload the return first, then the Delaware report.
Rules: Only available when the Taxes page offers declaring that year externally filed or adding a missing confirmation to a known external filing. Never replaces an existing PDF, changes a Finta report being prepared, with payment authorized or filing underway/already completed, or changes another tax year. Filling a missing external confirmation preserves the filing date. tax_year is the year the report covers, not the year it was filed. A 409 tax_upload_not_allowed is final for that filing state; do not upload a fresh file to bypass it.

tools_if_shown.name: upload_income_tax_return
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Record an income tax return the company already filed outside Finta, with its PDF, exactly as uploading it on the Taxes page does.
Not for: Delaware franchise tax reports (use upload_delaware_franchise_tax_report; this tool refuses them), returns Finta is preparing, or years other than last year and the year before.
Returns: The year's income tax record, marked filed, with the PDF in documents.
When to use: "Upload our 2025 return", or moving a customer's filed returns from another provider into Finta.
Workflow: Get an upload URL with create_file_upload, PUT the PDF, then call this tool with the file ID. For a company with no records for that year, upload the return first, then the Delaware report.
Rules: Only available when the Taxes page offers the income upload for that year. Creates a new income filing; never replaces a document or changes an existing Finta workflow. May create a missing externally filed Delaware record for the same year only when its filing status is already confirmed. Never starts Delaware preparation; existing records and other years remain untouched. Confirm the year, preparer and states with the user if the PDF doesn't make them clear. A 409 tax_upload_not_allowed is final for that filing state; do not upload a fresh file to bypass it.

tools_if_shown.name: submit_feedback
tools_if_shown.description:
Purpose: Send a question, feedback or bug report to Finta support, either for the user or on your own about these Finta tools. It arrives as an email from the user, and support replies to them by email.
Not for: Changing data in Finta. Getting an answer in this conversation; replies come by email later.
Returns: The ticket id, type and reported_by.
When to use: The user asks, such as "Ask Finta whether you can import from QuickBooks", "Tell Finta the upload keeps failing" or "Report this as a bug" (reported_by: user). Or on your own (reported_by: agent) when a Finta tool fails unexpectedly or returns something that looks wrong, when a tool's description or inputs misled you, or when no Finta tool can do what the user asked.
Workflow: Write the message yourself from what the user said and what happened in this conversation, and send it right away; don't ask the user to write, format or approve a draft. Then tell the user in one line what you sent and, when they asked, that support will reply by email. When reporting on your own, send it once per issue and carry on with the user's task.
Rules: Never include passwords, API keys or full account numbers. In your own reports, also leave out amounts and the names of merchants, accounts, people and files.

detail_provenance.offline_parser_correction: Decoded escaped leading dollar literals and omitted Flight undefined properties; original HTML hash/timestamp retained.

published_auth_text: GraphOS MCP Server does not require authentication. It is a public MCP endpoint you can connect without logging in.

published_tools.source: published FAQ (same names as visible imported tool chips)

tools_if_shown.name: DeleteSubgraph
tools_if_shown.description: Remove a subgraph from a variant and start composition, the same write that `rover subgraph delete` performs. Returns the composition errors that the removal causes. This deletes the subgraph from the variant and can break the running router. Set dryRun to true first: the response then reports the composition result that the removal would produce, including updatedGateway, and deletes nothing. Provide the graph ID, the variant name, and the subgraph name.

tools_if_shown.name: GetSchemaChecks
tools_if_shown.description: List past schema checks for a graph: each check's ID, status, timestamps, the subgraph it checked, the variant it ran against, the commit, and the status of each task in the check, plus the total count for the filter. Use this to find a check, then pass its ID to GetCheckResults for failure details. Provide the graph ID. Optionally filter by status (PASSED, FAILED, PENDING), subgraph names, branches, variants, authors, or check IDs, and page with limit and offset.

tools_if_shown.name: GetPersistedQueryListStatus
tools_if_shown.description: Check whether a graph variant has a Persisted Query List (PQL), and return its ID, its name, and its current build (revision and operation count). Pass the ID to PublishPersistedQueries. Use to assess PQL configuration — a production variant with no PQL is a security gap. Provide the graph ID and variant name.

tools_if_shown.name: GetSupergraphSchema
tools_if_shown.description: Read the composed supergraph schema (SDL) for a graph variant, with the composition ID and any composition errors. This is the same read that `rover supergraph fetch` performs. A supergraph schema is the single schema that composition builds from every subgraph, and it carries federation directives that the API schema does not. The response holds the whole document and is not truncated, and a supergraph schema is larger than the API schema it produces. Expect the same order of size: a large federated graph exceeds 800,000 characters, roughly 200,000 tokens. A variant that is not federated has no composition result, and the tool returns null for it rather than an empty document. Provide the graph ID and the variant name.

tools_if_shown.name: ApolloDocsRead
tools_if_shown.description: Reads an Apollo documentation page by slug in chunks. Use slugs returned by ApolloDocsSearch.

tools_if_shown.name: GetCheckResults
tools_if_shown.description: Read the outcome of one schema check run: the overall status, and for each task in the run the composition errors, lint diagnostics, schema changes with the client operations they affect, downstream variant results, and custom check violations. Use this after GetSchemaChecks gives you a check ID. Provide the graph ID and the check ID. The affected operations are paged with affectedOperationsLimit and affectedOperationsOffset; the change list is capped by the server, and areChangesTruncated reports when that happened.

tools_if_shown.name: ApolloDocsSearch
tools_if_shown.description: Searches official Apollo documentation for GraphQL, GraphOS, Apollo Router, Apollo Client, MCP Server, schema design, deployment, and Connectors. Returns URLs, slugs, and excerpts.

tools_if_shown.name: ValidateOperations
tools_if_shown.description: Validate client GraphQL operations against a variant's published schema and return each problem's type (FAILURE, WARNING, INVALID), code, description, and the name of the operation it came from. This is the same check that `rover client check` runs. Nothing is published and no state changes. Provide the graph ID and the operations, each one a body and an optional name. Optionally name the variant to validate against; the default is "current".

tools_if_shown.name: PublishContract
tools_if_shown.description: Create or update a contract variant and start a launch for it, the same write that `rover contract publish` performs. A contract variant is a filtered view of another variant's schema, built by including and excluding schema elements by tag. The filter configuration replaces the previous one in full, so send the complete include and exclude lists rather than only the tags you want to change. The same applies to hideUnreachableTypes, which has no default: when you update a contract, pass the value it has now. GetContractConfig states that value in its description. Returns the contract variant and a link to the launch, or the error messages that stopped it. Provide the graph ID, the contract variant name, the source variant, the include and exclude tag lists, and whether to hide unreachable types.

tools_if_shown.name: PublishReadme
tools_if_shown.description: Replace the README of a graph variant, the same write that `rover readme publish` performs. The README is the Markdown document shown on the variant's page in GraphOS Studio. The new text replaces the whole README, so read the current one with GetReadme first if you intend to keep any of it. Provide the graph ID, the variant name, and the full README text.

tools_if_shown.name: GetLatestLaunch
tools_if_shown.description: Inspect the most recent launch for a graph variant: status, completion time, subgraph changes, composition errors, and a schema diff summary vs the previous launch (additions/removals/edits/deprecations plus affected operations). Use to assess schema composition health and the impact of recent schema changes. Also returns the latest approved launch for comparison. Provide the graph ID and variant name.

tools_if_shown.name: GetLaunch
tools_if_shown.description: Inspect a single launch by ID for full detail: status, timestamps, which subgraphs changed, composition errors, and the schema diff summary. Use to drill into a specific launch — e.g. a failed or superseded one found via GetLaunchHistory (pass its id here). Provide the graph ID, variant name, and launch ID.

tools_if_shown.name: LintSchema
tools_if_shown.description: Lint a GraphQL schema document against the graph's lint rules and return each diagnostic's coordinate, severity level, message, rule, and source location, plus the error, warning, total, and ignored counts. This is the same check that `rover graph lint` and `rover subgraph lint` run. Nothing is published and no state changes. Provide the graph ID and the schema as SDL. Optionally provide baseSdl to report only the diagnostics that the new schema introduces against that base.

tools_if_shown.name: ApolloConnectorsSpec
tools_if_shown.description: Returns the Apollo Connectors specification for guidance on creating or modifying GraphQL schemas that use @connect or @source.

tools_if_shown.name: GetLintResults
tools_if_shown.description: Retrieve schema lint violations from a graph's most recent schema checks: each diagnostic's coordinate, severity level, message, rule, and source location, plus error/warning/total/ignored counts. Use to assess schema quality and naming/best-practice violations. Provide the graph ID and optionally a limit (default 5 most recent schema checks).

tools_if_shown.name: GetContractConfig
tools_if_shown.description: Read the filter configuration of a contract variant: the tags it includes, the tags it excludes, the source variant it is built from, and a human-readable description of the configuration. This is the same read that `rover contract describe` performs. A contract variant is a filtered view of another variant's schema, built by including and excluding schema elements by tag. The filter configuration does not include whether unreachable types are hidden. The description states it, so read it there before you update a contract with PublishContract. A variant that is not a contract returns null for the filter configuration. Provide the graph ID and the contract variant name.

tools_if_shown.name: GetClientMetrics
tools_if_shown.description: Traffic broken down by client for a graph over a time window, as compact CSV. Columns: start timestamp, end exclusive timestamp, client name, client version, operation name, request count, request latency p50 ms, request latency p99 ms, request with error count. Answers which clients call a graph, which client versions are still on the wire, and which client drives errors or latency. Clients that do not report `apollographql-client-name`/`-version` come back with empty name and version columns. Ranked by `orderBy` descending: default REQUEST_COUNT (busiest); REQUEST_WITH_ERROR_COUNT for most error-prone, REQUEST_LATENCY_P99_MS for slowest. `variantName` and `operationName` scope to one or more variants or operations by exact name (omit for all). Rows are one per client + version + operation, so a busy graph has far more groups than the other metrics tools: scope by `operationName` or raise `limit` when a breakdown looks truncated. Keep the default `resolution` of ENTIRE_RANGE for totals and top-N, which gives one row per group ranked over the whole window. DAY/HOUR/MINUTE give one row per group per bucket ranked within each bucket, so a window total then needs a per-group sum plus a `limit` big enough to cover every bucket; too small a `limit` silently undercounts. Only HOUR and MINUTE accept a `to` of now, so use them for bursts in the last 24 hours. Avoid MONTH: it labels buckets by calendar month, not by the requested window.

tools_if_shown.name: RunSchemaCheck
tools_if_shown.description: Start a schema check of a proposed schema against a variant, the same check that `rover graph check` starts. Use this for a monograph or for a whole supergraph schema; use RunSubgraphCheck for one subgraph. The check runs in the background, so this returns a workflow ID and a Studio URL, not a result. Pass the returned workflowID to GetCheckResults to read the outcome. Provide the graph ID, the variant name, and the proposed schema as SDL. Optionally provide the git branch and commit to label the run in Studio.

tools_if_shown.name: PublishGraphSchema
tools_if_shown.description: Publish a schema to a graph variant, the same write that `rover graph publish` performs. Use this for a monograph; use PublishSubgraph for one subgraph of a federated graph. Returns a result code, whether the publish succeeded, a human-readable message, and the hash of the published schema. This changes the schema registry and can change what clients see. Run RunSchemaCheck first to see the effect on client operations. Provide the graph ID, the variant name, and the schema as SDL. Optionally provide the git branch and commit to label the publication.

tools_if_shown.name: PublishSubgraph
tools_if_shown.description: Publish a subgraph schema to a variant and start composition, the same write that `rover subgraph publish` performs. Returns whether the subgraph was created or updated, any composition errors, and the launch that started. This changes the schema registry and can change what the router serves. Run RunSubgraphCheck first to see the effect on client operations. Provide the graph ID, the variant name, the subgraph name, and the schema as SDL. Provide the routing URL when you add a subgraph or move its endpoint. Optionally provide a revision label and the git branch and commit.

tools_if_shown.name: DeleteGraph
tools_if_shown.description: Delete a graph, the same write that `rover graph delete` performs. This is a soft delete: the data is not removed permanently and Apollo support can restore the graph. Every variant of the graph stops serving, so confirm the graph ID with the user before you call this. Returns null on success. Provide the graph ID.

tools_if_shown.name: GetSubgraphSchema
tools_if_shown.description: Read one subgraph's published schema (SDL) from a variant, with its routing URL, revision, and last update time. This is the same read that `rover subgraph fetch` performs. Read one subgraph at a time: a whole supergraph document is much larger and can pass the token limit of the model. Provide the graph ID, the variant name, and the subgraph name. Use GetVariantDetails first if you do not know the subgraph names.

tools_if_shown.name: GetSubgraphMetrics
tools_if_shown.description: Top subgraphs/connectors by traffic/health for a graph over a time window, as compact CSV. Columns: start timestamp, end exclusive timestamp, fetch service name, fetch count, fetch latency p50 ms, fetch latency p99 ms, fetch with errors count. Ranked by `orderBy` descending: default FETCH_COUNT (busiest); FETCH_WITH_ERRORS_COUNT for most error-prone, FETCH_LATENCY_P99_MS for slowest. `variantName` scopes to one or more variants (omit for all). `subgraphName` scopes to one or more subgraphs by exact name (omit for all); pattern/substring matching is not supported. `clients` scopes to the fetches driven by one or more clients; omit `clientVersion` to match every version of that client, and use GetClientMetrics to discover the names a graph sees. Keep the default `resolution` of ENTIRE_RANGE for totals and top-N, which gives one row per subgraph ranked over the whole window. DAY/HOUR/MINUTE give one row per subgraph per bucket ranked within each bucket, so a window total then needs a per-subgraph sum plus a `limit` big enough to cover every bucket; too small a `limit` silently undercounts. Only HOUR and MINUTE accept a `to` of now, so use them for bursts in the last 24 hours. Avoid MONTH: it labels buckets by calendar month, not by the requested window.

tools_if_shown.name: GetVariantDetails
tools_if_shown.description: Retrieve metadata for a graph variant: its identifier, federation version, the URL of its GraphQL endpoint, and its subgraph inventory (names only). Use this to assess a variant's composition setup, such as subgraph inventory and federation version compliance. Provide the graph ID and variant name (e.g., "production").

tools_if_shown.name: GetOperationMetrics
tools_if_shown.description: Top operations by usage/health for a graph over a time window, as compact CSV. Columns: start timestamp, end exclusive timestamp, operation name, request count, request latency p50 ms, request latency p99 ms, request with error count. Ranked by `orderBy` descending: default REQUEST_COUNT (busiest); REQUEST_WITH_ERROR_COUNT for most error-prone, REQUEST_LATENCY_P99_MS for slowest. `variantName` scopes to one or more variants (omit for all). `clients` scopes to one or more clients; omit `clientVersion` to match every version of that client, and use GetClientMetrics to discover the names a graph sees. Keep the default `resolution` of ENTIRE_RANGE for totals and top-N, which gives one row per operation ranked over the whole window. DAY/HOUR/MINUTE give one row per operation per bucket ranked within each bucket, so a window total then needs a per-operation sum plus a `limit` big enough to cover every bucket; too small a `limit` silently undercounts. Only HOUR and MINUTE accept a `to` of now, so use them for bursts in the last 24 hours. Avoid MONTH: it labels buckets by calendar month, not by the requested window.

tools_if_shown.name: RunSubgraphCheck
tools_if_shown.description: Start a schema check of one proposed subgraph schema against a variant, the same check that `rover subgraph check` starts. The check runs in the background, so this returns a workflow ID and a Studio URL, not a result. Pass the returned workflowID to GetCheckResults to read the outcome. Provide the graph ID, the variant name, the subgraph name, and the proposed subgraph schema as SDL. Optionally provide the git branch and commit to label the run in Studio.

tools_if_shown.name: GetReadme
tools_if_shown.description: Read the README of a graph variant, with the time it was last updated and who updated it. This is the same read that `rover readme fetch` performs. The README is the Markdown document shown on the variant's page in GraphOS Studio. Provide the graph ID and the variant name.

tools_if_shown.name: GetLaunchHistory
tools_if_shown.description: Retrieve recent launches for a graph variant (most recent first) to detect deployment instability such as repeated failures or frequent superseded launches. Each entry includes the launch id, status, and timestamps, so you can identify a specific launch and drill into it with GetLaunch. Use to assess deployment stability. Provide the graph ID, variant name, and optionally a limit (default 20 most recent launches, max 100 per page) and an offset to page further back.

tools_if_shown.name: GetMyIdentity
tools_if_shown.description: Resolve the caller's identity from their API key or OAuth token. Call this FIRST when the user asks about "my graph" but has not provided a graph ID. For a graph/service key, `me` resolves to a Graph: use `id` as the graphId and `variants[].name` as the variant for the graph-scoped health-check tools, so the user does not have to supply either. For a user (personal key or OAuth), `me` resolves to a User instead: there's no single graph, so each org membership's `graphs[].id` / `graphs[].variants[].name` lists the graphId/variant options the graph-scoped tools need, across every org the user belongs to. Also handles service-account keys.

tools_if_shown.name: GetGraphSchema
tools_if_shown.description: Read the schema (SDL) that is currently published to a graph variant, with its hash and publication time. This is the same read that `rover graph fetch` performs. The response holds the whole document and is not truncated. A large federated graph measured over 800,000 characters, roughly 200,000 tokens, which exceeds the context window of most models. Prefer GetSubgraphSchema, which reads one subgraph at a time, and use this tool only when you need the whole API schema. Provide the graph ID and the variant name.

tools_if_shown.name: PublishPersistedQueries
tools_if_shown.description: Publish operations to a persisted query list, the same write that `rover persisted-queries publish` performs. A persisted query list is the set of operations a router accepts when it is configured to reject anything else. Operations you do not mention stay in the list unchanged: pass operations to add or replace entries, and remove to drop them. Returns the new revision and the total operation count, or reports that nothing changed. Use GetPersistedQueryListStatus to find the list ID and its current revision. Provide the graph ID and the persisted query list ID.

tools_if_shown.name: GetTopOperations
tools_if_shown.description: Identify the most-used operations on a graph variant for a time range, with request counts, types, and signatures. Use to find high-traffic operations, detect unused operations, and prioritize findings by traffic impact. Provide graph ID, variant, and a from/to time range (ISO 8601 timestamps; `to` must be at least 6 hours before now), plus an optional limit (default 50). This report is rate limited.

tools_if_shown.name: get_attachment
tools_if_shown.description: Retrieve an issue attachment by ID. Use format=url to get its title and download URL without fetching the file content.
