published_auth_text: Whalesync requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.

published_tools.source: published FAQ (same names as visible imported tool chips)

tools_if_shown.name: sync_list_connectors
tools_if_shown.description: Every connector Whalesync supports, with its auth method (API key fields vs browser OAuth) and capabilities. Start here to learn what a sync side needs.

tools_if_shown.name: sync_pause
tools_if_shown.description: Turns an active sync off. Mappings can only be edited while paused.

tools_if_shown.name: sync_activate
tools_if_shown.description: Turns a paused sync on. A draft whose mappings a person has not yet reviewed fails with confirmation_required — relay the required_action's url so they can review and start it in the app. A sync still working through its initial sync fails with initial_sync_running — it turns itself on at the end, so poll instead.

tools_if_shown.name: sync_get_status
tools_if_shown.description: A live snapshot: pending pushes and each side's polling/initializing state. Makes live calls, so it can take a few seconds — use sync_get for the cheap summary.

tools_if_shown.name: sync_list_bases
tools_if_shown.description: The bases/sites/databases the credential on one side can reach, fetched live from the connected app (can take a few seconds). Reference a base by its remote id — names are not unique.

tools_if_shown.name: sync_list_operations
tools_if_shown.description: The record-level change log for one sync, newest first: what was created, updated, or deleted, where, and why. The place to verify a sync is actually moving data.

tools_if_shown.name: sync_get_operation
tools_if_shown.description: One operation in full, including per-field changes.

tools_if_shown.name: sync_list_issues
tools_if_shown.description: Open issues on one sync, each with a remediation hint. Empty means healthy.

tools_if_shown.name: sync_get_issue
tools_if_shown.description: One issue in full, including its remediation.

tools_if_shown.name: sync_list_pending_deletes
tools_if_shown.description: Deletes waiting on a person for one sync. When a record goes missing on one side, Whalesync holds the delete rather than applying it to the other side, so an accidental delete or an app outage cannot destroy data. Each entry links to the record in the connected app so a person can look before deciding. Approving or ignoring is irreversible and deliberately not in this API — relay the entry's review_url. A sync that auto-approves deletes has no queue and answers delete_approval_disabled; sync_get reports which mode a sync is in before you call.

tools_if_shown.name: sync_retry_issue
tools_if_shown.description: Re-attempts the failed work behind an issue. An issue is what holds a record or table back, so clearing it is how syncing runs again — "retry syncing", "sync that record again" and "try it again" all mean this tool, and there is no other retry. Fix the cause (see remediation) first, or it fails the same way. When a person names a record instead of an issue, sync_search_records then sync_get_record_status name the issue blocking it; sync_list_issues lists them for a whole sync.

tools_if_shown.name: sync_search_records
tools_if_shown.description: Find a record in one sync by its id in the connected app (e.g. an Airtable "rec…" id), its Whalesync rec_… id, or its display text (fuzzy). The first step when a person asks why a specific record is not syncing — take a result's id to sync_get_record_status. Exact id matches come first. Results are capped, not paginated: when has_more is true, narrow the query.

tools_if_shown.name: sync_get_record_status
tools_if_shown.description: Everything known about one record's sync state — the diagnosis tool for "why isn't this record syncing". Returns open issues blocking it, a pending delete awaiting a person's review, operations queued right now, per-side flags (deleted / filtered out by a sync filter / sync disabled), links to the record in both apps, and its most recent operations. queued_operations null means the queue could not be consulted, not that it is empty. For older history call sync_list_operations with record. Diagnose from the flags and issues before assuming the sync itself is broken: a filtered or sync-disabled record is excluded on purpose, and a pending delete waits for a person to approve it in the app.

tools_if_shown.name: sync_list
tools_if_shown.description: The account's syncs, newest first. Paginate with cursor when has_more is true.

tools_if_shown.name: sync_get
tools_if_shown.description: Full sync details: status, both sides, open issue count, review_url, and pending_actions. When pending_actions is non-empty, relay each action's url and instruction to the person verbatim — those steps (browser sign-in, reviewing before starting) can only be done by a human.

tools_if_shown.name: sync_create
tools_if_shown.description: Creates a draft sync between two connectors. NEVER ask the person for credentials in chat: create the sync with connector names only (no auth, no base) and it comes back with a pending_actions link per side where the person connects securely in the app — relay each link. That is the only option for OAuth connectors (the person picks the base in the browser; even a remote_id you know from another sync cannot be pre-selected), and the default for API-key connectors too; include auth inline only when the credentials were already handed to you programmatically. Validation reports the first problem it finds, so fix and retry rather than expecting every issue at once. Not idempotent: if a call fails ambiguously, check sync_list before retrying.

tools_if_shown.name: sync_update
tools_if_shown.description: Rename the sync, amend a draft side, or update credentials.

tools_if_shown.name: sync_delete
tools_if_shown.description: Stops and deletes the sync. The connected apps and their data are not touched.

tools_if_shown.name: sync_list_tables
tools_if_shown.description: The tables on one side of the sync, from Whalesync's cached schema (fetched automatically the first time). Pass refresh: true after changing the connected app's schema; refresh requires the sync to be off. May block for up to a minute while a fetch completes.

tools_if_shown.name: sync_list_fields
tools_if_shown.description: The fields of one table with type metadata, from the cached schema. Reference the table by table_… id, remote id, or exact name — resolution tries them in that order, so when the same string names tables on both sides (Postgres remote ids are bare table names), pass side to pin which one you mean. May block for up to a minute while a fetch completes. When choosing what to map: fields with write: false (formulas, created-time, Whalesync's synthesized record id, …) can only be the SOURCE side of a one-way mapping — include them only when the person wants that value in the other app (syncing a record id across is a common, legitimate case). Skip fields whose type_details.mapping_disabled is true, and map link/reference fields only when the table they point at is also mapped.

tools_if_shown.name: sync_get_mappings
tools_if_shown.description: The sync's declarative mappings document plus its revision. Keep the revision and send it back with sync_update_mappings so a concurrent edit fails instead of being silently overwritten. Also the place to find a table pair's sync filter and advanced settings when asked why some records never sync.

tools_if_shown.name: sync_update_mappings
tools_if_shown.description: Replaces the whole mappings document (fetch with sync_get_mappings, modify, send back — there is no partial edit). Validate first with sync_validate_mappings. Referenced tables whose fields were never fetched are fetched during the call, so a first update can take a few seconds. The sync must be paused or draft.

tools_if_shown.name: sync_validate_mappings
tools_if_shown.description: Checks a candidate mappings document (or the stored one, if tables is omitted) without changing anything. Empty issues means valid. Can take a few seconds if referenced tables need a schema fetch.

tools_if_shown.name: live_export_list_connectors
tools_if_shown.description: The connectors usable for live exports, each with the roles it can play (source, destination) and its auth. A separate registry from sync_list_connectors — the same brand can differ per surface.

tools_if_shown.name: live_export_list
tools_if_shown.description: The account's live exports, newest first. Paginate with cursor when has_more is true.

tools_if_shown.name: live_export_get
tools_if_shown.description: Full live export details: status, both sides, schedule, last run, and pending_actions. When pending_actions is non-empty, relay each action's url and instruction to the person verbatim — browser sign-ins can only be done by a human.

tools_if_shown.name: live_export_create
tools_if_shown.description: Creates a draft live export: a one-way scheduled copy from a source app into destination tables the export creates. NEVER ask the person for credentials in chat: create with connector names only and the export comes back with a pending_actions link per side where the person connects securely in the app — relay each link. Include auth inline only for api_key connectors whose credentials were already handed to you programmatically. Not idempotent: if a call fails ambiguously, check live_export_list before retrying.

tools_if_shown.name: live_export_update
tools_if_shown.description: Rename it, complete an api_key side's withheld auth, or set the destination's location (where created tables live, from live_export_list_locations).

tools_if_shown.name: live_export_delete
tools_if_shown.description: Deletes the live export and its schedule. Tables already created in the destination stay put.

tools_if_shown.name: live_export_list_source_tables
tools_if_shown.description: The exportable tables in the source app. Live — the connector enumerates them, so it can be slow.

tools_if_shown.name: live_export_list_source_fields
tools_if_shown.description: One source table's exportable fields, each with the name and type it would get in the destination. Pick from these when writing mappings — field types are planned by the server, never chosen by you.

tools_if_shown.name: live_export_list_locations
tools_if_shown.description: Where the destination can host created tables (an Airtable base, a Notion parent page). Pick one with live_export_update. Only destinations with pickable locations return any.

tools_if_shown.name: live_export_get_mappings
tools_if_shown.description: The working mappings document: which source tables copy into which to-be-created destination tables, field by field. Carries the revision to send back on live_export_update_mappings.

tools_if_shown.name: live_export_update_mappings
tools_if_shown.description: Declarative full replace of the mappings document. Edits the working draft only — nothing is created in the destination until live_export_save. The document: {"tables": [{"source_table", "destination_table": {"create": {"name"}}, "fields": [{"source_field", "destination_field": {"create": {"name", "primary?"}}}]}]}. Reference source tables/fields by the ids the list tools return. Send back the revision you read — a stale revision fails instead of overwriting someone's edit.

tools_if_shown.name: live_export_validate_mappings
tools_if_shown.description: The checks live_export_update_mappings would run, as a report instead of a rejection.

tools_if_shown.name: live_export_save
tools_if_shown.description: Create the mapped tables and fields in the destination app, then apply the runnable pipeline. This is the apply point: mapping edits change nothing until a save lands. The call stays on the line while the save runs (usually well under a minute), streaming progress; a still-running result says to call live_export_get_save for the outcome. succeeded is authoritative — it also requires unsaved_changes to be false on the export. Runs overwrite the destination tables this export manages — treat destination data as replaceable before pointing an export at anything a person cares about.

tools_if_shown.name: live_export_get_save
tools_if_shown.description: The latest save: how it ended (with per-table errors), staying on the line while one is still running. succeeded is authoritative — it is only reported when no edits remain unsaved. If it returns a still-running state, simply call it again.

tools_if_shown.name: live_export_get_schedule
tools_if_shown.description: The export's cadence and on/off switch, plus allowed_cadences from the person's plan. There is no pause/activate — the schedule IS the lifecycle switch.

tools_if_shown.name: live_export_update_schedule
tools_if_shown.description: Turn the export on or off and set its cadence. Creates the schedule on first use; missing fields keep their current values. Requires a saved export. Runs overwrite the destination tables this export manages — treat destination data as replaceable before pointing an export at anything a person cares about.

tools_if_shown.name: live_export_get_status
tools_if_shown.description: The live view: whether a run is in flight right now, and when the next scheduled run fires.

tools_if_shown.name: live_export_trigger
tools_if_shown.description: Run the export now, regardless of the schedule. One run at a time — a trigger while one is active returns run_in_progress. Unsaved mapping edits return the unsaved_changes conflict (the run would use the last-saved pipeline, not them): live_export_save first, or — only if the person explicitly wants the old pipeline — pass force. Runs overwrite the destination tables this export manages — treat destination data as replaceable before pointing an export at anything a person cares about.

tools_if_shown.name: live_export_list_runs
tools_if_shown.description: One export's recent runs, newest first — the monitoring surface (live exports have runs, not issues; a failed run's error is the diagnostic). History is retention-bounded.

tools_if_shown.name: live_export_get_run
tools_if_shown.description: One run with its ordered steps (pull → map → write) — where a failed run explains itself.

tools_if_shown.name: live_export_cancel_run
tools_if_shown.description: Stop an in-flight run. A run that already finished returns run_not_active.

tools_if_shown.name: live_export_whats_next
tools_if_shown.description: The happy-path compass for live exports: given where an export actually is, the ordered next steps — including the browser connection steps only a person can do (relay those verbatim). Call it with no arguments to get oriented, or whenever unsure.

tools_if_shown.name: sync_whats_next
tools_if_shown.description: Reports where a sync is in the setup flow and the recommended next steps, including any action only a person can do (relay those verbatim). Call it with no arguments to get oriented, or whenever unsure.

tools_if_shown.name: fx_forecast

tools_if_shown.name: search_products
tools_if_shown.description:
Search 100M+ products across thousands of retailers for one product type. Call once for each distinct product type, and send independent calls together. Put relevant constraints in `query`.
Returns up to 8 product cards plus structured product data. The result includes a `thread_id`. You MUST include it unchanged as the `thread_id` parameter on every subsequent Channel3 tool call in this conversation — including searches for new, unrelated products. Never omit it once you have one.

tools_if_shown.name: get_products
tools_if_shown.description:
Get full product data (offers, description, attributes, images) by product ID from a search result, or by retailer URL. Pass several IDs in one call to compare.
Use search_products to find products. Returns details in the storefront UI. The result includes a `thread_id`. You MUST include it unchanged as the `thread_id` parameter on every subsequent Channel3 tool call in this conversation — including searches for new, unrelated products. Never omit it once you have one.

tools_if_shown.name: search_availability
tools_if_shown.description:
Search for available court times at nearby facilities.
Only call after the user has provided or confirmed sport, location, date, and time. If any are missing, ask the user before calling. Duration is optional and defaults to 60 minutes.
Returns sportId (use for get_booking_link), facilities with available slots, and hint. Facilities may include perPlayerFeeDollars, perPlayerFeePolicy, and checkInPolicy when set — mention these to the user when present.

tools_if_shown.name: get_booking_link
tools_if_shown.description:
Get a booking link for a court.
Requires facilityId, date, time, sportId, and duration.
Optional players (1–8, default 2) pre-fills the booking page and is used for per-player fee totals.
Returns a URL to the booking page with pre-filled details and pricing info (court + player fees).

tools_if_shown.name: get_facility_details
tools_if_shown.description:
Look up authoritative facility information from the CourtsApp database. Use this tool ANY TIME the user asks about a racket sports facility — hours, location, amenities, phone number, policies, what sports they offer, or any other detail. Do not search the web; always use this tool first.
Accepts partial name matches, city, state, or zip. facilityId is optional — use it only when you already have a real facility id from another CourtsApp tool; otherwise use name and location fields. At least one search field is required.
Returns up to 5 matching facilities, bookable first, then connected, then listed, by name. Each includes: name, listingTier (bookable, connected, or listed), comingSoon status, description/about, seoDescription, timezone, full address, phone number, website, bookingUrl, hours of operation, amenities, booking/cancellation policies, per-player fees, check-in policy, available sports, indoorCourtCount, outdoorCourtCount, courtSurfaces, courtGroups (listed and connected: courts per sport, setting, and surface), bookable court details (name, environment, surface, sports), and a link to the facility page. website and bookingUrl are https links, or null when the stored value is missing or not a normal web URL.
Facilities with comingSoon: true are joining CourtsApp but not yet bookable. For connected facilities, send the user to bookingUrl. For listed facilities, send the user to website. Do not search availability or create a CourtsApp checkout for either.
bookingPolicies.advanceBookingDays is the maximum advance booking window across all sports. When different sports have different windows, advanceBookingDaysBySport lists each sport and its window (e.g. Pickleball 7 days, Tennis 14 days). If a user asks about a date that one sport allows but another doesn't, explain which sport(s) can be booked that far out and which cannot.
When bookingPolicies includes perPlayerFeeDollars or perPlayerFeePolicy, ALWAYS tell the user about the per-player fee — it affects total cost beyond the court rental price. When checkInPolicy is present, share it so the user knows what to expect on arrival.

tools_if_shown.name: list_facilities
tools_if_shown.description:
List facilities by location. Search by city+state (50-mile radius), state alone, zip code (50-mile radius), or lat+lng coordinates (50-mile radius).
Returns facility id, name, city, state, comingSoon, listingTier, bookingUrl, website, and the CourtsApp page url.
City, zip, and coordinates return the nearest facilities within 50 miles, not every club in range: up to 50 bookable (including coming soon), 10 connected, and 10 listed. State alone returns up to 50 bookable, 10 connected, and 10 listed facilities in that state, by name. Results come bookable first, then connected, then listed.
For connected facilities, send the user to bookingUrl. For listed facilities, send the user to website. Do not search availability or create a CourtsApp checkout for either.

tools_if_shown.name: search_open_play
tools_if_shown.description:
Find open play (drop-in) sessions with spots left at CourtsApp facilities near a location, or at one facility. Use when the user wants to join a session with other players rather than reserve a whole court.
Requires location (city+state or zip preferred), facilityName, or facilityId. When the user names a facility, pass it as facilityName right away — do not ask for the city first. date, time, sport, and level are optional filters; with no date it looks 7 days ahead.
Returns available (false means open play is not live yet — tell the user it is coming soon) and facilities, each with up to 5 sessions: level, when (facility-local), price per player, spotsLeft, maxPlayers, and url. The url is the booking page for that session — share it once the user picks a session.

tools_if_shown.name: search_legal_sources
tools_if_shown.description: Semantic search over eulaw.ai's corpus of European legislation and case law. Use it whenever a question turns on what a European or national European law actually says, or on how a court has applied it, and you need the authoritative text rather than recollection. Returns one entry per matching document: title, jurisdiction, document type, publication date, the identifiers that document carries (CELEX, ELI, ECLI where they apply), a source URL, an opaque document_id, and a passage from the document. It returns passages, not whole documents - call get_document with the document_id when the surrounding text matters. It cannot answer about jurisdictions outside the covered set: call list_jurisdictions first if you do not already know which codes are covered. It is not a general web search and holds no material outside the legal corpus.

tools_if_shown.name: get_document
tools_if_shown.description: Fetch the text of a single document from the eulaw.ai corpus by the document_id and jurisdiction that search_legal_sources returned for it. Use it when a passage from search is not enough to answer accurately - to read the provision around a quoted fragment, to check a definition, or to confirm wording before relying on it. Documents can be long, so it returns a slice: the response states the total length and whether more remains, and offset pages through the rest. It takes only identifiers this server issued; it cannot fetch a document from a URL or a citation.

tools_if_shown.name: list_jurisdictions
tools_if_shown.description: List the jurisdiction codes this server can search, with their names. Call it before the first search of a conversation, or whenever a question names a country whose coverage you have not confirmed, so the search is scoped to codes that exist rather than guessed ones. Coverage changes as jurisdictions are added, so treat the returned list as current and do not assume a code is covered because it was covered before.

tools_if_shown.name: firecrawl_research_search_papers
tools_if_shown.description:
Search paper metadata and abstracts with a natural-language query across the indexed corpus, which spans biomedical, life-science, and clinical literature (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv) alongside arXiv and other scientific sources. Optional author, category, and date filters constrain results.

Several distinct framings of the same question surface different papers than a single query does.

Returns ranked papers with canonical IDs, titles, authors, and abstracts.

tools_if_shown.name: firecrawl_research_inspect_paper
tools_if_shown.description: Retrieve canonical metadata for one paper ID, such as an arXiv, PMC, PMID, or DOI identifier. Returns the title, abstract, authors, categories, source IDs, and dates as markdown.

tools_if_shown.name: firecrawl_research_related_papers
tools_if_shown.description:
Find citation-graph candidates from one to ten `seed_ids`; the first ID is the primary seed and later IDs are anchors. `mode` defaults to `similar` (co-citation/bibliographic coupling); `citers` returns papers citing a seed and `references` papers cited by a seed. `intent` ranks candidates.

Returns ranked candidates and the evaluated pool size.

tools_if_shown.name: firecrawl_research_read_paper
tools_if_shown.description:
Retrieve in-body passages from one paper that are relevant to a specific question. Full text is available only for indexed papers; `k` controls the number of passages.

Returns matching passages or a notice when full text is unavailable.

tools_if_shown.name: firecrawl_developer_search
tools_if_shown.description:
Search an index of public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation for programming questions that need external documentation or upstream evidence.

Returns ranked results with an ID, source type, URL, title, and the matched passages in markdown.

tools_if_shown.name: firecrawl_gov_search
tools_if_shown.description:
Search US federal, state, and local statutes, regulations, codes, court opinions, and other government publications for legal or regulatory questions that need primary text. Clarify a missing jurisdiction or ambiguous as-of date before identifying the governing rule.

Returns ranked results with a position, title, URL, and matched snippet. Results may include historical versions, bill text, agency guidance, and third-party reproductions. Verify the issuer, jurisdiction, enacted/effective status, and version before citing current governing law. Read a known URL or additional page context with firecrawl_scrape. Use general search for non-US questions or missing coverage; no hits does not establish that no applicable law exists.

tools_if_shown.name: firecrawl_search
tools_if_shown.description:
Search web and specialized indexes, returning ranked results with query-relevant highlights. Each web result is a title, URL, and description. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. `includeDomains` and `excludeDomains` are mutually exclusive hostname filters; categories limit result types to `research`, `pdf`, `developer`, or `gov`.

For a programming question, add `categories: ["developer"]`. It searches an index of public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation, and returns the results in `data.web` with `category: "developer"`.

For a legal or regulatory question, `categories: ["gov"]` returns results in `data.web` with `category: "gov"` and cannot be combined with other categories; `firecrawl_gov_search` is the dedicated tool. Verify gov results' issuer, jurisdiction, status, and version before citing current law.

Authenticated search combines web results, semantic tool summaries and domain matches. Use sources: ["alexandria"] for semantic tools only. A search with sources: ["web"] omits semantic provider discovery; domainTools: true can still return website-matched tools. Web-only results use domainTools: false. Tool matches describe available structured-data capabilities, not executed data. toolDetail: "compact" (default) returns only provider, capability and description; "summary" adds metadata; "full" includes their input and output contracts. firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body executes a selected capability; firecrawl_find_tools provides catalogue browsing and full contracts.

Returns result groups in `data` and an operation `id`.

tools_if_shown.name: firecrawl_find_tools
tools_if_shown.description: Browse Alexandria data providers and workflows or read a selected contract. Alexandria covers companies, people, jobs, finance and filings, public records and government spending, real estate, places and restaurants, retail and prices, package registries and developer data, news, research, and more: typed, sourced records through published contracts. Prefer normal firecrawl_search for a data task; it already returns matching providers. Use this tool when the contract you need was not returned in full, to browse a category when search found nothing, or before scraping the same fields from several pages. Discovery is free. Use query for semantic discovery or urls to find providers for a website. With no arguments, browse categories, then providers and tools. Contracts describe the inputs and outputs for execution through firecrawl_scrape. nextTool identifies further discovery or pagination. Discovery does not execute providers. Use firecrawl_search when you also need web results.

tools_if_shown.name: firecrawl_scrape
tools_if_shown.description:
Scrape one URL and return its content, or execute catalogued Alexandria capabilities. URL mode returns markdown by default, or HTML, links, screenshots, branding data, a targeted answer, or JSON matching a supplied schema, plus page metadata. Firecrawl may serve recently indexed content; set `maxAge: 0` for a live fetch. A successful response does not by itself confirm the page is still current. A named browser profile loads saved session data without saving changes to it.

`firecrawl_search` with `sources` unset and `firecrawl_find_tools` can discover providers for the same fields across several pages; a matching Alexandria provider returns typed records in one call.

Alexandria mode: `alexandria` selects catalogued capability execution and is mutually exclusive with `url`. Alexandria execution is billed at the capability's listed price and needs a team with Alexandria enabled.
