tools_if_shown.name: search_catalog
tools_if_shown.description:
Search the AirShelf cross-vendor product catalog by natural-language query. The catalog covers industrial-automation, wiring-devices, digital-signage, business-display, mfp, barcode-printer, laser-printer, inkjet-printer, mechanical-keyboards, cybersecurity, threat-intelligence-platform. Industrial-automation and wiring-device rows are indexed by manufacturer part number, so a brand or part number in the query ("Pepperl+Fuchs retroreflective sensor", "IN5409") retrieves more reliably than a bare product type; those rows carry no normalized spec facets, so the `specs` filter does not apply to them. Returns ranked products with prices, specs, and per-row match accounting.
Each row includes `unverified_specs`, the normalized spec names that lack claim-level receipts; never use those as decisive facts.
Example queries: "tactile mechanical keyboard under $150", "Toshiba A3 colour multifunction device", "industrial barcode printer for a warehouse", "threat-intelligence platform with dark-web monitoring".

Result fields:
• canonical_name — the exact catalog name of the product.
• spec_absence_note — spec fields absent from this product's golden record (AirShelf's verified product record); null when nothing is missing.
• constraint_match_score and matched_criteria — query constraints supported by claim-level receipts. unverified_criteria names matching catalog values that still need confirmation; missing_criteria names values that are absent or conflict.
• parsed.price_availability — all_null = true means every returned price is null. For quote-gated B2B pricing, a null price with a quote path is expected rather than an error; query_had_budget reports whether the query carried one.
• result.commercial_data — branch on actionable before using price or stock. Observations older than 24 hours are withheld from result.price/result.inStock and retained only as labelled last_observed history.
• parsed.weak_match — the response contains an unresolved constraint, query match, or product-identity warning. parsed.unverified_identity_count counts returned names without an identity receipt. parsed.no_match — no product satisfies a hard constraint, and candidates violating it were excluded server-side.

On a miss or near-miss for a specific brand+model the response may also carry a `tier3` block, meaning a real-time lookup for the exact SKU asked about; it can appear alongside fuzzy-neighbour rows.
• tier3.status = "resolved" — a single-source reading of the page at tier3.source_url. MPN-confirmed means the live lookup matched the manufacturer part number. Its verification is "live-unverified": confirmed on a live page during this run, but not yet matched to an AirShelf catalog record. A verified row is matched to the catalog record. tier3.cached = true means it came from a recent prior lookup, with fetched_at recording when the page was read.
• tier3.status = "abstain" — the lookup could not confirm the product exists as asked, so no specs, price, or availability were established. tier3.guidance describes the quote-request path.
• tier3.status = "declined" — an applicable lookup did not run; tier3.reason says why (disabled, rate_limited, daily_cap, negative_cache, error). No specs or availability were established, and none should be inferred.
No tier3 block at all means a live lookup was not applicable to this query (no parseable brand+model identity).

Optional `market` (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. "TH") excludes catalog rows whose country-specific URL conflicts with the buyer market and scopes tier3 lookup/cache. A remaining global URL is not local-availability proof: parsed.weak_match stays true and unsatisfied_constraints includes market_availability until every returned row has a matching country receipt. "Available in <market>" still does not guarantee stock.

tools_if_shown.name: find_products
tools_if_shown.description:
Discover candidate products for a buyer need. Takes a need in natural language (e.g. "best value home espresso machine", market "TH"), checks the verified catalog first, then uses live web discovery only when the catalog has no candidates. Returns up to 3 candidates with explicit fit accounting.

find_products is the quick candidate-list tool; research_shopping is the full verified-research job. For a specific brand+model, search_catalog is cheaper and returns the same live-lookup block on a miss.

Response fields:
• candidates[].verification — "catalog-candidate" for a catalog starting point whose fit still needs checking, or "live-unverified" for a live page read during this run.
• candidates[].status — "resolved" means both identity and the parsed buyer constraints were supported by the cited page; "abstain" means identity or need fit could not be established. Inspect constraint_check for matched, conflicting, and unverified requirements.
• candidates[].constraint_check.receipts maps each receipt-backed matched requirement to its supporting source URL and trust label.
• Candidates come from current web-search results, so they are a sample of what the market offers rather than a ranking.
• status at the top level — "no_match" means discovery ran but no candidate was confirmed as satisfying the need; "disabled", "rate_limited", or "unavailable" means no discovery ran.

• live_discovery.status="unavailable" means receipted catalog candidates were returned while live discovery was unavailable.

Optional `market` (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) biases discovery and marketplace checks toward seller pages serving that country and scopes the lookup cache. "Available in <market>" means the seller page serves that market, not that stock is guaranteed.

tools_if_shown.name: research_shopping
tools_if_shown.description: research_shopping is the full verified-research job; find_products is the quick candidate-list tool. It runs as a background job and returns status "running" with a research ID while the minutes-long research continues; the same research ID returns the run on later polls until completion. Unsafe medical, legal, financial-advice, and professional-service asks return status "refused" before any work is queued. Completed runs return a researched recommendation with per-claim source receipts, or an explicit refusal when evidence is insufficient. Missing decision details return clarification questions before research starts. `market` biases discovery and marketplace checks toward seller pages serving that country; "available in <market>" means the seller page serves that market, not that stock is guaranteed. Example answer keys include {"budget":"500 USD","market":"US","category":"espresso machine"}.

tools_if_shown.name: get_product
tools_if_shown.description:
Get the full golden record (AirShelf's verified product record) and latest price for one catalog product by slug ("<manufacturer>-<model>").

Returns the product's specs and provenance (which page each fact came from), plus canonical_name (its exact catalog name). A field's evidence_sha256 is the SHA-256 of the source document AirShelf archived when it extracted that claim. A caller holding the same bytes can compare the hash to check that the cited document has not changed. AirShelf does not serve those archived bytes, and the hash does not promise they remain retrievable. Branch on commercial_data.actionable before using price or stock: observations older than 24 hours are withheld from latestPrice and retained only as labelled last_observed history. For quote-gated B2B pricing, a null price with a quote path is expected rather than an error. In clients that render MCP Apps the response also draws one product card per call. related_products — relationships extracted from vendor documents (e.g. compatible toner or drum accessories with their source quotes, functional equivalents, supersessions); each entry names the related catalog slug, the relation type, its direction (direction is "from_this" when the relation reads this-product → related-product, "to_this" when it reads related-product → this-product), and the source URL and quote the relation was extracted from.

tools_if_shown.name: compare_products
tools_if_shown.description:
Compare 2-10 catalog products side-by-side on their datasheet specs. Slugs come from search_catalog and are case-insensitive and dash-tolerant ("e-STUDIO 331AC", "toshiba-e-studio-331ac" and "e-studio331ac" all resolve to the same product).

Returns one item per product with canonical_name and spec_absence_note (spec fields absent from that product's golden record, AirShelf's verified product record). Branch on each item's commercial_data.actionable before using price or stock; stale observations are withheld from action fields. A slug that does not resolve comes back as not_found with a did_you_mean suggestion. The `provenance` option adds the source page and source type already stored with each fact.

tools_if_shown.name: explain_product
tools_if_shown.description: Explain the evidence behind a catalog row. Returns stored processing stages when available and always returns a golden-record field summary with source coverage. A field's evidence_sha256 is the SHA-256 of the source document AirShelf archived when it extracted that claim. A caller holding the same bytes can compare the hash to check that the cited document has not changed. AirShelf does not serve those archived bytes, and the hash does not promise they remain retrievable. record.scraped_at is the catalog row's scrape time, not a per-claim evidence capture time.

tools_if_shown.name: list_merchants
tools_if_shown.description: List public AirShelf merchants that have an assigned slug and at least one active product. Internal/demo and empty catalogs are excluded. Returns each merchant's name, slug, and product count; the slug is the `merchant` argument for request_quote.

tools_if_shown.name: request_quote
tools_if_shown.description:
Send a quote request for catalog products to a merchant's sales team on behalf of a named buyer.

This is a two-step, double opt-in flow. The first call emails a confirmation link to `contact.email` and returns status "confirmation_required"; no lead exists and no merchant is contacted until the buyer confirms. A later call with the same arguments reports "awaiting_confirmation" while the email is unconfirmed, or "received" with a reference_number after confirmation.

Merchant slugs come from list_merchants. Network-catalog brands that are absent from that list use merchant:"airshelf-network" with brandSlug:"<manufacturer-slug>"; AirShelf routes the confirmed request to that brand.

tools_if_shown.name: check_tax
tools_if_shown.description: Check inputs to calculate a tax return for a given jurisdiction. The 'input' argument must conform to the JSON schema returned by the tax_namespace_schema tool. Returns 'Success' on success, or validation errors if the input is invalid. If some inputs trigger a PARTIAL DISQUALIFICATION, the check still succeeds but includes disqualification details — proceed to calculate_tax to get the document and estimate the impact. Use this tool to validate inputs before calculating the tax return.

tools_if_shown.name: calculate_tax
tools_if_shown.description: Calculate a tax return for a given jurisdiction. The 'input' argument must conform to the JSON schema returned by the tax_namespace_schema tool. Returns computed tax return document on success, or validation errors if the input is invalid. If some inputs trigger a PARTIAL DISQUALIFICATION, the document is still returned for the supported fields; review the disqualification details and estimate the impact of the unsupported fields on the taxpayer's tax owed or refund due. Use the check_tax tool first to validate the input before calculating the tax return with this tool.IMPORTANT RULES: (1) All field values must be wrapped as {"value": <val>} — never pass bare values. (2) Currency amounts are whole-dollar integers (e.g. $19,312.42 = 19312). (3) Every item in an array namespace (NamespaceList) must have a "uuid" field with a valid UUIDv4 string. UUIDv4 format: xxxxxxxx-xxxx-4xxx-[89ab]xxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx — the 3rd group MUST start with '4' (version) and the 4th group MUST start with '8', '9', 'a', or 'b' (variant). NEVER construct UUIDs manually (e.g. 'B1111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111' is invalid). Use a UUID generator; example valid value: 'a3b4c5d6-e7f8-4a9b-8c0d-1e2f3a4b5c6d'. (4) Nested arrays (e.g. w2_state_local_tax_grp inside a w2) also require a UUIDv4 on each item. (5) Use "who_applies_to" to cross-reference entries: {"value": "taxpayer"} for singletons, {"value": "<namespace>#<uuid>"} for array items (e.g. "dependent_detail#<uuid>"). Other named reference fields (e.g. "person" in qualifying_person_grp, "student" in student_educational_instn_grp) use the same "<namespace>#<uuid>" format. (6) For state returns with Extended Links (state namespace extending a federal NamespaceList), each extended link item must use a UUIDv5 generated from the source item's UUID (as the namespace) and the extended namespace name (as the name). Matching is UUID-based, not positional. The number of expected instances depends on the source formula — it is NOT always a 1:1 match with the federal list. Incorrect or random UUIDs cause SILENT DATA LOSS — the server drops unrecognized UUIDs and replaces them with empty instances. Use the generate_uuid_v5 tool with the source item's UUID as the source_uuid and the extended namespace name as the namespace input. Example: generate_uuid_v5(source_uuid: <source item uuid>, namespace: "ca_irsw2_g") links a federal Form W-2G item to its California extension. NOTE: ordinary Form W-2 data does NOT use an extended link — state returns derive it automatically from the federal w2 namespace, so do not generate a UUIDv5 for it. Call tax_namespaces for the jurisdiction to see which extended namespaces it actually exposes. (7) return_header is top-level, NOT nested inside return_data. Use tax_simple_return first to see the full input structure and examples. When returning the tax calculation inform the user that I'm just a tax estimator, you should consult with a tax professional.

tools_if_shown.name: tax_years
tools_if_shown.description: List all supported tax years.

tools_if_shown.description: List all supported tax jurisdictions for a given tax year.

tools_if_shown.name: tax_namespace_schema
tools_if_shown.description: Get the TCB input schema for a single namespace (e.g. "irs1040", "irs1040_schedulec", "ca_form540"). Returns the properties and types for that namespace. HOW TO READ THE SCHEMA: (1) Each field references a type like tcb_string_null, tcb_integer_null, or tcb_boolean_null. All values must be wrapped as {"value": <val>}. (2) If the namespace title ends in '_list' (e.g. 'w2_list', 'dependent_detail_list'), it is a NamespaceList — an array of objects. Each array item MUST include a "uuid" field (non-null UUIDv4 string). (3) Reference fields link entries to other namespaces e.g. "person" in qualifying_person_grp, "student" in student_educational_instn_grp. All use the same format: {"value": "<namespace>#<uuid>"} (e.g. "dependent_detail#<uuid>"). (4) Nested arrays within a namespace (e.g. w2_state_local_tax_grp inside w2) also require uuid on each nested item. (5) Pattern-validated strings (e.g. SSNs, ZIPs, dates) have regex constraints in the schema $defs. SSNs/EINs: 9-digit string (no dashes). ZIPs: 5 or 9 digits. Dates: YYYY-MM-DD.

tools_if_shown.name: tax_namespaces
tools_if_shown.description: List all available input namespaces for a given jurisdiction. Use the returned names with the tax_namespace_schema tool to get the schema for a specific namespace. Requires a jurisdiction (e.g. "us" for federal, "ca" for California). Use the tax_jurisdictions tool first to discover available jurisdictions. NAMESPACE NAMING CONVENTIONS: Federal namespaces: irs1040, irs1040_schedule1, irs8962, w2, dependent_detail, etc. State namespaces: always prefixed with the state abbreviation (ca_form540, ny_it201, az_form140). NAMESPACE TYPES: Some namespaces are singletons (object), others are NamespaceLists (array) that can hold multiple items — e.g. w2 (multiple W-2s), dependent_detail (multiple dependents), irs1040_schedulec (multiple businesses). NamespaceList items require UUIDv4 fields. State NamespaceLists may act as Extended Links that extend a federal NamespaceList (e.g. ca_irsw2_g extends the federal Form W-2G list). Extended link items must use UUIDv5 (deterministic, derived from source item UUID as namespace + extended namespace name as name). Matching is UUID-based, not positional. Wrong UUIDs cause silent data loss. Use the generate_uuid_v5 tool with the source item's UUID as the source_uuid and the extended namespace name as the namespace input. Example: generate_uuid_v5(source_uuid: <source item uuid>, namespace: "ca_irsw2_g"). NOTE: ordinary Form W-2 data does NOT use an extended link — state returns derive it automatically from the federal w2 namespace. The list this tool returns for a jurisdiction is authoritative: only namespaces it names can be passed to tax_namespace_schema or included in an input payload.

tools_if_shown.name: tax_simple_return
tools_if_shown.description: Call this FIRST when beginning any tax return. Returns the curated namespace list, top-level structure guide, example input, and step-by-step filing workflow. By default returns a simple scenario (single or MFJ filer, W-2 income only, standard deduction, no dependents). Pass scenario="with_dependents" for returns that include dependents, child care (Form 2441), and education credits (Form 8863). Optionally pass a state jurisdiction (e.g. "ca") to also include state-level namespaces — if you don't know which state applies, ask the user before calling.

tools_if_shown.name: generate_tax_pdf_tool
tools_if_shown.description: Start async PDF generation for a tax return. The 'input' argument must conform to the JSON schema returned by the tax_namespace_schema tool. Returns a job ID to poll with get_tax_pdf.Use the check_tax tool first to validate the input before generating the tax PDF with this tool.The input follows the same rules as calculate_tax: all values wrapped as {"value": <val>}, array items require UUIDv4 fields (extended link items use UUIDv5), references use who_applies_to, and return_header is top-level (not inside return_data). Use tax_simple_return to see the full input structure.

tools_if_shown.name: get_tax_pdf_tool
tools_if_shown.description: Check status of a PDF generation job. Returns the status and a download URL when completed, only     use this tool after generating the tax PDF with the generate_tax_pdf tool and it successfully returns a job ID.     When returning the url of the PDF inform the user that I'm just a tax estimator, you should consult with a tax     professional.

tools_if_shown.name: generate_uuid_v5
tools_if_shown.description: Generate a UUID v5 based on a source uuid and namespace.

tools_if_shown.name: whoami
tools_if_shown.description: Introspect this connection: key type, the org and site it is scoped to (with names), and its granted scopes (mcp:read for reads, manage:write for write tools). Call this once at the start of a session to learn your permission envelope instead of discovering it by failed calls.

tools_if_shown.name: get_site_context
tools_if_shown.description: Return the full Flusterduck MCP snapshot for a site: scores, open issues, active alerts, deploys, and recommendations. Start here for any investigation. Score fields: score is the baseline-normalized confusion score (0-100, higher = more confusion, dampened for tiny samples); raw_score is the pre-normalization weighted signal total; baseline 0 with deviation 0 means the page has no learned baseline yet.

tools_if_shown.name: get_scores
tools_if_shown.description: Return current confusion scores for every tracked page, sorted by friction intensity. score is baseline-normalized (0-100, higher = more confusion, dampened for tiny samples); raw_score is the pre-normalization weighted signal total; baseline 0 with deviation 0 means the page has no learned baseline yet.

tools_if_shown.name: get_page
tools_if_shown.description: Return the full context for one page: score history, active issues, element friction, deploys, annotations, and confusion budgets. Use after get_scores or get_site_context to drill into a specific page.

tools_if_shown.name: get_elements
tools_if_shown.description: Return element-level friction summaries: which buttons, forms, and links generate the most behavioral signals. Site-wide by default; pass page to scope to one page.

tools_if_shown.name: get_issues
tools_if_shown.description: Return UX issues for a site, newest activity first. Returns { issues, total, offset, limit } so you can page. Filter by status to focus on what needs attention (status "open" is the active inbox; "regressed" means a previously fixed issue came back).

tools_if_shown.name: get_issue
tools_if_shown.description: Return one UX issue with full evidence, session links, verification history, and deploy correlation. Use after get_issues to drill into a specific issue.

tools_if_shown.name: get_alerts
tools_if_shown.description: Return active or historical alerts, newest first. Returns { alerts, total, offset, limit } so you can page. Status "fired" means nobody has looked yet; use it to find alerts needing attention.

tools_if_shown.name: list_alert_rules
tools_if_shown.description: List all alert rules configured for the site: trigger types, thresholds, channels, and enabled status. Call this before create_alert_rule or delete_alert_rule to see what already exists. Requires manage:write scope.

tools_if_shown.name: get_session_detail
tools_if_shown.description: Return the full event timeline for a specific session: every signal, click, scroll, and page view in order. Get session ids from explore (mode "list"), get_issue evidence, or query_raw_rows on the sessions table.

tools_if_shown.name: get_flows
tools_if_shown.description: Return page-to-page flow edges from recent sessions, showing where users come from and where they go.

tools_if_shown.name: get_trends
tools_if_shown.description: Return confusion score history for a site or page. Use to spot regressions after deploys.

tools_if_shown.name: get_conversion_insights
tools_if_shown.description: Return the confused-vs-calm conversion analysis: it splits the site's sessions into a "confused" cohort (produced at least one friction signal) and a "calm" cohort (zero friction), then compares conversion rate, session duration, pages per session, and bounce rate between them. Use it to state plainly how much less confused sessions convert (e.g. "confused sessions convert 12 points lower"), which pages and traffic sources bleed the most conversions to confusion, and the ranked insights. cohorts/deltas are the headline; by_page and by_source break the gap down; insights[] are pre-written narratable findings (check `confident` before quoting a number, and note low_confidence cohorts). What counts as a conversion comes from the site's configured conversion goal. Optional days (1-90, default 7).

tools_if_shown.name: get_deploys
tools_if_shown.description: Return deploys known to Flusterduck for this site, including confusion_before/after scores for each.

tools_if_shown.name: compare_pages
tools_if_shown.description: Compare confusion score records side-by-side for two page paths.

tools_if_shown.name: get_recommendations
tools_if_shown.description: Return prioritized fix recommendations ranked by estimated confusion reduction.

tools_if_shown.name: get_revenue_impact
tools_if_shown.description: Return revenue impact estimates for active friction when conversion data is connected.

tools_if_shown.name: get_heuristics
tools_if_shown.description: Return the full Flusterduck friction heuristic catalog: all signal types, thresholds, and scoring weights.

tools_if_shown.name: diagnose_journey_friction
tools_if_shown.description: Return high-friction journey edges from recent sessions. Filter by signal type or minimum friction weight to focus on the worst paths.

tools_if_shown.name: query_raw_rows
tools_if_shown.description: Return SQL-style raw rows from an allowlisted Flusterduck table, scoped to the authorized site. Default 100 rows sorted by the table's time column, newest first. Filters only apply where they make sense: event_type on events, signal_type on signals, status on ux_issues/alerts, session_id on events/signals/sessions.

tools_if_shown.name: explore
tools_if_shown.description: Run a deterministic, typed query against a site's session data. No natural language, no LLM: a closed vocabulary the engine validates before touching a row, built explicitly so an agent can compose it directly. Give it a window (window_days, 1-90, default 7) and up to 12 AND-ed filters over a fixed field list: signal (a friction/heuristic type, e.g. "rage_click", "dead_click", "form_abandonment"), page (exact path, or substring with op "contains"), source (referrer/utm source, exact or "contains"), confused (boolean: session produced at least one friction signal), converted (boolean: session reached the site's configured conversion event), event_type (one of click, move, scroll, keyboard, form_focus, form_blur, form_submit, touch, navigation, error, signal, pageview, custom_signal, performance, visibility, sdk_error). Ops are is / is_not / contains. contains only makes sense for page and source; signal and the boolean fields only take is/is_not (contains is coerced to is for signal). Then choose exactly one output. {mode: "list", limit?, offset?} returns matching sessions (id, timing, pages visited, signal counts, source, confused/converted) ranked most-recent-first, limit 1-200 (default 50) with offset for paging: use it to pull concrete example sessions as evidence. Or {mode: "measure", metric, group_by?} computes metric ("count" | "avg_pageviews" | "conversion_rate" | "avg_dwell_ms" | "bounce_rate") as a single scalar, or as a series when group_by is set ("page" | "source" | "day" | "signal" | "cohort", where "cohort" splits confused vs. calm sessions). Example: "sessions that rage-clicked on /pricing in the last 7 days" -> filters: [{field:"page",op:"is",value:"/pricing"},{field:"signal",op:"is",value:"rage_click"}], output: {mode:"list"}. Example: "does confusion actually hurt conversion here?" -> output: {mode:"measure",metric:"conversion_rate",group_by:"cohort"}.

tools_if_shown.name: download_events_csv
tools_if_shown.description: Return a CSV export of raw event rows for the authorized site. The client can save the returned text as a .csv file. Default 1000 rows; narrow with page/since/until filters before raising the limit so the response stays manageable.

tools_if_shown.name: get_degradation
tools_if_shown.description: Return active and recent backend degradation events (operational health for ingest, scoring, and delivery). Check this when data looks stale or missing.

tools_if_shown.name: update_issue
tools_if_shown.description: Update a UX issue: change its status (open/triaged/in_progress/verified/resolved/ignored), add a triage note, or set an assignee. Resolving or ignoring removes the issue from active triage views. Requires manage:write scope.

tools_if_shown.name: send_feedback
tools_if_shown.description: Send product feedback about Flusterduck itself to the Flusterduck team. Use kind "suggestion" for a missing capability, confusing tool output, or data you wished you had while working; use kind "bug" when a Flusterduck tool or surface misbehaved. Say which tool you were using, what you expected, and what happened. Requires manage:write scope.

tools_if_shown.name: update_alert
tools_if_shown.description: Acknowledge, mark as investigating, or resolve an alert. Resolving stops all channel delivery including PagerDuty. Optionally include a resolved_reason when closing. Requires manage:write scope.

tools_if_shown.name: add_annotation
tools_if_shown.description: Add a timeline annotation to the site to mark deploys, investigation findings, resolved incidents, or any notable event. Requires manage:write scope.

tools_if_shown.name: create_alert_rule
tools_if_shown.description: Create a new alert rule. Trigger types: spike (sudden confusion jump), anomaly (statistical deviation from baseline), new_page (a new page starts generating friction), trend (sustained drift), co_occurrence (many users confused at the same time), positive (score drops BELOW the threshold; fires on improvement), budget (confusion budget burn), revenue_threshold (estimated revenue at risk), stalled_signups (signup flow stalls). Omitted threshold and cooldown get sensible per-trigger defaults. Requires manage:write scope.

tools_if_shown.name: update_alert_rule
tools_if_shown.description: Update an existing alert rule: toggle enabled, change threshold, adjust channels, rename, or update page_pattern. Prefer this over delete_alert_rule when you want to temporarily silence a rule. Requires manage:write scope.

tools_if_shown.name: delete_alert_rule
tools_if_shown.description: Permanently delete an alert rule by ID. This cannot be undone; prefer update_alert_rule with enabled false to silence a rule temporarily. Requires manage:write scope.

tools_if_shown.name: get_editor_status
tools_if_shown.description: Check whether the user has a Raylight editor tab open and connected, and which project it is editing. Call this FIRST: every editing and rendering tool routes through that live tab. If nothing is connected, tell the user to open their project at raylight.app (use list_projects to give them the exact link) and wait for them to confirm.

tools_if_shown.name: list_projects
tools_if_shown.description: List the user's Raylight projects (newest first, capped at 50) with an editUrl for each, plus the projects other people shared with them by link or invite that aren't already in one of the user's workspaces (sharedWithMe, with sharedBy and which of the user's workspaces each is filed under) and the user's workspaces. Works even when no editor tab is connected, so use it to tell the user exactly which link to open.

tools_if_shown.name: file_shared_project
tools_if_shown.description: Choose which of the user's workspaces a project someone shared with them shows up in on their projects page. Only for sharedWithMe entries from list_projects. This is the user's own filing: it gives nobody access and the owner's project is not moved.

tools_if_shown.name: get_editor_capabilities
tools_if_shown.description: Return the full list of tools this server exposes and the recommended workflow. Optional discovery helper: you never need to call this before working, just start with get_editor_status. It exists so a capabilities query resolves cleanly instead of erroring.

tools_if_shown.name: get_project_overview
tools_if_shown.description: Read the whole project at a glance: the coordinate system and visible canvas bounds in world units (canvasWorldUnits.center + visibleX/visibleY; the center is NOT always (0,0)), every shot with its absolute start/duration and asset list, the styleDigest (every color in use with its roles, every font family with its weights: match these when adding elements so the project stays cohesive), the mediaLibrary (every image/video/audio available to the project: media used in shots plus everything uploaded to the Assets panel, usageCount 0 = uploaded but not yet placed; placeable via add_image/add_shot), savedEasings when the user has saved any (easings they kept from the timeline, applied by name with easingPreset: the count plus the newest few names, or unavailable when the library could not be loaded, which does not mean it is empty), where the user currently is (playhead, current shot, selection), and on projects imported from another app an import block (decision counts, fidelity score, and the renderedLayers that were placed as media because they could not be rebuilt natively, each with its assetId and reason code). A fresh copy of this exact data is already included in the user's message as project_state; call this tool only to RE-read after apply_edits changes the project, never at the start of a run. Pass section: "savedEasings" to get ONLY the user's complete saved easing library instead of the overview (every name, newest first, each with the curve or spring it plays in the form the easing op fields take); use it when the name you need is not among the newest few, or to read a saved curve's values.

tools_if_shown.name: get_shot_details
tools_if_shown.description: Read one shot in full detail: every asset with transform (world units, degrees), MEASURED rendered footprint (sizeWorld: width/height plus left/right/top/bottom world edges; use these for spacing and overlap math, never guess sizes), lifetime (shot-local ms), entrance/exit, animation blocks, per-kind extras (crop and video trim, enabled layerEffects, frame size/clipContent, containerId = the frame a layer belongs to, icon identity on inserted icons, audio mix, material on extruded layers and bevel on extruded paths), groups with their members, their explicit pivot when one is set (absent = the measured visual center of the members), and group animation blocks, plus camera framings/moves (framings report rollDeg when set), enabled effects, and the key light for the shot (resting pose plus its animation blocks) when it has one. Fields at their rest defaults are OMITTED from asset summaries: no rotationDeg means {0,0,0}, no scale means 1, no opacity means 1, no entrance/exit means type "none", no name means unnamed, no depth on a shape, path, or text layer means flat (depth is reported in world units when the layer is extruded), no material means Matte, no bevel means square depth edges, no light means the shot is unlit, and only enabled effects are listed. Scale animation blocks report amount as amountUnit "multiplierOfRest"; the same multiplier basis add_animation accepts, so a block you wrote as 1.1 reads back as 1.1 and can be passed back to update_animation unchanged. Non-uniform scale reads back as a {x, y, z} object instead of a single number (read-only: update_asset.scale writes a uniform scalar, so adjust size via sizeWorld-aware position/size edits rather than by flattening a non-uniform scale). When the shot has geometric problems, the payload includes lint: findings for layers clipped by the frame edge, buried behind opaque layers in paint order, colliding text, frame members clipped away, near-miss alignment, and cramped gaps; fix warnings before adding anything new. Call this for any shot you intend to edit before editing it.

tools_if_shown.name: render_stills
tools_if_shown.description: SEE your work: renders 1-4 real frames of the final film at the given ABSOLUTE project times and returns them as images. Each frame is the true render the user will see: camera moves, entrance/exit animations mid-flight, animation blocks, effects, background, everything. Use this after apply_edits to review composition, spacing, legibility, and effect intensity with your own eyes, then fix what reads wrong and render once more to confirm. Pick decisive moments: just after entrances settle (shot start + ~700ms), the composed mid-shot hold, just before a cut. To judge motion over time, prefer render_filmstrip. Pass region to ZOOM onto part of the canvas at full resolution: use it to verify small text is legible and details are crisp (region frames render with camera moves suppressed, so also check the real framing without a region). The first content block is a JSON calibration record: with a region it is {regionView: {zoom, center, visibleWorld {minX,minY,maxX,maxY}, imagePx, pxPerWorldAtZ0}} computed from the framing actually rendered (the region is FIT inside the image at the project aspect, so visibleWorld is usually wider or taller than the rect you asked for; never assume pxPerWorld = imagePx.width / region.width), and without a region it is {frameView: {imagePx, canvasWorld, pxPerWorldAtRest}} (exact only while no camera move is active). Each still's label also carries layers: [{assetId, name, kind, px: {x, y, w, h}}], the resting pixel rect of every visible layer in that image (top-left origin, z=0 plane through the camera active at that time), so you can point at what you see. Morphs are the one motion the rects follow: a layer a morph has taken out of the picture at that time (a morph target before the flight lands, a layer after it has become its target) is left out, and a layer a morph is flying or landing is listed where the morph has it, marked morphing: true. A frame with a missing or half-loaded asset means media was still loading; render that time again.

tools_if_shown.name: render_filmstrip
tools_if_shown.description: SEE MOTION: renders 4, 6, or 9 evenly spaced real frames across a time span and returns them as ONE contact-sheet image (reading order left to right, top to bottom, each tile labeled with its absolute time). This is how you judge animation: whether an entrance cascade actually cascades, whether a camera move eases in, whether elements collide mid-flight, how a cut lands. Span one beat at a time: an entrance (shot start to start + ~1200ms), a camera move, the 600ms around a cut. Use 6 frames by default, 9 for a long or busy span, 4 for a quick check. Tiles are smaller than single stills; for fine detail or small-text legibility follow up with render_stills (optionally with a region).

tools_if_shown.name: render_waveform
tools_if_shown.description: HEAR your work: renders the real project mix across a time span as a waveform + spectrogram strip (one image, timeline-aligned), with the span's visual beats - cuts, entrances, animation starts - overlaid as numbered markers and listed with absolute times. This is the audio filmstrip: use it after placing sounds to see whether transients land on the markers, whether a music bed leaves room for SFX (spectrogram shows competing energy), whether a sound is present at all, and where dead air sits. The mix is the true export mix: block envelopes, fades, per-layer effects, ducking, everything. Span one moment at a time (the ~1500ms around a cut or entrance) for precise reading, or a whole shot for the energy arc. For exact numeric offsets between sounds and beats, use check_sync; this tool is for seeing the shape.

tools_if_shown.name: check_sync
tools_if_shown.description: MEASURE audio-visual sync: detects transient onsets in the real project mix and correlates them with the span's visual beats (cuts, entrances, animation starts). Returns JSON: per beat, the nearest onset and the signed offset in ms (positive = the sound lands LATE, negative = early, null = no sound marks that moment within 250ms), plus unmatched onsets (sounds that mark nothing visual). Use it after sound work to verify hits land where they should, then fix offsets with move_sound (impacts land ON the cut; whooshes typically lead it by ~60-120ms so the energy peak arrives with the visual). Omit startMs/endMs to check the whole timeline. A null onset on a beat you scored means the sound is missing, too quiet, or too soft-attacked to register - render_waveform shows which.

tools_if_shown.name: get_design_guide
tools_if_shown.description: Raylight's motion design guide, distilled from the official hand-built templates (recreations of top-tier motion design from Linear, Apple, Fey, Revolut and others). Topic "craft-rules" returns the full craft ruleset (identical to the in-app director's brief; skip it if those rules are already in your system prompt). Topic "measured-craft" returns the aggregate timing/text/camera/effects numbers; a template topic returns that template's scene-by-scene beat sheet (exact arrival times, amounts, easings, camera beats, palette) plus preview images. The templates are the ground truth of what looks good: fetch the closest template's topic BEFORE authoring any scene's motion (not just when recreating a known look) and mirror or transplant its beats; its "Scene N" numbering matches apply_template_motion's sceneIndex. Topics: craft-rules, measured-craft, 3d-mobile-app, twitter-app, raylight-launch, airbnb-3d-app, nowak, liquid-glass, linear-agent, revolut-app, framer, raylight-agent-launch, raylight-marketplace, macbook-pro-around-linear, linear-hero, image-slide, manicule, limelight, drop-in, fey, lines, linear-reviews, prompt-button-press, bouncy-liquid-glass, apple-news, rubik-s-cube-liquid-glass.

tools_if_shown.name: save_as_video
tools_if_shown.description: Copy the CURRENT project, which must be a design (a still: get_project_overview reports a designSize), into a NEW video project so it can be animated. The layers, lights, effects, and background carry over; the canvas snaps to the nearest video aspect ratio and the camera pulls back if needed so the whole design stays in frame. Returns the new project id and an editUrl. It does NOT open or switch to the new project: give the user the editUrl and keep working in the current project unless they switch. Pass "name" to title it (default: "<design name> (Video)"). Use when the user wants motion on a design; a design itself never plays.

tools_if_shown.name: list_videos
tools_if_shown.description: List the user's exported videos (hosted share pages), newest first, capped at 50. Each entry has a shareId, title, shareUrl, status (ready or pending), visibility ("public" = anyone with the link can watch, "private" = only the user; a private video's shareUrl does not play for anyone else, so check it before handing out a link, and change it with update_share_page video.visibility, asking the user before making a video public), durationMs, viewCount, reactions (count per one-tap reaction viewers left), signups (new Raylight accounts that started on that video's page; each one counts toward the user's referral earnings), and the video's page settings (description, cta, allowRemix). Use it to find the shareId for update_share_page, or to hand the user a link to a video they already exported.

tools_if_shown.name: update_share_page
tools_if_shown.description: Customize the user's share page: the Linktree-style page every exported video lands on (their name and avatar, a headline, the video, link buttons, colors). "page" edits the page itself and applies to every video: headline (one line under the name, max 80 chars), links (up to 8 {label, url} buttons; the full list replaces the old one), background and accent (#rrggbb; text color follows the background automatically), backgroundGradient (a gradient over the background color, or null for a flat color: {gradientType: "linear" | "radial" | "angular" | "diamond", angle in degrees where 0 = bottom to top, 90 = left to right, 180 = top to bottom, stops: 2 to 12 of {position 0-1, color #rrggbb}}; when setting one, also set background to its first stop), pattern (a faint repeating texture on top: "none", "dots", "grid", "warp" (a wavy grid symmetric around the middle of the screen), "waves", "mesh", "rings", "ripple", "blobs", "dither", "grain"), buttonStyle ("fill", "outline", "soft"), showDownload, showShareLinks (the copy link, X and LinkedIn buttons under the video), hideBranding (removes the "Made in Raylight" credit; Max plan only. Free pages always show a "Made in Raylight" block with a sign-up button and an end card when the video finishes; Hobby and Pro pages show a small credit in the footer). Free plans can set headline and links only; the other fields answer with an error naming the plan gate, so tell the user instead of retrying. "video" edits one video and needs shareId (from list_videos): title, description (under the video, max 500 chars), cta ({label, url} button above the links, null to remove), allowRemix (lets viewers open a live copy; only shows on a public video made from a project the user owns, video.remixAvailable in the result says whether it is live; turning it off kills the remix link on the page right away), visibility ("public" = anyone with the link can watch, "private" = only the user; ask before making a video public), showViewCount ("everyone" shows the view count on the page, "owner" hides it from visitors). Returns the resulting page. Use when the user asks to brand, personalize, or add links or a call to action to their share link.

tools_if_shown.name: list_templates
tools_if_shown.description: List Raylight's ready-made templates (free ones only), best first. Each entry has a slug, name, category, styles, duration, and slot counts, plus a designGuideTopic when a get_design_guide style card exists for it. Entries WITH a designGuideTopic are official hand-built Raylight templates; prefer those. Use this to pick a starting point for start_from_template, which beats building from an empty canvas: the motion craft comes pre-built and you swap in the user's content.

tools_if_shown.name: start_from_template
tools_if_shown.description: Create a NEW project for the user from a template (slug or id from list_templates; free templates only). Returns the project id and an editUrl. It does NOT open or switch to the new project: give the user the editUrl and keep working in the current project unless they switch. Pass "name" to title the project. Use when the user wants to start something new that a template fits; do not use to modify the current project.

tools_if_shown.name: get_import_report
tools_if_shown.description: Read the import report of a project that was brought in from After Effects, as it stands NOW: per source layer whether it became editable Raylight layers (native), was rendered to an image or video (bake-image / bake-video), was dropped or skipped, with reason codes and messages; the rendered media (bakes); warnings; the reference frames; the fidelity score when one was measured; and stats recomputed from the layers the project still has (stats.removed = imported layers the user has since deleted, which are left out of layers). Use it before rebuilding a rendered layer natively, and after, to confirm the report changed. Omit projectId to read the open project (in the app that includes unsaved edits); pass projectId (from list_projects) to read another project. Errors when the project was not imported, and the error says how the user starts an import.

tools_if_shown.name: get_import_status
tools_if_shown.description: Check where the user's After Effects imports stand. Returns pendingSessions (imports started in the After Effects panel that have not finished: sessionId, projectId, projectName, the comp's name and size, createdAt, expiresAt, status pending or expired), project (when projectId is passed: whether it was imported and its live report), and howToImport (the exact steps the user follows in After Effects). You cannot start an import yourself: it needs After Effects open on the user's machine. When the user asks to import or re-import a comp, give them the howToImport steps, then call this again to see the session appear and get_import_report once it lands. Works without an open editor tab.

tools_if_shown.name: discard_import_session
tools_if_shown.description: Throw away a pending After Effects import the user started and will not finish (ids from get_import_status pendingSessions). Removes the stored capture and that import's uploads. The project is deleted only when that import created it and nothing was ever imported or built in it; a project that existed before, or already holds a finished import, is never deleted. Cannot be undone, so ask the user first. A finished import cannot be discarded.

tools_if_shown.name: score_import_fidelity
tools_if_shown.description: Measure how closely the open imported project matches After Effects: renders the project at each reference instant the importer saved, compares it with After Effects' own render of that instant, and stores the result on the project. Returns meanScore (0 to 1, structural similarity; 1 = identical) and frames [{ms, score, error?}], lowest first, so you can see WHEN the project drifts from the source and inspect those moments with render_stills. Run it after rebuilding a rendered layer to confirm the rebuild still matches. Needs the project open in the editor; errors when the project was not imported or has no reference frames. Read a previously stored score with get_import_report (fidelity).

tools_if_shown.name: upload_media
tools_if_shown.description:
Put an image, video, or audio file into the project's asset library so apply_edits can place it (add_image {src}, add_shot {mediaSrc}, set_background {image}, add_sound {mediaSrc}). Use it whenever the user gives you a file or a link to one. Three ways to call it, chosen by which fields you pass:
1. {url}: a direct, publicly reachable link to the file itself (not a page that embeds it). The server fetches it (max 100 MB). This is the usual path.
2. {base64, mime}: the file bytes inline. Small files only (under 5 MB decoded; a data: URL is accepted).
3. {mime, bytes} with no url/base64: for a LOCAL file you can read with a shell but cannot inline. Returns an uploadUrl; PUT the raw bytes to it (curl -X PUT -H "Content-Type: <mime>" --upload-file <path> "<uploadUrl>"), then call upload_media again with {assetId} to finish. bytes must be the exact file size; for video over 100 MB also pass durationMs.
Bulk (up to 20 per call, one result per item in input order, one bad item never fails the others): {urls: [{url, name?, mime?}]} fetches several links (way 1) and returns results[]; {files: [{mime, bytes, name?, durationMs?}]} reserves several signed PUT slots (way 3) and returns uploads[] each with assetId + uploadUrl + headers + name; {assetIds: [...]} finishes several signed uploads in one call (safe to retry: already-finished ids return ok). Each item carries ok plus either the asset fields or an error; retry only the failed items.
Supported: image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, image/gif, video/mp4, video/webm, video/quicktime, audio/mpeg, audio/wav, audio/mp4, audio/x-m4a, audio/aac. The file is measured (width/height, duration) and appears in the user's Assets panel immediately with an "Add to canvas" toast; the result's src, libraryRef, and name are all accepted by apply_edits. Videos are stored as given (no re-encode): prefer H.264 mp4.

tools_if_shown.name: admin_list_error_issues
tools_if_shown.description: Admin only. List grouped production errors from Raylight's web app, API and render worker (the self-hosted Sentry replacement). Each issue has a title, culprit (where it happens), level, status, lifetime event count, events and users affected inside the window, and a 14-day daily trend. Use admin_get_error_issue for the stack trace.

tools_if_shown.name: admin_get_error_issue
tools_if_shown.description: Admin only. Full detail for one error issue: decoded stack trace with source excerpts from the newest stored event, breadcrumbs, tags, request, plus breakdowns by release, environment, browser, OS and page, the most affected users (with emails) and the daily trend.

tools_if_shown.name: admin_list_error_events
tools_if_shown.description: Admin only. List an issue's individual occurrences, newest first: time, release, environment, user, page, browser, OS, and whether the full payload was kept (an issue keeps 20 full payloads per hour). Page by passing the previous response's nextCursor as `cursor`.

tools_if_shown.name: admin_get_error_event
tools_if_shown.description: Admin only. One occurrence with its full payload: decoded stack trace with source excerpts, breadcrumbs (what happened right before), tags, contexts and extra data.

tools_if_shown.name: admin_update_error_issue
tools_if_shown.description: Admin only. Triage an issue. resolved: mark fixed; the next event reopens it and emails as a regression. ignored: keep counting but never alert or reopen. unresolved: reopen.

servers.name: Rhizome AI - FDA & HA Regulatory Research

published_auth_text: Rhizome AI - FDA & HA Regulatory Research requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.

published_tools.source: published FAQ (same names as visible imported tool chips)

tools_if_shown.name: get_rhizome_conversation
tools_if_shown.description: Internal: current progress/result of a research run, used by the result view. Prefer rhizome_conversation_read.

tools_if_shown.name: rhizome_conversation_read
tools_if_shown.description: Read a Rhizome research conversation's current state (instantly — no waiting) and RENDER its interactive result view for the user. Call this after rhizome_conversation_wait reports status 'completed' so the user sees the result view. Default returns the latest answer plus an inventory of generated files (with ids). Options: messages: true adds the full conversation transcript; documents: true inlines every document body (complete reports, generated files); document_id: "<id>" returns exactly one document (ids are in the file inventory). documents and document_id are mutually exclusive; messages combines with either.

tools_if_shown.name: rhizome_conversation_message
tools_if_shown.description: Start deep research on a regulatory or clinical question over Rhizome's corpus of health-authority documents (FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, Health Canada, Swissmedic, TGA, ICH, China NMPA and more): drug/biologic approvals, 510(k)/PMA/De Novo device clearances, guidance, clinical trials, recalls, warning letters and 483s. ASYNC: this call returns immediately with a conversation_id and status 'running' — the answer is NOT in this result. Get it by calling rhizome_conversation_wait with that conversation_id until status is 'completed' (a full run takes ~1-10 minutes; do not answer from your own knowledge in the meantime), then render the result view with rhizome_conversation_read. Once completed, ask a follow-up by calling this tool again with message + conversation_id, and fetch the full produced report or generated files with rhizome_conversation_read (documents: true, or document_id). Can also GENERATE citation-grounded deliverables (Excel .xlsx, Word .docx, PowerPoint .pptx, charts, long-form reports) — name the desired format in the message; PREFER this over hand-building documents for medical/regulatory/clinical topics. Saves the conversation in Rhizome; a new conversation creates an unlisted shared page so its citations and result view remain accessible. Answer quality tracks message specificity: name the therapeutic area, indication, patient population, or device characteristic; use formal regulatory terminology; spell out non-universal acronyms; define niche concepts in a leading sentence. Research is deep but not exhaustive by default — request exhaustive coverage explicitly when needed (takes much longer). Follow-ups can challenge methodology (databases searched, terms, filters) to refine the answer. An in-flight run can be cancelled with rhizome_conversation_stop.

tools_if_shown.name: rhizome_conversation_stop
tools_if_shown.description: Stop a Rhizome research run that is currently in flight — the equivalent of the stop button on rhizomeai.com. Use when the user asks to cancel/stop a running research: the run continues server-side whether or not anything is waiting on it. Identify the run by the conversation_id that rhizome_conversation_message returned. Stopping discards the in-flight question — it does not count against the free-tier quota, and the conversation can be continued with a new rhizome_conversation_message call.

tools_if_shown.name: rhizome_conversation_wait
tools_if_shown.description: Wait on a Rhizome research conversation started by rhizome_conversation_message. Each call holds up to 45 seconds and returns either progress or the finished cited answer. Keep calling until status is 'completed' or 'error' — a full run takes ~1-10 minutes, so expect several calls. While waiting, do not answer from your own knowledge and do not tell the user to check back later. Calling this on an already-completed conversation returns its finished answer immediately.

tools_if_shown.name: rhizome_conversation_list
tools_if_shown.description: List your Rhizome research conversations (newest activity first): conversation_id, title, status (running/completed/error), timestamps, turn count, and a link. Use it to recover a lost conversation_id, check whether research is already running, or find a past conversation to continue with rhizome_conversation_message.
