tools_if_shown.name: load_braintrust_skill
tools_if_shown.description:
Load a Braintrust workflow guide before using its related tools.

Available skills:
- braintrust/automations-workflow: Set up, validate, and manage Braintrust alerts and scheduled Loop automations, including Patterns, threshold-triggered work, Slack or webhook delivery, and existing automation refinement. Use when a user asks to react to matching log or environment events, monitor a threshold, schedule recurring agent analysis, configure Patterns, or inspect an alert or Loop automation.
- braintrust/bro: Restate the last message in plain human language, with no jargon.
- braintrust/evaluator-workflow: Create, test, refine, deploy, rewind, and visualize Braintrust evaluators (scorers and classifiers) interactively. Use when a user asks to build or improve an evaluator, apply it to production logs with an online-scoring rule, backfill results, or review results.
- braintrust/topics-workflow: Topics allow you to discover clusters from traces using a pipeline that involves preprocessing traces (converting raw trace data into a textual representation with JavaScript code), computing facets (using an LLM to convert the preprocessed data into 1-2 sentences), and clustering (using algorithms like HDBSCAN). These clusters are useful for discovering use cases, monitoring failures, and tracking these trends over time. Use when configuring, evaluating, or improving Topics, facets, preprocessors, or Topics automations.
- braintrust/pattern-analysis: Investigate Braintrust project traces for high-confidence recurring behaviors, then create, validate, or update Pattern records with supporting evidence. Use when a user asks to find patterns, investigate a suspected recurring behavior, or create or update an existing Pattern based on trace analysis. Do not use for routine queries, summaries, chart creation, or configuring a Patterns automation.

Follow the returned Markdown for the rest of the conversation.

tools_if_shown.name: get_trace_work_items
tools_if_shown.description:
Only call this tool while analyzing the work steps of a trace from the trace Work view. It returns a deterministic, chronological list of meaningful LLM and tool spans for work-section and per-span analysis.

Do not use it for general trace queries, summaries, or debugging.

tools_if_shown.name: update_trace_work_report
tools_if_shown.description:
Only call this tool while analyzing the work steps of a single trace from the trace Work view. Its sole purpose is to save chronological work sections and concise annotations for the meaningful LLM and tool spans in that trace.

Call this tool exactly once after the entire trajectory has been partitioned. Define each contiguous section with span IDs from parallel_inference, covering every item exactly once in chronological order. Include one annotation per work item in the same order with its matching span ID. Do not calculate time or token totals because the UI derives them from the trace. Do not call this tool for general trace debugging, summaries, or unrelated analysis.

tools_if_shown.name: update_debug_report
tools_if_shown.description:
Save or replace the diagnosis report for one trace. Use this independently from update_trace_work_report after identifying concrete failure modes and evidence, or when a user asks to edit the existing diagnosis.

Pass the complete replacement report, not a partial patch. Every evidence item should identify its supporting span and exact field or JSON path.

tools_if_shown.name: generate_monitor_chart
tools_if_shown.description:
Preview a Braintrust Monitoring chart for project logs.

CHART DESIGN:
- Use a timeseries for trends over time: bars for countable discrete things (sums and counts) and lines for gauges (averages and percentiles). Use a toplist for groups ranked by an aggregate, and a single value for one simple large number.
- For counts, use a raw BTQL value with a separate count aggregator, such as { btql: "1", aggregator: { type: "count" } }. If you write the aggregate inline, use count(1); count() is invalid.
- Use a meaningful unit for the measure if applicable.
- Group when it makes the chart easier to interpret or reveals interesting trends. Avoid high-cardinality groupings that can be slow to query or difficult to read.

Use this after inspecting the available fields and before saving a chart. It returns a timeless chartConfig plus the optional page-level timeFrame used for the preview, without modifying any Monitoring view. Relative timeFrame presets remain live; omit timeFrame to use the Monitoring default. If the user asks to save it, pass chartConfig unchanged as an entry in create_monitoring_view.charts or as update_monitoring_view.chart. When creating a view, pass timeFrame separately as create_monitoring_view.timeFrame.

tools_if_shown.name: list_monitoring_views
tools_if_shown.description: List the saved Monitoring views and chart IDs for a project so the user can choose a view or chart to inspect or edit.

tools_if_shown.name: get_monitoring_view
tools_if_shown.description: Inspect a saved Monitoring view, including its options and ordered chart definitions. Copy the returned chart_id unchanged when updating or deleting a chart.

tools_if_shown.name: create_monitoring_view
tools_if_shown.description:
Create a project-scoped Monitoring view, optionally containing charts that were already previewed with generate_monitor_chart.

Only call this when the user explicitly asks to create or save a view. Pass each returned chartConfig unchanged in the charts array, using a one-element array for a single chart. Pass the preview timeFrame separately as the optional view-level timeFrame; relative presets such as "3d" remain live. Omit timeFrame to use the Monitoring page default.

tools_if_shown.name: update_monitoring_view
tools_if_shown.description:
Apply one or more chart or section edits to an existing project Monitoring view. Pass project_id and view_id. For a single chart edit, set the top-level operation to exactly insert, update, or remove. For section edits or bulk edits, pass an operations array instead; all operations are applied in order with one save. insert_group creates a section containing the provided existing chart_ids. remove_group deletes the section and keeps its charts at the section's position.

Use get_monitoring_view first. For update or remove, pass its chart_id unchanged as chart_id. For insert or update, pass chartConfig returned unchanged by generate_monitor_chart as chart. Use bulk operations when several charts need the same coordinated change. Only call this when the user explicitly asks to save the change.

tools_if_shown.name: create_prompt
tools_if_shown.description:
Create a versioned Braintrust prompt using the same function representation as project.prompts.create() and bt functions push.

Provide either a completion-style prompt or chat messages. By default, the tool fails if the slug already exists; set if_exists to replace to create a new version, or ignore to leave the existing prompt unchanged.

tools_if_shown.name: create_evaluator
tools_if_shown.description:
Create a versioned Braintrust LLM or inline code evaluator. Set output_type to score for numeric scores or classification for categorical labels.

For an LLM score evaluator, provide choice_scores. For an LLM classification evaluator, provide choices without numeric mappings. By default, the tool fails if the slug already exists; set if_exists to replace to create a new version, or ignore to leave the existing evaluator unchanged.

tools_if_shown.name: create_human_review_score
tools_if_shown.description: Create a native Human Review score definition for a project: categorical choices, a numeric slider, or a free-form text field such as Review notes. Call once per score. Fails if the name already exists.

tools_if_shown.name: list_automations
tools_if_shown.description: List a project's automations, including online scoring rules, alerts, exports, retention policies, Topics automations, and other automation kinds. Returns complete configurations so an existing automation can be inspected before using a specialized update tool.

tools_if_shown.name: set_automation_status
tools_if_shown.description: Pause or activate an alert, scheduled job, or online scoring rule. This controls configured online scoring rules, not reusable scorer functions. Repeating the current status is a successful no-op. In hosted Agent Runtime, call braintrust_context to obtain the current project ID.

tools_if_shown.name: test_evaluator
tools_if_shown.description: Run one saved, global, or inline evaluator on representative inputs without writing results. Inputs may be inline evaluator rows containing fields such as input, output, expected, and metadata, or canonical span, trace, and group references. Inline rows can include only the fields the evaluator needs. The function field accepts a saved function_id, a global_function, or inline_evaluator using the same definition as create_evaluator. Inline evaluators do not need to be saved first. Inline code must define a top-level handler function. Use representative passes, failures, and ambiguous cases before creating an online-scoring rule.

tools_if_shown.name: update_online_scoring_rule
tools_if_shown.description: Save or rewind an online-scoring rule that runs saved evaluator functions. This tool is the approval surface for both mutations: state the proposed parameters, then call it without asking the user to type a separate confirmation. For save, provide function_ids, the rule scope, filters, and sampling rate. New rules default to paused; pass status active only when the user has authorized processing new traffic. Existing rules preserve their status when omitted. A group scope requires group_by and placement and accepts optional interval_seconds and max_traces. For rewind, require an existing active automation_id and choose start_time from the user's requested window. Activate a paused rule with set_automation_status before rewinding it. Do not repeatedly resubmit it to poll for progress.

tools_if_shown.name: enable_topics_automation
tools_if_shown.description:
Enable Topics for a Braintrust project.

Before using this tool, load and follow "braintrust/topics-workflow" with load_braintrust_skill, then inspect existing automations with list_automations using kind "topic". Provide a distinct name to create an additional Topics automation; reusing a name returns the existing automation without changing it. This creates the configured facet topic maps, supports span, trace, or group scope, and defaults new automations to trace scope and the Task facet when omitted. It seeds processing for new traffic but does not rewind historical data.

tools_if_shown.name: set_topics_automation
tools_if_shown.description:
Update an existing Topics automation's configuration.

Before using this tool, load and follow "braintrust/topics-workflow" with load_braintrust_skill and inspect the current automation with list_automations using kind "topic". This changes facets, topic maps, scope, filters, sampling, or timing without rewinding historical data.

tools_if_shown.name: rewind_topics_automation
tools_if_shown.description:
Rewind an existing Topics automation to process historical data from an explicit start time or recent window.

Before using this tool, load and follow "braintrust/topics-workflow" with load_braintrust_skill. Estimate the eligible population and obtain authorization for the historical scope before calling it.

tools_if_shown.name: create_facet
tools_if_shown.description:
Create a versioned Braintrust facet that extracts structured information from spans or traces.

Before using this tool, load and follow "braintrust/topics-workflow" with load_braintrust_skill. Topics and topic-classification requests use that workflow.

This is a deployment/promotion tool, not a prompt-testing tool. Develop with inline test_facet_on_trace calls and run_eval experiments first; do not create a facet merely to test a candidate.

Facet extraction always uses Braintrust's built-in facet model; callers do not select a model.

The project default preprocessor is used when none is provided. By default, the tool fails if the slug already exists; set if_exists to replace to create a new version, or ignore to leave the existing facet unchanged.

tools_if_shown.name: create_preprocessor
tools_if_shown.description:
Create a versioned Braintrust preprocessor from inline JavaScript using the same QuickJS runtime as the Braintrust UI.

When the preprocessor is for Topics or a facet, first load and follow "braintrust/topics-workflow" with load_braintrust_skill.

By default, the tool fails if the slug already exists; set if_exists to replace to create a new version, or ignore to leave the existing preprocessor unchanged.

tools_if_shown.name: get_project_settings
tools_if_shown.description: Get the typed settings for a Braintrust project. The response includes the stored settings and the effective default preprocessor, resolving an unset default to the built-in "thread" preprocessor.

tools_if_shown.name: set_project_default_preprocessor
tools_if_shown.description:
Set or clear the default preprocessor for a Braintrust project.

When configuring Topics, first load and follow "braintrust/topics-workflow" with load_braintrust_skill. Pass a saved preprocessor reference, a global preprocessor such as "thread", or null to restore the built-in default. This changes the default used by facets and other project functions that do not explicitly select a preprocessor.

tools_if_shown.name: test_preprocessor_on_trace
tools_if_shown.description:
Run a saved, global, or inline preprocessor on one to 50 canonical span, trace, or group references concurrently using the same preview path as the Braintrust UI. For trace and group references, a custom preprocessor runs independently on each source span. Top-level array items are merged in trace order and exact-deduplicated; distinct joined transcript strings remain separate items, so return atomic items such as {role, content} for conversations. Each result is capped at 128 KiB. Use run_eval for larger sets.

When testing for Topics or a facet, first load and follow "braintrust/topics-workflow" with load_braintrust_skill.

This executes code and may create invocation logs, but it does not write a score to the source trace.

tools_if_shown.name: test_facet_on_trace
tools_if_shown.description:
Run an inline facet definition with a saved, global, inline, or project-default preprocessor on one to ten canonical span, trace, or group references concurrently using the same preview path as the Braintrust UI. Use run_eval for larger sets.

Before using this tool, load and follow "braintrust/topics-workflow" with load_braintrust_skill. Do not use one or a few previews as a substitute for its representative-trace discovery stage.

Inline facet previews use Braintrust's built-in facet model; callers do not select a model.

This may call an AI provider and create invocation logs, but it does not write the facet result to the source trace.

tools_if_shown.name: run_eval
tools_if_shown.description:
Run a Braintrust experiment through the authenticated Eval API with a hosted dataset, inline rows, or a prior experiment, any saved or inline functional task, and zero or more saved or inline scorers.

When a prior experiment is used as data, its outputs become expected values unless an expected value was already recorded. This does not require sandbox credentials. It creates an experiment and may execute user-supplied code or invoke AI providers, so it can incur compute and model usage. The MCP service supplies the caller's Braintrust token, forces streaming for long runs, and returns the experiment start metadata and final summary.

tools_if_shown.name: edit_dataset_rows
tools_if_shown.description:
Insert, update, or delete up to 1000 Braintrust dataset rows using explicit operations.

Target an existing dataset by ID or name. Set create_if_missing only when a new named dataset should be created. In hosted Agent Runtime, call braintrust_context to obtain the current project and page dataset IDs.

tools_if_shown.name: add_to_dataset
tools_if_shown.description:
Add up to 1000 project log rows to a Braintrust dataset by row ID, like the UI's "Add to dataset", without reading and re-sending their contents.

Find candidate rows with sql_query against project_logs, then pass their `id` values. Each copied row keeps the log's input, metadata, and tags, takes its expected value from the log's expected (or output), and links back to the source log via origin. Target an existing dataset by ID or name. Set create_if_missing only when a new named dataset should be created. In hosted Agent Runtime, call braintrust_context to obtain the current project ID.

tools_if_shown.name: list_slack_channels
tools_if_shown.description:
List the Slack workspaces connected to a project's org and the public channels in a workspace, so a Slack alert action targets the channel the user named instead of a guessed ID.

Call this before setting any Slack action's workspace_id and channel, passing the user's requested channel name as query. Match the requested channel to a returned channel and use its exact id; never invent or reuse a channel ID from context. If the org has multiple connected workspaces, workspace_id is null and channels is null until you call again with a specific workspace_id. If the channel isn't listed, ask the user for the channel ID rather than guessing. In hosted Agent Runtime, call braintrust_context to obtain the current project ID.

tools_if_shown.name: create_log_alert
tools_if_shown.description: Create an alert for individual matching project logs. config.btql_filter is a boolean expression, not a SELECT query, and config.interval_seconds throttles repeated notifications without aggregating logs. In hosted Agent Runtime, call braintrust_context to obtain the current project ID.

tools_if_shown.name: create_environment_update_alert
tools_if_shown.description: Create an alert for environment updates. Use config.environment_filter to limit notifications to specific environment slugs, or omit it to match all environments. In hosted Agent Runtime, call braintrust_context to obtain the current project ID.

tools_if_shown.name: create_threshold_alert
tools_if_shown.description:
Create a threshold alert for an aggregate over a recent project-data window. Use this for averages, counts, rates, percentages, percentiles, distributions, or other conditions evaluated on a schedule.

config.threshold.calculation.btql_query must return at most one row with the numeric or null column named by config.threshold.calculation.output.value_column. Put any minimum sample size in the query, and do not add absolute time bounds because the runtime supplies the evaluation window. Use config.window.evaluation_delay_seconds when ingestion or asynchronous scoring arrives late. config.threshold.policy.pending_seconds controls how long a breach must persist, while renotify_interval_seconds controls reminders.

tools_if_shown.name: create_scheduled_loop_job
tools_if_shown.description: Create a custom Loop job that runs on an interval or cron schedule over a recent project-data window. The config must include Loop instructions and cannot include a threshold, so the job runs for every scheduled window. Delivery actions are exposed to Loop as tools. In hosted Agent Runtime, call braintrust_context to obtain the current project ID.

tools_if_shown.name: search_docs
tools_if_shown.description:
Search Braintrust documentation to find relevant information and guidance.

      IMPORTANT: For SDK installation/setup tasks, do not use this tool. Instead, read the mcp resource docs://sdk-install

This tool searches through the official Braintrust documentation using semantic search to find the most relevant content for your query.

Use this tool to:
- Learn more about what experiments, datasets, prompts, playgrounds, and logs are, and how to use them in the API or SDK.
- Understand how to write evals and create scorers
- Find sample code and guidance on how to add tracing for custom code as well as popular frameworks like the Vercel AI SDK.
- Find code examples that are relevant to your use cases.

What it returns:
- Multiple documentation snippets ranked by relevance
- Each snippet includes the content, headers hierarchy, and path
- Content is Markdown formatted

Example queries:
- "How do I create an experiment?"
- "Setting up scorers"
- "Using metadata fields"
- "Prompt playground features"

tools_if_shown.name: lookup_users
tools_if_shown.description:
Look up human Braintrust organization members by exact user IDs, partial name or email, or an explicit request to list all users. Provide exactly one of user_ids, search, or list_all: true.

Use this to resolve span_attributes.created_by_user_id and Braintrust reviewer or assignee IDs. Do not interpret arbitrary metadata.user_id values as Braintrust organization users. When resolving query results, deduplicate and pass all user IDs in one call rather than making one call per ID. If a name search returns multiple possible users, ask the user to disambiguate before continuing.

tools_if_shown.name: lookup_api_keys
tools_if_shown.description:
Look up Braintrust API keys and service tokens by exact IDs, exact name, or an explicit request to list all visible keys. Provide exactly one of api_key_ids, name, or list_all: true. Results follow the existing API-key and service-token visibility rules; inaccessible IDs remain unresolved.

Use this to resolve span_attributes.created_by_api_key_id, which may identify either a personal API key or a service token. When resolving query results, deduplicate and pass all IDs in one call rather than making one call per ID. If an exact name lookup returns multiple possible keys, ask the user to disambiguate before continuing.

tools_if_shown.name: resolve_object
tools_if_shown.description: Convert names to IDs (or vice versa) and parse Braintrust URLs. App URLs retain their organization scope. Pattern, prompt, and scorer links return the containing project as object_id and the resource as row_id; query that project collection with an id filter. Read docs://url-formats for supported URL patterns.

tools_if_shown.name: list_recent_objects
tools_if_shown.description:
List recently created projects, experiments, datasets, prompts, or functions you have access to. You can use this to browse for objects
and as a crude way of searching for objects (you will need to filter the results yourself).

If an object you expect does not show up, then use the `startin_after` parameter to paginate through more results.

If a user asks for something like "list my recent experiments", then you do not need to list through the set of projects. You can just provide
the project name, and then list the experiments within that project. If you get an error, then perhaps the project name is incorrect, and you
should fall back to listing projects first to find the one the user is referring to.

tools_if_shown.name: infer_schema
tools_if_shown.description:
Analyze the structure and content of a data source by inferring the schema and showing the most common values for each field.

This tool discovers:
- All available fields in the data source (input, output, metadata.*, scores.*, etc.)
- The data type of each field (string, number, array, object)
- The most frequently occurring values for each field with their counts
- The complete field paths for use in SQL queries

For each field, you'll see:
- The full path as an array (e.g., ['metadata', 'user_id'] which translates to metadata.user_id in SQL)
- The data type (string, number, boolean, etc.)
- Top 10 most common values sorted by frequency with exact counts

Large results are truncated to fit the context window: sample values may be shortened and capped at 3 per field, and if there are still too many fields, data contains a subset and totalFields reports the full field count. When totalFields is present, use sql_query to explore fields not shown here.

This is essential for:
- Discovering what fields exist before writing queries
- Understanding the actual values in your data (e.g., what user IDs exist, what models are used)
- Finding the exact field paths for SQL queries
- Identifying patterns in your data (e.g., most common inputs, frequent error types)
- Understanding cardinality (how many unique values exist)

Example insights from the tool:
- See all metadata fields like metadata.user_id, metadata.model, metadata.session_id
- Discover custom fields you may not know about
- Find the most active users or most used models
- Understand what values to filter on in your queries


Time range filter guidance:
- All queries MUST have a time range filter.
- If you do not provide a time range filter the request will fail.
- If the user does not specify a time range, always use the default time range filter provided in the prompt.
- If the user specifies a time range in the prompt, always use the time range they specified.
- If default time range is missing and user does not specify a time range, always use the last 3 days.
- Unless the user specifies a specific from and to hour, always provide 06:00:00.000Z as the from hour and 05:59:59.999Z as the to hour to go along with the year, month, and day.
- When generating a custom time range for a relative date request, derive the year, month, and day from the <current_date> tag or user's specified date rather than from examples.

tools_if_shown.name: new_pattern
tools_if_shown.description: Report a new project pattern. First load braintrust/pattern-analysis, which uses search_patterns to check for potential duplicates and defines evidence and reporting limits. Always include Frequency (evidence.frequency) when existing data can identify affected traces. Other monitor charts are optional additions, not a substitute. If Frequency cannot be measured, attach representative trace evidence and explain the missing signal. Include an audit reason.

tools_if_shown.name: search_patterns
tools_if_shown.description: Search existing patterns in a project by text, semantic similarity, ID, status, or quality. limit must be 1–100. Omit query for a listing. Ordinary listings and text searches use stable insertion order, newest first; while has_more is true, pass the returned cursor with the same project and filters to continue. Cursors do not support similar_to. Load braintrust/pattern-analysis before a pattern investigation. Use similar_to with one or more existing pattern IDs or unreported pattern drafts to catch duplicates with different wording.

tools_if_shown.name: update_pattern
tools_if_shown.description: Update an existing project pattern's content, status, quality, or feedback, and optionally attach quoted evidence to matching traces. Closing an active pattern saves the reason as feedback. Before using this tool, load braintrust/pattern-analysis and use search_patterns to inspect the current pattern. When revising evidence, include Frequency (evidence.frequency) whenever measurable; other monitors are optional additions.

tools_if_shown.name: sql_query
tools_if_shown.description:
# Braintrust MCP `sql_query` tool

This tool is NOT a SQL string. You fill separate parameters and the server assembles:

```
SELECT {select} FROM {object_type}({object_ids}[, shape => '{shape}']) [WHERE {where}] [GROUP BY {group_by}] [ORDER BY {order_by}] [LIMIT {limit}]
```

Every clause parameter holds ONLY the fragment after its keyword — never include `WHERE`, `GROUP BY`, `ORDER BY`, `SELECT`, or `FROM` inside `where`/`group_by`/`order_by`/`select`, and never write a `FROM` yourself (`object_type`/`object_ids` generate it).

## Parameters

| Param                 | Put                                                                                                                                                                                              | Never put                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `select`              | columns/exprs, comma-separated: `"id, root_span_id, created, error"`                                                                                                                             | `SELECT`, a `FROM`                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `object_type`         | one of `project_logs` \| `experiment` \| `dataset` (also valid but rarer: `prompt_session`, `playground_logs`, `project_prompts`, `project_functions`, `org_prompts`, `org_functions`)           | anything else                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `object_ids`          | array of UUID strings, same type, e.g. `["<project_id>"]`                                                                                                                                        | mixed object types in one call                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `where`               | condition text only: `"error IS NOT NULL AND created > now() - interval 1 day"`. **`project_logs` must be scoped** — either a `created` range **or** an `id`/`root_span_id` filter (see Filters) | leading `WHERE`; a `created` range added on top of an `id`/`root_span_id` lookup (silently returns nothing if the target is older); a `created` range on `experiment`/`dataset`/`view`                                                       |
| `group_by`            | column list only: `"metadata.model"`; keys must be columnar — see Grouping                                                                                                                       | leading `GROUP BY`; a dynamic expr like `lower(metadata.model)` (blocked, see table); `input`/`output` or any path under them (blocked, see Grouping)                                                                                        |
| `order_by`            | `"created DESC"` — **only `created` sorts via the index**                                                                                                                                        | leading `ORDER BY`; `metrics.*`, a computed expr (`metrics.end - metrics.start`), `root_span_id`, or multi-key sorts (all trip the sort-pushdown lint — drop `order_by` and sort client-side, or `force_ignore_linter` if already id-scoped) |
| `limit`               | integer, default 10, max 1000                                                                                                                                                                    | omit when projecting large fields (see lint table)                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `shape`               | `spans` (default) \| `traces` \| `summary`                                                                                                                                                       | any `group_by`, aggregate, or `order_by` with `summary` — always lint-blocked (do those on `spans`; see Shape selection)                                                                                                                     |
| `preview_length`      | leave default (1024) unless you need full untruncated values (`-1`)                                                                                                                              | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `force_ignore_linter` | only after rewriting per the lint message once; use when the query is already selective/bounded and the residual warning is unavoidable                                                          | as a first response to a lint block                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `return_url`          | `true` only for large/unbounded downloads                                                                                                                                                        | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

## Field names that actually exist (bind errors are silent-wrong, not always loud)

- `type`, `parent_id` as bare fields **fail to bind**: `Field 'type' not found in schema`. Use `span_attributes.type`, `span_parents`.
- **Span hierarchy lives in `span_parents`, an array of parent `span_id`s — there is no `parent_id` column.** To attribute spans to their parents: select `span_parents` on the child rows, then run a second query filtering `span_id IN (<those ids>)`. Do not try to join in one query.
- Token/latency fields are **shape-dependent** (picking the wrong one is silent — returns `null`, no error):
  - On `spans`/`traces`: per-span `metrics.tokens` (also `metrics.prompt_tokens`, `metrics.completion_tokens`); latency is `metrics.end - metrics.start`. `metrics.duration`/`metrics.total_tokens` are null here.
  - On `summary`: the per-trace rollups `metrics.total_tokens` and `metrics.duration` (`metrics.tokens` is null) — but reachable only via a plain summary read (no GROUP BY/aggregate/ORDER BY; see Shape selection). **To aggregate tokens/latency across traces, use spans**: `SUM(metrics.tokens)`, `metrics.end - metrics.start`.
- **`metrics.estimated_cost` aggregates but never filters.** It is a computed value, not a stored column — the binder rewrites it to `estimated_cost()`, and a function on the field side cannot be pushed into the index. `SUM(metrics.estimated_cost)` / `AVG(...)` in `select` are fine; **any** use in `where` is blocked (`metrics.estimated_cost IS NOT NULL`, `metrics.estimated_cost > 0`, and the explicit `estimated_cost() ...` all fail with `Cannot execute filter over the index`). To restrict to rows that have cost, filter a real column instead — `metrics.prompt_tokens IS NOT NULL` or `span_attributes.type = 'llm'` — or drop the filter and let the aggregate skip nulls.
- Nested fields always need the parent: `metadata.user_id`, `scores.Factuality`, `span_attributes.name`.
- Braintrust organization members are recorded in `span_attributes.created_by_user_id`. Resolve those IDs in bulk with `lookup_users`. API keys and service tokens are recorded in `span_attributes.created_by_api_key_id`; resolve them in bulk with `lookup_api_keys`. These are system span attributes, not metadata. `metadata.user_id` and similarly named metadata fields are application-defined and must not be assumed to identify Braintrust users or keys.
- `is_root = true` restricts to root spans (needed for root-only metadata/latency).
- Aggregate functions: `count`, `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `percentile(expr, p)` (not `PERCENTILE_CONT`/`percentile_cont`).
- **Aggregation only constrains `select` once you use an aggregate.** A plain projection needs no `group_by` — `select: "id, root_span_id, created, error"` returns a table of rows and is the normal shape for browsing. As soon as `select` contains an aggregate, every _other_ column in `select` must also appear in `group_by`:
  - aggregate + a bare column, no `group_by` → `Cannot mix aggregate and non-aggregate expressions without GROUP BY`
  - `group_by` set, but a selected column is missing from it → `Each measure must contain an aggregate function` (the "measure" is that ungrouped column)
  - Fix either by adding the column to `group_by`, or removing it from `select`.
- Bucketing a timestamp: `date_trunc('<unit>', <field>)`, e.g. `date_trunc('hour', created)`. Units include `minute`, `hour`, `day`, `week`, and arbitrary intervals such as `'300 seconds'`. Works on any timestamp field.
- **This is not ClickHouse, Postgres, or BigQuery SQL.** Builtins from those dialects do not exist and fail with `Unknown function: X` — there is no `date_bin`, `toStartOfHour`/`toStartOfDay`, `toDate`, `countIf`, `has`, or `position*`. Use only the functions listed here; if you need something else, compute it from the returned rows instead of inventing a builtin.
- Time: `now()`, `interval N day` — number **unquoted**, unit **singular** (`interval 7 day`, `interval 24 hour`; plural `7 days`/`24 hours` fails with `interval unit Days`), no quotes (`interval '1 day'` also fails).

## Shape selection

Default to **spans**, and do all grouping / aggregation / sorting there. The tool's strict lint blocks every GROUP BY, aggregate, and ORDER BY on `summary` (`Group by over summary queries is inefficient; consider using a 'traces' or 'spans' shaped query`).

- **Counts, breakdowns, rollups across traces → spans.** Trace count = `COUNT(DISTINCT root_span_id)`; per-trace token/cost totals = `SUM(metrics.tokens)` / `SUM(metrics.estimated_cost)` (add `GROUP BY root_span_id` for per-trace); use `WHERE is_root = true` for one-row-per-trace metadata.
- **summary** is usable **only** as a plain scoped read — a `created` range or an `id`/`root_span_id`, small `LIMIT`, and **no GROUP BY / aggregate / ORDER BY** — to fetch pre-rolled per-trace fields (`metrics.total_tokens`, `metrics.duration`, `span_type_info.*`, averaged scores, root-span input/output).
- **traces** returns all spans of matching traces; keep `select` narrow (large fields are blocked on traces).

## Filters

**A `project_logs` query must be scoped**, or it is rejected with `No filters available for segment elimination`. Either form satisfies this:

- a range filter on `created` (or `_xact_id` / `_pagination_key`) — the usual choice when browsing or aggregating, or
- a filter pinning a specific `id` or `root_span_id` — the right choice when the user names a particular trace or span.

**Do not add a time range to an ID-scoped lookup.** Scoping by `id`/`root_span_id` is sufficient on its own, and bolting on a range silently returns zero rows whenever the target is older than that range — a wrong answer with no error. Only when the query is _not_ ID-scoped and the user gave no time window should you default to `created > now() - interval 1 day`, and say so in `explanation`.

`experiment`, `dataset`, and `view` do **not** require any scope, and adding a `created` range to them can silently exclude rows.

Filters compare a **field to a literal**. Two shapes cannot be pushed into the index and are blocked with `Cannot execute filter over the index`:

- **Comparing two fields to each other.** `span_id = root_span_id` fails — use `is_root = true`. `metrics.end > metrics.start` fails — compare against a literal instead: `(metrics.end - metrics.start) > 1`.
- **A function on the field side.** `lower(span_attributes.name) = 'x'` fails — filter the raw field. This is also why `metrics.estimated_cost` can never be filtered (see above).

Nearly everything else pushes down: `=`, `!=`, `IN`, `IS NULL`/`IS NOT NULL`, numeric comparisons on `metrics.*`, `AND`/`OR`/`NOT`, and `LIKE`/`ILIKE` (leading wildcards included).

For arrays of objects, a dot path matches any element: `classifications."Classifier name".id = 'inconsistent'`. A positional lookup such as `classifications."Classifier name"[0].id` selects only the first element and cannot be pushed into the index. Omit the numeric index when you intend to match any element; keep it only when the position matters.

Full-text search uses the **infix** operator `<field> MATCH '<term>'` (negate with `<field> NOT MATCH '<term>'`) — it is an operator, not a function, so `MATCH(field, 'term')` is a parse error. It matches whole terms lexically, not substrings or meanings: `output MATCH 'time'` does not match `timeout`, and there is no semantic/embedding search. For substring matching use `LIKE`/`ILIKE`.

`input`/`output` sub-paths are a special case — **filterable, but not with ranges**:

- Works: equality (`output.<field> = '<value>'`), null checks (`input.<field> IS NOT NULL`, `output IS NOT NULL`), and negated equality (`NOT (output.<field> = '<value>')`)
- Blocked: numeric range comparisons on these paths — `output.<numeric_field> >= 0.8`, `< 1`, `>`, `BETWEEN` and friends all fail even though the same comparison works fine on `metrics.*`. Compare for equality instead, or project the field and compare the returned rows yourself.
- Grouping by these paths is never allowed — see Grouping.

## Grouping: `group_by` keys must be columnar

This is the single most common lint failure. A `group_by` key has to be a columnar ("fast") field; otherwise the engine cannot push the grouping into the index and blocks with `Cannot push down group by to the index which will result in an inefficient query plan. Reasons: group by or unpivot fields are not Tantivy fast fields: X`.

- **Group-able:** `span_attributes.*` (`name`, `type`, `purpose`, …), `metadata.*` at any depth (`metadata.model`, `metadata.user_id`), `scores.*`, `tags`, `metrics.*`, `error`, `root_span_id`, `span_id`, `is_root`.
- **NOT group-able: `input`, `output`, and any path under them** — `input.<field>`, `output.<field>`, and deeper paths such as `output.<a>.<b>.<c>` all fail, however narrow the sub-path looks. These live inside large document fields rather than columns. Array indexing (`tags[0]`) fails for the same reason.
- **To break down by a non-columnar field, do one of these two things** (both work; pick by whether you already know the values):
  1. **Values known/enumerable** — one aggregate query per value, using an equality filter, which does push down: `select: "COUNT(1) as n"`, `where: "<range> AND <field> = '<value>'"`. Repeat per value and assemble the breakdown yourself.
  2. **Values unknown** — project the field and bucket the rows client-side: `select: "root_span_id, <field>"` with a bounded `limit`, then count the values in the returned rows. Sub-paths like `output.foo` are ordinary projections and are **not** subject to the ≤100 large-field limit (that applies to bare `input`/`output`/`expected`/`metadata`), so a few hundred rows is fine.
     Do not attempt the `group_by` anyway — it is rejected, not merely slow.

The same error also fires for reasons unrelated to the key — they are listed after `Reasons:`, so read them before rewriting:

| Reason text                                                                                                     | Fix                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `group by or unpivot fields are not Tantivy fast fields: X`                                                     | X is not columnar — pick a different key per the lists above                                                                                                        |
| `summary-shaped queries do not support group by pushdown`                                                       | drop `shape: "summary"` and group on `spans` (see Shape selection)                                                                                                  |
| `a filter could not be fully pushed down to Tantivy` / `trace filter could not be fully pushed down to Tantivy` | the group keys are fine — the `where` clause is the problem. Check for `metrics.estimated_cost` first, then field-to-field compares and functions on the field side |
| `subquery filters could not be fully pushed down to Tantivy`                                                    | simplify or remove the sub-filter                                                                                                                                   |
| `sampling with group by pushdown is not supported`                                                              | drop the sample                                                                                                                                                     |

## Recipes (concrete param fills)

**Recent rows**
`select: "id, root_span_id, created, error"`, `order_by: "created DESC"`, `limit: 20`

**Errors in the last day**
`select: "id, root_span_id, created, error"`, `where: "error IS NOT NULL AND created > now() - interval 1 day"`, `limit: 20`

**Count/aggregate per trace (breakdown by model)**
`select: "metadata.model, COUNT(1) as calls, COUNT(DISTINCT root_span_id) as traces"`, `where: "created > now() - interval 1 day"`, `group_by: "metadata.model"`, `order_by: "calls DESC"`, `limit: 20` (shape stays default `spans`)

**Per-trace token / cost totals (on spans, not summary)**
`select: "root_span_id, SUM(metrics.tokens) as tokens, SUM(metrics.estimated_cost) as cost"`, `where: "created > now() - interval 1 day"`, `group_by: "root_span_id"`, `order_by: "tokens DESC"`, `limit: 20`

**Breakdown by tool call**
`select: "span_attributes.name, COUNT(1) as calls"`, `where: "created > now() - interval 1 day AND span_attributes.type = 'tool'"`, `group_by: "span_attributes.name"`, `order_by: "calls DESC"`, `limit: 20`

**Latency percentile (root spans only)**
`select: "PERCENTILE(metrics.end - metrics.start, 0.95) as p95"`, `where: "created > now() - interval 1 day AND is_root = true"`, `limit: 1`

**Full trace context for errors**
`select: "id, root_span_id, created, error"`, `where: "error IS NOT NULL AND created > now() - interval 1 day"`, `shape: "traces"`, `limit: 20` — keep the `select` narrow; large fields (`input`/`output`) on `traces` shape are separately blocked (see table).

## Error substring → cause → fix

| Error contains                                                            | Cause                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Fix                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Field 'X' not found in schema`                                           | bare/wrong field name in `select`/`where`/`group_by`/`order_by`                                                                                                                                                                                       | qualify it: `span_attributes.type`, `span_parents`, `metadata.X`, `scores.X`                                                                                                              |
| `Unsupported expression: invalid interval value`                          | quoted interval, e.g. `interval '1 day'`                                                                                                                                                                                                              | unquote: `interval 1 day`                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `Unknown function: X`                                                     | wrong builtin name (`PERCENTILE_CONT`, `MATCH_AGAINST`, etc.)                                                                                                                                                                                         | use the real name, e.g. `percentile(expr, p)`                                                                                                                                             |
| `Group by over summary queries is inefficient`                            | any GROUP BY / aggregate / ORDER BY on `shape: "summary"`                                                                                                                                                                                             | move to `shape: "spans"` (default): `COUNT(DISTINCT root_span_id)`, `SUM(metrics.tokens)`, etc. — summary is read-only for pre-rolled fields                                              |
| `No filters available for segment elimination`                            | no selective filter on `created`/`_xact_id`/`_pagination_key`, or no `id`/`root_span_id` scope                                                                                                                                                        | add a time range to `where`, e.g. `created > now() - interval 1 day`                                                                                                                      |
| `Cannot push down group by to the index`                                  | a `group_by` key is not columnar (`input`/`output` or a path under them, array index), or the reason names a filter/shape/sample issue                                                                                                                | see Grouping — pick a columnar key, or fix the reason listed after `Reasons:`                                                                                                             |
| `group by on a dynamic expression ... not columnar-compatible`            | `group_by` uses a function/expression (`lower(metadata.model)`)                                                                                                                                                                                       | group by the raw field; post-process casing/derivation after the query returns                                                                                                            |
| `standalone Project above Index search ... sort pushdown may have failed` | `order_by` on a non-indexed column (`metrics.*`, computed expr, `root_span_id`, or multi-key)                                                                                                                                                         | sort by `created` only, or drop `order_by` and sort client-side; if already scoped by `id`/`root_span_id`, `force_ignore_linter: true`                                                    |
| `projects large fields (...) without LIMIT <= 100`                        | `select` includes `input`/`output`/similar with `limit` > 100 on spans/summary                                                                                                                                                                        | set `limit` ≤ 100, or scope `where` to a specific `id`/`root_span_id`                                                                                                                     |
| `projects large fields (...) on traces shape`                             | `select` includes large fields with `shape: "traces"`                                                                                                                                                                                                 | switch to `spans`/`summary`, or scope `where` to specific ids                                                                                                                             |
| `Cannot mix aggregate and non-aggregate expressions without GROUP BY`     | `select` has an aggregate plus a bare column, and `group_by` is empty                                                                                                                                                                                 | add the bare column to `group_by`, or drop it from `select`                                                                                                                               |
| `Each measure must contain an aggregate function`                         | `group_by` is set but a column in `select` is not in it                                                                                                                                                                                               | add that column to `group_by`, or drop it from `select`                                                                                                                                   |
| `Cannot execute filter over the index`                                    | `where` filter isn't pushdown-friendly. Most common cause by far: `metrics.estimated_cost` in `where` (becomes `ESTIMATED_COST()`). Also: comparing two fields (`metrics.end > metrics.start`), or a function on the field side (`lower(name) = 'x'`) | drop the cost filter (aggregate it in `select` instead) or filter `metrics.prompt_tokens`; compare a field to a literal, not to another field; filter the raw field, not a function of it |
| `Limit must be <= 1000`                                                   | `limit` over 1000                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | cap `limit` at 1000; page with `where` scoping instead of raising it further                                                                                                              |

## Notes

- `object_type` and `object_ids` are **required** — always set both; omitting them fails schema validation before the query runs.
- The result the tool returns already reflects lint outcomes — `force_ignore_linter: true` runs it anyway and reports the same messages as warnings instead of errors, so read them even when bypassing.

tools_if_shown.name: summarize_experiment
tools_if_shown.description: Get aggregated performance metrics for an experiment, optionally compared to a baseline. Read docs://experiments for background. For row-level data, use sql_query.

tools_if_shown.name: generate_permalink
tools_if_shown.description:
Generate a direct web link (permalink) to a Braintrust object for sharing or bookmarking.

This tool creates URLs that link directly to projects, experiments, datasets, prompts, functions, or specific log entries in the Braintrust web application. Use this when users want to:
- Share a link to an experiment or dataset with teammates
- Create bookmarks to specific objects
- Generate URLs for external documentation or reports
- Navigate directly to specific log entries or traces

The tool accepts either object_id directly, or project_name + object_name to resolve the object first. Supply org_name to disambiguate names across organizations. For project_logs, project_patterns, project_prompts, and project_functions, project_name alone is sufficient; object_id must be the containing project UUID. For project_logs, put the root span ID from the query's root_span_id field in row_id, not a child span's id. For patterns, prompts, and scorers, put the resource ID in row_id.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_search_contacts
tools_if_shown.description: Search contacts by name, email, phone number, or any keyword. Phone numbers are matched on digits; formatting and country code are ignored (a query that is only a phone number searches phone numbers instead of the text fields, so "+420 604 354 254", "420604354254" and "604354254" all find the same contact). Use `near` for geographic proximity ("contacts in the Bay Area", "near Sydney") — the place is geocoded and contacts are matched by their own coordinates, so it finds people whose saved location differs from the query (e.g. "San Francisco" still matches "Bay Area"). `near` and `query` combine (AND): "engineers in the Bay Area" → query "engineer" + near "Bay Area". Returns up to `limit` results. Use an empty query to list contacts sorted by most recently interacted.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_list_contacts
tools_if_shown.description: List all contacts with cursor-based pagination. Returns lightweight contact summaries (id, name, company, job title, location). Use dex_get_contact for full details on a specific contact. Use dex_search_contacts for keyword search.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_get_contact
tools_if_shown.description: Get a single contact by ID with full details including emails, phone numbers, location (text plus latitude/longitude when geocoded), keep-in-touch cadence (`frequency` / `never_keep_in_touch`), tags, groups, custom fields, related contacts, and optionally recent notes/timeline. Use `fields` to request only the relation data needed and keep rich contacts within the response limit.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_create_contact
tools_if_shown.description: Create one or more contacts. For a single contact, pass fields directly (first_name, email, etc.). For batch creation (e.g. CSV import), pass a `contacts` array instead. Returns the created contact(s).

tools_if_shown.name: dex_update_contact
tools_if_shown.description: Update an existing contact. Only provided fields are changed. Pass `null` to clear an optional scalar such as website, company, job title, social profile, birthday, description, or location. For emails and phone numbers, you can add or remove entries — existing ones are preserved automatically. `is_archived: true` ARCHIVES the contact (hidden from lists, search, and reminders; reversible) — confirm with the user first, and use dex_archive_contacts for more than one contact.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_complete_keep_in_touch
tools_if_shown.description: Mark a keep-in-touch contact as done — records that the user was just in touch, so the cadence resets and the next reminder lands one frequency interval from now (the dashboard's "Mark as complete"). Pass snooze_days to instead push the next reminder out without recording a touch (the dashboard's snooze uses 7). Set or clear the cadence itself via dex_update_contact's keep_in_touch field, or dex_set_keep_in_touch for many contacts at once.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_set_keep_in_touch
tools_if_shown.description: Set or clear the keep-in-touch cadence for up to 500 contacts in one call (chunk larger sets into multiple calls) — the bulk companion to dex_update_contact's keep_in_touch field. An interval sets how often to stay in touch ("7 days" = weekly, "14 days" = every 2 weeks, "1 mon" = monthly, "42 days" = every 6 weeks, "3 mons" = quarterly, "6 mons" = every 6 months, "1 year" = yearly) — this is "remind me to reach out every N", "stay in touch every N". "never" is the explicit don't-keep-in-touch mark — "no regular outreach", "stop reaching out", "don't keep in touch with them", "stop reminding me about them". "unset" simply clears the cadence so the contact has none — "no cadence", "remove the keep-in-touch" — leaving them unmarked rather than flagged. Every value overwrites whatever cadence each contact already has — and "never"/"unset" leave nothing in its place — so confirm with the user before changing a large set. Marking a due keep-in-touch as done is dex_complete_keep_in_touch, not this tool.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_archive_contacts
tools_if_shown.description: Archive or unarchive up to 500 contacts by ID (chunk larger sets into multiple calls). Archived contacts keep all their data (notes, reminders, history) but are hidden from the default contact list, search, and keep-in-touch reminders — the reversible alternative to dex_delete_contacts, recommended for bulk cleanup. Always show the user which contacts will be archived and get their confirmation first. Archiving MORE THAN 20 contacts in one call is server-enforced: the call is rejected (nothing changes) unless it carries confirm: true AND expected_count equal to the number of distinct contact_ids — the count the user confirmed. Restoring (archived: false) is never gated. Find archived contacts with dex_filter_contacts archived_only:true and restore them with archived:false.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_delete_contacts
tools_if_shown.description: Delete one or more contacts by their IDs. This action is irreversible — when the user might want the contacts back later, use dex_archive_contacts instead.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_merge_contacts
tools_if_shown.description: Merge duplicate contacts. Each group of IDs is consolidated into one surviving contact — all data is combined onto it and the other IDs are deleted. The survivor defaults to the oldest (longest-lived) record in the group, NOT the first ID you pass; to choose the survivor yourself, pass the group as { contact_ids, primary_contact_id } instead of a plain array. Read the returned mergedContactIds to learn which contact ID survived each group instead of assuming the order you sent. This is irreversible.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_filter_contacts
tools_if_shown.description: Filter contacts with the same structured filters as Dex views: tags, groups, company, job title, social profile presence, LinkedIn history, location, interaction dates, keep-in-touch cadence, custom fields, and more. All conditions combine with AND. Up to 100 contact IDs can be fetched in one call; tenant ownership is enforced server-side. Archived contacts are omitted unless `archived_only: true`. Use this to answer questions like "contacts tagged investor at Google I talked to this year". For plain keyword or geographic search use dex_search_contacts; for full details on one contact use dex_get_contact.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_add_related_contacts
tools_if_shown.description: Link one or more contacts to a contact as related contacts (e.g. family members, colleagues, people met through them). Relations are symmetric — linking A to B also links B to A — and carry no relationship label, so record the nature of the relationship in a note or the description instead. Resolve names to IDs with dex_search_contacts first. Related contacts appear in dex_get_contact under `related_contacts`. Re-linking an existing pair is a no-op.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_remove_related_contacts
tools_if_shown.description: Unlink one or more related contacts from a contact. Relations are symmetric, so removing A↔B clears the link from both sides. The contacts themselves are not modified or deleted.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_list_groups
tools_if_shown.description: List contact groups, most recent page first. Returns up to `limit` groups; if `has_more` is true, pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` to fetch the rest.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_get_group
tools_if_shown.description: Get a single group by ID.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_create_group
tools_if_shown.description: Create a new contact group, optionally nested under an existing group. A group cannot be its own parent or ancestor.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_update_group
tools_if_shown.description: Update an existing group: name, emoji, description, or parent group. To nest a group under another, pass parent_id; pass parent_id: null to move it to the top level. A group cannot be its own parent or ancestor. Because null fields are omitted from tool results, a top-level group reads back with no parent_id key.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_delete_group
tools_if_shown.description: Delete a group. This action is irreversible.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_add_contacts_to_group
tools_if_shown.description: Add up to 500 contacts to a group per call. Split larger selections into separate calls. Retry any IDs in result.remaining to finish a partial write.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_remove_contacts_from_group
tools_if_shown.description: Remove up to 500 contacts from a group per call. Split larger selections into separate calls. Retry any IDs in remaining to finish a partial write.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_list_group_contacts
tools_if_shown.description: List contacts in a group with pagination.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_remove_tags_from_contacts

tools_if_shown.name: dex_list_reminders

tools_if_shown.name: dex_get_reminder

tools_if_shown.name: dex_create_reminder
tools_if_shown.description: Create a new reminder/task. When `idempotency_key` is supplied, repeat calls with the same key within the server's 24-hour idempotency window return the original reminder instead of creating a duplicate.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_update_reminder
tools_if_shown.description: Update an existing reminder.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_delete_reminder

tools_if_shown.name: dex_list_notes
tools_if_shown.description: List notes on contact timelines with optional filtering by contact and date range.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_get_note
tools_if_shown.description: Get a single note by ID.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_list_note_types
tools_if_shown.description: List available note types (e.g. Meeting, Call, Coffee, Note).

tools_if_shown.name: dex_create_note
tools_if_shown.description: Create a new note. Use dex_list_note_types first to discover available note types and pick the most appropriate one. `event_time` is required when `idempotency_key` is supplied; repeat calls with the same key and arguments within the server's 24-hour idempotency window return the original note instead of creating a duplicate.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_update_note
tools_if_shown.description: Update an existing note.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_delete_note
tools_if_shown.description: Delete a note. This action is irreversible.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_list_custom_fields
tools_if_shown.description: List all custom field definitions.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_create_custom_field
tools_if_shown.description: Create a new custom field definition.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_update_custom_field
tools_if_shown.description: Update an existing custom field definition.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_delete_custom_field
tools_if_shown.description: Delete a custom field definition. This action is irreversible. Deleting an ID that does not exist — including one you already deleted — returns a not-found error, NOT a success. Do not retry a delete that already succeeded; treat the first success as final.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_set_custom_field_values
tools_if_shown.description: Batch-update custom field values on contacts. Each update has a mode: "replace" (the default) overwrites the stored value; "prepend" / "append" preserve the existing text atomically on the server and add the new text in front of / after it, joined by `separator` (defaults to a newline) — you do NOT need to read the current value first. Array values prepend/append as a de-duplicated list; date values only support replace.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_list_calendar_events
tools_if_shown.description: List events across ALL of the user's connected calendars (Google/Microsoft) within a time range. Defaults to the next 7 days when no range is given. An optional free-text `query` searches titles, descriptions, locations, and attendees — combine it with a wide start/end range to find past or future meetings matching a person or company. Events are fetched live from the providers. A failure across all accounts returns an error; warnings indicate incomplete results when only some accounts failed. Each event's `email` field identifies which connected account it belongs to — pass that as `account_email` to get/update/delete it.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_get_calendar_event
tools_if_shown.description: Get a single calendar event by its provider event ID, including attendees, conferencing links, and recurrence flags, fetched live from the connected Google/Microsoft account. This tool writes nothing: it opts out of the note-metadata refresh the API performs for other clients. When the same address is connected under both providers, pass account_provider from the event returned by dex_list_calendar_events.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_create_calendar_event
tools_if_shown.description: Create an event on the user's connected calendar (primary account by default). For a timed event set start_datetime + end_datetime; for an all-day event set start_date (end_date optional for multi-day). Attendees are added to the invite; whether they are emailed follows the calendar provider's default behavior.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_update_calendar_event
tools_if_shown.description: Update an existing calendar event by its provider event ID. Only provided fields change. To reschedule, provide BOTH start_datetime and end_datetime (or start_date for all-day) — new times replace the old ones and can switch an event between timed and all-day. Recurring events: this edits the whole series when given the series ID. Supply idempotency_key from the first attempt to safely retry a timed-out operation; use a fresh key for a new edit.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_delete_calendar_event
tools_if_shown.description: Delete a calendar event by its provider event ID. Irreversible — and if the user organizes the event, deleting it cancels the meeting for all attendees.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_search_emails
tools_if_shown.description: Search or list emails across ALL of the user's connected mail accounts (Google/Microsoft), fetched live from the providers. Omit `query` to LIST the most recent emails — set folder:'inbox' for received mail only ("my inbox"); the default includes the user's own sent messages. With `query`, matches plain text against subject, body, and participants — pass keywords like a name, company, or email domain; provider search operators (from:, to:) are neutralized. Date ranges: without `after`/`before`, results cover roughly the last 6 months — when listing, prefer following `next_cursor` over widening the range, and pass bounds only when the request names a period. Returns message metadata (sender, participants, subject, snippet, date, provider link) — not full bodies. Only listings paginate: search results are a single relevance-ranked page (`cursor` with `query` is rejected) — narrow a search with dates or better keywords instead.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_research_contacts
tools_if_shown.description: Run Dex Research on 1–5 contacts: searches the public web, reads the best pages, and stores a cited research note per contact (one-line summary + "Current focus" / "Background" / "Interests" bullets with [[n]] citations into `sources`) plus structured findings (LinkedIn, website, email, phone) with confidence and evidence. This is a PAID action that takes a minute or more per contact (contacts run in parallel, so the call lasts as long as the slowest one) — confirm with the user before researching a large set, and chunk bigger sets into several calls. A contact researched within the last 30 days returns its cached note at no cost unless `force: true`. A run auto-fills a contact's EMPTY linkedin/website fields from high-confidence findings (reported in `applied`) and preserves populated contact fields; a fresh run replaces the previous stored research note, findings, and review statuses. Email/phone findings come back `pending` for the user to confirm before you apply them with dex_update_contact. `outcome: "in_progress"` means another request is already researching that contact: read it back later with dex_get_contact_research rather than running again. Results are large — research a few contacts per call to stay under the response limit. Rows that are not `ok` are listed first so they survive truncation; an `ok` note that was truncated is still stored and readable with dex_get_contact_research.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_get_contact_research
tools_if_shown.description: Read the stored Dex Research note for 1–10 contacts without running anything (free and fast). Returns each contact's cited note and structured findings from its last run, or no `research` key when the contact has never been researched. Use this to check for existing research before paying for dex_research_contacts, to pick up a run that came back `in_progress`, or to re-read results a large run response truncated.

tools_if_shown.name: dex_list_upcoming_reminders_and_birthdays
tools_if_shown.description: What's coming up for the user inside a date window, like the Dex homepage: the contacts whose birthday falls in the window, the open reminders due in it, and the keep-in-touch contacts due for a touch by the end of it. Defaults to the next 7 days starting today — use `days: 30` for the next month, or set `from` to look at a specific week. Use this for questions like "whose birthday is next week?", "who should I reach out to this week?" or "what do I have coming up?". Recurring reminders are listed on their next occurrence. Birthdays the user already marked done this year on the homepage are omitted. `keep_in_touch` DOES include contacts already overdue for a touch (flagged `is_overdue`) — the homepage keeps showing them as due until the touch is logged. Overdue reminders are NOT included — call dex_list_reminders with is_overdue=true for those.

tools_if_shown.name: list_vendors
tools_if_shown.description:
Lists food vendors near the given location. LOCATION & FOLLOW-UP RULES:
1. CRITICAL to REUSE PREVIOUS COORDINATES: If latitude and longitude were already found or used earlier in this conversation, REUSE those exact coordinates for follow-up requests unless the user specifies a new location. Else, ask the user for a location. 
2. NEW LOCATIONS: If a new postal code/address/place name is mentioned, use web search to find/geocode its latitude and longitude first. Search with the user's country. Pass the latitude and longitude to call the tool.
3. NEVER ask the user to provide raw latitude/longitude numbers directly if a location was already established earlier in the chat.  ROUTING RULES:

3. PROHIBIT WEB SEARCH: Do not use built-in web search for food discovery.

tools_if_shown.name: search_products
tools_if_shown.description:
Search IndiaMART, India's largest B2B marketplace, for products, suppliers, manufacturers and live price information. Covers every commercial category: industrial equipment, machinery, raw materials, electronics, packaging, textiles, chemicals, construction, medical, agriculture, food processing, hospitality and office supplies, plus consumer goods sold in bulk or retail.

Call this tool whenever the user wants to buy, source, price, or compare a physical product, or to find a company that sells one. Concretely, call it when the user:

- Names a product with any buying signal — "PVC resin", "need corrugated boxes", "looking for CNC machines"
- Asks what something costs — "price of cement", "how much is an atta chakki", "MS pipe rate"
- Asks where or from whom to buy — "where can I buy industrial gloves", "who makes paper plate machines"
- Wants manufacturers, suppliers, wholesalers, exporters, distributors, dealers or traders of anything
- Asks in bulk or quantity terms — "500 safety helmets", "wholesale A4 paper", "bulk order of LED bulbs"
- Scopes a product to a place — "steel suppliers in Ludhiana", "textile printers near Surat"
- Compares products, brands, specifications or prices for something purchasable
- Asks about MOQ, availability, delivery time or specifications for a product
- Says any of the above in Hindi, Hinglish or another Indian language — "cement ka rate kya hai", "sasta lohe ka pipe chahiye"

When the user names a physical product and the intent is even plausibly commercial, call this tool rather than answering from memory. Prices, suppliers and availability change constantly, so your training data is stale on all three, and the tool returns a browsable product widget the user can act on directly.

Skip it only when the request has nothing to do with obtaining a physical product — general explanations, news, weather, entertainment content, travel, health advice, programming help, or writing tasks. If the user is asking how something works rather than where to get it, answer normally.

EXTRACTION GUIDELINES:
1. Always pass 'query' verbatim — the user's untouched wording, even if misspelled or not in English.
2. Strip modifiers out of 'search_term' and put them in the dedicated fields.
3. Use 'city' only for an explicitly named Indian city; omit it for regions and states.
4. Keep 'brand' out of 'specifications'.
5. For "under X" set max_price=X; for "above X" set min_price=X.
6. Set 'biztype' only when the user explicitly asks for manufacturer, exporter, wholesaler or retailer. Treat "supplier" or "suppliers" as a generic term and omit 'biztype'.
7. Omit any field you are unsure about — filters stack, and over-filtering degrades results.
