tools_if_shown.name: search_hotels
tools_if_shown.description:
Search for hotels in a specific location.
Use this when the user wants to find hotels, accommodation,
or places to stay. Returns top 8 hotels matching the criteria
with photos, ratings, and prices.

CRITICAL - PROMPT FIELD:
- Copy the user's EXACT message into "prompt" - character-for-character, no changes.
- If user wrote "أبحث عن فندق في دبي", pass that EXACT Arabic text.
- NEVER translate the prompt field.

OTHER FIELDS: Must be in English (location, dates, etc).

IMPORTANT - LOCATION FORMAT: Always provide the full location name with city and country:
- For cities: "City, Country" (e.g., "Dubai, United Arab Emirates", "Riyadh, Saudi Arabia")
- For areas/neighborhoods: "Area, City, Country" (e.g., "Dubai Marina, Dubai, United Arab Emirates", "JBR, Dubai, United Arab Emirates", "Al Olaya, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia")
Always use the official/correct area name as it appears on maps.

PRICE FIELDS IN THE RESPONSE - read this carefully so you don't misquote prices:
Each hotel has price.perNight (average per-night rate), price.total (sum across all nights),
and price.nights (number of nights). When mentioning a price to the user, use the field
that matches what they asked for:
- "X per night" / "Y a night" / "ليلة" → use price.perNight
- "total trip cost" / "for the whole stay" / "السعر الإجمالي" → use price.total
- If unclear, mention both: "SAR 1,500/night (SAR 7,500 total for 5 nights)".
NEVER invent a per-night value by dividing price.total by anything. NEVER claim price.total
is a per-night rate. The two numbers are already computed for you.

DATE PRE-VALIDATION (HARD — DO NOT CALL THE TOOL IF ANY OF THESE FAIL):
Before calling search_hotels, validate the dates against today. If any check fails, do NOT
call the tool. Reply directly to the user, explain which date is invalid, and ask them to
provide corrected dates.
- checkIn must be today or later. If checkIn is in the past, do NOT call the tool.
- checkOut must be strictly after checkIn. If checkOut is the same day or earlier than
  checkIn, do NOT call the tool.
- Stay length (checkOut - checkIn) must not exceed 28 nights. If longer, do NOT call.
Calling the tool with invalid dates and letting the schema reject is NOT acceptable —
catch it before the call.

OCCUPANCY LIMITS (HARD — DO NOT CALL THE TOOL): The hotel search supports at most 4 rooms
per query, and at most 8 total guests (adults + children) across all rooms combined. If the
user asks for more (e.g. "5 rooms", "10 people", "9 guests across 3 rooms"), DO NOT call
the tool — tell them the limit and ask them to reduce the party size or split the request.

STAY LENGTH LIMIT (HARD): Maximum 28 nights per search (checkOut - checkIn ≤ 28 days).
If the user requests a longer stay (e.g. "2 months", "30 days"), DO NOT call the tool —
tell them the 28-night limit and ask them to split the stay into separate searches.

FILTER RULES — READ CAREFULLY, THIS IS THE #1 SOURCE OF BUGS:
The "filters" object must be OMITTED entirely unless the user's words explicitly match a
specific filter. "Explicitly" means the user used words that directly name the filter concept.
Common mistakes to AVOID:
- "cheap" / "affordable" / "budget" → set sortBy: "priceAsc". Do NOT invent a priceRange.max
  number. Only set priceRange when the user states a specific number (e.g. "under $100",
  "less than 500 SAR", "max budget 200").
- "comfy" / "nice" / "good" / "cozy" / "clean" → these are vibes, NOT filters. Do NOT add
  starRating, freeCancellation, or priceRange. Leave filters empty.
- "organize a trip" / "plan a vacation" / "travel to X" → general travel intent. Do NOT add
  starRating (e.g. 3-5 stars) or any other filter. Leave filters empty.
- "two bedroom" / "apartment" / "suite" → ONLY set propertyType if it matches the enum.
  Do NOT add freeCancellation or any other unrelated filter.
- freeCancellation → ONLY when user literally says "free cancellation", "refundable",
  or "cancel for free". Words like "flexible", "affordable", "safe" do NOT mean free cancellation.
- starRating → ONLY when user says "5-star", "at least 4 stars", "3-star or above", etc.
  General quality words ("nice", "good", "decent") are NOT star ratings.
If in doubt, OMIT the filter. A search with no filters returns more results, which is always
better than a search that silently excludes matches the user would have wanted.

tools_if_shown.name: search_flights
tools_if_shown.description:
Search for flights between two airports.
Use this when the user wants to find flights, airfare,
or air travel options. Returns available flight itineraries
with prices, schedules, and airline information.

CRITICAL - PROMPT FIELD:
- Copy the user's EXACT message into "prompt" - character-for-character, no changes.
- If user wrote "أبحث عن رحلة إلى دبي", pass that EXACT Arabic text.
- NEVER translate the prompt field.

IMPORTANT - ENGLISH ONLY: All OTHER input argument string values MUST be in English.
If the user writes in Arabic, translate the intent to English before calling this tool.
Do NOT include Arabic script in any argument values except "prompt".

IMPORTANT - AIRPORT CODES: Always use 3-letter IATA airport codes:
- Riyadh: RUH
- Jeddah: JED
- Dubai: DXB
- Abu Dhabi: AUH
- Doha: DOH
- Kuwait: KWI
- Bahrain: BAH
- Muscat: MCT
- Cairo: CAI
- London Heathrow: LHR

DATE PRE-VALIDATION (HARD — DO NOT CALL THE TOOL IF ANY OF THESE FAIL):
Before calling search_flights, validate the dates against today. If any check fails, do NOT
call the tool. Reply directly to the user, explain which date is invalid, and ask them to
provide corrected dates.
- departureDate must be today or later. If departureDate is in the past, do NOT call.
- If returnDate is provided, it must be strictly after departureDate. If returnDate is
  the same day or earlier than departureDate, do NOT call the tool.
Calling the tool with invalid dates and letting the schema reject is NOT acceptable —
catch it before the call.

ROUND-TRIP DURATION LIMIT (HARD): Round-trip searches are capped at 110 days
(returnDate - departureDate ≤ 110). If the user asks for a longer trip (e.g. "6 months",
"leave in May, return in October"), DO NOT call the tool — tell them the 110-day limit
and ask them to shorten the trip or split into separate one-way searches.

FILTER RULES — READ CAREFULLY:
The "filters" object must be OMITTED entirely unless the user's words explicitly name a
specific filter concept. Common mistakes to AVOID:
- "cheap" / "affordable" / "budget" → use sortBy: "cheapest". Do NOT add any filter.
- "plan a trip" / "organize travel" / "I want to go to X" → general intent. Do NOT add
  directOnly, departureTime, or any filter. Leave filters empty.
- "business trip" → does NOT mean cabin: "Business". Only set cabin when user explicitly
  says "business class" or "first class".
- "comfortable" / "good" / "nice" → vibes, NOT filters. Leave filters empty.
If in doubt, OMIT the filter. More results is always better than silently excluding
flights the user would have wanted.

tools_if_shown.name: list_workspaces
tools_if_shown.description:
List the Avo workspaces you have access to. Returns name + workspaceId for each. This is usually the first call in a session — every other tool (`search`, `get`, `save_items`, `workflow`) takes a `workspaceId`.

Use cases:
- Starting a fresh session.
- Switching context between client workspaces.
- Confirming auth scope before a write.

tools_if_shown.name: describe_tool
tools_if_shown.description:
The on-demand schema/contract index for the Avo MCP — call it to get the exact shape of the call you are about to make.

- describe_tool() — capability map: every tool, its types/actions, what to call next.
- describe_tool(tool:"save_items", type:"<type>", op:"<op>") — the field contract for that item type + op (name, jsonType, required, doc). Call before your first write of a type.
- describe_tool(tool:"workflow", action:"import") — the import payload schema.
- For save_items, format:"concise" returns the fields table only.

Read-only and local: no workspace data, no branch, no side effects.

tools_if_shown.name: search
tools_if_shown.description:
Find tracking-plan items in two modes, auto-selected by params.

(1) Semantic search — pass query for similarity. Cap 20, default 10; index may lag recent changes.

(2) Structured listing — pass filters (e.g. tags, includeVariants) for exact matches across events, properties, metrics, event variants; or itemType with no query to enumerate source/destination/group_type/gateway/journey. event/property accept a checkpoint lens (see field). Branch + keyset pagination; filter listings cap 500, default 10; enumerations unpaged, journey 25/100.

Query with filters is rejected; use get for id lookups.

tools_if_shown.name: get
tools_if_shown.description:
Look up a SINGLE item by id or exact name (defaults to main); for discovery use search. Types: see the type field.

- event/property/event_variant add owner + stakeholders; event/property also accept a checkpoint lens.
- Enumerate metadata (source, destination, group_type, gateway) via search.
- branch takes branchId/branchName + include + sourceId.

tools_if_shown.name: save_items
tools_if_shown.description:
Create, update, archive, or unarchive tracking-plan items in one branch-scoped batch (max 50). Each item is an envelope {op, type, id?, name?, tempId?, fields?}; op defaults to "create". type: event, property, event_variant, property_bundle, metric, destination, source, group_type, category, gateway (camelCase aliases ok).

Call describe_tool(tool:"save_items", type:"<type>", op:"<op>") for a type's exact fields — served on demand, not advertised here.

Contract:
- Writes need an open draft branch (open one via workflow create_branch; rejected on main). The MCP never merges to main.
- Identify: create takes name (event_variant: nameSuffix + a caller-supplied variantId + baseEventId); update/archive/unarchive take the identity id via id or fields (event→eventId, event_variant→baseEventId+variantId). Resolve names to ids with get/search first; never invent ids.
- $tmp: set tempId on a create, then reference it as "$tmp:<tempId>" in another same-batch item's id/ref fields; the server resolves them before saving.
- Placement: scalar renames go in fields.set; collection deltas (add*/remove*/clear*) at fields top level.
- Owner/stakeholder changes are branch-independent — they take effect immediately workspace-wide, not undone by discarding the branch.

tools_if_shown.name: workflow
tools_if_shown.description:
Open branches and edit branch metadata. For tracking-plan item edits use save_items. Call describe_tool(tool:"workflow", action:"import") for the import payload schema.

Actions:
- create_branch { branchName, description? }
- update_branch_description { branchId or branchName, description }
- pull_main { branchId } — pull latest main (Codegen; main wins on overlap).
- set_source_language { sourceId, language, branchId or branchName } — find sourceId via search(itemType:"source").
- import { branchId, format:"csv"|"json_schema", payload, importMethod? } — bulk-import (Admin).

tools_if_shown.name: give_feedback
tools_if_shown.description: Share feedback about the Avo MCP tools — call proactively, especially when the MCP could NOT do what you set out to do (a gap, a dead-end, a workaround). Say what you tried, expected, and got; name the tool(s); no secrets or private customer data.

tools_if_shown.name: list_branches
tools_if_shown.description: List branches in a workspace with optional filtering, paginated newest-first (pageSize 1–50, default 25; use nextPageToken for more). Filter by creator/reviewer/collaborator (email or userId), date range (createdAfter/createdBefore), impactedSourceId, branchName substring, and branchStatuses. Returns a compact summary per branch — use get(type:"branch", branchId:"...") for full reviewer/collaborator arrays. For the current user's branches, pass their email as creatorEmail/reviewerEmail (no auto-inject).

tools_if_shown.name: ask_firm_memory
tools_if_shown.description:
Retrieve governed evidence or a canonical deterministic answer for an Inspired Capital question. Set `question` to the complete user message. Preserve exact numbers, cohorts, source links, dates, and `[Unclear]` in deterministic results. A `firm-memory-mode: financial-authority` result is final Markdown from the controlling holdings ledger. Return it verbatim without broadening, narrowing, reclassifying, recomputing, adding, or omitting any row or subtotal. When the result is marked `firm-memory-mode: qualitative-evidence`, use it as source material and answer the original question in your own concise prose; do not reproduce irrelevant packet sections. An interim `job:<uuid>` receipt must be resolved with fetch before answering.

Query Inspired Capital's institutional memory (portfolio companies, pipeline entities, prior partner discussions, memos, meeting notes, email threads).

INVOKE when the user asks about a known Inspired portfolio company, a pipeline entity Luke is tracking, prior partner discussions, portfolio-founder work history, attributed reading highlights, or a firm-internal topic. Examples: 'what did we say about Solace?', 'have we seen anything like Summer Health?', 'similar pass reasons around team scaling', 'what's our relationship with Aleph?', 'where is X today?', 'what have we highlighted about AI agents?', 'search our Readwise highlights for vertical software', 'which portco founders worked at Stripe?', 'do any of our portco founders have Meta Ads experience?', 'where is ShopMy's cap table?', 'how many companies are in our portfolio?', 'PortCo Smash rankings', 'which active Fund II companies are growing revenue fastest?', or a pasted forwarded email thread. Firm-memory owns fund membership and active/current portfolio categorization. Do not rebuild those cohorts in the host from a separate connector. For 'summarize the deck / data room / spreadsheet they just sent', the dedicated read_email_attachments tool is preferred (reads the files live), but this router also handles it the same way: it returns a `job:<uuid>`; call `fetch(id="job:<uuid>")` after the stated retry interval, or after 30 seconds by default, for up to five minutes. If metadata proves the attachment exists but it cannot be read, say so and ask the partner to upload it. Never infer its contents.

ASYNC RESULT CONTRACT: investment-to-now company evolution and larger finite named-company analyses may also return a `job:<uuid>` interim receipt so the request stays inside Cowork's host budget. Do not present that receipt as the answer and do not end the turn. Call `fetch(id="job:<uuid>")` after the stated interval, or after 30 seconds by default, and keep polling while the job is queued, pending, or running. Return only the final completed Markdown from fetch, preserving every heading, table, source link, and line break.

DO NOT INVOKE for general-knowledge questions about external companies Inspired hasn't engaged with (e.g., 'tell me about Brex/Stripe/Plaid' when those aren't portcos or pipeline). Answer those from your general knowledge and end with: 'Want me to check firm-memory for any Inspired context on X?'.

FAST-BAIL CONTRACT: the tool runs a sub-100ms probe before the heavy retrieval stack. If the target entity has no substantive context after alias-expanded entity matching, the tool returns `## Answer` with `[Unclear]`. Preserve that firm-specific gap. You may then add a separately labeled general-knowledge section for the unsupported clause, without presenting it as Inspired memory or altering any firm-memory facts.

For qualitative evidence packets, answer the partner's actual question and cite the relied-on sources. If two unrelated current situations are comparably plausible, ask one short follow-up question. For deterministic calculations and complete enumerations, preserve the returned facts and citations exactly. For multi-company pipeline meeting/email prep where the user names the companies, use pipeline_email_meeting_prep instead.

tools_if_shown.name: portfolio_founder_experience
tools_if_shown.description: Deterministic, source-backed search over the trailing-ten-year employment history of founders linked to companies in Inspired's latest portfolio snapshot. Use for a named founder's work history, an exact past employer, or a specific experience area. Examples: 'Where has Teddy Jungreis worked in the last 10 years?', 'Which portco founders worked at Stripe?', and 'Do any of our portco founders have Meta Ads experience?'. Compound experience searches require the employer and the function. For example, Meta Ads includes Meta/Facebook ads-facing roles and excludes generic Meta/Facebook engineering. Returns source links, role dates, snapshot freshness, and explicit current-roster coverage. Output the returned markdown verbatim.

tools_if_shown.name: read_email_attachments
tools_if_shown.description:
Read the LIVE contents of files attached to an email or data room (deck, spreadsheet, financial model, memo). Downloads and extracts the text on demand — NOT the cached / ingested copy, so the financials are current.

INVOKE when the partner asks to 'summarize / read / open the deck / spreadsheet / data room / files they just sent / emailed / forwarded' or 'what are the key metrics in the attachment'. The reader is identity-scoped. It can read Luke's reporting mail, messages sent to pipeline@ / portfolio@ for any authenticated partner, or the caller's own mailbox when an exact caller-specific Gmail token is configured. Also try the partner's native Gmail / Drive connector for mail sent only to them.

Pass a Gmail search string: a company name ('Kalepa data room'), `from:sender`, `subject:deck`, etc. Returns a `job:<uuid>` handle immediately, then you MUST call `fetch(id="job:<uuid>")` to get the extracted text (file names, deck/spreadsheet/memo text, thread link). If `fetch` says still extracting, wait for the stated retry interval, or 30 seconds when none is stated, and poll for up to five minutes. Output returned markdown verbatim. If attachment metadata proves a file exists but the contents cannot be read, explicitly say the file was detected but not read and ask the partner to upload it. Never infer attachment contents.

tools_if_shown.name: finalize_source_reconciliation
tools_if_shown.description: Fail-closed finalizer for a comparison between a named pitch and an internal technical discussion, with an optional white paper only when the question asks for it. Call only after independently reading every requested document and retrieving the identity-bound internal discussion. Attempt those retrievals FIRST, before asking the user anything: run the document reads and the internal-discussion query immediately. Never ask where a document lives, whether it exists, or which company is meant until every retrieval attempt has reached a terminal state; a clarification request without an attempted retrieval is an error. When sources remain missing after the attempts, call this tool anyway and return its bounded partial statuses verbatim. Pass each complete connector result verbatim. The tool derives the four exact statuses read, partial_read, detected_not_read, and not_found. It withholds the claim matrix unless every requested source is read and every comparison row contains an exact source-local quote plus a URL present in that source result. Output the returned Markdown verbatim.

tools_if_shown.name: list_post_pitch_capture_candidates
tools_if_shown.description: Read the continuously synced Granola corpus for the authenticated caller's accessible team-shared, not-yet-captured completed meetings in an inclusive date window. It returns only sources with server-verified membership in the exact Pitches folder in the Inspired Capital team space. Missing or mismatched folder metadata fails closed. Caller attendance is not required. Private, restricted, stale, and unsettled sources are excluded. It never writes Affinity. Within that folder, capture completed meetings about a non-portfolio founder's company when that founder attended. A formal pitch label or fundraising discussion is not required. Returned records distinguish verified source access from actual meeting attendees and include any structured attendee roles available from Granola.

tools_if_shown.name: capture_meeting_to_affinity
tools_if_shown.description: Capture a completed meeting with a non-portfolio founder only after list_post_pitch_capture_candidates verifies the canonical Granola source in the exact Inspired Capital team Pitches folder. The server rechecks explicit firm-shared source access, folder membership, fresh source evidence, and authenticated caller identity before any Affinity access. The caller need not have attended. Never add the executing caller to meeting attendees or owner selection merely because it runs the service. A formal pitch or fundraising label is not required. The write is idempotent by source and calendar event. Set first_pitch_verified only for a positive introductory founder conversation. Every eligible meeting ensures one Deals entry, including follow-ups. The core checks exact company identity and fresh native Deals membership before creation. Reuse existing entries and preserve every existing owner, including blanks. Only two existing Status transitions are permitted: To Reach Out to First Meeting, and First Meeting to 2+ M'tgs & Diligence after a verified prior distinct pitch. All other statuses and deal fields stay unchanged. For any newly created entry the core derives owners from known Granola named participants, without additional transcript proof for ownership. Partners take priority over Luke/Lex, who may own only when solo. Multiple partners use the participating meeting scheduler, verified from canonical calendar creator/organizer evidence. Unknown or conflicting scheduler evidence leaves ownership unresolved. Mailing-list expansion does not establish participation. owner_email is only a legacy hint and may be omitted. Read the complete owner set from the returned owner_emails and owner_ids. Pass founder_company_meeting_verified, founder_present_verified, meeting_completed_verified, and verified company-domain evidence. Set prior_pitch_verified only when a separate prior completed pitch is established. Never infer first-pitch or prior-pitch evidence from a missing record. Use dry_run=true for setup and smoke tests. repair_missing_deal_entry=true is only for an explicit user request to repair a missing Deals entry on this exact successful note capture, including a follow-up. It preserves the note, repeats every creation check, and never changes existing owners. Repair mode may also reconcile a verified missing-entry coverage incident. Never blindly retry an uncertain repair. New entries use First Meeting unless a distinct prior founder-company meeting is verified, then 2+ M'tgs & Diligence. repair_owner_assignment=true is Luke-only explicit correction of an exact workflow-created owner assignment. It requires unchanged native owners matching the original audit, the unchanged full note, and current canonical source/company/portfolio proof. It changes only Owners and never replays the note.

tools_if_shown.name: submit_firm_memory_smoke_report
tools_if_shown.description: Store one complete privacy-safe firm-memory smoke artifact in the dedicated QA archive. Invoke exactly once after the smoke report and parity ledger are frozen. The authenticated caller is derived from the MCP session. The tool never accepts a caller override, never writes sources or mentions, and never makes the report answer evidence. Pass the minimal rule-53 REFERENCE_PACKET or COMPARISON_RESULT archive projection, not the complete in-session report. Only a Luke REFERENCE may include verbatim raw output for SHARED_EXACT records. Every COMPARISON record, including SHARED_EXACT, must use the strict redacted functional envelope and the fixed shared_exact_fields hash map. The server resolves the archived Luke reference and enforces its probe inventory, parity classes, and hashes before accepting a passing grade. Never include the device-local private appendix or comparison raw output. Reusing the same run ID with the same bytes is idempotent. Reusing it with different bytes is rejected. Use dry_run=true only during partner setup validation.

tools_if_shown.name: firm_memory_smoke_reports
tools_if_shown.description: Luke-only read access to the dedicated firm-memory smoke QA archive. Omit report_id to list recent runs, optionally filtered by partner_email. Pass report_id to return the complete untruncated privacy-safe artifact. Reports are QA-only and are never firm-memory answer evidence. Every non-Luke caller is denied.

tools_if_shown.name: twitter_recent_posts
tools_if_shown.description: Fetch a public X/Twitter handle's recent posts (default: last 14 days, up to 30 posts). Use when a partner wants to see what a founder, competitor, or operator has been posting before a meeting / pitch / portco check-in. Pass the handle WITHOUT the leading @ (e.g. `elonmusk` not `@elonmusk`). Returns markdown with post text + engagement metrics + date + link, in reverse-chrono order. Backed by Apify; firm pays per-call cost.

tools_if_shown.name: linkedin_recent_posts
tools_if_shown.description: Fetch a public LinkedIn profile's recent posts (default: last 30 days, up to 20 posts). Use when a partner wants to see what a founder, competitor, or operator has been posting on LinkedIn before a meeting / pitch / portco check-in. Pass the full profile URL (e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/in/lukebender`). Returns markdown with post text + engagement metrics + date + link, in reverse-chrono order. Backed by Apify; firm pays per-call cost.

tools_if_shown.name: search
tools_if_shown.description: Search Inspired Capital's approved firm-memory index for cited sources and mentions. For direct questions, returns a top answer:<id> result that should be fetched first for a routed, cited answer. Read-only.

tools_if_shown.name: fetch
tools_if_shown.description: Read the source body or mention context for a specific result ID returned by search. If the ID starts answer:, returns a curated workflow-specific firm-memory answer. For `job:<uuid>`, queued, pending, or running text is interim: wait for its stated interval and call fetch again. When the job is done, output its completed Markdown verbatim with every heading, table, source link, and line break, then end the turn. Read-only; does not modify, send, or publish data.

tools_if_shown.name: pipeline_email_meeting_prep
tools_if_shown.description: Use when the user names several companies for an upcoming pipeline meeting, pipeline email, or pipeline discussion and wants past analogous firm judgments, hesitations, pass reasons, or forgotten precedents. Pass every named company in `company_names`. Returns the current debate anchor for each company plus past analogous Inspired discussions of *other* companies, with exact quotes and inline source/date links. Output the markdown verbatim. Do not reconstruct this manually with ask_firm_memory or direct Drive/Gmail/Granola reads. For rosters >5 companies the tool auto-switches to async: it returns a `job:<uuid>` markdown; the caller polls via `fetch(id="job:<uuid>")` until the heavy enrichment fanout finishes (typically 1–4 minutes).

tools_if_shown.name: pitch_meeting_prep
tools_if_shown.description: Use when a partner has a pitch / founder meeting scheduled and wants a comprehensive brief on the company. Single-company version of pipeline_email_meeting_prep — same enrichment fanout (sector taxonomy + memo-fragment retrieval + outcomes-on-analogs + factor-based pattern matches) scoped to one named company. Output the returned markdown verbatim; preserve every quote and blockquote attribution. Cold calls auto-switch to async: the tool returns a `job:<uuid>` markdown; the caller polls via `fetch(id="job:<uuid>")` until the enrichment fanout finishes (typically 1–2 minutes). Recently-computed briefs return synchronously.

tools_if_shown.name: pitch_meeting_retrospective
tools_if_shown.description: Use when a partner asks 'of all my pitch meetings in the last [N] days, which deserve a second look?'. Requires the requesting partner's email / own Granola context; never scans all-firm Granola when identity is missing. Scans that partner's recent Granola pitch / founder meetings and returns researchable second-look hypotheses plus contributing signals. Cold calls auto-switch to async: the tool returns a `job:<uuid>` markdown; the caller polls via `fetch(id="job:<uuid>")` until the outcomes refresh finishes (typically 1–2 minutes). Recently-computed retrospectives return synchronously.

tools_if_shown.name: follow_on_pattern_match
tools_if_shown.description: Use when partners are weighing a follow-on investment decision on an existing portco. Three modes: `pro_rata` (standard pro-rata election), `offensive` (proactive between-round note when the portco is doing well), `defensive` (distress / bridge / walk-away). Surfaces past Inspired precedents matching the decision shape, with verbatim partner rationale + outcome.

tools_if_shown.name: fund_position
tools_if_shown.description: Deterministic, cited, source-of-truth lookup for Inspired fund financials — for ONE fund OR ALL funds at once. Use for: a single fund ('Fund 3 position', 'How is Fund III constructed?'), AND for firmwide / multi-fund breakdowns ('Funds 1-3 financial breakdown', 'break down all our funds', 'committed/deployed/NAV across the funds', 'compare the funds', 'firmwide MOIC'). Covers committed size and vintage from Standard Metrics fund rows; deployed, capital plan, called capital, and fees from tracker accounting; NAV/current value and per-company cost/marks from Standard Metrics company rows; ownership/history from the tracker position packet where loaded; value-over-cost, position count, vintage, dry-powder caveats, management fees, per-company check size, 'what did we invest in X', and 'what is X worth now'. AUM is committed capital plus separately labeled SPVs. Deployed is tracker-authoritative and the Standard Metrics company-cost figure is its reconciliation cross-check. Do not recompute or blend these fields in the host. Reads the fund-position cache; never falls back to PortCo Smash rankings or general recall. A `firm-memory-mode: financial-authority` result is final: return its Markdown verbatim and do not reclassify or omit holdings.

tools_if_shown.name: missing_plan_analysis
tools_if_shown.description: Use for current portfolio questions about which companies are missing, behind, on, or ahead of plan, why they missed, and which interventions are explicitly documented. The tool enumerates the current portfolio pool and accepts only dated company-level explicit plan-versus-actual evidence or formal board/management status. It reports coverage and preserves `[Unclear]` for unsupported causes or interventions. It never uses raw KPI deltas, runway, marks, MOIC, or sentiment rankings as plan evidence.

tools_if_shown.name: portfolio_analysis
tools_if_shown.description: Use before the standalone Standard Metrics connector whenever a question asks which companies are active/current in an Inspired fund or ranks a fund-scoped cohort. This tool owns fund membership and held-position categorization; Standard Metrics online/pending/offline is reporting connectivity only. Use for deterministic base metrics and structured analytical questions across Inspired funds and portfolio companies: current Standard Metrics company-list count with explicit abstention on an unverified active-only count; fund committed/deployed/NAV/AUM and position counts; company invested cost, current value, MOIC/value-cost, ownership; active/current fund-scoped cohorts, using fund-tracker membership and held-position fields while treating Standard Metrics online/pending/offline as reporting connectivity only; current Standard Metrics fields such as ARR, revenue, growth, margin, burn, runway, cash, and headcount; PortCo Smash sentiment, follow-on/reserve analysis, ownership/MOIC exposure, healthcare or sector cuts, concentration/correlation, and partner-sentiment matrices. Returns answer-ready markdown with source and as-of dates. Base metric questions bypass semantic recall and model composition. Use portco brief workflows only for qualitative single-company narrative, not for a base metric lookup. Use missing_plan_analysis for plan-status, root-cause, and intervention questions.

tools_if_shown.name: firm_memory_health
tools_if_shown.description: Operational visibility for partners. Returns a markdown table of retrievable `sources` + approved `mentions` per `source_type`, latest source-event age, last successful automated check, embedding coverage, and async-job queue state. Use when the partner asks 'what's in firm-memory right now?' or 'when was the last sync?' or to check if a stuck ingest is hiding stale data. No arguments. Output the markdown verbatim. Staleness markers apply to automated checks, not quiet event streams.

tools_if_shown.name: granola_exclusion_diagnostic
tools_if_shown.description: Read-only acceptance diagnostic for the Granola preparatory-note exclusion contract. It derives live canaries internally and returns only one-way hashes, candidate counts, pre/post ranks, fixed influence flags, completeness state, and a terminal PASS, FAIL, or TEST_INCOMPLETE grade. It never returns meeting titles, attendees, note text, transcript text, snippets, companies, people, or exception messages. Use for firm-memory smoke G6 and partner-device setup. No arguments. Output the JSON verbatim. Never turn TEST_INCOMPLETE into PASS.

tools_if_shown.name: airtable_authority_diagnostic
tools_if_shown.description: Read-only acceptance diagnostic for Inspired's authoritative portfolio Airtable views. It checks the pinned point-person, memo, board-update, founder, talent, network, Revenue and M&A intro, and fundraising-intro contracts inside firm-memory. It returns only table and view IDs, counts, stable source IDs, lowercase manifest_sha256 and inventory_sha256 values, privacy-safe sync freshness fields, fixed booleans, and failure reason codes. It never returns record names, people, intro details, memo text, board text, or exception messages. Use for firm-memory smoke AT1. No arguments. Output the JSON verbatim. Never turn TEST_INCOMPLETE into PASS.

tools_if_shown.name: augment_with_alphasense
tools_if_shown.description: Use when the partner has run an AlphaSense GenSearch query in their browser and wants to splice the response into a prior firm-memory brief. Takes the prior brief markdown + the pasted AlphaSense response (the GenSearch output with `[[N • Source]]` citations and themed sections). Persists the paste as a real firm-memory source so future briefs auto-include it; returns the augmented brief with the AlphaSense content spliced into the industry-baseline section (or appended if no such section). Trigger phrasing: 'augment with: <paste>' or 'augment this brief with this AlphaSense response: <paste>'.

tools_if_shown.name: firm_deliberation_history
tools_if_shown.description: Returns exact excerpts from qualifying multi-partner Inspired team discussions after a date. Use for past debate, tensions, disagreement signals, consensus signals, decisions, and open questions. Results never substitute generic industry views, company analogs, founder pitches, CRM text, or personal prep. Candidate states remain pending until Luke confirms or rejects the exact excerpt. Individual speakers stay blank unless a separate exact reviewed span supports the name.

tools_if_shown.name: discussion_question_patterns
tools_if_shown.description: Returns exact, cited passages from past Inspired discussions that can inform target-specific diligence questions. Each row includes an underwriting axis, suggested question, resolution evidence, source lane, recurrence status, team-versus-meeting attribution, and speaker-review status. Internal rows are labeled Inspired team discussion while the individual speaker stays blank pending exact human review. Founder pitches may appear only as unattributed observed_diligence_question evidence, never as firm belief. Use this after grounding the target's facts; pass that target context in query.

tools_if_shown.name: review_firm_deliberation
tools_if_shown.description: Records Luke's explicit confirmation or rejection of one exact excerpt returned in a firm_deliberation_history deliberation_review field. The write is source-local, transcript-snapshot-bound, audited, and idempotent. Call only after Luke answers that exact prompt. A post-founder internal debrief retained in the same meeting may be reviewed only with review_scope='post_external_internal_debrief' and exact departure evidence that ends before the excerpt. Confirming an event state does not name a speaker or prove who held each side.

tools_if_shown.name: confirm_discussion_speaker
tools_if_shown.description: Records Luke's explicit speaker confirmation for one exact Granola transcript excerpt returned in a discussion_question_patterns speaker_review field. Call only after Luke directly answers who said that exact excerpt. The write is source-local, snapshot-bound, audited, and idempotent. Never infer from attendees, transcript labels, nearby turns, vocatives, or topic ownership.

tools_if_shown.name: pattern_match_structured
tools_if_shown.description: Returns up to N companies analogous to the query, with full provenance and verifier reasoning per candidate. Use when you (the skill / partner) want analog candidates the firm has seen with structured fields: company, source URL, quote, speaker, verifier score, verifier axis_match. Replaces the markdown-rendered pattern_match for skill use cases. Fail-closed: empty list on retrieval / verifier failure.

tools_if_shown.name: recall_historical_structured
tools_if_shown.description: Returns up to N verbatim quotes from firm-memory about a specific company, with source URLs, timestamps, speakers, and entity status. Combines entity-linked retrieval with text-match fallback so recent mentions not yet linked to the canonical entity still surface (Q8 Niural fix). Deterministic policy filters run (test-data, AI-Analyst, injection, phatic, metadata). No Claude verifier — recall is quote retrieval, not relevance scoring.

tools_if_shown.name: companies_in_space_structured
tools_if_shown.description: Returns companies in firm-memory matching the topic/sector/theme, with verifier reasoning per candidate (axis_match, score, confidence). The verifier filters semantic noise — if asked for 'healthcare workflow AI', returns only candidates whose actual business is on that axis, not every cosine-similar neighbor. Fail-closed: empty on retrieval / verifier failure.

tools_if_shown.name: pitch_summary_structured
tools_if_shown.description: Returns one structured record per pitch meeting in a date range. Each record: company, meeting_date, granola_url, 1-2 sentence summary, Granola transcript coverage fields, entity_status, and is_portco. Inclusive by default: does not suppress meetings solely because a firm-memory entity label says portco. Use for /pitch-retrospective coverage plus analyst hypotheses and public outcome lookup.

tools_if_shown.name: environment_get
tools_if_shown.description: Lists the Make zone, organizations, and teams reachable through this connection, including private spaces. Most Make resources belong to a team; other tools require the organizationId and teamId returned here. Call this first when you need ids. A private space id is valid wherever a teamId is accepted.

tools_if_shown.name: scenarios_list
tools_if_shown.description: List scenarios (scenarios): List all scenarios for a team. Results can be narrowed to one folder (optionally including its subfolders) and/or to scenarios carrying at least one of the given scenario labels. Returned scenarios include their assigned labels.

tools_if_shown.name: scenarios_get
tools_if_shown.description: Get scenario (scenarios): Get a scenario and its blueprint by ID.

tools_if_shown.name: scenarios_create
tools_if_shown.description: Create scenario (scenarios): Create a new scenario from a blueprint. Verify every module name in the blueprint via app-modules_list before creating — never invent module identifiers. The created scenario starts INACTIVE: call scenarios_activate before scenarios_run can execute it.

tools_if_shown.name: scenarios_update
tools_if_shown.description: Update scenario (scenarios): Update a scenario. The `blueprint` parameter wholesale-REPLACES the existing blueprint (no merging): always fetch the current blueprint with scenarios_get first, edit that JSON, and send the complete result. Tool scenarios (created via tools_create) cannot be blueprint-edited with this tool — use tools_update.

tools_if_shown.name: scenarios_delete
tools_if_shown.description: Delete scenario (scenarios): Delete a scenario.

tools_if_shown.name: scenarios_activate
tools_if_shown.description: Activate scenario (scenarios): Activate a scenario. Required before scenarios_run can execute it. If this fails with 'Scenario is already running', the scenario is already active — treat that as success and do not retry.

tools_if_shown.name: scenarios_deactivate
tools_if_shown.description: Deactivate scenario (scenarios): Deactivate a scenario. If this fails with 'Scenario is not running', the scenario is already inactive — treat that as success and do not retry.

tools_if_shown.name: scenarios_run
tools_if_shown.description: Run scenario (scenarios): Execute a scenario with optional input data. The scenario must be ACTIVE — a run of an inactive scenario fails with 'Scenario is not activated', so call scenarios_activate first (newly created scenarios start inactive). Returns an executionId: after a failed or suspicious run, inspect it with executions_get-detail BEFORE retrying or editing the scenario. A scenario cannot run twice concurrently — on 'Scenario is already being executed', wait for the running execution instead of retrying.

tools_if_shown.name: scenarios_replay
tools_if_shown.description: Replay scenario execution (scenarios): Replay a past execution of a scenario, re-running it with the trigger data the original execution received. Get candidate execution IDs from executions_list. Only executions whose input data is still stored can be replayed — 'Execution is not replayable' means that execution's data has expired or was never stored, so try a MORE RECENT execution instead of retrying the same one. Only the first ID in executionIds is replayed. The scenario must be ACTIVE. A replay starts a real execution and consumes operations exactly like scenarios_run; it returns the executionId of the NEW execution, which you can inspect with executions_get-detail.

tools_if_shown.name: scenarios_interface
tools_if_shown.description: Get scenario interface (scenarios): Get the interface for a scenario.

tools_if_shown.name: scenarios_set-interface
tools_if_shown.description: Set scenario interface (scenarios): Update the interface for a scenario.

tools_if_shown.name: executions_list
tools_if_shown.description: List executions (executions): List executions for a scenario.

tools_if_shown.name: executions_get-detail
tools_if_shown.description: Get execution detail (executions): Get the full per-module detail of an execution: the inputs and outputs of each module, the failing module and its error. ALWAYS call this after a failed or suspicious run BEFORE retrying or editing the scenario. For lightweight status/duration metadata only, use executions_get instead.

tools_if_shown.name: executions_get
tools_if_shown.description: Get execution (executions): Get execution metadata only: status, duration, operations consumed and error class — NOT per-module inputs/outputs. To see what each module did or why a run failed, use executions_get-detail instead.

tools_if_shown.name: folders_list
tools_if_shown.description: List folders (folders): List scenario folders for a team. If you do not know the teamId, find it via organizations_list (each organization lists its teams) or teams_list, or ask the user — never guess IDs.

tools_if_shown.name: folders_create
tools_if_shown.description: Create folder (folders): Create a new folder.

tools_if_shown.name: folders_update
tools_if_shown.description: Update folder (folders): Update an existing folder.

tools_if_shown.name: folders_delete
tools_if_shown.description: Delete folder (folders): Delete a folder.

tools_if_shown.name: scenario-labels_list
tools_if_shown.description: List scenario labels (scenario-labels): List a team's scenario label catalog, including how many scenarios carry each label. Scenario labels are team-scoped tags that can be assigned to scenarios, independent of folders. If you do not know the teamId, find it via organizations_list (each organization lists its teams) or teams_list, or ask the user — never guess IDs.

tools_if_shown.name: scenario-labels_create
tools_if_shown.description: Create scenario label (scenario-labels): Create a new scenario label in a team. Labels are team-scoped tags that can be assigned to scenarios. If you do not know the teamId, call users_me to learn it.

tools_if_shown.name: scenario-labels_update
tools_if_shown.description: Update scenario label (scenario-labels): Update the name, colour, or description of an existing scenario label. Provide at least one property to change; omitted properties are left unchanged. Changes are reflected on every scenario carrying the label.

tools_if_shown.name: scenario-labels_delete
tools_if_shown.description: Delete scenario label (scenario-labels): Delete a scenario label. The label is removed from the team catalog and unassigned from every scenario carrying it. This cannot be undone.

tools_if_shown.name: scenario-labels_assign
tools_if_shown.description: Assign scenario label (scenario-labels): Assign a scenario label to a scenario. The label and the scenario must belong to the same team. Assigning an already-assigned label succeeds without changes. To label many scenarios, call this tool once per scenario.

tools_if_shown.name: scenario-labels_unassign
tools_if_shown.description: Unassign scenario label (scenario-labels): Remove a scenario label from a scenario. Removing an already-absent assignment succeeds without changes. The label itself stays in the team catalog.

tools_if_shown.description: List webhooks/mailhooks (hooks): List webhooks/mailhooks for a specific team.

tools_if_shown.name: hook-incomings_stats
tools_if_shown.description: Get webhook queue stats (hook-incomings): Get the current size and limit of a webhook's processing queue.

tools_if_shown.name: hook-incomings_get
tools_if_shown.description: Get webhook queue item detail (hook-incomings): Get the full detail of a single queued item, including its payload when available. Confidential hooks omit payload data.

tools_if_shown.name: hook-incomings_delete
tools_if_shown.description: Delete webhook queue items (hook-incomings): Delete items from a webhook's processing queue. Specify `ids` to delete specific items, or `all: true` (with `confirmed: true`) to clear the entire queue. An item currently being processed cannot be deleted.

tools_if_shown.description: List credential requests (credential-requests): Retrieve a list of credential requests. Each request can contain multiple credentials (connections and API keys). Filter by team, user, provider, status, or name to find specific requests.

tools_if_shown.name: credential-requests_get
tools_if_shown.description: Get credential request details (credential-requests): Retrieve detailed information about a specific credential request by its ID. Returns all associated credentials with their authorization status, provider configuration, user details, and authorization URLs for pending credentials. Use this to check the state of credentials within a request.

tools_if_shown.name: credential-requests_delete
tools_if_shown.description: Delete credential request (credential-requests): Permanently delete a credential request and all associated credentials (connections and API keys) by ID. Any scenarios using connections from this request will lose access to the corresponding services. This action cannot be undone.

tools_if_shown.name: credential-requests_credential-decline
tools_if_shown.description: Decline credential (credential-requests): Decline a credential authorization request by ID, setting its status to "declined" and preventing it from being authorized. An optional reason can be provided to explain the decision. This operation is idempotent - declining an already-declined credential has no additional effect.

tools_if_shown.name: credential-requests_credential-delete
tools_if_shown.description: Delete credential (credential-requests): Delete a credential (e.g., revoke OAuth tokens or remove stored API keys) and reset its state to pending. Use this when a credential needs re-authorization with updated permissions, tokens have become stale, or you want to force re-authentication. After deletion, the credential can be authorized again through the normal flow.

tools_if_shown.name: credential-requests_create
tools_if_shown.description: Create credential request (credential-requests): Create a credential request for the currently authenticated user to set up connections and keys. This will return a URL where the user can authorize the credentials, so that they can be used in scenarios.

tools_if_shown.name: credential-requests_create-by-credentials
tools_if_shown.description: Create credential request by connection/key types (credential-requests): Create a credential request for one or more connections (OAuth) and/or keys (API keys) by their type identifiers (e.g. "google", "slack", "apikeyauth"). Use this when you know the exact connection or key types needed. The response includes the created request, an array of credentials associated with the request, and a publicUri where the end-user must go to authorize the requested credentials. At least one connection or one key must be provided.

tools_if_shown.name: credential-requests_extend-connection
tools_if_shown.description: Extend connection OAuth scopes (credential-requests): Add new OAuth scopes to an existing connection. Use this when a connection exists but lacks the permissions (scopes) needed for a specific operation. Creates a credential request that the end-user must authorize via the returned publicUri to grant the additional scopes. Fails if all requested scopes are already present on the connection — that error means the connection already satisfies the requirement: treat it as success and use the connection as-is; do not retry.

tools_if_shown.name: credential-requests_list-app-modules-with-creds
tools_if_shown.description: List app modules with credentials (credential-requests): List all modules of a given Make app (and version) that require credentials, along with the required credential type and OAuth scopes. Use this to discover which modules exist for an app before constructing a credential request — the returned `id` values are what you pass in `credentials[].appModules` for `credential-requests_create`. For custom/SDK apps, prefix the app name with `app#` (e.g. `app#my-custom-app`).
