tools_if_shown.description: List timezones (enums): List all available timezones.

tools_if_shown.name: public-templates_list
tools_if_shown.description: List public templates (public-templates): Search and list public (approved) templates available for anyone. Supports name-based search for template discovery. Results are sorted by usage by default.

tools_if_shown.name: public-templates_get
tools_if_shown.description: Get public template (public-templates): Get details of a public template by its URL slug (e.g. "12289-add-webhook-data-to-a-google-sheet"). Use this for templates discovered via public-templates_list.

tools_if_shown.name: public-templates_get-blueprint
tools_if_shown.description: Get public template blueprint (public-templates): Get the full blueprint of a public template including scenario flow, controller configuration, scheduling, and metadata. Use this for templates discovered via public-templates_list.

tools_if_shown.name: templates_list
tools_if_shown.description: List templates (templates): List templates. Omit teamId to list every status the caller can see; provide teamId to scope the list to that team's own templates.

tools_if_shown.name: templates_get
tools_if_shown.description: Get template (templates): Get details of a template by its ID. Use this for templates discovered via templates_list.

tools_if_shown.name: templates_get-blueprint
tools_if_shown.description: Get template blueprint (templates): Get the full blueprint of a template including scenario flow, controller configuration, scheduling, and metadata.

tools_if_shown.name: templates_create
tools_if_shown.description: Create template (templates): Create a new template in a team's library from a blueprint.

tools_if_shown.name: templates_update
tools_if_shown.description: Update template (templates): Update a template's name, blueprint, scheduling, or controller configuration.

tools_if_shown.name: templates_delete
tools_if_shown.description: Delete template (templates): Delete a template.

tools_if_shown.name: private-spaces_list
tools_if_shown.description: List private spaces (private-spaces): List the private spaces of an organization. Requires the organization's private-spaces feature to be enabled (error IM903 otherwise) and the 'personal team manage' permission. Private spaces cannot be created or deleted through the API — they are provisioned automatically by organization settings.

tools_if_shown.name: private-spaces_get
tools_if_shown.description: Get private space (private-spaces): Get details of a specific private space, including usage totals (operations, transfer, centicredits). Callers who are not members of the space receive a 404 even when the space exists.

tools_if_shown.name: private-spaces_update
tools_if_shown.description: Update private space (private-spaces): Update a private space's operations limit. Set operationsLimit to null to remove the limit (unlimited); the transfer limit is derived automatically. When the new limit is below the space's current consumption the call fails with IM004 unless 'confirmed' is true — confirming pauses the space.

tools_if_shown.name: custom-property-structures_list
tools_if_shown.description: List custom property structures (custom-property-structures): List the custom property structures defined for an organization. Requires the organization's custom-properties feature to be enabled (error IM027 otherwise). At most one structure can exist per combination of associated type, belonger type, and belonger ID — currently 'scenario'/'organization' is the only supported combination — and structures cannot be deleted through the API.

tools_if_shown.name: custom-property-structures_create
tools_if_shown.description: Create custom property structure (custom-property-structures): Create a custom property structure for an organization. Only one structure can exist per (associatedType, belongerType, belongerId) combination — creating a second one for the same organization fails with IM005. Once created, a structure cannot be deleted through the API. Use 'scenario' as associatedType and 'organization' as belongerType — these are the only values the API currently accepts.

tools_if_shown.name: custom-property-structure-items_list
tools_if_shown.description: List custom property structure items (custom-property-structure-items): List the items (field definitions) of a custom property structure. Use custom-property-structures_list to find the structure ID.

tools_if_shown.name: custom-property-structure-items_create
tools_if_shown.description: Create custom property structure item (custom-property-structure-items): Create an item (field definition) in a custom property structure. The item's name and type cannot be changed after creation. `options` is required for the 'dropdown' and 'multiselect' types and not allowed for any other type.

tools_if_shown.name: custom-property-structure-items_update
tools_if_shown.description: Update custom property structure item (custom-property-structure-items): Update a custom property structure item. The item's name and type cannot be changed. When updating `options` of a 'dropdown'/'multiselect' item, the new set fully replaces the current one — existing scenario data referencing removed options is not remapped.

tools_if_shown.name: custom-property-structure-items_delete
tools_if_shown.description: Delete custom property structure item (custom-property-structure-items): Delete a custom property structure item. Deleting an item also deletes any scenario data filled in for it — this is irreversible. If scenarios already have data for the item, the call fails with IM004 unless 'confirmed' is true.

tools_if_shown.name: scenario-custom-properties_get
tools_if_shown.description: Get scenario custom properties data (scenario-custom-properties): Get the custom properties data filled in for a scenario.

tools_if_shown.name: scenario-custom-properties_create
tools_if_shown.description: Fill in scenario custom properties data (scenario-custom-properties): Fill in custom properties data for a scenario for the first time. Fails with IM005 if the scenario already has data — use scenario-custom-properties_update or scenario-custom-properties_replace instead. Every item marked required in the custom property structure must be given a value. Use custom-property-structure-items_list to see the available items.

tools_if_shown.name: scenario-custom-properties_replace
tools_if_shown.description: Replace scenario custom properties data (scenario-custom-properties): Replace all custom properties data for a scenario. Fails with IM013 if the scenario has no data yet — use scenario-custom-properties_create first. Every item marked required in the structure must be given a value.

tools_if_shown.name: scenario-custom-properties_update
tools_if_shown.description: Update scenario custom properties data (scenario-custom-properties): Merge-update custom properties data for a scenario; only the specified items are changed. Fails with IM013 if the scenario has no data yet — use scenario-custom-properties_create first.

tools_if_shown.name: scenario-custom-properties_delete
tools_if_shown.description: Delete scenario custom properties data (scenario-custom-properties): Delete all custom properties data for a scenario. This is irreversible.

tools_if_shown.name: audit-logs_list
tools_if_shown.description: List organization audit logs (audit-logs): List the audit log entries of an organization: who changed what and when, across the organization and all of its teams. Entries carry no event-specific payload — call audit-logs_get with the organizationId and uuid from the entry to see that. Requires the Admin or Owner role on the organization.

tools_if_shown.name: audit-logs_list-for-team
tools_if_shown.description: List team audit logs (audit-logs): List the audit log entries of a single team: who changed what and when within that team. Entries carry no event-specific payload — call audit-logs_get with the organizationId and uuid from the entry to see that. Use audit-logs_list instead to cover a whole organization.

tools_if_shown.name: audit-logs_get
tools_if_shown.description: Get audit log detail (audit-logs): Get a single audit log entry together with its event-specific detail payload — the part the list tools omit. Call this to find out what actually changed in an event surfaced by audit-logs_list or audit-logs_list-for-team.

tools_if_shown.name: audit-logs_get-filters
tools_if_shown.description: Get organization audit log filters (audit-logs): Get the values accepted by the filters of audit-logs_list for an organization: selectable users for author, teams for team, and events for event. Call this first when building a filtered audit log query, so the filter values are real rather than guessed.

tools_if_shown.name: audit-logs_get-filters-for-team
tools_if_shown.description: Get team audit log filters (audit-logs): Get the values accepted by the filters of audit-logs_list-for-team: selectable users for author and events for event. Call this first when building a filtered team audit log query, so the filter values are real rather than guessed.

tools_if_shown.name: apps_list
tools_if_shown.description: Retrieves a list of Apps available for Scenario Building in the given Organization and Team.

tools_if_shown.name: app-modules_list
tools_if_shown.description: Retrieves a list of Modules available for the given App in the given Organization and Team. Every module of a premium app carries `premiumApp: true` and, when known, `premiumTier` (1 = paid plans only, 3 = Enterprise only); an organization whose plan is below that tier cannot run a scenario containing the app.

tools_if_shown.name: app-module_get
tools_if_shown.description: Retrieves a single Module from the given App in the given Organization. A module of a premium app is annotated `premiumApp: true` and, when known, `premiumTier` (1 = paid plans only, 3 = Enterprise only) — in `_annotations` in JSON format; an organization whose plan is below that tier cannot run a scenario containing the app.

tools_if_shown.name: hook-config_get
tools_if_shown.description: Retrieves the manifest and form configuration of a hook TYPE (not a hook instance — use hooks_get for that). Use this to understand what fields are required when configuring a hook, e.g. before hooks_create.

tools_if_shown.name: connection-metadata_get
tools_if_shown.description: Retrieves metadata of the given connection, or returns an error when the connection type doesn't exist.

tools_if_shown.name: hook-metadata_get
tools_if_shown.description: Retrieves metadata of the given hook TYPE (not a hook instance — use hooks_get for that), or returns an error when the hook type doesn't exist.

tools_if_shown.name: key-metadata_get
tools_if_shown.description: Retrieves metadata of the given key, or returns an error when the key type doesn't exist.

tools_if_shown.name: rpc_execute
tools_if_shown.description:
Executes a Make Remote Procedure Call (RPC) with the provided input.
	Before executing an RPC, be sure you know its exact name and the input parameters that should be passed to the 'data' field.
	There is no RPC-listing tool — never guess RPC names. Discover them via 'app-module_get' (requires the
	'apps:read' scope): the module's parameter instructions reference the RPCs it uses (e.g. as 'rpc://...'
	option sources). If 'app-module_get' is not available in this conversation, ask the user for the exact RPC name.
	You can also use RPCs to provide answers for simple "read" or "list" queries, if the corresponding RPC is available,
	so it's not needed to create a full Tool to achieve such a thing.

tools_if_shown.name: apps_recommend
tools_if_shown.description: Based on the user's intention, recommend applications that can assist in achieving their goals. This tool should provide a list of applications that are relevant to the user's needs, including their names and versions.

tools_if_shown.name: tools_create
tools_if_shown.description:
This tool creates a new Tool in the system based on provided parameters.
It allows users to define custom tools that can be used in various scenarios.
Use it to add new functionalities to the platform by specifying tool details.

Use this tool also when you're tasked to perform a simple action.
It's easier to configure a tool rather than a whole Scenario.

Important! Before creating a tool, call 'app-module_get' to check how the module should actually be mapped,
then create the mapping, and only then create the tool with this mapping.
Even more important is to call 'app-module_get' with the 'instructions' format requested.
That way, you'll get perfect instructions for how to fill in the module's configuration.

Don't create unnecessary inputs. Create them only for values that should be dynamic,
hardcode everything else in the module parameters.

When the Module requires a Credential (Connection or Key) to be set,
list the existing connections or keys of the corresponding type to see if there are any available.
If there are available connections or keys for the Module, ask the user whether they want to use one of the available connections or keys.
When asking this question, also provide the user with an option to not use available connections, and to create a new connection or key instead.
In case user chooses an option to create a new connection or key, you should request the User to provide you with a new Connection or Key, for that, use the Credential Request Create Tool.
In case there are no available connections or keys of the corresponding type for the Module you are creating,
you should also request the User to provide you with a new Connection or Key, for that, use the Credential Request Create Tool.

If you need to run the Tool, use 'scenarios_run', passing the Tool ID as the scenarioId.
Note: a Tool's blueprint cannot be edited via 'scenarios_update' — use 'tools_update' instead.

tools_if_shown.name: tools_get
tools_if_shown.description: Retrieves details of a specific Tool by its ID.

tools_if_shown.name: tools_update
tools_if_shown.description:
This tool updates an existing Tool's details based on provided parameters.
It allows users to modify the properties of a Tool to keep it up-to-date with changing requirements.
Use it to refine or correct Tool information as needed.

tools_if_shown.name: validate_module_configuration
tools_if_shown.description:
This tool validates that parameters and mapper collection are correctly configured for a given module in a given app.
Use this tool before creating a new Make Tool or Make Scenario to verify that the configuration of modules is correct.
Use this tool to iterate towards a successful validation result.
Before generating parameters and mapper objects for the module,
learn instructions for filling them in by getting the module detail in the "instructions" format.
Required fields with declared defaults that you omitted are filled automatically, including fields
that only exist after remote resolution; when the result contains "appliedDefaults", the
"normalizedValues" object carries the filled configuration. When "valid" is true, send
"normalizedValues.default" as "parameters" and "normalizedValues.expect" as "mapper" instead of
inventing values for fields you did not see in the schema; when "valid" is false, fix the reported
errors on top of those objects first.

tools_if_shown.name: validate_epoch_configuration
tools_if_shown.description: Validates the Epoch Configuration of particular Trigger Module.

tools_if_shown.name: validate_blueprint_schema
tools_if_shown.description: Validates the overall structure of the Scenario Blueprint against the Schema. STRUCTURAL check only — it does NOT verify that module names exist or that module parameters are correct, so a valid blueprint can still fail at scenarios_create with "Module not found". Verify module names via app-modules_list and module configurations via validate_module_configuration.

tools_if_shown.name: validate_scheduling_schema
tools_if_shown.description: Validates the Scheduling of the Scenario against the Schema.

tools_if_shown.name: app_documentation_get
tools_if_shown.description:
Retrieves markdown documentation for the specific Make App.
Use when configuring Make Apps and Modules and when you need to learn more about the available capabilities.

tools_if_shown.name: validate_hook_configuration
tools_if_shown.description:
This tool validates that hook configuration values are correctly set for a given hook type.
Use this tool before creating a hook to verify that the configuration is correct.
Use this tool to iterate towards a successful validation result.
Before generating values, learn instructions by getting the hook config in the "instructions" format.

tools_if_shown.name: validate_scenario_interface
tools_if_shown.description: Use this tool to validate a typed Scenario Interface before applying changes. Either side (`input`, `output`) may be omitted; only the side(s) supplied are validated.

tools_if_shown.name: extract_blueprint_components
tools_if_shown.description:
This tool analyzes a given Blueprint and extracts a list of various Connections, Keys, Hooks and other components that are required to be provided in order to map the Blueprint properly.
Use this tool to identify all necessary components to collect before creating a new Make Scenario based on the Blueprint.
The output will help in preparing the Scenario by ensuring all required resources are available.

tools_if_shown.name: extract_module_components
tools_if_shown.description: Extracts the list of Components required by the particular Module. Use to identify what Connections, Keys, Hooks and other resources are needed to work with the Module.

tools_if_shown.name: connection-requirements_get
tools_if_shown.description: Reports which connections and API keys a set of planned modules require, and which of the team's existing credentials already satisfy each requirement (with their ids). Each module returns one SLOT per required credential parameter; a slot's `options` are ALTERNATIVE provider types — any one of them satisfies the slot. Use it to verify a build plan before presenting it: pass every module the scenario will contain. Connections of a matching type whose granted scopes do NOT cover the slot's required scopes are listed separately in `existingInsufficientScopes` (re-auth candidates, never counted as satisfying). Modules that do not exist in the catalog for this organization are returned in `notFound`; credential types whose lookups transiently failed are listed in `failedLookups` (with human-readable diagnostics in `errors`) and must be treated as unknown rather than missing.

tools_if_shown.name: hooks_learn_start
tools_if_shown.description: Starts learning mode ("Detect new values") on a webhook/mailhook: the hook determines its incoming data structure from the next request it receives, without the scenario running. Learning stops automatically once data arrives.

tools_if_shown.name: hooks_learn_stop
tools_if_shown.description: Stops learning mode ("Detect new values") on a webhook/mailhook without waiting for data.

tools_if_shown.name: hooks_ping
tools_if_shown.description: Returns the live status of a webhook/mailhook: its address, whether it is attached to a scenario, whether learning mode ("Detect new values") is active, and whether it is gone. `learning: false` after a learn-start means the data structure was captured (or learning was stopped).

tools_if_shown.name: data-structures_generate
tools_if_shown.description: Generates Data Structure Definition in Make Parameters Format from the sample data provided as input.

tools_if_shown.name: show_scenarios_list
tools_if_shown.description: Renders an interactive UI in the chat — a searchable, folder-filterable, sortable list of the team's scenarios showing each scenario's status, used apps, and usage. Only call this when the user explicitly wants the list displayed. Do NOT call this while iterating/authoring — use `scenarios_list` instead, which returns the same data without rendering a UI.

tools_if_shown.name: show_executions_list
tools_if_shown.description: Renders a scenario’s execution history as an interactive widget in the chat — each past run with its status, trigger type, duration, and consumption. Only call this when the user explicitly wants the history displayed. Do NOT call this while iterating/debugging — use `executions_list` instead, which returns the same data without rendering a UI.

tools_if_shown.name: show_execution_result
tools_if_shown.description: Renders a scenario execution’s outcome — status, outputs, and consumption — as an interactive widget in the chat, for a past or in-progress run. Only call this when the user explicitly wants the result displayed. Do NOT call this to check on a run you just triggered — `scenarios_run` already renders its own live-updating result and needs no follow-up call. For headless status/output checks while iterating, use `executions_get`/`executions_get-detail` instead. A `RUNNING` status means the execution is still in progress. Requires the `scenarios:read` scope on the scenario’s team: on “Insufficient rights” or “Access denied”, verify the scenarioId via `scenarios_list` instead of retrying — the scenario likely belongs to a team your token cannot read. On “Too Many Requests”, stop polling and wait before the next call.

detail_provenance.offline_parser_correction: Decoded escaped leading dollar literals and omitted Flight undefined properties; original HTML hash/timestamp retained.

published_auth_text: pietro.zullo requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.

published_tools.source: published FAQ (same names as visible imported tool chips)

tools_if_shown.name: init_skilder
tools_if_shown.description: Initializes a Skilder session and lists the available roles, skills, and the tools they unlock. Required before any other Skilder tool — they return an error while no session is initialized. The response includes a session id: subsequent Skilder tool calls require it in their `sessionId` argument and return an error without it. Accepts an optional agent-authored task summary — one sentence, never the user's verbatim message — that labels the session and steers which role Skilder suggests.

tools_if_shown.name: learn
tools_if_shown.description:
Access roles, skills, and resources using path-based navigation. Roles are the entry point: init_skilder lists the available roles — learn one to unlock its skills and their tools. Always provide a full path with a role or skill name — "/" alone is not a valid path.

Path formats (the leading "/" is optional):
- `roles/Role Name` - Learn a role and all its skills at once (start here — init_skilder lists the roles)
- `Skill Name` or `/Skill Name` - Revisit a single skill from a learned role to get its instructions and tools again
- `Skill Name/document.md` - Get a specific resource from a skill

Examples:
- `learn(path="roles/Developer")` - Learn all skills in the Developer role
- `learn(path="Data Processing")` - Revisit the Data Processing skill
- `learn(path="Data Processing/readme.md")` - Get the readme resource

tools_if_shown.name: execute_script
tools_if_shown.description:
Execute a script from a skill with optional CLI-style arguments.

Path format: `/Skill Name/script.py [args]`

Examples:
- `execute_script(path="/Data Processing/transform.py")`
- `execute_script(path="/Data Processing/transform.py --input data.csv --output result.json")`
- `execute_script(path="/Automation/deploy.sh --env staging")`

Scripts run on their linked runtime.

Files: pass an `@skilder-file:/<fileId>/<name>` path from `upload_skilder_file`, `learn` or another tool, or an `@skilder-asset:` path, as a whole argument or as `--name=<path>`, unchanged and in double quotes if it contains a space or an apostrophe — the script receives a local path to a fresh copy of the file. A `@skilder-file:/<fileId>/<name>` path does not expire, while an `@skilder-asset:` path changes when its skill is published; any other `@skilder-file:` path is refused. Files the script returns come back as `@skilder-file:/<fileId>/<name>` paths kept in the workspace, which any later call can take; fetch one with `read_skilder_file`.

tools_if_shown.name: feedback_skill
tools_if_shown.description: Report feedback about a skill or tool; it is recorded in the workspace activity trace for the skill's author. Useful when: (1) a skill/tool call fails or blocks the task, (2) the user re-asks for the same outcome shortly after a skill attempt, (3) the user explicitly corrects you about a skill/tool's behavior, or (4) you notice a concrete, specific defect yourself (e.g. instructions that were ambiguous and caused a wrong first attempt, a schema mismatch, information you had to guess at). Not intended for successful completions or vague quality opinions. Keep the feedback concise (1-3 sentences) and concrete: what was attempted, what actually happened vs. expected, and — if evident — the likely cause.

tools_if_shown.name: run_read_tool
tools_if_shown.description: Execute a read-only tool unlocked by learning a skill. Only tools whose upstream server declares them read-only are served here; write-capable tools return an error naming run_write_tool. Use the tool_name exactly as provided when you learned the skill, and pass the arguments as a JSON object matching the tool's input schema.

tools_if_shown.name: run_write_tool
tools_if_shown.description: Execute a write-capable tool unlocked by learning a skill (any tool not declared read-only by its upstream server; read-only tools return an error naming run_read_tool). Use the tool_name exactly as provided when you learned the skill, and pass the arguments as a JSON object matching the tool's input schema.

tools_if_shown.name: read_skilder_file
tools_if_shown.description:
Get a short-lived signed download URL for a Skilder-managed file. Use this to pull the file's actual bytes somewhere — e.g. onto your own local disk/repo checkout, or into another tool that needs a real file rather than a path — for a file another tool (e.g. a screenshot tool) already produced at a `@skilder-file:` or `@skilder-asset:` path.

Always returns two content blocks, regardless of file type (image, text, or other binary):
- A `resource_link` block with the signed HTTPS URL.
- A text block with the file's name/size/mime type, the URL's expiry, and a ready-to-run `curl` command to download it (e.g. `curl -sSL '<url>' -o '<name>'`).

Accepted path forms:
- `@skilder-file:/<fileId>/<name>` — a file kept in the workspace: one a tool or script produced (e.g. a screenshot), one uploaded with `upload_skilder_file`, or a skill's asset as `learn` prints it. Pass the path exactly as it was returned.
- `@skilder-asset:/<resourceId>/<filename>` — any skill file: an asset, a reference or a script. `learn` prints this form for a reference, a script, or an asset not yet moved to the store.

Any other `@skilder-file:` path is refused. A fresh signed URL is minted on every call.

Examples:
- `read_skilder_file(path="@skilder-file:/3f2c9a7e-1b4d-4c8e-9a6f-2d5e7b8c0f13/step-01.png")`
- `read_skilder_file(path="@skilder-asset:/0xabc/report.csv")`

Requires `curl` on your host: the bytes move only through the signed URL. Without curl, stop and report the missing prerequisite — do not try another way to transfer the file, and never pass its contents (e.g. base64) through the conversation.

tools_if_shown.name: upload_skilder_file
tools_if_shown.description:
Push a file INTO Skilder so a tool can read it. Use this whenever a tool needs a real file you hold locally (a PDF to fill, a spreadsheet to process, an image to attach) and you only have it on your own disk.

Returns a text block containing:
- A ready-to-run `curl` command that PUTs your file to a short-lived, single-use signed HTTPS URL.
- The `@skilder-file:/<fileId>/<name>` path the file will be stored at in the workspace. The path does not expire. Pass it, whole and unchanged, as the file argument of any tool or script, also inside a list or object; the tool receives a copy of the file under its name. A tool on a remote MCP server cannot open it and refuses it.

Two steps, in order:
1. `upload_skilder_file(filename="contract.pdf")` → gives you the curl command and the path.
2. Run the curl command, then call the tool with the path, e.g. `{ "filePath": "@skilder-file:/<fileId>/contract.pdf" }`.

The curl PUT returns once the file is stored in the workspace, and its JSON response repeats the same path. If the PUT answers 409 (the URL was already used), 401 (it expired), 404 or a 5xx, call `upload_skilder_file` again for a fresh URL; a second 404 means the workspace is no longer available. 413 means the file is above the maximum size. To go the other way — pull a file out of Skilder — use `read_skilder_file`.

Requires `curl` on your host: the bytes move only through the signed URL. Without curl, stop and report the missing prerequisite — do not try another way to transfer the file, and never pass its contents (e.g. base64) through the conversation.

tools_if_shown.name: analytics
tools_if_shown.description: Read-only analytics over what Skilder agents did: activity and value summaries, breakdowns, and the session and call records behind them. Pass tool_name plus a tool_input object for that sub-tool. Records of what happened only — skills, roles and other definitions are not here. Your workspace permissions decide whose numbers come back, never an argument: every result echoes its scope and names in "withheld" what a narrower scope did not get. window is "24h", "7d", "30d", "90d", "all" or ISO dates {from, to}; default 30d for figures, 7d for lists. Sizes start small and the same call raises them: lists 20 (up to 50), breakdown rows 10 (up to 50), a session trace 100 calls (up to 500), get-call payloads 4000 characters (up to 20000). A short result says so: hasMore means pass nextOffset back as offset; an "other" row holds every group ranked after the page; truncated and resultsTruncated mean a scan hit its bound, so narrow the window before relying on affected groups or rows. A sub-tool's full input schema is available via analytics(tool_name="describe-tool", tool_input={"tool_name": "<name>"}). Available tools, with their REQUIRED tool_input arguments — optional arguments are counted, not listed: activity-overview() [+1 optional]; value-overview() [+2 optional]; activity-breakdown(metric: "calls"|"failures"|"value"|"unpriced"|"sessions"|"guardrail-decisions", by: "skill"|"tool"|"user"|"role"|"status"|"client"|"day"|"outcome"|"guardrail") [+4 optional]; list-sessions() [+8 optional]; get-session(sessionId: string) [+2 optional]; list-calls() [+13 optional]; get-call(callId: string) [+1 optional].

tools_if_shown.name: manage
tools_if_shown.description: Admin-only dispatcher for managing Skilder content: roles, skills, skill-content (references/scripts/assets), guardrail rules, org-units, and MCP servers. Pass tool_name plus a tool_input object matching that tool's arguments — for management/CRUD operations rather than learned-skill tools (no prior "learn" step is needed). Note: the list_* operations here return the full ADMIN view (including drafts, disabled items and raw ids) — this is distinct from the consumption-oriented view that "learn"/"init_skilder" surface, so it is not suitable for deciding what to learn/use. All operations run under your workspace permissions. Consent: the write operations (create/update/delete/publish/add/remove/attach/detach/reparent/install/enable) act on shared workspace content, so they need the user's explicit request or explicit approval — never modify Skilder content on your own initiative. If you judge a change is warranted, describe the change you intend and ask the user to confirm it, then call. The read operations (list-*/get-*/suggest-*/describe-tool) and test-guardrail, which runs only the rule's own script and calls no tool, need no such confirmation. Best practices and architecture context for these tools are available (admin-only) via learn(path="roles/Skilder Platform Assistant"). A sub-tool's full input schema is available via manage(tool_name="describe-tool", tool_input={"tool_name": "<name>"}). tools_if_shown.name: search
tools_if_shown.description:
Search the tldraw Editor API spec by writing JavaScript that receives a `spec` object and returns a result. The spec contains: spec.members (all Editor methods/properties with name, kind, signature, description, category), spec.categories (category names), spec.types.shapes (focused shape type definitions with props), spec.types.shapeTypes (list of all shape type strings), spec.helpers (exec helper functions with descriptions, params, examples).

Examples:
- Find shape methods: return spec.members.filter(m => m.category === "shapes").map(m => ({ name: m.name, signature: m.signature }))
- Get arrow shape props: return spec.types.shapes.find(s => s.shapeType === "arrow")
- List all categories: return spec.categories
- Find a helper: return spec.helpers.find(h => h.name === "createArrowBetweenShapes")

tools_if_shown.name: exec
tools_if_shown.description:
Execute JavaScript code on a tldraw canvas. The code runs in the widget with access to the live `editor` instance, helper functions, and normal js. Use the `search` tool first to discover available Editor methods and shape types.

Each canvas has a unique `canvasId`. Omit `canvasId` to create a new blank canvas. To edit an existing canvas, pass the `canvasId` that was returned by a previous exec call.

Shapes and text grow depending on the amount of text they have. Use clever scripting to ensure there are no unintended overlaps.

Examples:
- Create a rectangle: editor.createShape({ _type: 'rectangle', shapeId: 'box1', x: 200, y: 120, w: 320, h: 180, text: 'Hello' })
- Connect shapes with an arrow: editor.createShape({ _type: 'arrow', shapeId: 'a1', fromId: 'box1', toId: 'box2', x1: 0, y1: 0, x2: 100, y2: 0 })
- Select and zoom: editor.select('box1'); editor.zoomToSelection()
- Read shapes: return editor.getCurrentPageShapes()
- Distribute evenly: editor.distributeShapes(editor.getSelectedShapeIds(), 'horizontal')
- Box around shapes: boxShapes(['box1', 'box2'], { text: 'Group label', color: 'blue' })
- Stack shapes dynamically: editor.createShape({ _type: 'rectangle', shapeId: 'a', x: 0, y: 0, w: 300, h: 200, text: 'First box\nwith wrapping text' }); const bounds = editor.getShapePageBounds('a'); editor.createShape({ _type: 'rectangle', shapeId: 'b', x: 0, y: bounds.maxY + 20, w: 300, h: 200, text: 'Below first' })

tools_if_shown.name: discover_zapier_actions
tools_if_shown.description: Search 9,000+ apps to find actions you can enable. For authenticated services (Google Docs, Gmail, Sheets, Notion, Slack, Outlook, etc.), check here - generic web fetch tools cannot authenticate with these services. ALWAYS call this before saying 'I can't access X' or 'that app isn't available'. Call inspect_zapier_actions first: it lists the apps already enabled, and THEN call this tool to discover and enable any apps and actions that you need but that are not returned by the inspect call. After finding what you need, use enable_zapier_action to add it.

tools_if_shown.name: enable_zapier_action
tools_if_shown.description: Enable an app's actions on this MCP server. Use discover_zapier_actions first to get the exact selected_api ID, then pass it here. Always pass app_display_name from the app field returned by discover_zapier_actions so confirmations show a friendly name rather than the raw selected_api ID. Returns action details including the execute tool to use (execute_zapier_read_action or execute_zapier_write_action) and parameters. If authentication is required, also returns a URL to authenticate the app.

tools_if_shown.name: disable_zapier_action
tools_if_shown.description: Remove an app's actions from this MCP server. Use inspect_zapier_actions to see which apps are enabled and their selected_api values. Always pass app_display_name (the human-readable app name from inspect_zapier_actions) so confirmations show a friendly name rather than the raw selected_api ID. Optionally specify an action key to remove only that specific action.

tools_if_shown.name: inspect_zapier_actions
tools_if_shown.description: Call `inspect_zapier_actions` first when you create a workflow or automation, before configuring a trigger or action for Gmail, Google Sheets, Google Drive, Slack, or any other app the user has connected, and before any execute_zapier_read_action or execute_zapier_write_action call. Call `inspect_zapier_actions` with no arguments first to list every enabled app with its exact `selected_api`; then call it again with one `selected_api` from that listing for the app's actions (`action`, `action_type`, `tool_name`), including the read action that samples a trigger, then with `tool_name` for one action's parameter schema. These apps handle OAuth automatically — use them instead of generic URL fetching for authenticated services. For a parameter flagged `is_dynamic_enum: true`, call `inspect_zapier_actions` again with `tool_name`, `enum_property`, and any parent values in `params` to resolve values. For actions with `dynamic_properties_depends_on`, settle those parameters first, then call this tool again with `tool_name` and `params` to get `dynamic_properties_schema`. To learn what an action returns, call `inspect_zapier_actions` with its `tool_name`, the same `params`, and `include_output_schema: true`; `output_schema` is the declared shape of the records, nested to match them. For a trigger, type the workflow's trigger input from it when a sample read returns no records. Sampled records win where they disagree, and declared types are advisory: a field declared as a string can arrive as a list. If the unfiltered listing has no entry for the app you need, you MUST call discover_zapier_actions next — NEVER say 'I can't do that' without checking discover_zapier_actions first. When you resolve a value from the user's request, matching a single record is not proof it is the one they meant: if their input is partial or ambiguous (e.g. a first name, or a search with several close matches), enumerate the candidates and let the user pick before passing a value to an execute call. Each app's `connections.default` names the account its actions run against. If that account doesn't fit the apparent context of the request (e.g. a personal address on a work task), flag it to the user before executing and note the account can be switched per action by passing a different `connection_id` (list the options with list_zapier_connections, or connect the right account via manage_zapier_connections) — do this even when only one account is connected.

tools_if_shown.name: execute_zapier_read_action
tools_if_shown.description: Execute a search or read action to get data from a connected app. REQUIRED: You MUST call inspect_zapier_actions first to get the exact action key, tool_name, and parameter schema. NEVER guess action names — they are NOT intuitive and WILL fail. If the app isn't enabled, use discover_zapier_actions then enable_zapier_action first. Pass exact argument values in `params`. For dynamic enum parameters, call inspect_zapier_actions again with `tool_name`, `enum_property`, and parent values in `params`. For actions with `dynamic_properties_depends_on`, call inspect_zapier_actions again with `tool_name` and settled parent params to learn `dynamic_properties_schema`. Before executing, be confident that every value in `params` correctly and uniquely identifies what the user asked for — especially fields naming a person, recipient, channel, account, record, or file. If the user gave only partial or ambiguous information (e.g. just a first name, or a term that could match several entities), do NOT assume a lookup that returns a single match is the right one: many lookups return one 'best' match even when others exist. Enumerate the candidates first — prefer a search or list action that can return multiple matches, or widen your query — and when more than one plausibly fits, present the options and let the user choose rather than guessing.

tools_if_shown.name: execute_zapier_write_action
tools_if_shown.description: Execute a write or create action in a connected app. REQUIRED: You MUST call inspect_zapier_actions first to get the exact action key, tool_name, and parameter schema. NEVER guess action names — they are NOT intuitive and WILL fail. If the app isn't enabled, use discover_zapier_actions then enable_zapier_action first. Pass exact argument values in `params`. For dynamic enum parameters, call inspect_zapier_actions again with `tool_name`, `enum_property`, and parent values in `params`. For actions with `dynamic_properties_depends_on`, call inspect_zapier_actions again with `tool_name` and settled parent params to learn `dynamic_properties_schema`. Before executing, be confident that every value in `params` correctly and uniquely identifies what the user asked for — especially fields naming a person, recipient, channel, account, record, or file. If the user gave only partial or ambiguous information (e.g. just a first name, or a term that could match several entities), do NOT assume a lookup that returns a single match is the right one: many lookups return one 'best' match even when others exist. Enumerate the candidates first — prefer a search or list action that can return multiple matches, or widen your query — and when more than one plausibly fits, present the options and let the user choose rather than guessing. Write actions have real, often irreversible side effects (sending messages, creating or modifying records), so confirm the target whenever there is any doubt.

tools_if_shown.name: list_zapier_connections
tools_if_shown.description: List the Zapier connections (authenticated accounts) available for an app. Use the `selected_api` from discover_zapier_actions or the action-listing tool. Returns each connection's `connection_id` field. Pass that value as the `connection_id` argument to execute_zapier_read_action / execute_zapier_write_action to run with that specific account. By default only the user's own connections are returned; pass `include_shared: true` to also return connections shared with them, but only show the user their shared connections if they explicitly ask for it. Paginated via `cursor`.

tools_if_shown.name: manage_zapier_connections
tools_if_shown.description: Manage an app's Zapier connections. Returns a URL the user can open to connect a new account, and optionally sets the app's default connection. An app REQUIRES a default connection before any of its actions can run. If the user has no default connection for the app they want to use, share the returned `auth_url` with them and ask them to tell you once they have added the connection; after they confirm, call list_zapier_connections to find the new connection's `connection_id`, then call this tool again with that value as `default_connection_id` to set it as the default. `selected_api` MUST come verbatim from discover_zapier_actions or inspect_zapier_actions — never guess or construct it (e.g. Gmail is `GoogleMailV2CLIAPI`, not `GmailCLIAPI`). If you don't already have it, call discover_zapier_actions first. To set the default account every action for this app should use, pass `default_connection_id` (look it up with list_zapier_connections). Share the returned `auth_url` with the user; after they finish, call list_zapier_connections to see the new connection.

The code is generated from your requirements and executes in a secure sandbox with authenticated API access. IMPORTANT: Never include API keys, tokens, passwords, or other credentials in the requirements — code actions authenticate automatically through Zapier's connected accounts.
